job.title: Milton Academy Saturday Course Teacher
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Position: Saturday Course Teacher

Department: The Saturday Course

Location: CSG 128, Milton Academy Campus, Milton, MA

Hours: Saturdays - Academic Year, 7:00am - 3:00pm

FLSA: Exempt

Salary: $1,440 stipend per session (5 Saturdays, 40 hours' total or 8 hours a day from approximately 7am - 3pm)

Milton Academy is an independent college preparatory K–12 school, boarding and day in grades 9–12, located just outside of Boston.

Milton Academy cultivates in our students a passion for learning and respect for others. Milton students grow by developing their own identities, learning from and listening to the lived experiences of others, and living and working among peers whose differences they accept with respect and care.

In our ongoing work to create an environment that confronts bias, injustice, and bigotry, we encourage each other to be open to learning, explore our histories and identities, and seek to understand the world around us with a critical lens. At Milton, we prepare students to partner with their future communities to create a more just world and to have the courage to speak up and live by our motto, “Dare to be true.”

Summary of Position:

Milton Academy seeks teachers for The Saturday Course, an enrichment program for public school children in Grades 4-8 with strong academic skills. Independently motivated students can learn compelling material in a fun and exciting environment. Founded in 1978, The Saturday Course has been an integral part of the Academy’s commitment to public/private partnerships. Ideal candidates will have experience in teaching subjects in which they are passionate.

Please review our Sample Course List. as an example of the types of classes we have offered. Some specific subject areas that we are seeking at this time include but are not limited to: animals (zoology), archaeology, astronomy, aviation, creative writing, journalism, sports science, speech and debate. We encourage applicants to provide a cover letter with details about the course(s) you’d be interested in teaching.

Hours for this position are 7:00 a.m.- 3:00 p.m. on Saturdays during program dates. There are 5 sessions during the academic year – each session consists of five Saturdays. Candidates are not required to commit to teaching all sessions.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities:

  • A successful candidate will have a demonstrated ability to work in a diverse and inclusive community. Additional key qualities for this position include warmth, compassion, cultural competence, flexibility, and humility. able to work effectively and constructively with teachers, staff, administrators, and parents for the benefit of students and the community. The essential functions and basic skills have been included in this job description; it is not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all functions, responsibilities, skills and abilities. Additional functions requirements may be assigned by supervisors as deemed appropriate. This position description is subject to change at any time.

Supervision to be received: Supervised by the Saturday Course Director.

Supervision to be exercised: None.

Education/Certification/Licensure

Required: A bachelor’s degree preferred

Experience

Required: Minimum of three years of proven experience in a specific course of study.

Preferred: Experience teaching students in Grades 4-8

Competencies

Required:

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Demonstrated computer expertise, including proficiency in Google Workspace, Microsoft Office and Adobe Creative Cloud.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with internal and external constituencies.
  • Understanding of confidentiality and related issues.
  • Receptive to supervision and professional development.
  • Desire to be a part of a dynamic educational community.

Physical Abilities

Required:

  • Must be able to move around the Milton Academy campus without restriction.
  • Must be able to lift up to 10 pounds.

All interested internal candidates must complete an application for promotion or transfer and inform your supervisor as soon as possible.

The essential functions and basic skills have been included in this job description; it is not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all functions, responsibilities, skills and abilities. Additional functions and requirements may be assigned by supervisors as deemed appropriate. This position description is subject to change at any time.

An equal opportunity employer, Milton embraces diversity and the pursuit of excellence. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of race (including natural and protective hairstyle), color sex (including pregnancy and pregnancy related condition), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, religion, religious creed, physical or mental disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, ancestry, citizenship, national or ethnic origin or any other status protected by application law.

job.title: Milton Academy Dean of Students
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Position: Dean of Students

Department: Upper School

Location: Warren, Milton Academy Campus, Milton, MA

Hours: Full-time with the flexibility to work nights and weekends

FLSA: Exempt

Classification: Staff (12-month)

Residential Status: Housed Position -- On-campus residency required

Salary Range: $110,000 to $150,000 annually, based on experience and qualifications

Milton Academy is an independent college preparatory K–12 school, boarding and day in grades 9–12, located just outside of Boston.

Milton Academy cultivates in its students a passion for learning and a respect for others. Embracing diversity and the pursuit of excellence, we create a community in which individuals develop competence, confidence and character. Our active learning environment, in and out of the classroom, develops creative and critical thinkers, unafraid to express their ideas, prepared to seek meaningful lifetime success and to live by our motto, “Dare to be true.”

Summary of Position:

The dean of students oversees and directs the key elements of the Upper School's Office of Student Life for 700+ students, comprised of both boarding and day students, including international students. The Office of Student Life serves as a hub - both literally and figuratively - of student culture & norms, services, policies, programming, and accountability, centrally located on campus and ultimately responsible for both the day-to-day management of the student experience and the overarching wellness of the community. In partnership with other members of the Upper School administrative team generally, and the dean of operations and dean of faculty specifically, the dean of students also helps to build the framework of support and expectations for the adults working most closely with Milton students. At its best, the work of the dean of students is student-facing, proactive, and energizing, including situations requiring students to take ownership for their missteps and move forward. At its most challenging, the work of the dean of students is central to the immediate and long-term management of student crises. Ultimately, the dean of students must embrace work that is immersed in the complexities of adolescent development and buoyed by each student’s journey and growth. To that end, the dean of students will join Milton at a time of self-reflection, bold vision, and strategic thinking regarding the student experience both within, and beyond, the classroom.

Ideal candidates will be passionate, empathetic, steady, and student-centered; thrive as an eminently present community member; have strong communication skills; have broad and deep experience working with students’ families; find joy in 24/7 community; and draw inspiration and energy from teenagers.

A member of the Upper School administrative team and the Office of Student Life, the dean of students reports to the Upper School principal and collaborates closely with the dean of operations, Upper School director of equity & inclusion, director of counseling, dean of academics, dean of faculty, director of restorative practices, and director of athletics.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities:

  • Management of the Office of Student Life.
  • Partnership with the director of counseling and school physician regarding the comprehensive health of students (including programming, student medical leaves, kidwatch).
  • Oversight of Milton's Accounting for Students policy.
  • Oversight of student discipline processes in collaboration with the dean of academics.
  • Oversight of opening of school programming, in close partnership with members of the Upper School Administrative Team.
  • Oversight of student leadership programming/training, in close partnership with the Office of Equity & Inclusion and the student Self Governing Association (SGA).
  • Partnership with the dean of faculty, dean of academics, and director of residential life in the hiring, housing, onboarding/orientation, and mentoring of new faculty.
  • Partnership with the director of restorative practices regarding Milton’s relational support process.
  • Supervision of several co-curricular program directors.
  • Supervision of colleagues managing faculty advisors and class deans.
  • Oversight of the annual review and update of the student handbook.
  • Participation in the annual review and revision of the faculty handbook.
  • Participation in the weekly creation of the upper school family newsletter and other US communications.
  • Oversight of the OSL budget.
  • Membership on various committees.
  • Participation in weeknight and weekend administrative/supervisory duties as an on-campus resident and an AOD (administrator on duty).
  • Fulfillment of core Upper School responsibilities, including serving as an advisor; contributing actively to student life and the broader school community; and meeting all professional expectations related to collaboration, communication, school programming, and institutional policies. Additional details regarding advising, community engagement, and professional responsibilities are outlined in the Upper School Faculty Handbook.
  • Other responsibilities as assigned.

Supervision to be received: The dean of students will report to the Upper School principal as a member of the Upper School Administrative Team, comprising the dean of faculty, dean of academics, dean of operations, dean of college counseling, Upper School director of equity & inclusion, Upper School director of athletics, director of residential life, director of health services, and the principal's executive assistant/project manager.

Supervision to be exercised: The dean of students will supervise the director of residential life, the director of activities & student life, the student trips coordinator, and the administrative coordinator (in collaboration with the dean of academics).

Education/Certification/Licensure:

Required: A bachelor's degree.

Valid driver's license and ability to pass an insurance and driver's record check.

Preferred: A graduate degree.

Experience:

Required: Experience as a dean of students (or a comparable position) working with colleagues, adolescents, and parents/guardians in an independent boarding high school (preferably) for a minimum of 5 years.

Preferred: Proven leadership and management experience in an independent boarding high school (preferably) for 10+ years as a dean of students (or a comparable position).

Competencies Required:

  • Demonstrated ability to lead and manage teams and implement initiatives.
  • Demonstrated ability to navigate emergencies and manage conflicts effectively, both internally (employees and students) and externally (families).
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple projects and tasks in a fast-paced work environment.
  • Experience in developing and administering student programs, services, and policies.
  • Demonstrated computer expertise, including proficiency in Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, and Adobe Creative Cloud, with a willingness to learn new tools/systems such as Reach and Veracross.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with internal and external constituencies.
  • Understanding of confidentiality and related issues.
  • Receptive to supervision and professional development.
  • Commitment to be a part of a dynamic educational community.

Physical Abilities Required:

  • Must be able to work at a computer for up to 8 hours each day in conjunction with OSHA requirements.
  • Must be able to move around the Milton Academy campus without restriction, including accessing all residential houses on Milton's campus.
  • Must be able to drive various school vehicles.
  • Must be able to lift up to 10 pounds.

All interested internal candidates must complete an application for promotion or transfer and inform their supervisor as soon as possible.

To be considered for this role, all interested internal and external candidates must submit a resume, letter of interest, and response to the applicable prompt below.

  • EXTERNAL candidate: assignment
  • INTERNAL candidate: assignment

To open an assignment in a separate tab, right-click the link and select “Open link in new tab.”

The essential functions and basic skills have been included in this job description; it is not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all functions, responsibilities, skills and abilities. Additional functions and requirements may be assigned by supervisors as deemed appropriate. This position description is subject to change at any time.

Milton Academy is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of any category protected by federal, state, or local law, including but not limited to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, religion, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, ancestry, citizenship or national or ethnic origin.

job.title: Milton Academy Chief Learning Officer
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Position: Chief Learning Officer

Department: Leadership Team

Location: Milton Academy Campus, Milton, MA

Hours: Full-time with the flexibility to work nights and weekends

FLSA: Exempt

Classification: Staff (12-month/Academic Year)

Salary Range: $180,000 to $210,000 annually, based on experience and qualifications

Milton Academy is an independent college preparatory K–12 school, boarding and day in grades 9–12, located just south of Boston.

Milton Academy cultivates in its students a passion for learning and a respect for others. Embracing diversity and the pursuit of excellence, we create a community in which individuals develop competence, confidence and character. Our active learning environment, in and out of the classroom, develops creative and critical thinkers, unafraid to express their ideas, prepared to seek meaningful lifetime success and to live by our motto, “Dare to be true.”

Summary of Position:

Milton Academy seeks its first-ever K-12 Chief Learning Officer (CLO). Reporting to the Head of School, the CLO will serve as a key academic leader and thought partner, overseeing the ongoing excellence of our K-12 academic program while inspiring and leading our community - faculty, staff, students, and families. The CLO will join Milton at a time of great excitement and institutional strength, adding capacity to our academic leadership and unlocking new possibilities for the school. With a strong reputation, a robust academic program, talented faculty, and a dynamic team of divisional leaders, Milton is at a moment of real energy as we embark on a bold vision for our next chapter.

Specifically, the CLO will work to address the following opportunities:

K-12 Academic Leadership

The CLO will serve as an educational thought leader on campus - empowering and supporting teachers with the best of what is known about teaching and learning. This work has three dimensions: bridging research and practice, building programmatic coherence K-12, and inspiring educators.

  1. Bridging research and practice. The CLO will track the latest developments in the field of education. Notably, this includes oversight of Milton’s approach to artificial intelligence, guaranteeing that our students grow as users, developers, and critics of technology in age- and discipline-appropriate ways.
  2. Building programmatic coherence K-12. Working alongside divisional academic leaders and faculty, the CLO will help develop shared language and common goals across grade levels and subject areas, so that a Milton education is intentional, cumulative, and carefully scaffolded through our Lower, Middle, and Upper School divisions.
  3. Inspiring educators. Above all, the CLO will inspire and support faculty and administrators by championing their curiosity, empowering their growth, and celebrating the creativity that makes education at Milton distinctive.

Shaping Milton’s Next Chapter

The incoming CLO will also be a strong strategic partner to the Head of School, Leadership Team, and the Board of Trustees as we pursue our bold new strategic vision, Still Daring. The vision’s pillars are (1) to nurture Milton’s identity as a hub for bold ideas; (2) to cultivate a joyful, vibrant 24/7 community; and (3) to capitalize on our proximity to Boston and Cambridge. Within those pillars, the CLO will take the lead on three initiatives:

  1. Interdisciplinary academic centers. Inspired by higher education, we plan to create three K-12 centers: The Center for Humans and Technology; The Center for Environment and Economy; and the Center for Democracy and Civic Engagement. These centers will bring together students, faculty, alumni, and Boston-based experts to tackle the biggest questions of the day in ways no classroom or subject area can alone.
  2. In-house teacher education program. Concerned by the decline in people both seeking and remaining in careers in education, the CLO will lead efforts to explore our own teacher education program.
  3. Summer program for students and educators. Building on these centers, and our position as an educational leader, we will develop a cutting-edge summer program offering year-round learning opportunities for Milton and non-Milton students and educators alike.

The CLO will oversee these efforts, ensuring that they are carried out in ways that support Milton’s long-standing commitments to academic excellence, inclusion, and creativity.

The successful candidate will possess deep classroom expertise, as well as at least 10 years of experience as a senior academic leader in a K-12 independent or public school.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities:

  • Inspire and lead ongoing curricular and pedagogical renewal within and across all three divisions of the school.
  • Serve as a member of the K-12 Leadership Team, collaborating with other senior leaders to lead and manage the school.
  • Oversee the ongoing design, development, and implementation of Milton’s interdisciplinary academic centers, ensuring their presence and impact within all three divisions. Serve as the supervisor for the directors of the centers.
  • Oversee the ongoing design, development, and implementation of Milton’s teacher development program, intended to provide support for K-12 beginning teachers, as well as mid-career and veteran teachers. Supervise the program’s director.
  • Oversee the development of a mission-driven summer program, providing opportunities for Milton and non-Milton students to expand their learning and pursue academic opportunities aligned with the centers.
  • Serve as the leader of the school’s efforts around artificial intelligence - overseeing all related policies and practices, and cultivating programming for students that develops their skills as users, developers, and critics.
  • Assist the head of school and development office in fundraising efforts associated with the strategic plan.
  • Support K-12 and divisional leadership with all aspects of the professional development program for both faculty and staff, making certain that Milton’s employees receive inspiration and support at all stages of their careers.
  • Facilitate and lead collaboration among all those leading instructional programs, including athletics, academic support, clubs, community engagement, and the outdoor program.
  • Collaborate with the Chief Equity and Inclusion Officer to ensure that our curriculum reflects the diverse identities and experiences of our community.
  • Collect and coordinate multiple forms of data related to the achievement of our students.
  • Demonstrate exceptional verbal and written communication skills.
  • Communicate in a voice that is thoughtful, inspiring, and authentic.
  • Listen empathetically.
  • Communicate effectively and consistently with a wide variety of school constituencies, including students, faculty, families, staff, and administrators across multiple channels including in writing, conversation, public speaking, and various digital channels.
  • Regularly speak in front of large audiences, managing dynamic conversations and adeptly responding to real-time questions.
  • Work with the Chief Equity and Inclusion Officer and other senior leaders to drive measurable progress on access, equity, and belonging among all community members, supporting Milton’s aspirations to serve as a model for other institutions.
  • As a member of the residential life community, support the Upper School in the oversight of the boarding program.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Supervision to be received: Supervised by the head of school.

Supervision to be exercised: The CLO will build and directly supervise a team of directors helping to implement aspects of the strategic plan.

Education/Certification/Licensure

Required: A bachelor’s degree.

Preferred: A master’s or doctoral degree in education or a related field.

Experience Required:

  • At least 10 years of progressive academic leadership experience.
  • Demonstrated effectiveness in inspiring faculty and students.
  • Deep experience leading professional development for faculty.
  • Exceptional understanding of artificial intelligence and its applications in schools.
  • Successful track record of change management, including the demonstrated ability to consider all sides of an issue, make decisions, and navigate implementation
  • Demonstrated ability to prioritize among multiple initiatives and projects.
  • Understanding of the developmental needs of K-12 students.

Competencies Required:

  • Ability to lead, manage, motivate and inspire groups and individuals across the organization.
  • Proven consensus-building skills.
  • Ability to communicate difficult concepts and nuanced issues, both verbally and in writing.
  • Demonstrated technological expertise.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with internal and external constituencies.
  • Understanding of confidentiality and related issues.
  • Receptiveness to feedback, supervision and professional development.
  • Desire to be a part of a dynamic educational community.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple projects and tasks in a fast-paced work environment
  • Ability to work collaboratively with internal and external constituencies.
  • Understanding of confidentiality and related issues.

Physical Abilities Required:

  • Must be able to work at a computer for up to 8 hours each day in conjunction with OSHA requirements.
  • Must be able to move around the Milton Academy campus without restriction.
  • Must be able to lift up to 10 pounds.

All interested internal candidates must complete an application for promotion or transfer and inform their supervisor as soon as possible.

The essential functions and basic skills have been included in this job description; it is not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all functions, responsibilities, skills and abilities. Additional functions and requirements may be assigned by supervisors as deemed appropriate. This position description is subject to change at any time.

job.title: Catlin Gabel School Assistant Director of Beginning & Lower School Enrollment
job.description:
Position Description & Application

WHO WE ARE

Catlin Gabel is an independent, progressive PreK-12 school whose mission is to foster compassionate and curious citizens of the world by inspiring in every student a love of learning and the courage to take responsible action. The School is nestled in the southwest hills of Portland, OR on a 67-acre wooded campus. All team members are an integral part of the student experience and are expected to uphold our core values of Kindness, Integrity, and Inclusion in all that they do.

Enrollment is both relational and strategic work. Our team has the privilege of introducing families to Catlin Gabel, helping them navigate an important decision for their children, and partnering across the School to build a vibrant community of mission-aligned students and families.

Catlin Gabel School is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, marital status, disability, or any other protected characteristic under federal, state, or local law. If you have any questions, please reach out to HR@catlin.edu.

Department: Enrollment| Reports to: Director of Enrollment Management | Hiring Range: $70-$80,000

FTE: 1.0, Full-Time, Benefit-Eligible | FLSA: Exempt | EEO: 2

THE ROLE

Catlin Gabel School is seeking an Assistant Director of Beginning & Lower School Enrollment to lead the enrollment experience for prospective families from Preschool through Grade 5. This role is often one of a family's first relationships with Catlin Gabel and plays an important part in helping children and families discover whether our School is the right place for them.

The ideal candidate is a warm, highly organized and relationship-oriented enrollment professional who genuinely enjoys connecting with children and families. You will guide families from initial inquiry through admission and matriculation, build community relationships that strengthen our enrollment pipeline, and partner closely with Beginning and Lower School colleagues and the Enrollment team to create a thoughtful, welcoming and highly personalized experience.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

The Assistant Director of Beginning & Lower School Enrollment reports to the Director of Enrollment Management and is responsible for:

  • Lead Beginning & Lower School Enrollment: Guide the Preschool through Grade 5 enrollment process from inquiry through matriculation, including tours, applicant assessment, student visits, admission committees, decisions, yield, and retention.
  • Build Relationships & Drive Recruitment: Develop recruitment and outreach strategies, cultivate relationships with schools and community organizations, and lead the BLS Parent/Guardian Ambassador Program to build a strong pipeline of prospective families.
  • Create an Excellent Family & Applicant Experience: Create welcoming, thoughtful and well-organized tours, visits, events, and communications that help families understand Catlin Gabel and feel supported throughout the enrollment process.
  • Collaborate, Analyze & Strengthen Enrollment Practices: Partner across the Enrollment team and School, use enrollment data and trends to inform strategy, and continually improve recruitment, yield, retention, and enrollment practices.

WHO YOU ARE & KEYS TO SUCCESS

To be successful in this role, you will excel in these areas:

  • Relationship Builder & Communicator: You connect naturally with children and adults, communicate with warmth and clarity, and build trust with families, colleagues, volunteers, and community partners.
  • Organized & Reliable: You can manage a complex annual cycle, multiple families and events, detailed timelines, and confidential information with excellent follow-through.
  • Collaborative & Culturally Responsive: You work effectively across teams and with people of varied backgrounds and family structures, listen with curiosity, and contribute positively to a team-oriented environment.
  • Sound Judgment & Adaptability: You exercise discretion and diplomacy, solve problems thoughtfully, balance competing priorities, and remain effective during the intensity of peak enrollment periods.
  • Strategic & Data-Informed: You see how individual family experiences connect to broader enrollment goals and use data, trends, and institutional knowledge to strengthen recruitment, yield, and retention.

We are looking for someone with three to five years of relevant experience, preferably in independent school enrollment. Related college or boarding school enrollment, school administration, or teaching experience may also provide relevant preparation. Strong written and verbal communication, technology and data skills are important. A bachelor's degree is required; a master's degree is preferred.

WHAT ELSE YOU SHOULD KNOW

This is a full-time, benefit-eligible position with year-round on- and off-campus commitments. The role requires regular movement around our wooded campus and limited evening and weekend work for community outreach, tours, applicant visits, and enrollment events.

The annual enrollment cycle includes both quieter periods of independent work and busy seasons that require energy, flexibility, and strong prioritization.

The School offers a generous benefits package. Please see our website for details: https://www.catlin.edu/about/employment.

job.title: Catlin Gabel School Interim Lower School Spanish Teacher
job.description:
Position Description & Application

About Catlin Gabel School

Catlin Gabel is an independent, progressive school (preschool-grade 12) whose mission is to foster compassionate and curious citizens of the world by inspiring in every student a love of learning and the courage to take responsible action. The school is located in the southwest hills of Portland, OR on a 67-acre wooded campus. All team members are an integral part of the student experience and are expected to uphold our core values of Kindness, Integrity, and Inclusion in all that they do.

Catlin Gabel School is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, marital status, disability, or any other protected characteristic under federal, state, or local law. If you have any questions, please reach out to HR@catlin.edu.

The Lower School team creates engaging, inquiry-based learning experiences that nurture students’ academic, social, and emotional growth while fostering curiosity, confidence, and a strong sense of belonging. As a member of this collaborative community, you will partner with colleagues across disciplines to support every learner and contribute to a culture that values innovation, relationships, and continuous learning.

Department: Lower School | Reports to: Nick Zosel-Johnson | FTE: 1.0, Full-Time, Limited Duration through June 16, 2027| Hiring Pay Range: $51,652 - $98,960 per Faculty Scale | Benefit-Eligible

About the role

The Lower School Spanish Teacher leads Spanish language learning for students in Grades 1–5, helping children develop communicative proficiency, cultural awareness, and a lifelong appreciation for language and global perspectives. Through engaging, developmentally appropriate instruction, this role creates an inclusive classroom environment where students build confidence, take risks, and learn through meaningful communication, active participation, and authentic experiences.

The ideal candidate is a collaborative, student-centered educator who is passionate about language acquisition and committed to supporting the growth of every learner. They thrive in a community-oriented environment, value strong partnerships with colleagues and families, and bring curiosity, flexibility, and enthusiasm to their work. Successful candidates are skilled at creating engaging learning experiences, adapting instruction to meet diverse needs, and fostering a joyful culture of learning where all students feel seen, supported, and empowered to succeed.

What you'll do

The Lower School Spanish Teacher reports to the Lower School Head and is responsible for:

  • Spanish Language Instruction & Curriculum Development: Design and deliver engaging Spanish learning experiences for students in Grades 1–5 that build communicative proficiency, cultural awareness, and enthusiasm for language learning. Develop and refine curriculum, assessments, and learning activities aligned with world language standards and best practices in language acquisition.
  • Student Learning, Assessment & Inclusion: Create an inclusive classroom environment where all students can thrive. Differentiate instruction, support diverse learning needs, and use ongoing assessment to monitor progress and promote student growth.
  • Family & School Collaboration: Partner with families, colleagues, and school leaders to support student success through clear communication, curriculum alignment, and interdisciplinary learning opportunities. Contribute to departmental and divisional initiatives that strengthen the student experience.
  • Community Engagement & Professional Responsibilities: Foster a positive classroom culture aligned with the school's values and social-emotional learning practices. Participate actively in the life of the school community through meetings, events, student supervision, professional learning, and other responsibilities that support the Lower School program.

Keys to Success

To be successful in this role, you will excel in these areas:

  • Student-Centered Teaching: You create a welcoming and inclusive classroom where students feel comfortable taking risks, making mistakes, and actively engaging in language learning. You build strong relationships that foster confidence, curiosity, and a sense of belonging.
  • Language Acquisition Expertise: You apply your knowledge of second-language acquisition and developmentally appropriate practices to create engaging learning experiences that support communicative proficiency and cultural understanding.
  • Collaboration & Communication: You partner effectively with colleagues, families, and school leaders through clear and respectful communication, contributing to a collaborative learning environment and a positive student experience.
  • Adaptability & Professional Responsibility: You respond thoughtfully to the diverse needs of learners, adapt your approach when needed, and manage responsibilities with professionalism, organization, and attention to detail.

Minimum qualifications

Candidates should have a bachelor's degree in Spanish, World Language Education, Elementary Education, or a related field, along with experience teaching Spanish language learners, preferably at the elementary level. Successful candidates will demonstrate advanced or professional-level fluency in Spanish, proficiency in English, and knowledge of second-language acquisition practices and proficiency-based instruction, including familiarity with ACTFL standards and frameworks.

What else you should know

SCHEDULE & WORKING CONDITIONS

This is an interim full-time position, for the remainder of the 2026-2027 school year. Full-time faculty teachers are expected to travel to retreats, conferences and workshops as well as accompany students on various experiential activities throughout the year. There are some mandatory evening and weekend commitments.

The requirements listed below are representative of physical requirements and may not be all-encompassing. Incumbents must be able to perform job duties with or without accommodations. Work is primarily performed in a classroom setting and includes occasional to frequent work leading students off campus activities.

job.title: Deerfield Academy Early Career Teaching Fellow
job.description:
Position Description

Deerfield Academy, a private coeducational boarding school founded in 1797 and annually serving approximately 650 students grades 9-PG, seeks Early Career Teaching Fellows with a start date in July 2027.

Summary:

The Early Career Fellowship at Deerfield offers curious, optimistic, and energetic individuals an opportunity to explore independent school teaching. Our program gives novice teachers the essential skills they need for successful careers in education. With the ongoing support of an experienced mentor teacher, fellows immerse themselves in all aspects of life at Deerfield. Appointments in specific academic departments vary year-to-year depending on the Academy’s needs. Fellowships are initially two-year positions; fellows who have demonstrated success in their areas of responsibility may apply for reappointment for additional years should appropriate openings become available. Deerfield believes that the best faculty is a learning faculty, and fellows will be eligible for support for professional development and education in their field of study.

Responsibilities:

The primary classroom responsibility will be teaching two sections (Year 1) or three sections (Year 2) in an assigned academic department or departments. The primary out-of-classroom responsibilities will include assisting with co-curricular activities (varsity or sub-varsity teams, community service activities, publications, etc.), dormitory residence or supervision, advising, and family-style dining hall meals with students. Fellows meet regularly with the program director and their mentor teacher to learn about effective pedagogical techniques, assessment design and grading, methods for cultivating students’ sense of belonging and inclusion, and curricular design.

Qualifications:

We are looking for candidates who have a keen interest in boarding school life and a desire to work in a high-challenge, high-support environment. Candidates must be prepared to engage in and reflect upon work in the classroom and in the activities and less formal spaces that help define a strong residential educational community. Additionally, candidates should possess the following specific attributes/qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree required
  • Significant depth of knowledge and experience in an academic discipline
  • Interest in and some experience working with adolescents
  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to effectively facilitate group discussion
  • High level of patience and diplomacy
  • Excellent organizational skills
  • Ability to manage, and sensitivity to, highly confidential information
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Google Suite, and basic classroom technologies
  • Demonstrated multicultural competency and commitment to inclusivity
  • Excitement for learning and professional growth
  • The ability to work with colleagues as part of a team
  • A sense of humor

Working Conditions:

  • Close visual acuity to view a computer terminal, analyze text, data and/or figures.
  • Ability to frequently stand and/or sit for sustained periods of time
  • Ability to frequently reach items and paperwork
  • Ability to frequently sustain substantial movements of the wrists, hands and/or fingers
  • Ability to frequently receive and communicate information, verbally and in writing
  • Ability to occasionally stoop or kneel
  • Ability to occasionally lift/carry/push up to 10 pounds

Salary Range: The salary range for this position is $42,500 for the 1st year and $47,500 for the 2nd year.

job.title: Milton Academy Director of Human Resources
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Position: Director of Human Resources

Department: Human Resources

Location: Milton Academy Campus, Milton, MA

Hours: Full-time with the flexibility to work nights and weekends

FLSA: Exempt

Classification: Staff (12-month)

Salary Range: $110,000 to $150,000 annually, based on experience and qualifications

Milton Academy is an independent college preparatory K–12 school, boarding and day in grades 9–12, located just south of Boston.

Milton Academy cultivates in its students a passion for learning and a respect for others. Embracing diversity and the pursuit of excellence, we create a community in which individuals develop competence, confidence and character. Our active learning environment, in and out of the classroom, develops creative and critical thinkers, unafraid to express their ideas, prepared to seek meaningful lifetime success and to live by our motto, “Dare to be true.”

Summary of Position:

Milton Academy seeks an experienced Director of Human Resources to lead the School's HR function and support a community of more than 500 employees. Reporting to the Chief Financial and Operating Officer, the Director will serve as a trusted advisor to School leadership and oversee HR programs and operations that advance Milton's mission and foster a positive employee experience.

The Director will lead and develop a team of HR professionals and oversee recruitment and hiring, compensation and benefits, payroll, performance management, employee relations, compliance, HR systems, and workforce planning, including HR support for The Mountain School. A key priority will be strengthening Milton's approach to recruitment and workforce planning to anticipate and meet the School's evolving needs.

The Director will also support the upcoming implementation of Workday, the School's new HR and payroll system. Working with the HR team, the Director will integrate Workday into existing HR workflows and responsibilities, refine processes, and support employee training and adoption.

Working closely with leaders across the School, the Director will help ensure that HR programs and personnel decisions align with Milton's strategic priorities, long term plans, and resources.

The ideal candidate will be a thoughtful and collaborative HR leader energized by the opportunity to contribute to a dynamic educational community and help shape the employee experience at Milton.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities:

  1. Lead the HR Office and oversee the School's core HR programs and operations, including:
  • Payroll and employee benefits administration
  • Retirement plan administration
  • Compensation administration, including salary benchmarking and annual reappointment and pay rate letters
  • Staff performance reviews and support for faculty performance reviews
  • Recruitment and hiring
  • New employee onboarding, training, and orientation
  • Administration of the annual employee training program
  • Personnel policies and procedures, including maintenance of an up-to-date personnel policies manual
  • Employee departures and exit processes
  • Health and wellness programs
  • Employment compliance and required reporting
  • 403(b) plan audits and Form 5500 filings
  • Personnel records management
  • Background checks and employee screening
  • Oversight of HR systems, including Workday1
  • Lead, supervise, and mentor the HR team by setting priorities, supporting professional growth, and ensuring an effective team structure, clear distribution of responsibilities, and responsive support to the Milton community.
  1. Lead the School's recruitment, hiring, and workforce planning efforts in partnership with the HR team, principals, department leaders, and hiring managers. Develop proactive strategies to anticipate staffing needs, attract qualified candidates, and strengthen recruitment practices, while overseeing the hiring process from candidate sourcing through offers and onboarding.
  2. Oversee the development, coordination, and delivery of annual employee training, including compliance requirements and schoolwide professional development initiatives.
  3. Partner with the Leadership Team to foster a positive workplace culture, support employee engagement and retention, and advise managers on employee relations, performance, and personnel matters.
  4. Lead employee relations matters, including conflict resolution, performance and conduct concerns, and workplace investigations, ensuring fair and consistent practices.
  5. Partner with the Benefits Administrator to manage employee leaves, disability accommodations, and workers' compensation, ensuring compliance with applicable federal and state laws and regulations.
  6. Work with the Chief Financial and Operating Officer and the Business Office on compensation and benefits programs that are competitive, financially responsible, and effective in attracting and retaining employees.
  7. Develop and manage the annual HR budget to support operational needs and strategic initiatives.
  8. Keep HR policies and procedures current, clear, and accessible. Ensure they are applied consistently and comply with applicable employment laws and sound HR practices.
  9. Partner with the Controller's Office to ensure compensation, benefits, payroll, and personnel information is accurate and shared in a timely manner.
  10. Oversee workforce data and reporting related to staffing, recruitment, retention, compensation, benefits, employee engagement, and compliance. Use this information to identify trends, inform decisions, and help School leaders plan for hiring and organizational needs.
  11. Stay current on federal, state, and local employment laws and regulations, as well as relevant developments in human resources. Assess changes that may affect Milton and advise School leadership on appropriate actions.
  12. Work closely with the Chief Legal Counsel on employment matters, employee relations, HR policies, and other personnel decisions that involve legal or institutional risk.
  13. Review HR processes, systems, and programs on an ongoing basis and recommend practical improvements that make the work more efficient and improve the employee experience.
  14. Perform other related responsibilities as assigned.

Supervision to be received: Chief Financial and Operating Officer

Supervision to be exercised: Benefits Administrator, Analyst and Payroll Administrator, Human Resources Assistant and Recruitment Coordinator, and other part-time/temporary staff (TBD)

Education:

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree

Preferred:

  • Bachelor's degree or Master's degree in human resources or business administration.
  • HR certification (PHR/SPHR or SHRM CP/SCP)

Experience:

Required:

  • At least 10 years of progressive professional experience, including a minimum of 7 years in human resources.
  • Experience managing a team.
  • Demonstrated success in leadership and people management roles, including supervising and developing HR staff, leading cross-functional initiatives, and partnering with senior leaders to advance organizational goals.
  • Proven experience leading organizational change and guiding teams through periods of transition with effective communication, collaboration, and constituency engagement.

Preferred:

  • Experience working in an independent school or in higher education.
  • Experience working with educators.
  • Experience with Massachusetts compliance requirements.

Competencies

Required:

  • Knowledge of employment law, HR compliance, and HR best practices
  • Proficiency in Workday, ADP or similar HRIS platforms.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple projects and tasks in a fast-paced work environment
  • Ability to work collaboratively with internal and external constituencies.
  • Understanding of confidentiality and related issues.
  • Receptive to supervision and professional development.
  • Desire to be a part of a dynamic educational community.
  • Demonstrated computer expertise, including proficiency in Google Workspace, Microsoft Office and Adobe Creative Cloud.

Physical Abilities:

Required:

  • Must be able to work at a computer for up to 8 hours each day in conjunction with OSHA requirements.
  • Must be able to move around the Milton Academy campus without restriction.
  • Must be able to lift up to 10 pounds.

All interested internal candidates must complete an application for promotion or transfer and inform your supervisor as soon as possible.

The essential functions and basic skills have been included in this job description; it is not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all functions, responsibilities, skills and abilities. Additional functions and requirements may be assigned by supervisors as deemed appropriate. This position description is subject to change at any time.

Milton Academy is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of any category protected by federal, state, or local law, including but not limited to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, religion, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, ancestry, citizenship or national or ethnic origin.

job.title: The Pingry School Auxiliary Programs Rentals Coordinator
job.description:
Position Description

Position Summary

The Auxiliary Programs Rentals Coordinator leads the growth and management of The Pingry School’s facility rentals across three campuses, building lasting partnerships that generate revenue and strengthen community connections. This year-round role includes a focus on summer rentals coordinated alongside Pingry Summer, a vibrant “third semester” that brings together the school’s academic and athletic traditions with the energy of summer exploration. With more than 100 programs spanning signature day camps, athletics, arts, and academics, summer offers meaningful opportunities to grow partnerships while supporting a culture of belonging, honor, and safety.

The Coordinator manages the full year long rental process, from developing prospective partnerships and negotiating contracts to coordinating facility use, ensuring compliance with insurance and safety requirements, and initiating invoicing. As the primary contact for rental partners and a close collaborator with internal teams, the Coordinator balances excellent customer service with the school’s operational needs, student priorities, and mission. Clear communication, careful planning, and coordinated handoffs help ensure that colleagues have the information and arrangements needed to support successful rentals.

This is a full-time, salaried position with evening and weekend commitments. The role requires responsiveness to time-sensitive rental needs, including availability by phone outside standard business hours when needed. The Associate Director of Auxiliary Programs and the Director of Summer Programs will partner with you to coordinate your weekly schedule and coverage in support of rental and program commitments.

Candidate Profile

You are energized by people, motivated by building relationships, and proud of delivering an excellent customer experience. You combine the warmth of a hospitality professional with the initiative of a salesperson and the follow-through of a detail-oriented coordinator. You bring a positive, practical approach to challenges and enjoy turning a conversation into a lasting partnership.

You communicate clearly and build trust. You listen closely, ask thoughtful questions, and communicate confidently in person, on the phone, and in writing. You connect with a broad range of people, from rental partners and community organizations to facilities colleagues, school leaders, and board members. You make people feel welcome while setting clear expectations and handling difficult conversations with professionalism and care.

You take initiative and see opportunities for growth. You are comfortable picking up the phone, pursuing new leads, and following through to turn interest into confirmed partnerships. You also recognize the potential in existing relationships, helping clients discover additional ways to partner with Pingry. Curious and open to feedback, you bring fresh ideas for expanding summer and year-round rentals while respecting the needs of the school community.

You pair strong people skills with dependable organization. You understand that excellent service depends on careful preparation. You keep track of contracts, insurance documentation, scheduling, and billing details, and you follow through on commitments. You anticipate what colleagues will need and establish clear plans and handoffs so Facilities, Operations, Athletics, and program teams can support successful execution.

You collaborate well and exercise sound judgment. You balance responsiveness to clients with the responsibility to uphold school policies, safety requirements, and student priorities. Advanced business analysis does not need to be your specialty, but you are comfortable partnering with colleagues to understand reports and recommendations, use data to guide your work, and maintain accurate records. You know when to solve a problem independently and when to involve others.

Responsibilities

Revenue Generation & Pipeline Management

  • Business Development: Identify and vet external organizations and vendors to build a robust pipeline of "premium" rental partners (e.g., specialized camps, athletic organizations, theater productions) that align with Pingry’s brand standards.
  • Partner Relations: Serve as the primary relationship manager for all external rental organizations, ensuring high-quality customer service and long-term partnership retention.
  • Portfolio Growth: Partner with the Director of Auxiliary Programs to develop revenue strategies that maximize asset utilization during summer and off-peak periods.
  • New Business Acquisition: Actively identify, pursue, and close new avenues for revenue by scouting emerging market opportunities and converting prospects into long-term partners.

Risk Management & Compliance Governance

  • Contractual Stewardship: Manage the end-to-end contracting process, ensuring that every rental agreement is current, legally sound, and protective of the institution.
  • Compliance Guarding: Act as the final checkpoint for Certificates of Insurance (COIs) and all required safety documentation for external partners, ensuring zero compliance gaps before facility use.
  • Safety Coordination: Communicate and enforce all Pingry safety and security protocols with external partners, including emergency procedures and facility access standards.

Internal Coordination & Conflict Prevention

  • Resource Advocacy: Collaborate with Facilities, Operations, and Athletics to maintain the definitive master calendar for auxiliary facility use, preventing "rogue" bookings or internal scheduling conflicts.
  • Cross-Campus Alignment: Ensure that rental operations across all three campuses are coordinated and do not interfere with the primary student experience or signature programs.
  • Standardized Boundaries: Define clear operational handoffs for rental groups, ensuring that physical setup, signage, and custodial tasks are coordinated through the appropriate service departments rather than being absorbed as "floating work" by the coordinator.

Financial Integration & Workflow Execution

  • Systems & Workflow Optimization: Spearhead continuous improvement initiatives by designing, implementing, and optimizing robust operational systems and workflows to support scalable, high-volume rental operations while improving efficiency and the client experience.
  • Full Lifecycle & Strategic Partnership: Partner directly with the Assistant Director of Auxiliary Programs to drive the complete rental lifecycle, managing everything from lead intake and contract execution to on-site coordination, invoicing, and final billing reconciliation.
  • Administrative Liaison: Provide essential data and documentation to the Controller and Accounting Supervisor to ensure timely revenue reconciliation and financial reporting.

Qualifications

Experience & Business Mastery

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Event Management, or a related field.
  • Contractual Fluency: Proven experience in contract management, invoicing workflows, and financial compliance.
  • Relationship Expertise: Demonstrated ability to build meaningful, professional relationships with a broad range of constituents, including external vendors, faculty, and school leadership.

Operational Skills

  • Project Management: Exceptional organizational skills with the ability to manage the high-velocity logistics of a multi-campus rental portfolio.
  • Systems Proficiency: Skilled in the Google Suite, CampBrain, and financial reporting tools, with an ability to maintain data integrity across multiple platforms.

Temperament

  • Professional Diplomacy: A positive, optimistic approach to problem-solving and the "backbone" to enforce institutional standards with external clients.
  • Detailed Accuracy: A meticulously organized mindset that ensures every COI is valid and every contract is signed before a foot steps on campus.

Qualified candidates are invited to apply online at https://www.pingry.org/careers.

The salary range for this position is $70,000 to $80,000. Final compensation will be determined based on experience and education.

Pingry offers a comprehensive benefits package to full-time employees, including, but not limited to, medical, dental, and vision coverage; retirement plans with employer matching; life and disability insurance; tuition remission for employees' children; and access to wellness and professional development resources.

A full list of benefits is available at www.pingry.org/careers.

The Pingry School aspires to be an anti-racist community and is committed to the principles of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion. Pingry is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. The Pingry School's employment policy is that individuals will receive equal opportunity in all matters pertaining to recruitment, employment, salary, promotion, and assignment, regardless of race, religion, color, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy status, genetic information, marital status, amnesty or status as a covered veteran, or other basis proscribed by federal, state, and local law. All employment is decided based on qualifications, merit, and business need.

job.title: Gilman School Upper School Counselor
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Salary Range

$55,000.00 - $75,000.00 Salary/year

Level

Experienced

Position Type

Full Time

Education Level

4 Year Degree

Category

Education

OUR MISSION

Gilman is a diverse community dedicated to educating boys in mind, body, and spirit through particular emphasis upon academic excellence, athletic participation, and aesthetic appreciation. Gilman seeks to produce men of character and integrity who have the skills and ability to make a positive contribution to the communities in which they live and work.

OUR COMMITMENT

Educating the Whole Boy

For more than a century, Gilman’s mission has remained exceedingly focused: to unlock the greatness within each boy by educating the entire boy—mind, body, and spirit. To accomplish that goal, we provide space and opportunity for crucial learning and self-expression to take place. We believe that boys experience transformative learning when they connect disciplines, people, and ideas in ways that deepen their sense of self and serve the needs of others.

Our rich and comprehensive program, our immeasurably talented and interesting faculty and students, and our belief in the character traits embodied by the Gilman Five—Honor, Integrity, Respect, Humility, and Excellence—combine to form the foundation of an educational environment dedicated to helping boys grow into men of character.

Community, Inclusion, and Equity

Gilman’s commitment to inclusion and equity is founded on the belief that our community is strengthened by the vibrant exchange that occurs when individuals with different backgrounds and heritages share their perspectives with one another. Through the recognition and acceptance of our many differences, we learn to appreciate and respect the complexity of the world in which we live and develop essential skills that help us forge productive relationships with those around us.

We are proud of our history as a school that has, for several generations, taken the lead on matters of diversity, inclusivity, and equity. More than 35% of Gilman’s student body and 22% of the School’s faculty identify as people of color. We continue to build on that legacy through our steadfast commitment to inclusivity and equity and initiatives on local, state, and national levels.

OUR SCHOOL

Gilman School is a pre-kindergarten through twelfth-grade private independent day school for boys. Set on a 57-acre campus in the northern part of Baltimore City, Gilman serves roughly 1,000 students in three divisions. The School has a full-time faculty of nearly 140, and the average class size is 16 students.

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

Gilman School seeks an Upper School Counselor to support students’ social, emotional, and mental health needs for the remainder of the 2026–2027 school year. While this role is anticipated to be full-time, we recognize that talented candidates may seek alternative work arrangements. A part-time schedule may be considered for the right candidate.

  • provide individual and group counseling, classroom guidance, and support for students in the Upper School
  • provide crisis intervention and referrals as necessary to families and faculty
  • serve on the Upper School Student Support Team
  • serve as a member of a cross-divisional team of counselors, learning support specialists, and health practitioners to create a comprehensive plan to support students’ well-being
  • provide consultation to, collaboration with, and programs for faculty, parents, and administrators regarding students’ developmental and social-emotional needs
  • When appropriate, teach one section in an academic discipline that fits your undergraduate/graduate coursework and experience
  • When appropriate, coach two seasons of interscholastic sports or through our intramural program

WHAT YOU WILL NEED TO SUCCEED:

  • the ability to inspire and build relationships with students and colleagues
  • experience in a school setting and a willingness to grow as an educator
  • technological proficiencies in the areas of communication, presentation, and record-keeping
  • Master’s Degree in Counseling, Social Work, or School Counseling
  • Maryland Licensure Preferred (LGPC, LCPC, LMSW, or LCSW-C)

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

Gilman School follows a Faculty Salary Scale that recognizes direct years of experience and correlates to steps on the scale. Compensation for the role will depend on several factors, including a candidate's years of experience, education, skills, and job-related responsibilities. Candidates will be offered a salary between $55,000-$75,000. Candidates with additional experience or qualifications may be offered a salary outside the range shown.

In addition to the annual salary, Gilman School offers a comprehensive benefits package which includes medical, dental, and vision insurance, as well as life insurance, critical illness and accident coverage, and both short- and long-term disability. We offer a 403(b) retirement plan with an employer match to help you plan for the future.

ADDITIONAL DETAILS

  • POSITION TITLE: Upper School Counselor
  • STATUS/FLSA: Full-Time Preferred; Part-Time Considered
  • HOURS OF WORK: TBD (12 pm-4 pm required)
  • LOCATION: On-Campus

job.title: Peninsula School Controller
job.description:
Position Description

Peninsula School, a leader in progressive education since 1925, is a Preschool-8th grade school where children thrive and develop to their full promise as confident contributors in the world. At Peninsula, children learn about themselves and others, discover their passions, and grow intellectually in an inclusive community rich with choices, exploration, and play. In addition to intellectual development and social-emotional learning. Peninsula School has an explicit focus on educating for democracy, student choice and voice, and social justice. Peninsula School

celebrated its centennial in 2025.

Position Summary

Reporting to the Director of Finance and Operations, the Controller supports the School’s mission and serves as a key member of the Business Office Team, working collaboratively with colleagues, families, and vendors. Controller responsibilities include accounting functions, budgeting and audit support, reporting, compliance, and ensuring the integrity, accuracy, and timeliness of all financial activities.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities:

● Responsible for all general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, and cash management functions.

● Ensure timely, accurate monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements in accordance with GAAP and nonprofit accounting standards.

● Prepare detailed financial reports and analyses for the Director of Finance and Operations.

● Maintain the integrity of all financial records, schedules, and reconciliations.

Budget Support & Financial Operations

● Assist the Director of Finance and Operations with the preparation of the annual budget to align with the school’s goals and mission.

● Monitor budget-to-actual performance & identify discrepancies or emerging issues.

● Support the Director of Finance and Operations in forecasting and variance analysis.

● Partner with colleagues to ensure accurate expense coding and financial accountability, including sending monthly budget reports.

Restricted Funds & Endowment Accounting

● Oversee accounting for restricted, temporarily restricted, and unrestricted funds.

● Ensure accurate tracking and reporting of endowed funds, capital gifts, and donor-restricted contributions.

● Partner with Development and the Director of Finance and Operations to ensure compliance with gift agreements and donor intent.

Audit & Compliance

● Be responsible for and be the primary leader in the annual financial audit and any other audits by outside authorities.

● Ensure timely completion of audit schedules, confirmations, and required disclosures.

● Support preparation of Form 990 and other regulatory filings in partnership with the Director of Finance and Operations and external advisors.

● Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local financial and tax regulations applicable to independent schools and nonprofit organizations

Internal Controls & Fiduciary Integrity

● Design, implement, and continuously strengthen internal controls to safeguard institutional assets.

● Ensure segregation of duties, approval workflows, and documentation

standards across all financial processes.

● Monitor compliance with internal policies, donor restrictions, and

Board-approved financial practices.

● Serve as a key guardian of fiduciary discipline across the institution.

Systems, Processes & Continuous Improvement

● Maintain and optimize the School’s financial systems, including accounting platforms and reporting tools.

● Lead process improvements to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and

transparency.

● Ensure consistent financial procedures across functions and programs.

Other

● Attend meetings as customary for the position, including Staff Meetings.

● Perform other duties as required.

Qualifications

● Minimum of 5 years of progressive accounting experience, including prior experience as a Controller

● Bachelor's degree in accounting or finance required; CPA strongly preferred

● Significant experience in nonprofit accounting, preferably within an

independent school, foundation, or other educational institution, including

expertise in nonprofit accounting, including donor-restricted funds and

endowments

● Strong knowledge of GAAP, audit processes, and internal control best

practices

● High proficiency with QuickBooks and software platforms for enrollment and billing

● Excellent analytical, organizational, interpersonal, and communication skills

● High level of integrity, discretion, and commitment to the school’s mission and values

● Community engagement with genuine enthusiasm and a passion for finance.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, the ability to adjust focus, and sound hearing. The ability to speak clearly and coherently is required. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit, use hands, talk, and hear.

The employee is frequently required to reach with hands and arms. On occasion, the employee is required to stand, walk, stoop, kneel, or crouch. The employee must operate a computer and office productivity machinery, communicate across a variety of media, and work in proximity to others. The role may also require the employee to work in inclement weather during special activities and to work at a desk for extended periods of time.

Compensation: 1.0 FTE with benefits and retirement, $125,000 - $145,000 depending on experience

To Apply: Please fill out an employment application (also found on the Join Our

Team page of our website

https://www.peninsulaschool.org/about-us/join-our-team) and send it with a cover letter and resumé, to HR@peninsulaschool.org.

Peninsula School is an equal opportunity employer and we actively promote the principles and practices of diversity, equity and inclusion throughout the school community. We actively support equal opportunity for all people and encourage members of BIPOC communities and LGBTQ+ candidates to apply. Our school is strongly committed to learning about and promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion in all interactions and programs. We offer competitive compensation and a progressive community dedicated to learning and engaged citizenship. We encourage people of under-represented groups to apply. For more information, please visit our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, & Belonging webpage.

job.title: Charles River School Long-Term Substitute Librarian
job.description:
Position Description

Charles River School is a unique, inclusive independent PreK-8 school in Dover, MA, 16 miles west of Boston. CRS nurtures each student by igniting curiosity, encouraging creativity, and cultivating intellectual engagement. Our graduates know themselves, understand others, and shape the future of our diverse world with confidence and compassion.

We are seeking a warm, energetic librarian to cover a leave of absence from early December through April. The Long Term Substitute Librarian will welcome our Otters into a library where every child can find themselves in a book, and will help keep the library a vibrant, well-run part of daily life at CRS.

Responsibilities

  • Plan and teach library classes for students in PreK through Grade 6
  • Foster a love of reading through read-alouds, book talks, and readers’ advisory tailored to each child’s age and interests
  • Teach information literacy skills in developmentally appropriate ways
  • Support middle school students in using the library for book checkout and research
  • Manage circulation, shelving, and the day-to-day organization of the library
  • Collaborate with classroom teachers and specialists to connect library time with classroom learning
  • Provide recess and lunch coverage as part of our shared supervision schedule

Essential Skills and Qualifications

  • Experience working with children in a school or library setting preferred
  • Knowledge of children’s and young adult literature across the PreK-8 range

job.title: The St. Paul's Schools Assistant Auxiliary Programs Manager
job.description:
Position Description

The St. Paul’s Schools is a family of independent schools in Baltimore County, Maryland. Serving children from infancy through grade 12, our three schools share a 120-acre campus, an Episcopal tradition, and a focus on developing confident, well-balanced students who will use their education and ethics to improve the world. A coordinated structure allows The St. Paul’s Schools to preserve the small-school feel within each school while sharing resources and certain programs to maximize opportunities for students.

Mission: Guided by Episcopal values and a commitment to each student’s full journey, a St. Paul’s education inspires us to lead with love, discover and pursue our unique gifts, and act with courage in all we do.

Vision: St. Paul’s students thrive and serve in a global community. We create transformational experiences through innovative and responsive teaching in a diverse community of authentic belonging.

Position Overview

The Assistant Auxiliary Programs Manager serves as the primary operational partner and second-in-command to the Director of Auxiliary Services. This role supports the strategic planning, coordination, and execution of all auxiliary programs across the academic year and summer, including After School Adventures (ASA), Summer Programs, workshops, enrichment and internal auxiliary programs. This position is operations- and systems-focused, ensuring consistency, efficiency, and a high-quality experience for families, employees, and partners. The role balances leadership, logistics and administration with weekly student supervision. This is a 12-month position. Hours are approximately 10:00am – 6:00pm, with flexibility for events and program needs.

Primary Responsibilities

Auxiliary Operations & Leadership

  • Serve as operational lead and acting director in the absence of the Director of Auxiliary Services.
  • Support planning, launch, and continuous improvement of all auxiliary programs.
  • Manage CampBrain and related systems, including registration setup, billing, reporting, data integrity, and troubleshooting for ASA, summer camps and music lessons, in addition to other programs added in future years.
  • Oversee auxiliary calendars, rosters, staffing plans, and campus space usage.
  • Serve in lead role for ASA programming partnering with lower school leadership on staffing and behavioral work within the program.
  • Work with HR, if applicable, to help support employee onboarding, training, etc.
  • Help with tracking expenses, supplies, and operational efficiencies.

Communications & Marketing

  • Oversee family-facing communications and customer service workflows for all auxiliary programs, especially focused on ASA and summer camps.
  • Partner with the communications office on efforts including flyers, Instagram posts, forms, emails, signage, maps, and operational guides.
  • Ensure consistent branding and messaging across all auxiliary programs.

Qualiﬁcations & Skills

  • Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience in school, camp, or youth program operations.
  • Comfort managing systems, vendors, staffing logistics, and cross-department workflows.
  • Calm, professional, and solutions-oriented leadership style.
  • Strong skills in managing multiple simultaneous tasks and priorities.
  • Experience working with children under 12 years old.

At St. Paul’s Schools, we are dedicated to fostering a nurturing and inclusive learning environment where every individual is celebrated for their unique strengths and contributions. We believe that diversity enriches education, empowering students to reach their fullest potential. By embracing a culture of inclusion, we prepare our students to succeed in an increasingly interconnected and multicultural world. We stand firmly against all forms of prejudice, including those related to race, ethnicity, religion, socioeconomic background, gender identity, sexual orientation, and physical appearance.

The St. Paul’s Schools has a compensation scale based on direct years of experience and degree held. Compensation for the role will depend on a number of factors, including a candidate’s years of experience, education and skills. For this opportunity, our salary range is $60,000 - $65,000 annually. Candidates with additional experience or qualifications may be offered a salary outside of the range shown. In addition, full-time team members gain access to our robust benefits package designed to support your well-being, inside and outside of work. This includes a competitive healthcare package (medical, dental, and vision), disability protection, participation in our 403(b) retirement plan which has an immediate employer contribution and a generous time off package, including wellness days because we believe you may need a day off ‘just because!’.

Beyond the basics, we offer extras like a lunch stipend, access to multiple fitness centers on campus and professional development experiences to continue your learning. In addition, full-time employees who choose The St. Paul’s Schools for their children’s educational journey, are eligible to receive a tuition remission benefit. Your salary will be commensurate with your experience and reflect the value you bring to our team.

Ready to join our team? Please submit your cover letter, resume, and list of references to Shannon Duckett, Executive Director of Human Resources, at sduckett@stpaulsmd.org. The St. Paul’s Schools embraces diversity and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.
