job.title: Collegiate School Lower School Associate Teacher
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Salary Range:

$60,210.00 To $66,900.00 Annually

The Collegiate School seeks a Lower School Associate Teacher for a portion the 2026-27 academic year ( February 1st-June 15th 2027). The ideal candidate will be student-focused, projecting a vivid presence in the Lower School. Additionally, the Associate Teacher must possess an enthusiastic commitment to the importance of building and sustaining a diverse, just, inclusive, and equitable academic environment.

General Summary:

Under the general direction of the Assistant Head of Lower School, the Lower School Associate Teacher is involved in all aspects of the classroom program, assisting Head Teachers in running a Lower School classroom. The Lower School Associate Teacher is primarily tasked with helping to plan and teach all homeroom subjects. The Associate Teacher helps students learn and understand abstract concepts, solve problems, and develop critical thinking skills and enthusiasm for learning and hard work. Furthermore, the Associate Teacher is responsible for observing students and evaluating their abilities, strengths, and weaknesses in collaboration with the Head Teacher.

Essential Duties:

  • Instructs students individually and in groups, using various teaching methods;
  • Prepares syllabi and lesson plans, following curriculum guidelines or school objectives;
  • Implements instructional activities contributing to meaningful learning experiences;
  • Provides a variety of materials and resources for students to explore, manipulate, and use;
  • Plans and conducts activities for a balanced program of instruction, demonstration, and work time that provides students with opportunities to observe, question, and investigate;
  • Adapts teaching methods and instructional material to meet students’ varying needs and interests;
  • Manages student behavior in the classroom by establishing and enforcing rules, expectations, and procedures;
  • Observes and evaluates students’ performance, behavior, social development, and physical health;
  • Maintains accurate and complete records of students’ progress and development;
  • Collaborates with head teachers and administrators in the development, evaluation, and revision of the academic program.

Qualifications:

A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in teaching or related field required. Experience working with children preferred.

Additional Requirements:

  • Successful completion of all required background checks.
  • Regular attendance at school events, faculty meetings, and professional development days is expected.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Ability and willingness to participate fully in a dynamic day school located in New York City;
  • Excellent communication skills, both orally and in writing;
  • Ability to remain responsible at all times for the supervision of students during classes and generally at all times when on campus or off campus;
  • Ability to learn new technology and systems commensurate with program requirements;
  • Demonstrated ability to act as a role model of professionalism;
  • Ability to model honesty, accountability, understanding, respect, love, and kindness for the students;
  • Ability to multitask, keep calm under pressure, and treat everyone with respect;
  • Displays curiosity, a positive attitude, flexibility and a good sense of humor;
  • Ability to follow all policies and procedures of the School as written in the employee and parent handbooks.

About Collegiate School

Founded in 1628, Collegiate School is an independent, K–12 day school for boys located in New York City. Collegiate prepares young men to think critically, act compassionately, and lead with honor and purpose in a diverse and ever-changing world.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

Collegiate School is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or any other protected status under applicable laws.

job.title: Sequoyah School Interim 5th/6th Grade Full-time Teacher
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Founded in 1958, Sequoyah School is an independent progressive K-12 day school in Pasadena, California, built on the belief that diversity of all kinds is fundamental to a powerful education. Students find joy and deep learning as they navigate through curriculum while teachers guide problem-centered classrooms that foster curiosity through intellectual exploration and opportunities for application. The school’s mission to challenge the mind, nurture the heart, and celebrate human dignity is evidenced in its place-based program and signature experiences like Field Studies, the Social Innovation Program, Talking Leaves, and more.

Sequoyah’s learning program is designed collaboratively. In K–8, this Lead Teacher would work with the Associate Director of Middle School, subject-area Specialists, and the Director of Teaching & Learning, as well as the Assistant Head of School.

All Lead Teachers are primarily responsible for the academic, social, and emotional learning of a mixed-age class of students. As both designer and advisor, they build a class culture both in the classroom and in the student culture rooted in Sequoyah’s mission and Habits of Mind and guided by the Teaching Guide and Essential Expectations. It’s a culture where students belong, use their voice, make real choices, and learn how to be in a mentoring relationship.

Lead Teachers also help shape the grade-level program as a whole, at a moment when Sequoyah is reimagining the middle years as the bridge of its K–12 education, when students form their identity, gain independence, and begin to own their learning. We are looking for someone excited to help build the best progressive middle school program. They will be excited to extend the program’s interdisciplinary, project-based, and experiential work, building on programs such as Field Studies, Stewardship, and Community Engagement. The goal is a program that meets students where they are, takes their voice seriously, prepares them for a confident move into high school, and fits our K–12 vision.

Position Overview

We are currently accepting applications for the 2026-27 school year.

Roles and Responsibilities

Program Development

  • Plan and implement language arts, social studies, and spelling curriculum that includes high-quality projects that engage students in deeper learning and change-making.
  • Look for opportunities to integrate specialists’ instruction with other classroom activities and for opportunities to create emergent curriculum, responsive to student interests and current events.
  • Design opportunities for students to present learning to authentic audiences through exhibitions, portfolio presentations, publications, or community events.
  • Create and refine inquiry-based, project-driven units that reflect Sequoyah’s Habits of Mind—including Inquiry, Communication, Collaboration, and Stewardship.
  • Implement competency-oriented assessment practices that emphasize revision, reflection, and student ownership of growth.
  • Establish systems for program evaluation and improvement.

Student Experience and Well-Being

  • Able to complete the remainder of the school year.
  • Design classroom structures that support the development of early adolescent identity, executive functioning, autonomy, and agency.
  • Serve as students’ main point of support, building a classroom culture of dignity, curiosity, and growth. Keep the classroom physically and emotionally safe through clear, consistent management.
  • Use routines that support social-emotional and identity development, including morning meetings, circle practice, advisory, individual check-ins, and one-on-one coaching.
  • Oversee and participate in one Field Studies trip/semester, ensuring experiences promote independence, empathy, environmental awareness, and curricular integration.
  • Facilitate the design of programs and partnerships that allow students to practice stewardship and civic responsibility.
  • Continuously assess and evaluate student progress, keeping in mind subject-area and grade-level expectations.
  • Provide transparent feedback aligned to Learning Outcomes and Habits of Mind, supporting students in tracking and articulating their own progress.
  • Design proactively for a full range of learners, including neurodiverse students, for developmental needs. Work with Learning Services to put accommodations in place and to treat variability in learning as normal.

Family and Community Partnership

  • Communicate regularly and transparently with parents/guardians about students’ progress, including but not limited to: participating in parent-teacher conferences, narrative end-of-year reports, back-to-school nights, admissions events or other events at the request of the administration, sometimes outside of contractual hours.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by the supervisor.

Qualifications

We are seeking a candidate who:

  • Holds a Master’s degree or higher in education or a related field.
  • Has at least 2 years of experience in teaching.
  • Demonstrates a deep understanding of child development.
  • Shows commitment to progressive ed/experiential learning.
  • Is familiar with anti-bias/inclusive instructional pedagogical practices and has fluency in belonging, equity and justice work.
  • Possesses strong communication and organizational skills with an ability to build trust across students, faculty, and families.
  • Brings a collaborative, reflective, and adaptable collegial and leadership style.
  • Has experience with competency-based assessment practices (preferred).

Additional Information

Personal Attributes

  • Teacher with appreciation for young adolescents as thinkers and community members.
  • Joyful lover of children with institutional awareness and steady temperament.
  • Creative problem solver who sees complexity as opportunity.
  • Passion for field-based, interdisciplinary learning and a belief in the transformative power of community.
  • Seeker of knowledge of current instructional theories and best practices. Demonstrates a commitment to professional growth by participating in professional development opportunities.
  • Reflective practitioner committed to continuous growth, feedback, and collaboration for student-centered learning.

Diversity is a founding value of Sequoyah School, and we seek candidates willing and interested in upholding an equitable, inclusive environment. Sequoyah School is also an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate in any phase of employment. We consider applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, sexual orientation, age, disability, marital status, or any other legally protected status.

Hiring Term

2026-27 School Year

Reports To

Assistant Head of School and K-8 Director

Campus Location

K-8 campus

Salary Range

$71,000 to $116,000, depending on experience and education

Benefits

Sequoyah offers competitive salary and benefits.

job.title: Fay School Director of Auxiliary Programs

job.title: The Agnes Irwin School Campus Operations Coordinator and Project Manager
job.description:
Position Description & Application

The Campus Operations Coordinator/Project Manager is a 100% on site role that works closely with the Director of Facilities to support the day-to-day and strategic needs of the school. This role is responsible for overseeing and executing key operational and project-based initiatives aligned with the organization’s goals, blending hands-on operational support with the planning and delivery of both short- and long-term projects.

Immediate 18-Month Renovation Focus: In addition to core campus duties, this position will serve as our primary, in-house "boots on the ground" coordinator managing the complex internal logistics of vacating a 60,000 sq. ft. facility, transitioning operations into temporary classroom trailers, and managing the eventual return move. While an external Owner’s Representative firm and a Construction Manager handle the macro-level construction and structural engineering, this role will own the human, organizational, and moving logistics to ensure zero downtime for the school year and camp operations.

Position Responsibilities

  • Coordinate and manage key operational and minor capital projects across campus (e.g., scheduling, vendor transitions, space planning, localized facility updates).
  • Serve as the visible, daily bridge between campus staff (teachers, administrators) and the external Owner's Rep team to minimize daily operational friction.
  • Plan, schedule, and execute the physical move-out and move back into 60,000 sq. ft. facility. Coordinate internal packing, labeling, and asset tracking for staff. Act as the primary on-site liaison for the commercial moving company.
  • Coordinate the internal layout setup, furniture deployment, and staff move-in for temporary classroom trailers to ensure a seamless kickoff to the academic year.
  • Monitor project timelines, milestones, and resource allocation to ensure timely and effective execution.
  • Support the Director of Facilities in daily logistics, systems improvement, and process development.
  • Assist with compliance tasks including policy updates, regulatory documentation, vendor COI’s.
  • Prepare operational reports and summaries for leadership, tracking project impact and alignment with school goals.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Ideal Candidate

  • Embraces the Agnes Irwin School’s mission to empower each girl to learn, lead, and live a legacy, and is committed to the ethos of girls’ education.
  • Comfortably navigates moving between all three academic divisions and athletic departments and builds trust with administrators, faculty, and students.
  • Commits to continued development of cross-cultural awareness and necessary skills to engage across differences with empathy and understanding, demonstrating respect for different values and viewpoints.
  • Demonstrates a dedication to continuous growth and development in areas of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging and commits to our DEIB Philosophy
  • at Agnes Irwin.
  • Regards collaboration as an essential component of professional growth and values working on a team.

Successful candidates will possess:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Education Management, or a related field.
  • 3+ years of experience in school operations, corporate relocations, event logistics, project coordination, or high-volume administrative operations.
  • Exceptional organizational skills; a proven ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously and maintain highly accurate inventory/tracking lists.
  • Strong interpersonal skills; able to firmly hold external vendors and contractors accountable while remaining supportive and patient with internal school staff during a disruptive transition.

Physical Demands and Work Environment:

  • Ability to walk, stand, maintain balance, climb ladders, crouch, lift, carry, push, or pull up to 50 lbs., bend, stoop, and reach above shoulder level
  • Ability to prioritize and perform multiple tasks, to read, analyze, and interpret general business documents, invoices, forms, and government regulation
  • Ability to adapt behavior to function effectively in a school environment, including those specific to the traditions of the School
  • Ability to withstand indoor and outdoor environmental conditions including dirt, dust, pollen odors, sun, wetness, rain, fumes, temperatures, noise, or machinery vibrations

The Agnes Irwin School is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

job.title: Columbus School for Girls Operations Coordinator
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Columbus School for Girls (CSG) is an independent day school in Columbus, Ohio, founded in 1898, serving diverse students in grades pre-k through grade 12. CSG empowers girls to discover their distinct potential as learners and leaders. As a leader in the education of girls and young women, it is a vibrant community of more than 500 students, 120 faculty and staff, and 2,500 active alumnae. CSG’s bucolic 8-acre academic campus in the beautiful Bexley neighborhood is a ten-minute drive from downtown Columbus, a city bustling with the artistic, civic, and shopping experiences that belie the ease of lifestyle that the city affords its residents. CSG offers an exceptional, student-centered academic experience with strong offerings in the arts, an impressive athletic program, and a health and wellness curriculum that is unique in Central Ohio. This combination of academics and skills ensures that CSG students will be well prepared for life beyond CSG.

Columbus School for Girls seeks to hire a full-time Operations Coordinator. Reporting to the Operations Manager, this position provides administrative and logistical support for the School’s daily campus operations, including transportation coordination, event logistics, operational scheduling, and maintenance of access and safety records. Working collaboratively with departments across the School, the Operations Coordinator helps ensure the effective implementation of established procedures, clear communication, and smooth execution of school activities and special events. This full-time position follows a regular schedule of Saturdays and four weekdays to support the School’s operational needs.

  • Provide administrative and logistical support for daily school transportation, field trips, and special events, including scheduling, vendor coordination, coverage arrangements, and communication with internal stakeholders.
  • Support the planning and execution of campus events, including major school programs such as Thanksgiving, Alumnae Weekend, and Graduation, and participate in event planning committees as assigned.
  • Coordinate major school deliveries, including scheduling, receipt, setup, relocation, and storage of furniture, equipment, and other materials, as well as routine mail and package logistics.
  • Respond to routine operational requests related to safety, security, transportation, and events, referring matters requiring additional authority or decision-making to the Operations Manager or appropriate personnel.
  • Provide administrative support for campus safety and operational activities, including drills, training, documentation, scheduling, and follow-up.
  • Participate in weekly operations meetings and collaborate with the Operations Manager, Security Officer, Front Desk Receptionist, Rental Coordinator, and other school personnel to communicate logistical needs, coordinate assigned activities, and support daily campus operations.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by the Operations Manager.

Qualifications and Requirements:

  • High School Diploma required; associate’s degree in operations management or equivalent experience preferred.
  • Facility, event management, operations support, or transportation coordination experience (2-5 years) preferred.
  • High level of customer service.
  • Attention to detail.
  • Communication skills (oral and written) and confidence in conveying information to all types of community members, including administrators, faculty, staff, students, trustees, parents, and visitors.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects in a high-energy school environment and pivot as needed.
  • Proficient skills in Google Workspace.

Physical Demands

This position requires the ability to sit, stand, walk throughout campus, communicate effectively, use standard office equipment, and occasionally bend, reach, lift, or move materials and equipment weighing up to 40 pounds. The role involves a combination of administrative work and occasional hands-on support for campus operations and events. The position requires flexibility to support evening or weekend events.

Interested candidates should apply on the Career page of our website at: https://www.columbusschoolforgirls.org/about/careers and submit a cover letter outlining their interest in and qualifications for this specific position, including a resume

job.title: Crossroads School Head of Middle School
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Description

The new Head of Middle School will bring deep middle school experience, analytical thinking and planning, high emotional intelligence and excellent communication skills to the role. They will add structure, frameworks and systems where needed, while recognizing and giving consideration to the structures already in place. The Head must build trust within the Crossroads community and provide consistent and transparent communication to faculty, students and families. The Middle School has been described as “the magical nucleus” of the school, but there is also a need for better definition and articulation of the division’s place between Elementary School and Upper School. The new Head will provide a clear and confident vision for the Middle School and will execute on that vision in collaboration with all key constituencies.

Strategic Priorities

The Head of Middle School will be a strategic partner and thought leader who will help strengthen and advance Crossroads’ vision and strategic plan for the Middle School. By working collaboratively with both decisiveness and flexibility, the Head of Middle School will prioritize the following:

  • Assess curriculum and program, and finalize a published scope and sequence
  • Evaluate and implement new systems and frameworks as needed.
  • Consistently build bridges of trust, community, and connection.
  • Provide mission-aligned vision and direction to the Middle School division.
  • Help to attract, recruit, and retain a talented and diverse faculty.

Essential Functions

  • Support the Grade-Level Deans who oversee the Student Life Program; serve as counsel for higher-level disciplinary issues
  • Ensure articulation of diversity, equity, inclusion, and justice principles as they relate at Crossroads, and continue to bring them into the everyday life of the Middle School with the whole child and progressive principles in mind
  • Bring bold and innovative ideas to the table while respecting and honoring Crossroads’ traditions
  • Build community, culture, and trust
  • Work with the Assistant Head of Middle School to plan events and programs
  • Work with Elementary School and Upper School Heads to examine and improve all transitions from Elementary to Middle and Middle to Upper School — such as social emotional learning and curriculum
  • Work with Elementary School and Upper School Heads to clearly understand, define and articulate each division’s place within the Crossroads ecosystem
  • Develop strong relationship with the faculty; supervise, mentor, guide, and support them in their everyday activities and in their professional development
  • Be a visible and available leader to faculty, students, and families
  • Meet regularly with the Parent Association to share updates and answer questions

ATTRIBUTES AND COMPETENCIES

  • Sympathetic and empathetic; high emotional intelligence
  • Calm, unflappable, and strong in crisis situations
  • Relationship builder
  • Invested, excited, and willing to lead
  • Approachable
  • Ability to manage ambiguity
  • Multitasker
  • Decisive and direct
  • Ability to make others feel seen, heard, validated, and valued
  • High emotional intelligence
  • Warm, community-minded, with a good sense of humor

Philosophy and Core Commitments

The School was built upon five basic commitments: to academic excellence; to the arts; to the greater community; to the development of a student population of social, economic, and racial diversity; and to the development of each student’s physical well-being and full human potential.

It is the goal of Crossroads School to provide a strong college preparatory program from which each student will develop a personal commitment to learning, a respect for independent thinking, and an expanding curiosity about the world and its people. We consider certain skills to be essential for all graduates: to read well, to write clearly and coherently, to study effectively, to reason soundly, and to question thoughtfully.

Through the educational process, we assist students in gaining self-esteem, self-knowledge, and respect for the knowledge and opinions of others. We believe that education must not be a race for the accumulation of facts, but should be an enriching end in itself. We also believe that education is a joint venture among students, parents and teachers. To be effective with young people, teachers and parents must themselves continue to learn, so that they may perceive the young accurately and treat them wisely.

We believe that the arts are an essential part of the curriculum and that it is important for students to express themselves creatively and to use their imaginations freely. Therefore, music, drama, visual arts, film, writing and dance are significant parts of student life at Crossroads.

Through our academic and extra-curricular programs, we seek to promote social, political and moral understanding, and to instill a respect for the humanity and ecology of the earth.

We understand that there are many kinds of intelligence, and the traditional academic, cognitive area is one. Other important areas of intelligence are intuition, imagination, artistic creativity, physical expression and performance, sensitivity to others and self-understanding. To neglect any of these areas is to limit students in the development of their full human potential.

We believe that the uniqueness of children is revealed in their very existence and that it is the School’s responsibility to foster their innate sense of the mystery and joy of life.

Equity and Inclusion

Crossroads is a welcoming, inclusive community that seeks to reflect the diversity of the greater Los Angeles area and encourages the exchange of multiple viewpoints and experiences. The diversity of Crossroads’ families, faculty, and staff is apparent in their varied social, economic, and racial backgrounds; belief systems; ethnicities and religions; sexual orientations, gender expressions and identities; family structures; and much more. Crossroads’ diversity enriches the learning experience, exposing students to people of differing backgrounds and perspectives and helping them develop empathy and cultural competency. It also builds their awareness of systematic social inequities and empowers them to advocate for a more just world.

THE SCHOOL

Crossroads School for Arts and Sciences is a leading progressive school offering an educational environment as nurturing as it is inspiring. Founded in 1971, the community of 1,210 kindergarten through 12th graders connect and challenge one another in deep and meaningful ways. The extraordinary faculty and staff serve as academic and personal mentors as Crossroads students grow from 5-year-olds into young adults who are poised to effect positive change in the world.

Campus and Geography

Crossroads School has two campuses located a few blocks apart in a distinctly urban area of Santa Monica, California and easily reached by multiple forms of transportation. Santa Monica is located in Los Angeles County, enviably situated alongside the Pacific Ocean. A vibrant and diverse city, Santa Monica has something for everyone, from world-class restaurants to a vibrant art scene to street performers at the Third Street Promenade.

The Norton Campus is home to:

  • The Elementary School (grades K-5)
  • The Joanie Martin Community Room, a multi-purpose space for events
  • The K-12 Sports Center, which features a gymnasium, pool, and athletics field

The 21st Street Campus is home to:

  • The Middle and Upper Schools (grades 6-12)
  • The Alley, a vibrant centerpiece of campus life
  • The School’s administrative offices
  • Bezdek Center for Performing Arts (New 2026)

THE PROGRAM

Crossroads strives to prepare students to think critically, express themselves openly and respectfully, and commit themselves to lives that value community engagement and leadership. Crossroads aims to deliver a transformational educational experience that helps students find their passions, broaden their horizons, and develop the leadership skills they will use to make meaningful differences in the world around them.

Middle School

Middle School offers students opportunities for new experiences, increased freedom, and greater personal responsibility. Students discover new ideas through literature, experimentation, problem-solving, and discussion. Crossroads’ unique Core program integrates English, geography, social studies, and history to provide an interdisciplinary look at social movements and world events, while their Options program allows students to explore a wide variety of subjects outside of the curriculum. Supportive feedback from adults is a hallmark of the Middle School, where the educational environment honors process as well as product, and students flourish in a cooperative and collaborative learning environment.

The Middle School experience is defined by a harmonious balance of guidance and exploration. Crossroads students receive tailored instruction that channels their curiosity into unfamiliar curricular terrain and helps them make informed choices about their own educational pursuits. Surrounded by adults who understand and value this crucial developmental stage, students enter meaningful conversations with teachers, coaches, deans, and administrators. The Crossroads faculty members are mentors who create an environment for students to work collaboratively while fostering strong relationships.

The Middle School is characterized by exposure to new ideas and the freedom to explore developing interests. Self-advocacy and self-expression flourish as numerous Options classes and rotations in P.E. and the arts introduce new subject matter and inspire students to make educated decisions about their academic and extracurricular pursuits. Crossroads students joyfully tackle new material while sharpening their critical thinking and problem-solving skills. As they begin appreciating uncertainty, they also start seeking out intellectual complexities on their own by asking thoughtful questions and making connections across disciplines.

Fast Facts

Enrollment: 1210 (Middle School 335)

Students who identify as people of color: 56%

Full Time Faculty: 132

Faculty who identify as people of color: 46%

Campus size: ~70 acres

Affordability Program Budget: $11 million

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred
  • 7-10 years of experience in a K12 school environment; independent school experience preferred
  • 2-4 years of supervisory/management experience
  • Experience in progressive education and as a teacher and administrator in grades 6-8
  • Deep knowledge of and passion for students in this age range and what it means educationally and socially
  • Experience with DEIJ and strong value placed on the principles
  • Experience in navigating challenging conversations about sensitive issues
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to evaluate people and systems and provide feedback and guidance

Interested candidates are invited to submit the following materials confidentially as a single PDF file:

​​​​

  • A cover letter indicating the candidate’s particular interest in and qualifications for the position
  • A current résumé/CV
  • A statement of educational philosophy
  • The names, addresses, and telephone numbers of three references, including at least one recent supervisor. References should speak to the applicant’s ability to be an effective educator and administrator, to work successfully with children, and to work collaboratively and collegially with adults (references will be contacted only with the candidate’s permission).

Search Calendar

Applications due: December 11, 2026

Semifinalists interviews: Mid-January 2027

Finalists interviews: Early to Mid-February 2027

Hiring announcement: March 2027

job.title: St. Stephen's and St. Agnes School Middle School Teacher
job.description:
Position Description

This is a talent pipeline posting for prospective positions. While we do not currently have immediate active openings, we invite passionate educators to submit their materials for consideration for potential opportunities in the 2027–2028 academic year.

Are you a passionate, innovative educator eager to make a lasting impact on students' lives?

St. Stephen's and St. Agnes School (SSSAS) Middle School, a school grounded in Episcopal values, is looking for inspiring teachers who are ready to engage, challenge, and support middle school learners during one of the most transformative periods in their development.

Why SSSAS?

At SSSAS, we believe that goodness is as important as knowledge. We celebrate the middle school years as a time of exploration, growth, and discovery-helping students develop not just academically, but socially, emotionally, and spiritually. Our Episcopal identity calls us to create an inclusive, welcoming environment where every member of our diverse community is valued and respected. Whether you're looking to contribute now or in the future, we want to hear from enthusiastic educators ready to make a meaningful difference!

What's Special About Middle School at SSSAS?

Teaching in the middle school years is a unique and rewarding opportunity. This is a time when students are beginning to form their identities, question the world around them, and discover their passions. At SSSAS, we understand the importance of this developmental stage and are committed to nurturing students' curiosity, resilience, and empathy. Our teachers guide students through this pivotal period by fostering strong relationships, creating engaging, age appropriate challenges, and supporting their growth as whole individuals. We also have signature programs of Bonding Trip, Mini Courses, and Saints Got Talent!

We're Seeking Educators Who:

  • Inspire, support, and challenge students while actively engaging in the wider school community through extracurricular activities and leadership programs.
  • Are dedicated to creating equitable, inclusive classrooms where every student feels seen and heard.
  • Collaborate with colleagues across departments, contributing to a supportive, innovative professional environment.
  • Are flexible, creative, and passionate about designing curriculum that meets the needs of middle school learners.
  • Have a commitment to continuous growth and staying current with educational best practices.
  • Possess expertise in their subject areas while fostering the academic, social, and emotional development of their students.
  • Embody the school's mission by fostering collegiality, respect, and community within and beyond the classroom.

What We Offer: As a full-time Middle School teacher at SSSAS, you'll:

  • Teach engaging courses in English, History, Math, Languages, Science or Social Studies that inspire curiosity and critical thinking.
  • Collaborate with talented colleagues on curriculum design, student projects, and interdisciplinary learning.
  • Play an integral role in shaping student leadership and supporting extracurricular activities.
  • Be a valued part of a warm, supportive, and mission-driven community where educators are respected, and committed to professional growth and student success.

Qualifications: We seek educators with:

  • At least 3 years of middle school teaching experience.
  • A Bachelor's degree (Master's degree preferred).
  • A strong foundation in curriculum design, instruction, and differentiated learning.
  • A deep understanding of human development, particularly during the middle school years.

If you are passionate about teaching and excited about joining a high-performing, joyful, and Episcopal learning community, we encourage you to apply! Together, we'll guide students through one of the most formative stages of their lives and help them discover their full potential.

job.title: Crossroads School Annual Fund Manager
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Position overview:

Crossroads School for Arts & Sciences is seeking a fulltime Crossroads Annual Fund Manager to join a collaborative, fast-paced advancement team to strengthen and expand the Crossroads Annual Fund. This is a community builder, strategist and activator for the advancement team at Crossroads. Reporting directly to the Director of Development (DOD), the Crossroads Annual Fund Manager serves as the lead strategist and project manager for the School’s $5M annual fund (as part of the overall $5.5M annual giving goal), responsible for increasing philanthropic participation and unrestricted support across all constituents. Collaborating closely with the DOD, this position combines annual fund strategy, volunteer management, donor engagement and frontline fundraising to strengthen a culture of philanthropy throughout the Crossroads community.

Essential Functions:

Annual Fund Campaign Management, in partnership with Director of Development

  • Develop and execute a comprehensive annual fund strategy that meets or exceeds the School’s $5M+ annual fund goal, including
  • Operations plan of an annual solicitation calendar across mail, email, digital communications and personal solicitations for all constituents
  • Fundraising strategy, including goals for revenue, acquiring new donors, donor participation, retention and upgrades
  • Develop and manage segmented fundraising communications and/or designs, including mail and email solicitations, video content, outreach events, face-to-face visits, banners and other printed material
  • Coordinate with data and communication teams for needed assets and planning for solicitations
  • Utilize donor data and analytics to develop targeted segmentation, personalized solicitation strategies and donor upgrade opportunities
  • Develop recommended ask amounts and solicitation strategies based on research, engagement and giving history
  • Work with the Director of Alumni Relations (DOAR) pertaining to the timing and strategy of alumni and parent of alumni solicitations, which includes developing a solicitation calendar and concept and design of appeals
  • ​​​​​​​Work closely with Database Manager on reports, lists and tracking and analyzing annual fund data to assess growth, changes, and trends in giving for the Director of Development

Crossroads Annual Fund Parent Volunteer Management

  • Establish annual goals, expectations and engagement strategies for Crossroad Annual Fund parent volunteers
  • Recruit, train and manage annual fund parent volunteers to facilitate peer-to-peer outreach
  • Review and refresh volunteer materials on an annual basis, to include outreach templates and scripts, training materials, and schedule of outreach periods
  • Conduct annual training for new volunteers and on an as-need basis for returning volunteers
  • Create personalized assignments for volunteers, as well as a mechanism to share updates with volunteers and gather their feedback
  • Develop call sheets and outreach materials for Board of Trustees, including division of assignments, outreach sheets and asking for and tracking feedback
  • Develop grade-level participation strategies in partnership with parent volunteers and Director of Development

Fundraising Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute cultivation, solicitation and stewardship strategies for assigned prospects and donors
  • Conduct personal visits, phone calls and virtual meetings with Crossroads community members
  • Solicit and close annual fund gifts, while identifying and qualify new leadership gift prospects through annual fund activity and donor engagement
  • Other duties as assigned

Skills, Knowledge and Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • Three or more years of fundraising experience with demonstrated success in personally cultivating, soliciting, stewarding and managing relationships with donors in independent school, higher education, non-profit organizations or a related setting
  • Experience recruiting, training and managing volunteers
  • Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines simultaneously
  • Self-motivated and proactive with the ability to take initiative, anticipate needs and move projects forward independently
  • Strong interpersonal, leadership and relationship-building skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively and represent Crossroads with professionalism
  • Exceptional written and verbal communications skills, attention to detail and follow-through
  • Proficiency with Google Workspace and fundraising technology, including Blackbaud’s Raiser’s Edge NXT or similar constituent relationship management (CRM) platform; experience with GiveCampus and Canva a plus
  • Proven ability to handle sensitive information with discretion and confidentiality
  • Flexibility to travel and work evenings and weekends when necessary

job.title: Flint Hill School Sixth Grade Homeroom Teacher
job.description:
Position Posting

EOE Statement Flint Hill School provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, pregnancy, national origin, ethnic origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

Description

When passion and impact come together, an institution becomes more than a place to work. As many of our teachers and staff will tell you, Flint Hill is a place where they are challenged and inspired, and yet it still feels like home.

At Flint Hill, we believe in redefining what educational excellence looks like. Always curious, every day, we ask questions like, “Imagine if?” and “What’s possible?” And we encourage our students to do the same.

Our teachers’ expertise and commitment to innovative teaching are complemented by a personal approach that emphasizes respect and communication.

At Flint Hill, children are nurtured to be their very best, surrounded by people who know and care about them. Our Lower School, grades Junior Kindergarten - 6, sets new standards of excellence by relentlessly innovating our approach to learning, helping children develop in a positive environment and learn essential social and academic skills. We encourage students to take an active role in their education, as they become effective communicators and collaborative leaders. By emphasizing critical thinking, collaboration, personal goal-setting, and problem-solving skills, our Lower School students become productive and excited learners.

The Lower School Sixth Grade Homeroom Teacher supports the experience of Flint Hill students and faculty and embraces the mission, vision, and core values of the school, the Flint Hill Statement of Institutional Equity and Inclusion, and the Portrait of the Flint Hill Student.

The salary range for this position is $65,000 to $115,000. The pay range represents a good-faith estimate of the salary the school reasonably expects to pay for the position upon hire. The pay offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on a range of factors unique to each candidate, including, but not limited to, knowledge, skills, and abilities; relevant education; length, depth, and breadth of related experience; and any advanced skills the candidate may possess.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Serves as the homeroom teacher for one section of 6th grade.
  • Works collaboratively with colleagues on the grade-level team, Department Chairs, and the Director of Academics to create and deliver engaging curricula and lessons in social studies, math, and language arts
  • Collaborate with all Specialists to support, enrich, and extend the learning of all students
  • Prepares daily and long-range lesson plans in all social studies, math, and language arts
  • Teach pre-algebra and algebra concepts, and support students’ readiness for middle school mathematics
  • Offers additional help to students outside of class
  • Assesses individual and group skills, using a variety of tools, including observational, formative, and summative assessments
  • Keeps detailed and accurate records in the school’s learning management system, documenting curriculum maps and student progress
  • Completes and edits progress reports and report cards professionally and punctually using the school-provided guidelines
  • Finds opportunities to integrate technology purposefully and effectively into lessons
  • Communicates constructively with parents and works towards a mutual goal of partnership that is student-centered
  • Attends school meetings and events, including Back to School Night and parent-teacher conferences
  • Participates in appropriate committee work within the school community
  • Pursues professional development opportunities, both individually and collaboratively
  • Responds to student concerns through referral to school counseling and/or appropriate administrative staff
  • Other duties as assigned

Preferred Qualifications:

An undergraduate degree in Elementary Education or a related field, a minimum of 2-4 years of experience teaching at the upper elementary (Grades 4-6) and/or middle school level; an advanced degree is preferred.

  • Training and experience with direct, explicit reading and writing instruction.
  • Experience with exploratory, inquiry-based, and conceptual math instruction.
  • Demonstrated experience using educational technology tools, including the Google for Education Suite and Apple applications, with a willingness to learn and support students in digital literacy and integrate emerging tools that support teaching and learning.
  • Training and experience in Responsive Classroom practices.
  • Familiarity with Universal Design for Learning (UDL) and a commitment to implementing inclusive teaching strategies that support diverse learners.
  • A demonstrated commitment to creating a classroom environment that is inclusive, equitable, and responsive to students’ varied identities and needs.

job.title: The Harker School Head Varsity Baseball Coach, Upper School
job.description:
Position Description & Application

The Harker School seeks a Head Varsity Baseball Coach for the Upper School Athletic Program. The season begins February and runs through May 2027.

Position Summary

Our coaches must be committed to the personal development of our student-athletes. This includes teaching them skills relating to the sport. As a coach, you must also help students develop a competitive nature, teach them about ethical behavior and good sportsmanship, and assist in the development of leadership and life skills.

Qualifications

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Assumes the responsibility for safely and effectively managing groups of students
  • Organizes practice plans and game plans
  • Communicates effectively with the Athletic Director, other staff, students, and parents
  • Stays informed regarding weekly sports emails, updated developments, and changes
  • Follows all guidelines as expressed in the Upper School Coaches Handbook
  • Completes miscellaneous tasks and duties as requested

Other Duties and Responsibilities

  • Attends coaches meetings and mandatory seasonal parent meetings
  • Ensures students participate in a fair and sportsmanlike manner
  • Ensures safety and decorum of students while traveling to away games
  • Maintains knowledge of league, section, and state bylaws pertaining to volleyball
  • Provides guidance for middle and/or lower school programs where applicable
  • Assumes responsibility for related duties as required or assigned

Knowledge, Skill & Ability Requirements

  • Coaching students (Ages 13–19)
  • Experience in or a strong background in volleyball
  • Ability to model and promote a positive team culture and sportsmanship

Working Conditions

  • May be subject to extended periods of standing or walking
  • Majority of time may be spent indoors in a gym environment, but some outdoor exposure may occur during team travel

Qualifications

  • At least 18 years of age
  • Experience working with children preferred; must be comfortable working with and around school-age children
  • First Aid/CPR certified
  • 1–2 years of coaching experience (preferred)

Our Mission

Our mission is to educate students for success at college and beyond, and to foster kindness, respect, and integrity within a safe and nurturing environment. We achieve academic excellence through the development of intellectual curiosity, personal accountability, and love of learning. Our comprehensive program and exceptional faculty and staff help students discover, develop, and enjoy their unique talents. We honor individuality, embrace diversity, and promote leadership and service, preparing students to take their place as global citizens.

Compensation

Pay for this position is determined according to The Harker School's established pay scale and is based on relevant education and experience, as evaluated by the Human Resources Department. The posted pay range reflects the full pay scale for this position. While the maximum rate is included for transparency, most new hires can expect to fall within the lower to middle portion of the pay scale based on their qualifications and experience.

job.title: La Jolla Country Day School Long Term Substitute: Middle School English Educator
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Salary Range:

$65,000.00 To $88,000.00 Annually

La Jolla Country Day School seeks a thoughtful, engaging, and developmentally attuned English Educator to teach fifth grade in our Middle School, supporting students as they build independence, strengthen literacy skills, and grow as readers, writers, and critical thinkers.

This long-term substitute assignment begins in mid-December 2026 and continues through the end of the academic year, ending on or around June 12, 2027.

Why Join La Jolla Country Day School?

Our English program develops students’ abilities to read critically, write clearly, speak effectively, and think analytically, reflectively, and creatively. In fifth grade, students deepen their literacy skills through explicit instruction in vocabulary, morphology, grammar, and reading comprehension, alongside meaningful opportunities to analyze literature, develop their writing, and engage in collaborative discussion.

As a mission-driven community committed to equity and belonging, we value educators who cultivate curiosity, encourage diverse perspectives, and help every student grow as a confident reader, writer, and thinker.

What You’ll Do

  • Teaching & Learning
  • Teach fifth grade English, building students’ reading comprehension, analytical thinking, writing, and communication skills
  • Deliver engaging, differentiated instruction informed by research-based literacy practices, including the Science of Reading
  • Teach vocabulary, morphology, grammar, and written expression through explicit instruction and authentic reading and writing experiences
  • Guide students in analyzing literature, supporting ideas with textual evidence, and exploring diverse perspectives
  • Provide opportunities for analytical, academic, and creative writing, as well as discussion and presentation
  • Foster an inclusive classroom that encourages curiosity, collaboration, and intellectual risk-taking
  • Curriculum & Collaboration
  • Collaborate with English department and grade-level colleagues to implement curriculum and align instructional practices
  • Use student work and assessment data to guide instruction and monitor progress
  • Maintain continuity of instruction, assessment, and communication throughout the substitute assignment
  • Student & Family Partnership
  • Serve as an advisor to an assigned group of students
  • Build supportive relationships that foster student confidence, independence, and engagement
  • Communicate with families about student progress and areas for growth
  • Provide timely, constructive feedback that supports continued development
  • Community Engagement
  • Participate in faculty meetings, grade-level collaboration, and school activities as appropriate
  • Contribute positively to the School’s professional and communal life

Who You Are

  • Literacy-Focused: You understand how students develop as readers and writers and apply effective instructional practices.
  • Student-Centered: You create engaging learning experiences responsive to students’ strengths and needs.
  • Collaborative: You work effectively with colleagues and families to support student growth.
  • Reflective: You use assessment and feedback to refine instruction.
  • Equity-Minded: You foster an inclusive classroom where all students feel valued, challenged, and supported.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree required; master’s degree in English, education, literacy, or a related field is preferred
  • Experience teaching elementary or middle school English, literacy, or language arts preferred
  • Knowledge of literacy development, reading comprehension, and writing instruction
  • Familiarity with research-informed literacy practices, including the Science of Reading, preferred

Professional Skills

  • Ability to deliver differentiated reading and writing instruction
  • Strong classroom management, communication, and organizational skills
  • Ability to facilitate literary discussions and develop students’ analytical and critical-thinking skills
  • Proficiency with Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, and learning management systems such as Canvas or Blackbaud
  • Flexibility, adaptability, and a collaborative approach to teaching

Work Environment & Schedule

  • Full-time, in-person, campus-based position
  • Typical classroom and school environment with occasional variability during events
  • Requires regular standing, walking, and movement around campus, as well as extended computer use and the ability to lift up to 25 pounds.

Compensation

This long-term substitute assignment begins in mid-December 2026 and continues through the end of the academic year, ending on or around June 12, 2027.

The biweekly salary offer to a successful candidate will depend on factors including experience, education, training, and relevant skills, and will fall within the range of $2,500–$3,400.

To be considered, please submit:

  • Your current resume or CV
  • A cover letter outlining your interest in the position and La Jolla Country Day School, highlighting your relevant experience
  • A sample lesson plan

We value authenticity in the application process and ask that applicants refrain from using AI tools to generate their application materials.

job.title: The Chapin School Grade 1 Associate Teacher Leave Replacement
job.description:
The Chapin School, an independent K-12 day school for girls located in New York City, seeks a student-centered, collaborative, and innovative educator to serve as a Lower School Associate Teacher Leave Replacement in Grade 1 starting mid-December 2026 through mid-March 2027.

All candidates are encouraged to be familiar with Chapin’s website and mission.

Job Overview

Chapin seeks a collaborative and passionate educator to fill a temporary Associate Teacher position (Grade 1). This is an approximately 3 month leave replacement.

Our Lower School Associate Teachers work in an apprenticeship with a Head Teacher. Associate Teachers receive support, coaching, and in-house professional development with the goal of building confidence in their authentic teaching style, curricular mastery, and a deep understanding of child development as they gain skills necessary for head teaching positions. Many candidates are early career teachers with one or two years of student teaching experience and have obtained or are working towards a Master’s degree. Chapin also welcomes recent graduates and career changers with a variety of experiences in early childhood settings.

Responsibilities of this position include but are not limited to:

  • Supporting and collaborating with a Head Teacher in planning and preparing daily lessons and materials
  • Planning and conducting small group or whole group lessons
  • Assessing and documenting students’ needs
  • Attending and participating in grade-level meetings, student support meetings, Associate Teacher meetings, and professional development
  • Participating in conversations around curricular planning and classroom management
  • Working with Co-curricular teachers to engage in interdisciplinary lessons and projects with guidance from Head and Co-curricular teachers
  • Assisting Spanish teachers during classes
  • Supervising lunch, recess, and bus duties

Chapin’s Leave Replacement Grade 1 Associate Teacher Will Be:

A student-centered educator who values each student’s voice, experience, and history who

  • Understands and appreciates the Lower School learner within the context of child development
  • Demonstrates effective pedagogy, particularly in response to the needs of students with a variety of backgrounds, learning needs, and interests

An educator who actively cultivates a classroom and community of belonging by

  • Developing, alongside students, a safe and productive learning environment, building trust with students through clear guidelines and expectations
  • Cultivating an inclusive classroom that promotes diverse points of view and constructive dialogue

An educator who partners with students, their parents, and colleagues in teaching and learning by

  • Employing research-based strategies to reach all students through differentiated approaches, mindful of students’ receptive and expressive learning preferences
  • Enthusiastically approaching their work and demonstrating strong organizational skills, flexibility, and follow-through on assignments from Head Teachers and the Associate Head of Lower School

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s Degree
  • Previous experience with Lower School aged students

Preferred

  • Demonstrates a passion for and recognizes the importance of an all-girls setting
  • Reflective about their practice and pursues professional development opportunities.
  • Has strong collaboration skills as this position requires working closely with a Head Teacher, Associate Head of Lower School, and other colleagues
  • Bilingual speakers are of special interest as our students learn Spanish starting in Kindergarten
  • Have facility with digital tools such as Seesaw, Canvas, Outlook, and the Google Suite for Education

Compensation for this position will be commensurate with experience. The compensation for the leave replacement term will be pro-rated from an annual salary range of $63,000-69,000

How To Apply: Interested candidates should submit a resume and cover letter.

job.title: The Chapin School Director of Student Life
job.description:
About this role

The Office of Student Life is responsible for vibrant, student-led programming that fosters community, curiosity, and exploration. Reporting to the Associate Head of Upper School for Culture & Community and working alongside the Office of Student Life and Deans team, the Director of Student Life helps organize and maintain the pulse of the Upper School. Opportunities for learning and growth outside the classroom allow each student to explore their passions and build leadership skills through clubs, events, self-government, and division-wide programming.

As a member of the Upper School's leadership team, this individual will support division-specific activities and initiatives and provide mentorship to students. The Director of Student Life role is a half-time (50%), 10-month position with occasional evenings to support school events.

Core Duties & Responsibilities

Weekly Operational Oversight & Communications

  • Compose and email THE Weekly email to Upper School students and professional community; maintain THE Weekly as the primary homepage feature on the US Canvas Page and coordinate with Communications to feature highlights in The Chapin Weekly.
  • Review Orders of the Week (OOW) drafts (specifically Drafts 1 & 2) weekly to identify schedule conflicts, discrepancies, or special event needs, and proactively communicate with facilities, OSL, and students (when needed).
  • Schedule and publish weekly reminders on Canvas regarding schedule changes, special events, BCT, and upcoming opportunities; upload and maintain summer program listings for students.
  • Serve as the primary lead for OSL email inbox management; share details, dates, and times of upcoming student events with the Communications team for media and photography coverage.

Student Clubs & Extracurricular Programming

  • Oversee the annual Upper School club application review, audit, and selection process, including managing club reflection forms and flagging inactive programs.
  • Organize the annual Activity Fair (space booking, work orders, schedule announcements) and compile the master OSL Schedule (clubs, affinity groups, self-government, recess, chorus, art club, etc).
  • Guide student club leaders and faculty advisors; serve as the administrative point person for all student merchandise approvals, design reviews, and invoice execution.
  • Plan and coordinate select cross-divisional activities, such as Halloween Club events with LS/MS and mid-year student programming.
  • Support student leaders to create and maintain attendance for their groups.

Student Leadership, Governance & Elections

  • Support students in planning and designing well-organized, developmentally appropriate programming.
  • Manage the full all-school election cycle (Presidential, Vice-Presidential, and Secretarial races across Classes 8–11), including speech timelines, ballot creation, vote tallying, and community communications.
  • Mentor Club President & Secretary, and support with fostering ethical leadership, accountability, and student advocacy among student leaders.
  • Plan and execute student leadership sessions in collaboration with the OSL team.

Divisional Operations, Calendar & Event Oversight

  • Audit and preview the US and K-12 Academic Year Calendar continuously for upcoming events, changes, or conflicts, ensuring accuracy for Deans and administration; lead early calendar cross-referencing and submission for major dates, trips, conferences, and curriculum nights.
  • Oversee room reservations (via R-School/BCT/Assembly Room/GR) for all assemblies, clubs, affinity groups, and special events.
  • Organize and supervise major US events, including Club Nights, Semi-Formal, and Prom fundraisers (securing chaperones, work orders, catering, and raffles).
  • Serve as a core member of the Commencement Planning Team; manage 12th Night planning, gift procurement, and Junior/Senior Sing
  • Lead annual community drives (e.g., Thanksgiving Food Drive); support Council Presidents with programming (Humanities Week, Stress Less Week, etc).
  • Attend 1–2 Deans meetings per cycle, attend OSL meetings 1x per cycle, and attend opening and closing deans/administrative meetings as assigned.

Required Skills and Knowledge

  • Two or more years of experience in student life, advising, or student activities
  • Demonstrated experience mentoring high school students and advising student leaders
  • Proven event planning and logistical skills for executing student events, assemblies, club fairs, dances, and community service drives
  • Proficiency with learning management systems (e.g., Canvas) and facility/room reservation tools (e.g., R-School)
  • Working knowledge of Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Forms) for scheduling, data tracking, and election tallying
  • Strong operational and calendar management skills, including auditing Orders of the Week (OOW) drafts and resolving schedule conflicts
  • Exceptional communication skills for writing division-wide announcements (THE Weekly), Canvas updates, and presenting to students and faculty
  • Basic familiarity with budget tracking, processing invoices, and managing tax-exempt documentation for student merchandise

Highly Valued Experience

  • Experience collaborating on cross-divisional initiatives and events across Lower, Middle, and Upper School divisions
  • Demonstrated commitment to integrating equitable practices, diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging into student programming
  • Familiarity with student event scheduling, chaperone coordination, and facility work-order management

How to apply: Please submit your resume and letter of interest for consideration. Applications will be considered on a rolling basis.

Compensation: This is a faculty position and will be paid consistently with all faculty roles. For faculty applicants there is no change in salary; work responsibilities will be adjusted as necessary.

The salary range for a full time faculty position is $70,000-$130,000 annually.

job.title: Waldorf School of the Peninsula Grades Class Teacher
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Waldorf School of the Peninsula (Preschool - Grade 12) is celebrating it's 41st year of bringing Waldorf education to Northern California. Our school has two beautiful campuses: Preschool through grade 5 in Los Altos and a few miles away in Mountain View are grades 6-12. Our school is a full member of and accredited by the Association of Waldorf Schools of North America and fully accredited by the Western Association of Schools and Colleges. WSP is dedicated to hiring dedicated and highly capable faculty and administration. We invest in our learning and growth to best serve the needs of our students, teachers, community, and each other.

Waldorf School of the Peninsula is seeking an experienced, enthusiastic Grades Class Teacher. We are looking for a dynamic individual who is interested in joining our well-established grades faculty within a growing and thriving Silicon Valley community.

Our energetic group of students seeks a teacher who can engage their eagerness to know about their world and to experience its wonder. They love to move and explore everything that moves around them. We are looking for a teacher to guide their love of learning through a calming presence as they meet you with their bright eyes and passion for life. They cannot wait to meet you.

This position includes, but is not limited to:

  • Teach main lessons and other periods for grade levels 1-8, following the school’s scope and sequence.
  • Assess individual students’ progress, both academically and socially, while developing a trusting partnership with parents.
  • Create and maintain a socially functional and cohesive group of students and manage social and emotional class dynamics.
  • Attend and participate in faculty development conferences and Waldorf School of the Peninsula professional development days.
  • Write quarterly, semi-annual, and annual student reports.
  • Work closely with education support for assessments and students who need accommodations and to implement accommodations when required and feasible.
  • Schedule and organize parent class meetings throughout the year, with occasional one on one scheduled parent-teacher conferences.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in the field of Education or a closely related field
  • Two years of Waldorf class teaching experience.
  • Certificate of Completion in Waldorf Teaching

Benefits and Compensation:

The position is compensated at $72,000 - 75,000 per year.

Please note that relocation assistance and visa sponsorship are not available for this position.

We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, age, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

job.title: Flint Hill School Lower School Social Studies Teacher & Department Chair
job.description:
Position Posting

EOE Statement

Flint Hill School provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, pregnancy, national origin, ethnic origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

Description

When passion and impact come together, an institution becomes more than a place to work. As many of our teachers and staff will tell you, Flint Hill is a place where they are challenged and inspired, and yet it still feels like home.

At Flint Hill, we believe in redefining what educational excellence looks like. Always curious, every day, we ask questions like, “Imagine if?” and “What’s possible?” And we encourage our students to do the same.

Our teachers’ expertise and commitment to innovative teaching are complemented by a personal approach that emphasizes respect and communication.

At Flint Hill, children are nurtured to be their very best, surrounded by people who know and care about them. Our Lower School, grades Junior Kindergarten - 6, sets new standards of excellence by relentlessly innovating our approach to learning, helping children develop in a positive environment and learn essential social and academic skills. We encourage students to take an active role in their education, as they become effective communicators and collaborative leaders. By emphasizing critical thinking, collaboration, personal goal-setting, and problem-solving skills, our Lower School students become productive and excited learners.

The Lower School Social Studies Department Chair supports the experience of Flint Hill students and faculty and embraces the mission, vision, and core values of the school, the Flint Hill Statement of Institutional Equity and Inclusion, and the Portrait of the Flint Hill Student.

The salary range for this position is $80,000 to $120,000. The pay range represents a good-faith estimate of the salary the school reasonably expects to pay for the position upon hire. The pay offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on a range of factors unique to each candidate, including, but not limited to, knowledge, skills, and abilities; relevant education; length, depth, and breadth of related experience; and any advanced skills the candidate may possess.

Social Studies Specific Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Researches and reviews field trip opportunities that support the goals of the social studies curriculum (JK-6)
  • Ensures the Grades JK-6 curriculum, pedagogy, and assessments are aligned with the Pathway of a Student competencies
  • Stewards Responsive Classroom Practices JK - 6
  • Plans and facilitates Lower School Morning Meeting
  • Guides faculty in incorporating culturally responsive and inclusive resources and materials into their lessons

All Department Chair Duties and Responsibilities:

Curriculum Oversight

  • Provides leadership in developing, implementing, and supervising content and skill sequences for Grades JK-6 in the discipline
  • Ensures continuity of the curriculum across grades
  • Reviews and approves proposals for new curriculum and presents proposals for consideration and recommendation to the administration

Departmental Leadership:

  • Collaborates with the Director of Academics and Division Director to provide regular instructional feedback to faculty
  • Actively engages and supports faculty in professional growth and development through structured and unstructured facilitative peer coaching
  • Oversees the review of textbooks and instructional materials
  • Attends and presents at school meetings and events, including Back-to-School Night, parent-teacher conferences, the Parent Engagement Series, and admissions events
  • Participates in appropriate committee work within the school community. Mentors new faculty members in methodology, techniques, resources, and overall practice
  • Develops opportunities to integrate technology purposefully and effectively into the curriculum
  • Identifies subject-matter professional development needs and opportunities for faculty.
  • Establishes departmental goals for the academic year
  • Represents the department in Department Chair meetings
  • Communicates Department Chair information to faculty
  • Maintains an active teaching load as assigned by the Division Director, when needed
  • Reviews formal student progress report comments and provides constructive feedback for faculty
  • Organizes and replenishes the inventory of supplies and equipment
  • Creates and manages the department budget, in consultation with the Division Director and Director of Academics
  • Communicates constructively with parents

Instruction and Instructional Support

  • Team-teaches the discipline with homeroom teachers throughout Grades JK-6
  • Pursues and participates in professional development opportunities, both individually and collaboratively
  • Responds to student concerns through referral to school counseling and/or appropriate administrative staff
  • Works collaboratively with colleagues on the divisional team
  • Other duties as assigned.

Preferred Qualifications:

An undergraduate degree in History, Elementary Education, or a related field; a minimum of 5-7 years of experience teaching history or social studies at the elementary school level; an advanced degree is highly preferred.

  • Training and experience with direct, explicit reading and writing instruction
  • Experience with exploratory, inquiry-based, and conceptual instruction
  • Demonstrated experience using educational technology tools, including the Google for Education Suite and Apple applications, with a willingness to learn and integrate emerging tools that support teaching and learning
  • Training and experience in Responsive Classroom practices
  • Familiarity with Universal Design for Learning (UDL) and a commitment to implementing inclusive teaching strategies that support diverse learners
  • A demonstrated commitment to creating a classroom environment that is inclusive, equitable, and responsive to students’ varied identities and needs
