job.title: The Harker School Library Assistant, Upper School
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Salary Range

$24.00 - $30.00 Hourly

Position Type

Staff

Description

The Harker School, a private TK–12 school located in San Jose, CA, seeks qualified applicants for the position of Library Assistant at our Upper School campus. This is an hourly, part-time position beginning August 10. Regular work hours are Monday through Friday, 12:30 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.

Position Summary

Taking direction from the campus librarian, the Library Assistant provides a range of library services in a school library setting.

Qualifications

Qualifications

  • Ability to communicate in effective English with staff, outside firms, etc. in person, by telephone and via email.
  • Minimum one-year experience in a library, school, or bookstore
  • Minimum one-year experience working with groups of children (school, day camp, park district, etc.)
  • Minimum one year of clerical experience
  • High School diploma or equivalent (required)

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Instructional Support

  • Assist in preparation of the library for instruction.
  • Create and maintain library displays.
  • Use basic library information and communication technologies to assist library users in locating materials.

Communication

  • Monitor and maintain acceptable student behavior conducive to learning.
  • Contact faculty as needed, regarding library materials and programs.

Environment

  • Maintain a neat library by organizing chairs, picking up papers, shelving books, and general straightening.
  • Dust and clean computers, tables, shelves, lamps, displays and book carts.
  • Empty paper recycling containers.
  • Maintain an orderly workspace and circulation desk.
  • Maintain student supplies, library printers, copy machine and scanner.
  • Maintain a library lost and found, delivering unclaimed items to campus lost and found weekly.
  • Monitor student use of library resources.
  • Participate in campus emergency procedures as instructed by Campus Librarian.

Systems

  • Process, shelve, circulate, and repair books and other resources according to library procedure.
  • Maintain circulation records, including collecting and accounting for lost, damaged, or overdue materials.
  • Maintain and circulate audio-visual equipment to the adult school community.
  • Maintain records for Inter-Campus Loans.
  • Conduct regular inventories of library resources and maintain appropriate records.
  • Generate purchase lists based on librarian-annotated review materials.
  • Help enhance online catalog with content notes.
  • Deliver and collect library mail.
  • Participate in organizing library events as directed by the Campus Librarian.
  • Prepare periodic statistical reports.
  • Prepare purchase orders under the supervision of the library director or electronic resources librarian.
  • Participate in annual or semi-annual library inventories.
  • Participate in training as required.
  • Update the online classroom calendar

Other Duties and Responsibilities

  • Commute between campuses, on an as-needed basis, through a reliable means of transportation.
  • Assumes responsibility for related duties as required or assigned.
  • Dependably open and or close the library alone, managing computers, lights, locks, etc
  • Stand on a library stool to retrieve books.
  • Hear individuals, groups, telephone and intercom communications, public address announcements, emergency signals, etc.

Knowledge, Skill & Ability Requirements

  • Ability to work with children and young adults
  • Ability to job-share with co-workers
  • Skilled at using MS Office Word, Excel, and Google Docs
  • Familiarity with scanner and copier functions
  • Ability to communicate effectively with students, parents, staff, and faculty
  • Ability to develop positive cooperative relationships with others
  • Ability to receive and to give positive feedback and constructive criticism
  • Ability to operate library information and communication technologies
  • Ability to supervise students in an appropriate manner
  • Interest and ability to learn new skills

Working Conditions

  • Lift boxes weighing 20 pounds.
  • Push a book truck loaded with books.
  • Stand up and reach, bend down to shelve, retrieve, and inventory books.

Our Mission:

Our mission is to educate students for success at college and beyond, and to foster kindness, respect and integrity within a safe and nurturing environment. We achieve academic excellence through the development of intellectual curiosity, personal accountability and love of learning. Our comprehensive program and exceptional faculty and staff help students discover, develop and enjoy their unique talents. We honor individuality, embrace diversity, and promote leadership and service, preparing students to take their place as global citizens.

Compensation

Pay for this position is determined according to The Harker School's established pay scale and is based on relevant education and experience, as evaluated by the Human Resources Department. The posted pay range reflects the full pay scale for this position. While the maximum rate is included for transparency, most new hires can expect to fall within the lower to middle portion of the pay scale based on their qualifications and experience.

job.title: Georgetown Day School Associate Director of College Counseling (part-time)
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Georgetown Day School opened its doors in 1945 as the first integrated school in a segregated city. GDS was founded by seven changemaker families who envisioned a school committed not only to academic excellence and educational innovation but also to respect and care for others. Believing that diversity is a critical foundation for the most transformational learning, they established a school where all children would be welcomed, celebrated, and challenged to be their best selves.

Today, the School’s philosophy and programs strongly reflect its roots. GDS fosters a community of belonging while lifting up every student’s unique gifts, building in each the capacity for compassion, leadership, and creating positive change. 1125 engaged and talented PK-12 students across three divisions love to learn and learn to change the world in GDS’s exciting urban campus with its outstanding facilities. Recognized as one the most dynamic educational institutions in our capital city and nation, GDS today is in a uniquely attractive position, with a deeply-felt and lived history, clear mission, and genuine openness to the possibilities that lie ahead.

About the Position

DEPARTMENT: High School College Counseling

REPORTS TO: Director of College Counseling

SUPERVISES: N/A

FLSA: Exempt

TYPE OF ROLE: Part-time

START DATE: January 2027 (or sooner)

COMPENSATION: $ 45,000 - $58,000 annually (based on experience)

BENEFITS: Eligible

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis and preference will be given to early applications.

Georgetown Day School, an independent day school in Washington, D.C., invites applications for an Associate Director of College Counseling. The College Counseling team at GDS is a mission-driven, collaborative group that guides students and families through the college process with a focus on equity, wellness and balance. Our philosophy of equitable and accessible college counseling centers on student empowerment, self-advocacy and authentic self-reflection.

The Associate Director will work as part of a team, expertly guiding students to identify colleges and universities that match their goals and values, developing strong relationships with students and families, and providing sound advice at every step of the college process. As a diverse, inclusive school devoted to preparing our students to live and work in an increasingly globalized and multicultural society, GDS is particularly interested in professionals with demonstrated interest and experience in working in such a school setting.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities

  • Advise and support approximately 18 students through all phases of the college process. Counseling students and families with empathy and compassion through the stresses and challenges of the college search, application and enrollment process.
  • Play a key role in the development of an inclusive and forward-thinking college counseling program in collaboration with school leadership.
  • Write detailed, personal and incisive letters of recommendation in support of counselees.
  • Communicate clearly and effectively with students and parents on all issues and trends related to college admissions, standardized testing and financial aid.
  • Work closely with the College Counseling team to organize and run college counseling events and to develop new programming.
  • Stay abreast of new programs and policies at colleges and universities through professional conferences, college tours, networking and reading of relevant publications.
  • Develop and maintain strong relationships with admissions officers at a wide array of colleges and universities.
  • Represent GDS (its curriculum, mission and students) to colleges and universities in a manner that highlights the unique attributes of a GDS education.
  • Participate fully in the life of the school through faculty meetings, in-service learning opportunities, and academic advising.

Secondary Duties and Responsibilities

  • Additional duties outside this description may be assigned as necessary.

Qualifications

Education and Experience

  • B.A. or B.S. degree is required.
  • A minimum of 3 years of relevant experience in selective college admissions or college counseling is required.

Required Skills

  • Excellent communication skills - be a strong writer, a compelling speaker, a thoughtful listener, and have strong time-management skills.
  • Displays empathy, flexibility, maturity, optimism, and a strong work ethic will be highly valued in this position.
  • Energy to thrive in a dynamic and fast-paced office environment that encourages collaboration, mutual respect, compassion, and care.

Americans with Disability Specifications

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel objects, tools or controls; reach with hands and arms; climb stairs; balance; stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl; see, talk or hear; taste or smell. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.

Work Environment

Work environment characteristics described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

To Apply

Qualified candidates should submit a cover letter, resume, and list of three references using our online application system through ADP/Workforce Now: http://www.gds.org/Recruiting. To find out more about the school, candidates should visit our website at www.gds.org.

As an inclusive school devoted to preparing our students to live, work, and lead in an increasingly globalized and multicultural society, GDS is particularly interested in professionals with demonstrated interest and experience in working in such a school setting and is driven by the core charge of working to enhance and bring joy to every student’s individual learning experience in equitable and meaningful ways.

job.title: St. Mark's School Math Teacher
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Position Title: Math Teacher

Start Date: August 2027

Contract type: Yearly; 10-month

School Type: Boarding

Inspire students to think deeply, embrace challenging problems, and discover the beauty and possibilities of mathematics.

Why Join Us

At St. Mark’s, we believe we grow our minds by doing interesting math. Here, you’ll share your enthusiasm for mathematics in a community that values curiosity, creativity, and close connections between teachers and students. You’ll help students discover the beauty of patterns, the power of logical reasoning, and new ways to understand the world. Through thoughtful challenges and encouragement, you’ll guide them to become resourceful, tenacious problem solvers who take intellectual risks and discover they are capable of more than they imagined.

Teaching at St. Mark’s extends beyond the classroom. As a faculty member, you’ll also serve as an advisor, coach, and mentor, helping students navigate school, discover new talents, and build confidence and independence. Our community thrives on collaboration and connection, and we’re looking for educators who are excited to engage fully in all aspects of residential school life.

What You’ll Do

You’ll be a teacher, mentor, and co-creator of learning. Your role will include:

  • Teaching four sections of mathematics across grades 9–12.
  • Designing engaging, developmentally appropriate learning experiences that support a diverse community of learners.
  • Providing meaningful, timely feedback that challenges students and supports their growth.
  • Collaborating with department colleagues on curriculum development, course design, and innovative teaching practices.
  • Serving as an advisor and mentor, supporting students academically and personally throughout their St. Mark’s experience.
  • Engaging fully in boarding school life by leading two seasons of co-curricular activities, supervising students during residential evenings, and participating in weekend activities and programs.
  • Building thoughtful, respectful relationships with students and colleagues that strengthen the School’s inclusive and connected community.

What We’re Looking For

The successful candidate will:

  • Hold a bachelor’s degree in mathematics, physics, engineering, or a related field.
  • Bring secondary school teaching experience, with two or more years preferred.
  • Be prepared and eager to teach a range of courses from geometry through calculus, with the potential to teach advanced electives.
  • Bring a deep understanding of mathematics and make complex concepts accessible, engaging, and meaningful to high school students.
  • Use inclusive teaching practices to support students from diverse backgrounds and with varied learning needs.
  • Model creativity, flexibility, and intellectual curiosity in the classroom.
  • Collaborate thoughtfully with colleagues and participate fully in boarding school life.
  • Work with adolescents with warmth, empathy, and high expectations.
  • Demonstrate strong communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.
  • Use educational technology thoughtfully to support teaching and learning.

Why You’ll Love It Here

Join a close-knit community with opportunities to develop engaging courses and make a meaningful impact beyond the classroom. Benefits include housing, meals, health coverage, tuition remission, and access to campus facilities.

Salary Range

$43,500 – $85,000. Pay is commensurate with experience.

job.title: Deerfield Academy Varsity Volleyball Coach & Faculty Member
job.description:
Position Description & Application

General Summary:

Deerfield Academy, a private coeducational boarding school founded in 1797 and annually serving approximately 650 students grades 9-12, seeks a Varsity Volleyball Coach and faculty member with a start date in July 2027.

Responsibilities:

The Varsity Volleyball Coach is responsible for overseeing all aspects of the Volleyball program, including, but not limited to: supervision and instruction of varsity student-athletes during practices and games; working with athletics staff on the development of practice and competition schedules, promotion of the program (social media, website, etc.), management and development of program staff, and monitoring of student-athlete health and wellness; working with our admissions team to recruit student-athletes to the school; and working with student-athletes, their families, and our college advising team on college placement.

This position will be part of a larger full-time faculty role at The Academy, with the specific department dependent on existing or projected Academy needs and the successful candidate's area of expertise. Other responsibilities will include leading an additional co-curricular activity, dormitory residence or supervision, advising, committee work, and family-style dining hall meals with students. Faculty also have opportunities to design and lead domestic and international travel programs.

Qualifications:

We are looking for candidates who exhibit excellence in the classroom and who can help develop in students the fundamental learning traits outlined in The Deerfield Student and A Framework For Schools. Beyond the classroom, candidates must be prepared to fully engage in the activities and less formal spaces that help define a strong residential educational community. Additionally, candidates for this position will possess the following specific attributes/qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred
  • Previous volleyball coaching experience at the high school, club, or collegiate level
  • Previous experience as a faculty member in the classroom or another role (Admission, College Advising, etc.)

job.title: The Spence School 412 Squash Association Operations Coordinator
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Job Details

Job Location New York, NY

Position Type Part time; 30-35 hours per week; Benefits eligible

Salary Range $26.00 - $28.00 Hourly

Position Summary

The 412 Squash Association Operations Coordinator provides administrative and operational support to ensure the smooth day-to-day functioning of the facility and its programs. This position is responsible for managing schedules, court bookings, registrations, billing, member communications and customer service inquiries while assisting with program administration, events and facility operations.

The successful candidate will be highly organized, detail-oriented, and customer-focused, with the ability to manage multiple responsibilities in a fast-paced environment. As a key point of contact for members, students, families, coaches and guests, the Operations Coordinator helps create a welcoming and positive experience for all participants while supporting the continued growth of 412 Squash.

Required Qualifications

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Excellent customer service and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proficiency with Google Workspace, including Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Forms and Calendar.
  • Proficiency using Canva to create professional communications, flyers and marketing materials.
  • Ability to learn and utilize registration, scheduling, and membership management systems.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing positively to a collaborative team environment.
  • Demonstrated reliability, professionalism, sound judgment and a strong work ethic.
  • Commitment to providing exceptional service to students, families, members, guests and school partners.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous experience in customer service, education, athletics, recreation, hospitality or membership-based organizations.
  • Experience with ClubLocker, Playbypoint or similar scheduling and membership management platforms.
  • Experience supporting website updates and digital communications.
  • Familiarity with social media platforms and content creation.
  • Knowledge of squash or racquet sports is a plus.
  • Passion for youth development, athletics, health, wellness and community engagement.

Required Certifications & Compliance

  • AED/First Aid/CPR certification (or willingness to obtain upon hire).
  • Completion of sexual harassment prevention and mandated reporter training.
  • Successful completion of all required background checks.

Work Schedule

This is a year-round, part-time role requiring 30 to 35 hours per week and is fully eligible for benefits. Weekend coverage is an essential function of the role.

The regular work schedule is generally Thursday through Sunday, with the Operations Coordinator serving as a primary on-site representative during peak facility operating hours.

Approximate hours and schedule include:

  • Thursday and Friday: approximately 9:00 a.m. – 6:00 p.m.

Actual hours may vary based on programming, tournaments, camps, special events, school activities and facility needs. Evening, holiday and occasional additional hours may be required.

About Spence

The Spence School is an independent K–12 girls' school in New York City committed to academic excellence, intellectual curiosity, and the development of each student's full potential. Spence is committed to an equitable and inclusive program and a diverse faculty and student body. Candidates from diverse backgrounds are especially encouraged to apply

job.title: The Bishop's School Interim Math Teacher - Upper School
job.description:
Position Description & Application

About The Bishop’s School

Founded in 1909 and affiliated with the Episcopal Church, The Bishop’s School is an independent, all-gender college-preparatory day school serving 800 students in grades six through twelve. The School is located on a historic campus in the heart of La Jolla, just 10 miles north of downtown San Diego. With a student-teacher ratio of approximately 9 to 1, Bishop’s is known for academic, artistic, and athletic excellence while celebrating character development, diversity, inclusion, and belonging. Last year’s applicant pool drew from 72 zip codes and 168 middle and high schools throughout San Diego County and beyond. Fifty-one percent of the student population self-identify as students of color. Additionally, over $4 million in need-based grants is awarded annually.

What is Essential about Being a Teacher at Our School?

The Bishop’s School seeks engaging, collaborative, dynamic, and learner-centered teachers. We seek candidates who hold high expectations for students, design learning experiences that prioritize adolescent well-being and belonging, are enthusiastic about working on teams and are eager to pursue growth in their teaching practice.

Our goals are to foster curiosity, encourage active student engagement, encourage collaboration in the classroom and direct students to take ownership of their learning.

The Bishop’s School seeks a full-time mathematics teacher with immediate start. This is an interim position for the remainder of the 2026-2027 school year.

The ideal candidate will have a background in teaching mathematics at the high school level and will demonstrate capacity to teach a range of math subjects from second year algebra through honors-level calculus. Capacity to teach linear algebra is strongly preferred. The Mathematics Department seeks candidates who are enthusiastic about working with teaching teams and other departmental colleagues to develop, iterate upon, and align our student-centered and problem-based-learning mathematics curriculum.

The interim mathematics teacher will perform duties consistent with requirements for Bishop's faculty members including communicating regularly with students, parents, and administrators regarding student progress, supervising students in out-of-classroom activities during the school day and after school, and hosting daily office hours.

Responsibilities Include:

  • Teach four sections of math
  • Engage in co-curricular activities as assigned
  • Maintain a clean, safe, and organized work area
  • Collaborate with departmental colleagues in the development of curriculum and meaningful, relevant, learner-centered classroom experiences
  • Provide timely communication to students and their parents/guardians relating to grading and current academic standing
  • Employ a variety of pedagogical approaches to teach students with an array of learning styles
  • Be available to students during office hours and at other times throughout the day to provide guidance and support as needed
  • Uphold the School’s Core Values
  • Demonstrate professionalism and tact
  • Comply with School’s reporting policies and procedures

Required Qualifications:

  • A bachelor’s degree in Mathematics or a related field; advanced degree preferred
  • A minimum of 3 years of teaching experience in high school mathematics
  • Ability to teach both on-level and honors-level students
  • Ability to teach lower-level as well as advanced-level (e.g. multivariable calculus) math courses
  • Unequivocal passion for working with adolescents and supporting them in all facets of their lives
  • Demonstrated commitment to and competency in diversity, equity, inclusion and justice as expressed in the School’s Core Values statement
  • Ability to integrate technology into instruction
  • Enthusiasm to collaborate with other department and grade-level team members in creating meaningful, relevant, learner-centered classroom experiences
  • Demonstrate ability to communicate effectively with students, parents, faculty, staff, administrators, and the community
  • Strong work ethic, as well as time management, verbal, written language, and interpersonal skills
  • Irrespective of own religious orientation, the ability to support the School’s mission and values as a school founded in the Episcopal tradition
  • Commitment to well-being as the foundation for growth

The anticipated annual salary range for this position is $80,000 to $110,000 based on experience. Offered salary will be prorated according to start date.

In addition to competitive salary, The Bishop's School offers a comprehensive menu of benefits including medical, dental, and vision insurance plans, generous PTO, robust professional development opportunities, and chef-prepared lunch provided to employees at no charge on a daily basis when school is in session.

Application

Interested candidates are encouraged to use the link provided to submit a resume, cover letter, and a sample of work (a lesson plan, lab, or project) to the attention of Ian Hayden, Dean of Faculty. Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis until the position is filled.

job.title: The Chapin School Class 4 Math Teacher and Advisor -Leave Replacement
job.description:
Position Description & Application

The Chapin School, an independent K-12 day school for girls located in New York City, seeks a student-centered, collaborative, and innovative educator to serve as a Maternity Leave Middle School Class 4 Mathematics Teacher and Advisor for January, 2027-April, 2027.

Job Overview

The Maternity Leave Middle School Mathematics Teacher reports to the Head of Middle School and will teach four sections of math and serve as an advisor in Middle School, grade 4 from January through approximately April 2027. This teacher will also serve as an advisor. This position necessitates a thorough understanding of Middle School children as well as a desire to work with and advocate for them.

Chapin’s Mathematics Program

Chapin’s Mathematics Department believes all Chapin students are mathematicians in the making. Our next Middle School Mathematics Teacher will design a classroom environment where students work collaboratively to discover the beauty, interdisciplinarity, and myriad applications of mathematics; construct their understanding of rich concepts and complex algorithms; explain their thinking through daily discourse and writing; engage in frequent, purposeful practice needed to achieve fluency; and cultivate the skills of critical thinking and problem solving as they embrace challenges relevant to the world around them.

Chapin’s mathematics professionals work as a team to develop and refine a multi-layered pedagogy with an appropriate balance of access and challenge; competition and collaboration; inquiry and instruction; skills and conceptual understanding. Together, we are propelled by a shared commitment to sending curious, dedicated, skilled, innovative, and courageous young mathematicians into a field that would benefit deeply from their contributions.

Chapin’s next Middle School Mathematics Teacher and Advisor will be:

A mathematician who demonstrates a commitment to innovation and interdisciplinary curriculum development who:

  • Believes in and has experience teaching an integrated, inquiry-based curriculum.
  • Works collaboratively with colleagues to prepare, implement, and document appropriate lesson plans that meet the needs, interests, and abilities of all students.
  • Embodies the joy of learning and exploration by sharing their passion and enthusiasm for mathematics with students.
  • Designs and implements high quality, engaging learning experiences built around intellectual exploration and joyful discovery.
  • Identifies and facilitates interdisciplinary opportunities between the Math and other subject curriculum.
  • Uses diagnostic, formative, and summative assessment data to inform teaching and learning and set individual student goals.
  • Incorporates real-world applications and problem-solving opportunities to help students connect mathematical concepts to everyday life and global issues.

A student-centered educator who values each student’s voice, experience, and history who:

  • Demonstrates effective pedagogy, particularly in response to the needs of students with a variety of backgrounds, learning needs, and interests.
  • Understands and appreciates the middle school learner within the context of pre-adolescent development.
  • Believes that in order for young people to thrive, they must see in the curriculum both themselves and others.
  • Embodies a growth mindset and empowers students to develop their skills and see themselves as mathematicians.

An educator who actively cultivates a classroom and community of belonging by:

  • Engaging students in the process of creating an environment that fosters inquiry, diversity of thought, feedback, and collaboration;
  • Developing, alongside students, a safe and productive learning environment, building trust with students through clear guidelines and expectations.
  • Cultivating an inclusive classroom that promotes diverse points of view and constructive dialogue.

A partner to students, their parents, and colleagues in teaching and learning who:

  • Provides timely and specific feedback to students and parents;
  • Demonstrates a passion for learning by sharing their love of learning with students and colleagues and engaging in ongoing professional development.

Qualifications

Required

  • Masters’s degree in Mathematics
  • At least 3 years experience teaching math in Middle School
  • Experience teaching inquiry-based mathematics

Preferred

  • Experience with differentiated pedagogies and instruction
  • Familiarity with a variety of curricular materials, including standards-based materials
  • Experience as a Middle School Advisor

Compensation will be commensurate with experience: the salary will be pro-rated from an annual range of $70,000–$130,000.

How To Apply: Submit your cover letter, résumé, and statement of educational philosophy. The committee will begin review of applications immediately and will consider those that are submitted on a rolling basis.

job.title: Ashley Hall Lower School (K-4) Learning Specialist
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Reports to: Lower School (K-4) Division Director

Role Duration: Faculty 11 months, full time

Position Overview:

Ashley Hall seeks a full-time Learning Specialist for grades K-4 to begin immediately. The Grades K-4 Learning Specialist will partner with teachers, administrators, and families to support students who require accommodations in their learning environment based on diagnosed learning differences. The successful candidate will provide resource and support services to students in grades K-4 who have a diagnosed and documented need for academic accommodations, both in classrooms and individually. Additionally, the Learning Specialist will help evaluate students who are experiencing academic struggles by providing support through the referral process. Working in collaboration with the Lower School Division Director and the IB Primary Years Programme Coordinator, the Learning Specialist will also develop and implement professional development opportunities for Lower School faculty that will enhance their ability to provide purposeful differentiated instruction and strategies to help strengthen teaching and learning.

Major Responsibilities and Duties:

- Maintain confidential records of students who have psycho-educational testing and share necessary and appropriate summaries of accommodations and recommendations with teachers and the grades K-4 administration.

- Ensure teachers understand student diagnoses, accommodations, and recommendations and that these are correctly and consistently implemented and provided to students.

- Schedule individual appointments with students to discuss specific areas of challenge.

- Support students by submitting and following through with accommodation requests and appropriate documentation for standardized testing.

- Teach executive functioning skills to help students manage deadlines and learn study skills.

- Conduct classroom observations of students and administer diagnostic assessments to help identify potential skill deficits in specific academic disciplines, student needs, and progress, and communicate results and recommendations of observations and assessments with administration, teacher(s), and parents.

- Support teachers by communicating about accommodations and recommendations.

- Partner with teachers to prepare student-specific material that supports student learning.

- Develop and offer professional development for faculty based on collected and analyzed data of student learning behaviors and best practices gleaned from current brain-science and educational research on how students best learn. Professional development should include providing positive learning strategies related to specific learning concerns that improves the learning experience for all students.

- Collaborate/co-teach with teachers on content delivery.

- Maintain accurate student services records for the purpose of documentation and partner with families as needed to ensure records are updated to reflect current diagnoses.

- Communicate with parents regarding student evaluation needs, accommodations, and progress.

- Attend parent and/or parent/teacher conferences to offer suggestions or strategies to ensure school success.

- Meet with any new Lower School family whose child has a formal evaluation to review accommodations and recommendations and construct a learning plan.

- Along with the appropriate administrators, meet with parents who have concerns about their students in order to educate and inform about the benefits of third party testing and the development of a support system at Ashley Hall.

- Provide recommendations to parents related to tutors and/or formal evaluations based on diagnostic impressions and observations.

- Partner with other members of the learning support team in other divisions to ensure students smoothly transition between divisions.

- Maintain records and collection of data necessary for maintaining educational grants and the educational credit for students with exceptional needs program (ECENC).

- Perform additional duties as assigned.

Minimum Requirements:

- Master’s degree preferred in a relevant field.

- Minimum five (5) years experience working with students with special needs and/or learning disabilities at the lower school level, independent school experience preferred.

- Excellent written and oral communication skills.

- Excellent organizational skills to facilitate student record-keeping and timely feedback.

- Exceptional interpersonal skills with both students and adults.

- Deep understanding of developmentally appropriate strategies and practices for students in grades K-4.

- Positive, strong work ethic, with the ability to meet deadlines in a timely manner.

In addition, the ideal candidate will:

- Demonstrate a commitment to student-centered learning as defined by the IB Primary Years Programme.

- Embrace a collaborative, interdisciplinary, team-oriented academic environment.

- Enhance student life in grades K-4 through support of student co-curricular activities.

- Approach their work with students with patience, kindness, and humor.

Interested candidates are required to submit an official application through Ashley Hall’s website at www.ashleyhall.org/careers to be considered for the position.

As part of the online application, candidates will be required to upload a cover letter, resume, and list of references.

Questions regarding the position can be directed to:

Kimberly Ells-Payne, Talent Acquisition and Onboarding Manager

Email: ellsk@ashleyhall.org

Ashley Hall is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability or genetic information.

Charleston, SC

Onsite

Full Time

About Ashley Hall

Talented educators, committed professionals, and inspiring leaders, our faculty and staff are at the heart of all we do at Ashley Hall. Together, we form a supportive community where everyone feels valued, known, and heard. If you have any questions, please contact: Kimberly Ells-Payne | Talent Acquisition and Onboarding Manager ellsk@ashleyhall.org (843) 965-8477

job.title: Hong Kong International School Humanities Teacher (Social Studies & Religion)
job.description:
Position Description

In support of the HKIS Mission and Vision, and to meet HKIS Student Learning Results and appropriate grade level and subject area expectations, the Secondary Humanities (9-12 Religious Education, Social Studies) teacher will carry out broad and specific responsibilities across the following domains: Knowledge of Content, Pedagogy and Students; Instructional Strategies; Management; Assessment; Communication; Collaboration and Professional Practice.

The 9-12 Secondary School Humanities teacher will be able to:

  • plan, deliver and assess concepts that are socially relevant, while maintaining an inquiry approach; the humanities teacher must be able to maintain a neutral stance in the classroom while promoting critical thinking skills for all students
  • demonstrate a strong knowledge and comfort with the C3 framework for Social Studies, as well as with a curricular framework for religious education (Christian Studies Curriculum Framework or similar)
  • respond to students’ social and emotional needs in order to support student learning. This will be demonstrated through participation in the Pastoral Care Groups (PCG) program as well as our high school SEL framework; this includes participation in our high school Interim program
  • model interpersonal skills, respectful relationships, problem-solving, and positive risk-taking in order to promote a safe learning environment

KEY AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY:

KNOWLEDGE OF CONTENT, PEDAGOGY AND STUDENTS:

This describes the breadth and depth of knowledge of the discipline(s) and understanding of HKIS’ Shared Philosophy of Education. For educators this includes planning for instruction, reflection on curriculum content, knowledge of tools and resources, developmental characteristics of students and current pedagogy.

  • Demonstrates a sound knowledge of curricular standards; plans with student awareness and understanding of curricular standards and continually updates professional content knowledge
  • Demonstrates an understanding of levels of cognitive development and learning needs of diverse students through planning and instruction that reflect academic, cultural, spiritual and individual diversity of students.
  • Designs instructional and assessment opportunities that align with overall learning outcomes and match content appropriately

INSTRUCTIONAL STRATEGIES:

This describes the means by which classroom teachers establish a culture for learning, engage students in learning and deliver content. This includes flexibility in the choice of materials, use of appropriate technology and a variety of presentation, grouping and pacing techniques in response to student learning needs.

  • Utilizes a variety of questioning, discussion and reflection techniques that establishes a positive culture for learning in the classroom
  • Demonstrates and encourages a growth mindset in students that promotes accountability for high quality student work
  • Engages students in learning opportunities that build procedural and conceptual understanding
  • Uses a wide variety of digital and non-digital tools and resources for instruction and application activities

MANAGEMENT

This describes how time and resources are prioritized, organized and allocated to provide an effective learning environment. This involves organizing one's own work, planning work for others, anticipating needs and adjusting resources accordingly. For educators, this includes classroom management.

  • Organizes, adapts and maintains student learning data and resources to inform instructional practice.
  • Maintains a safe, accessible learning environment in the classroom and is able to accommodate a range of physical and social needs
  • Establishes and maintains clear classroom expectations and procedures that promote respect and positive relationships
  • Maintains student learning data to support instruction and assessment

ASSESSMENT

This describes the monitoring of student understanding through a balanced program of developmentally appropriate formative and summative assessments aligned to UbD elements (including articulated standards, enduring understandings, knowledge and skills, misunderstandings and academic vocabulary). This includes providing feedback to students and parents to promote learning and the use of assessment results in planning and instruction.

  • Designs and implements a variety of high quality assessments that are aligned with learning outcomes; this includes the use of rubrics and exemplars consistent with our HKIS Assessment Agreements (Secondary)
  • Collaborates with colleagues across the department and division to align assessment expectations that are clear and developmentally appropriate for students in each course and grade level
  • Is able to provide rich feedback on assessment to students in a timely fashion that furthers the next steps in learning
  • Models and explicitly teaches how students can constructively use feedback from the teacher and/or peers and self-assess to inform their learning.
  • Keeps students and families up to date about assessment feedback and a student’s progress through the learning objectives of a course

COMMUNICATION

This describes the verbal and non-verbal articulation of messages within the HKIS community (students, parents, colleagues) both in formal and informal situations. This includes clarity and accuracy of information, the choice of the most appropriate medium and active listening to facilitate a mutual understanding of needs, issues and concerns.

  • Provides clear, accurate and timely feedback to stakeholders
  • Maintains respectful dialogue that demonstrates care, respect for others and sensitivity to diversity
  • Proactively communicates with students, parents, colleagues, administrators and school staff as appropriate

COLLABORATION AND PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE

This describes the manner in which individuals build, promote and maintain strong learning communities. This includes building professional and reciprocal relationships, sharing information about students, curriculum and resources that enhance the success of the HKIS community.

  • Demonstrates a high degree of professionalism at all times and strives to uphold HKIS’s core values
  • Is a reflective practitioner and works in collaboration with colleagues, administrators and students in positive ways
  • Upholds the highest standards with regard to student and adult safety and safeguarding; this includes adherence to privacy and acceptable use of data and technology guidelines
  • Demonstrates initiative in professional learning and seeks out opportunities for professional development to enhance knowledge and pedagogical skillsUndertake other duties and functions as required that will impact and strengthen the contributions of the department and overall operations of the school.

Other

  • Undertake other duties and functions as required that will impact and strengthen the contributions of the department and overall operations of the school.

Education:

  • Bachelors degree in relevant subject area, Masters Degree preferred
  • Qualified Teacher Certification

Experience:

  • Minimum 5 years of full time teaching in the subject area
  • Successful experience working with students in the Secondary Division, High School preferred
  • Previous experience in an international school setting and familiarity with an American educational system preferred
  • Experience working with EAL students and families preferred
  • Experience in Understanding by Design, Inquiry models and strategies preferred
  • Experience and ability to collaborate with diverse teams of educators preferred

Required skills:

  • Excellent knowledge of the subject content and current pedagogy
  • Excellent knowledge of the developmental needs of students in High School
  • Knowledge of and experience with developing and using a variety of assessments and applying differentiated learning techniques
  • Strong grounding in understanding and practice of Standards Based Approaches to instruction and assessment
  • Strong communication skills; ability to communicate effectively (written and verbal) with a diverse community
  • Adept at using educational and classroom technology
  • Strong organizational and time management skills
  • HKIS seeks to hire candidates who are interested in the complex questions of faith and spirituality and who are keen to learn and interact with others of different faith traditions.

Child Protection Statement:

  • At HKIS, each child’s welfare is paramount. We act to ensure that our students enjoy the right to be protected from harm and exploitation and have their welfare safeguarded.

TO APPLY

Interested candidates, please forward your updated resume together with a cover letter and references to recruitment@hkis.edu.hk

Description

POSITION TITLE: Payroll & Benefits Coordinator

DEPARTMENT: Business Office

SUPERVISOR: Director of Human Resources

STATUS: Full Time

FLSA STATUS: Non-Exempt (Hourly)

HOURS OF WORK: 7:30 AM – 4:00 PM

CLASSIFICATION: Essential

SUMMARY: The Payroll and Benefits Coordinator is responsible for the accurate and timely administration of payroll and employee benefits for faculty and staff. This position serves as a key resource for employees regarding payroll, benefits, and related policies and processes, and works closely with Human Resources, Accounting, school leadership, and external vendors.

The Coordinator maintains accurate employee and payroll records, administers benefit enrollments and changes, supports compliance with applicable laws and regulations, and ensures that payroll and benefits processes are handled accurately, efficiently, confidentially, and with a high level of customer service.

This position requires strong attention to detail, high levels of customer service, discretion in handling confidential information, excellent organizational and communication skills, and the ability to manage recurring deadlines while responding effectively to employee needs.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES

Payroll Administration

  • Coordinate and administer the School's biweekly payroll process from beginning to end.
  • Review and process payroll changes, including new hires, salary changes, stipends, bonuses, deductions, leave, terminations, and other compensation adjustments.
  • Ensure accurate and timely entry of payroll and employee information into the School's payroll/HRIS system.
  • Review timekeeping records and follow up on discrepancies, missing information, or approval issues.
  • Calculate and process supplemental payments, stipends, reimbursements, and other payroll-related payments as appropriate.
  • Administer employee deductions, including benefits, retirement contributions, garnishments, and other authorized deductions.
  • Reconcile payroll-related reports and deductions, and work with the Accounting Department to resolve discrepancies.
  • Respond to employee questions regarding pay, deductions, tax withholdings, direct deposit, and payroll records.
  • Maintain accurate and confidential payroll records for insurance coverage, retirement plans, and personnel transactions, such as hires, promotions, performance reviews, and terminations, in accordance with School policies and applicable legal requirements.
  • Coordinate year-end payroll activities, including W-2 preparation and distribution, and other required reporting.
  • Work with payroll providers and other vendors to resolve payroll issues and ensure accurate processing.
  • Submit payroll invoices for payment.
  • Prepare the biweekly contribution report for the defined contribution plan and transmit it to the retirement plan vendor as scheduled.

Employee Benefits Administration

  • Administer the School's employee benefit programs, including medical, dental, vision, life, accidental death & dismemberment, critical illness & accident insurance, disability, flexible spending accounts, health savings accounts, retirement plans, and other employee benefits.
  • Coordinate benefits enrollment for new hires and eligible employees.
  • Process qualifying life event changes, benefit terminations, and other enrollment updates.
  • Monitor benefit eligibility and ensure employee records accurately reflect benefit elections and status.
  • Serve as a primary point of contact for employees regarding benefits questions and assist employees in understanding available options and processes.
  • Work with insurance carriers, third-party administrators, brokers, and other vendors to resolve enrollment, billing, claims, and eligibility issues.
  • Review benefit invoices and reports for accuracy and coordinate corrections as necessary.
  • Submit benefit invoices for payment.
  • Support the administration of retirement plan enrollment, employee contributions, and related processes.
  • Maintain accurate benefits records and documentation.

Compliance and Records Management

  • Maintain confidential and accurate personnel, payroll, and benefits records.
  • Support compliance with applicable federal and state employment, payroll, and benefits requirements.
  • Assist with required payroll and benefits reporting and audits.
  • Maintain required documentation related to employee eligibility, benefit elections, and payroll.
  • Assist with the preparation of information requested by auditors, benefit providers, consultants, and regulatory agencies.
  • Monitor changes in payroll and benefits requirements and communicate relevant changes to the Director of Human Resources.

Employee Support and Customer Service

  • Provide responsive, professional, and confidential service to employees regarding payroll and benefits.
  • Explain payroll and benefits policies and procedures clearly and accurately.
  • Assist employees with benefit enrollment, qualifying life events, and navigating vendor systems.
  • Help employees navigate whom to contact for claims, coverage, or other benefit-related concerns.
  • Handle sensitive employee information with discretion and maintain strict confidentiality.
  • Identify recurring employee questions or process issues and recommend improvements.

Human Resources and Administrative Support

  • Maintain accurate employee data in the School's HRIS and related systems.
  • Ensure employee status and compensation changes are accurately and promptly reflected.
  • Assist with HR projects, reporting, audits, and other initiatives as assigned.
  • Develop and maintain process documentation, calendars, checklists, and procedures related to payroll and benefits.
  • Participate in the ongoing improvement and streamlining of HR processes and systems.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned by the Director of Human Resources.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, or a related field preferred.
  • Minimum of 3–5 years of experience in payroll, benefits, human resources, or a related administrative function.
  • Experience administering payroll and employee benefits, preferably in an educational or similarly complex organization.
  • Experience with an HRIS/payroll system; experience with Paycom or comparable platforms preferred.
  • Strong understanding of payroll practices and employee benefits administration.
  • Working knowledge of applicable federal and state payroll, benefits, and employment requirements.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple deadlines.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong interpersonal and customer-service skills.
  • Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and Google.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with colleagues, school leadership, and external partners.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

We are committed to transparency and supporting our employees' well-being. For this role, we offer a competitive hourly range of $32-$34 based on experience and qualifications.

In addition to the annual salary, Gilman School offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision insurance, as well as life insurance, critical illness and accident coverage, and both short- and long-term disability. We offer a 403 (b) retirement plan with an employer match to help you plan for the future.

We also believe in the importance of work-life balance. Eligible employees receive paid vacation, sick leave, and winter and spring breaks as part of Gilman’s standard time‑off package. Vacation and sick leave are prorated based on hire date. At Gilman School, you'll find a supportive environment where your health, wellness, and professional development are valued.

Description

Reginald S. Tickner Writing Fellowship

Gilman School

Baltimore, MD

Gilman School, an independent boys’ school, announces its search to award the 28th Tickner Writing Fellowship to an emerging poet, playwright, or writer of fiction or creative nonfiction. The Tickner Fellowship is a two year position.

Responsibilities include teaching one senior elective in creative writing each semester, organizing a series of readings, advising the literary magazine, and working with the Lower and Middle Schools on select writing projects. The Tickner Fellow teaches every other day, affording time for independent writing projects.

Salary: $45,000 per year, plus full benefits package

To apply: Visit gilman.edu/careers and select the “Current Career Opportunities” icon to submit your CV, a cover letter, and a writing sample of up to 30 pages of published prose, 10 pages of published poetry, or an original play. We also require three confidential letters of recommendation, which should be emailed directly to Kelsey Carper (kcarper@gilman.edu) or sent through a dossier service. Application materials must be received by December 7, 2026 in order to receive consideration.

OUR MISSION

Gilman is a diverse community dedicated to educating boys in mind, body, and spirit through particular emphasis upon academic excellence, athletic participation, and aesthetic appreciation. Gilman seeks to produce men of character and integrity who have the skills and ability to make a positive contribution to the communities in which they live and work.

OUR COMMITMENT

Educating the Whole Boy

For more than a century, Gilman’s mission has remained exceedingly focused: to unlock the greatness within each boy by educating the entire boy—mind, body, and spirit. To accomplish that goal, we provide space and opportunity for crucial learning and self-expression to take place. We believe that boys experience transformative learning when they connect disciplines, people, and ideas in ways that deepen their sense of self and serve the needs of others.

Our rich and comprehensive program, our immeasurably talented and interesting faculty and students, and our belief in the character traits embodied by the Gilman Five—Honor, Integrity, Respect, Humility, and Excellence—combine to form the foundation of an educational environment dedicated to helping boys grow into men of character.

Community, Inclusion, and Equity

Gilman’s commitment to community, inclusion, and equity is founded on the belief that our community is strengthened by the vibrant exchange that occurs when individuals with different backgrounds and heritages share their perspectives with one another. Through the recognition and acceptance of our many differences, we learn to appreciate and respect the complexity of the world in which we live and develop essential skills that help us forge productive relationships with those around us.

We are proud of our history as a school that has, for several generations, taken the lead on matters of diversity, inclusion, and equity. Close to 41% of Gilman’s student body and approximately 22% of the School’s faculty identify as people of color. We continue to build on that legacy through our steadfast commitment to inclusion and equity and initiatives on local, state, and national levels.

OUR SCHOOL

Gilman School is a pre-kindergarten through twelfth-grade private independent day school for boys. Set on a 57-acre campus in the northern part of Baltimore City, Gilman serves roughly 1,000 students in three divisions. The School has a full-time faculty of nearly 140, and the average class size is 16 students.

Please visit gilman.edu/careers to learn more about our school community and to apply for this exciting opportunity.

2027-2028

OUR MISSION

Gilman is a diverse community dedicated to educating boys in mind, body, and spirit through particular emphasis upon academic excellence, athletic participation, and aesthetic appreciation.
