At the American International School of Johannesburg (AISJ), we are committed to providing an exceptional education that empowers global citizens to fulfill their future purpose. We are dedicated to justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion within our school community.

_______________________________________________________________________________________

Position Overview

The Elementary School Counsellor champions the social, emotional, and academic development of students from Pre-Kindergarten through Grade 5. Working collaboratively with educators, families, and school leadership, the Counsellor implements proactive multi-tiered support systems and social-emotional frameworks to foster an inclusive, nurturing, and culturally responsive learning environment. This role ensures that every learner thrives in alignment with the school’s vision and highest international standards of pastoral care.

Qualifications, Experiences, & Role Specific Requirements

Required Educational Qualifications & Certifications

  • Master’s Degree in School Counseling, Educational Psychology, or a closely related field from an accredited institution.
  • Active K–5 (or equivalent) valid state, national, or international school counseling license/certification.

Required Professional Experience

  • A minimum of 5 years of successful experience as an Elementary School Counsellor. Demonstrated experience leading child protection policies, safeguarding training, and child safety initiatives.
  • Proven expertise managing student profiles involving complex social, emotional, and behavioral challenges.
  • Proven ability to analyze psycho-educational assessments, conduct FBAs, and craft individualized BSPs.

Preferred Qualifications & Specialized Experience

  • Previous counseling leadership within an International Baccalaureate (IB) Primary Years Programme (PYP) school or top-tier international/multicultural elementary school environment.
  • Professional proficiency with Adaptive Schools frameworks and collaborative leadership practices.
  • Completion of Category 1 IB PYP workshop or training certification.
  • Experience delivering structured SEL programs, specifically the Second Step curriculum.
  • Track record of designing and facilitating impactful parent education workshops. Active membership and continuous engagement in recognized international counseling organizations and professional learning networks.

Key Responsibilities:

Direct Student Support & Case Management

  • Conduct targeted individual counseling sessions and facilitate small-group programs to support learners' social, emotional, and behavioral development.
  • Co-lead the Student Study Team (SST) process alongside the Director of Student Support Services and Elementary Learning Leader to design, monitor, and refine student intervention plans.
  • Design, conduct, and analyze Functional Behavior Assessments (FBAs) and author actionable Behavior Support Plans (BSPs) for students with complex behavioral needs.
  • Interpret psycho-educational evaluations and academic assessments to guide instructional accommodations and individualized support strategies.
  • Coordinate transition initiatives for learners and families entering or leaving the Elementary division, including the PK onboarding process and the Grade 5 to Grade 6 Middle School articulation.

Curriculum, Safeguarding & SEL Leadership

  • Oversee and deliver the Elementary Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) curriculum across all grade levels.
  • Coordinate and lead Child Protection training, workshops, and personal safety lessons for staff, students, and the broader community.
  • Serve as a divisional resource on student mental health, proactive behavior strategies, and pastoral care, assisting teachers through classroom observations and strategy co-development.

Collaboration, Admissions & Community Outreach

  • Collaborate regularly with the Principal, Director of Student Support Services, Learning Support, and English as an Additional Language (EAL) specialists to provide integrated support.
  • Partner with the Principal and educators to guide student class placements each academic year.
  • Assist the Admissions team through application reviews, candidate observations, and placement recommendations.
  • Facilitate parent education workshops and maintain clear communication channels to support family well-being and student development.

Documentation & Operational Contributions

  • Maintain up-to-date documentation regarding counseling notes, support plans, transition logs, and family communications.
  • Attend and constructively contribute to division, Student Support Services, and full faculty meetings.
  • Participate in break and recess supervision to observe peer interactions and provide real-time social coaching.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Chaperone and support students during the Elementary Classroom Without Walls (CWW) program and off-campus trips.
  • Sponsor or facilitate student service groups and lead/co-lead at least one Co-Curricular Activity (CCA) per academic year.
  • Perform assigned campus supervision duties during break times and recess.
  • Participate in and support school-wide weekend functions, community gatherings, and divisional events as required.

Teacher Competencies

Planning for Learning

  • Curriculum Design: Creates personalized, challenging learning sequences that build on prior knowledge while ensuring knowledge transfer and regular reflection opportunities.
  • Collaborative Planning: Partners across disciplines and specialties to create cohesive learning experiences

that connect global contexts while anticipating student needs.

  • Inquiry-Based Learning: Designs flexible conceptual units that honor student choice, pace, and multiple pathways to demonstrate understanding.

Maximizing Teacher Efficacy

  • Student Agency & Critical Thinking: Creates self-directed learners who think critically, set goals, and drive their own learning journey.
  • Research-Based Instructional Excellence: Implements proven teaching strategies that adapt to individual student needs through continuous assessment and adjustment.
  • Connected Learning Design: Weaves together global perspectives, real-world applications, and cross-disciplinary connections to create meaningful learning experiences.
  • Collaborative Leadership: Builds a learning community where students develop leadership skills through structured collaboration and personalized engagement.

Reflecting as Practitioners

  • Student Agency: Builds student capacity for self-assessment through modeling, tools, and targeted feedback that drives individual growth.
  • Data-Informed Practice: Analyzes student achievement data to align curriculum, refine teaching strategies, and measure instructional effectiveness.
  • Professional Growth: Engages in collaborative reflection and data analysis with colleagues to continuously improve teaching practices and student outcomes.

Promoting Relationships, Community, & Culture

  • Builds strong community-school partnerships and actively participates in community initiatives to enrich the learning environment.
  • Adapts teaching practices by staying informed of educational and societal changes while understanding each learner's unique cultural background, learning style, and needs.
  • Creates an inclusive learning environment that embraces diversity, challenges stereotypes, and connects learning to students' real-world experiences and cultural contexts.
  • Fosters a growth mindset by encouraging calculated risk-taking and developing students' autonomy, personal responsibility, and ownership of learning.

All community members are expected to be committed to the AISJ Community Principles.

job.description:

_______________________________________________________________________________________

Position Overview

This is a full-time position teaching both English and Social Studies in Grades 6–8. Our English program is aligned to the Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts, and our Social Studies program is aligned to the C3 Framework. We are looking for a teacher who is at home in both disciplines and who sees the natural connections between them. The ideal candidate designs concept-based, inquiry-driven units that link literature, writing and the social sciences, so students experience Humanities as a connected whole.

In the classroom, students develop as confident readers, writers, speakers and listeners. They explore history, geography, civics and economics through inquiry, and learn to build evidence-based arguments from a range of sources. We want students to leave as thoughtful, articulate, globally connected citizens who can debate ideas respectfully and use their voice.

This position also has a strong focus on Debate and Model United Nations (MUN). The successful candidate will lead and grow these programs in the Middle School. That includes coaching students, preparing delegations and debate teams for local and international conferences and competitions, and weaving argument, public speaking and global issues into everyday Humanities learning.

The Middle School operates on an 8-period rotating block schedule, and teachers are assigned to teach 5 of 8 blocks. Each Middle School Teacher is also responsible for an Eagle Forum cohort, which is integral to the Middle School experience as well as participating in our CWW, FLEX and Club programmes.

Qualifications, Skills & Experience

Required Educational Qualifications & Certifications

  • Bachelor's degree or higher in English, History, Social Studies, Political Science, Geography or a related field (Master's preferred)
  • Teaching license or certification for Secondary English and/or Social Studies, with the ability to teach both

  • Experience in an IB MYP school, including unit planning with MYP key and related concepts, global contexts, statements of inquiry and criterion-based assessment

  • Concept-based curriculum design and inquiry-based learning

  • Teaching reading and writing through workshop approaches, including conferring and feedback
  • Teaching source analysis, research skills and evidence-based argument
  • Leading student-centered discussion, for example Socratic or Harkness methods
  • Designing assessments, including performance tasks and rubrics
  • Understanding of MTSS and differentiating for a wide range of readers and writers, including multilingual learners
  • Knowledge of the CASEL SEL Framework
  • Adaptive Schools training
  • Integrating the ISTE Standards
  • Coaching, club facilitation or service learning (for example, Model UN, debate, student publications)

job.title: Mary McDowell Friends School Lower School Associate Science Teacher (Leave)
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Description

Mary McDowell Friends School (MMFS) invites applications for a full-time Lower School Associate Science Teacher (Leave Replacement) beginning November 2026.

Position Overview

Associate Teachers support the mission of the school by overseeing the safety and well-being of the students in advisory, content area classes, core classrooms, and homeroom classes by monitoring and stimulating educational and social-emotional growth within the framework of the school’s mission by collaborating with the teaching partner to implement a curriculum that meets the needs of the MMFS student.

Associate Teachers work alongside experienced classroom teachers to develop skills in working with individual children and small groups, as well as gaining experience and confidence in building relationships with families and communicating about students’ learning and development in person and through documentation.

Essential Responsibilities and Duties

  • Work in collaboration with their teaching partner to implement parts of the curriculum and gradually assume increased responsibilities.
  • Act as the advocate for homeroom students, supporting each student in their relationships with other teachers and working with the cooperating homeroom teacher to be the primary point person with parents.
  • Supervise homeroom students when participating in division-wide and school-wide activities such as silence, assembly, and meeting special guests.
  • Implement individualized student plans for homework, organization, and behavior.
  • Participating fully in the life of the school, including professional development, MMFS committee, weekly faculty meetings, regular supervisory meetings, and all school silence and staff meetings.
  • Write, edit, and submit timely trimester reports, grades, recommendations, evaluations, and other requests as needed.
  • Duties based on assigned schedules include supervising a study hall, arrival/lunch/dismissal duty, student trips (including overnight trips), and student clubs.
  • Leading a reading and math group independently.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Diversity and Equity Commitments

  • Understand and participate in all school-wide diversity and equity initiatives.
  • Examine administrative practice through the lens of race, identity, equity, and privilege.
  • Provide an equitable framework for leadership decisions.
  • Support a school culture that allows for social identities to feel welcome.

Supervisory Responsibility

This position has no supervisory responsibilities.

Position Type/Expected Hours of Work

This is a full-time, exempt ten-month position that follows the academic calendar. Days and hours of work are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. with a half-hour paid lunch; faculty meetings occur every Wednesday from 3:30 p.m. to 5 p.m. Evening and weekend work may be required as job duties demand and will be scheduled in advance.

Travel

On occasion, travel between campuses is necessary for meetings, which are scheduled with advance notice and are within walking distance from each other. School trips are also scheduled with advance notice, and teachers are required to chaperone day-long and overnight school trips.

Work Environment & Physical Demands

This position requires the ability to maintain the physical capacity required to navigate the school environment and to ensure the safety of the students. The ability to open filing cabinets and bend or stand for long periods of time, as necessary. This position occasionally ascends/descends stairs to reach different rooms in the building (one to five flights).

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Requirements

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • BA in Science; special education experience a plus.
  • Ability to work cooperatively and collaboratively with all levels of employees, management, and external agencies to maximize performance and problem-solving, and to achieve results.
  • Willingness to learn and adapt to a new environment is required.
  • Familiarity with new technologies; GSuite and Veracross a plus
  • Commitment to equity and justice, including knowledge and skills related to cultural competency, are desired.

Application

To apply, please upload a letter of interest, resume, and contact information for three professional references as a .pdf (preferable) or Word document. If your background and experience are appropriate for the position, you will be contacted directly by a member of our search committee.

We offer a rewarding work experience in downtown Brooklyn, NY, where we encourage employees to bring their whole selves to work. We recognize, appreciate, celebrate, and honor our diverse community as we build an awareness of who each individual is and who we are collectively.

Applicants who enhance the diversity of the school's faculty and administration are strongly encouraged to apply. Please visit our website for more information on our school and a full list of vacancies.

In compliance with NYC’s Pay Transparency Act, this position's annual base salary range is $50,000 - $59,000. Mary McDowell Friends School considers factors such as (but not limited to) the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate’s work experience, education/training, essential skills, internal peer equity, and market and organizational considerations when extending an offer.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Employment at Mary McDowell Friends School is based solely on qualifications and competence for a particular position, without regard to race, color, ethnic origin, nationality, age, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, disability, familial status, or any other category protected by the law. Mary McDowell Friends School’s policy of non-discrimination extends to all employment practices, including but not limited to hiring, transfer, promotion, training, compensation, benefits, layoffs, and termination.

job.title: Friends Seminary Communications Operations Manager
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Friends Seminary educates students from kindergarten through twelfth grade, adhering to the values of the Religious Society of Friends. We strive to build a diverse school where students exercise their curiosity and imagination as they develop as scholars, artists and athletes. In a community that cultivates the practices of keen observation, unhurried reflection, critical thinking, and coherent expression, we listen for the single voice as we seek unity. The disciplines of silence, study, and service provide the matrix for growth: silence opens us to change; study helps us to know the world; service challenges us to put our values into practice. At Friends Seminary, education is rooted in the Quaker belief in the Inner Light – that of God in every person. Guided by the testimonies of integrity, peace, equality, and simplicity, we prepare students to engage in the world that is and to help bring about a world that ought to be.

Founded in 1786, Friends Seminary, the oldest continually operating coeducational, independent Quaker school in New York City, seeks applications for a Communications Operations Manager to join our Communications team. The Communications Office at Friends Seminary works to advance the School’s mission and institutional priorities through thoughtful, strategic, and engaging communications with the School community and broader public.

The Communications Operations Manager is a full-time member of the Communications Office, reporting to the Director of Communications and working closely with the Senior Associate Director of Communications and Multimedia Producer. This position serves as the operational center of the department, leading project management and overseeing the systems, calendars, production workflows, and resources that support the team’s work. The ideal candidate is highly organized, proactive, and collaborative with strong writing and digital skills, and practical project-management experience who anticipates needs, enjoys creating order, and can keep multiple projects and priorities moving forward.

Responsibilities

  • Lead and coordinate project management for the Communications Office, maintaining a centralized system for projects, timelines, responsibilities, deliverables, and deadlines.
  • Develop and manage production schedules for major communications projects and publications, coordinating copy, photography, design, approvals, vendors, and other materials from project initiation through completion.
  • Manage communications deliverables associated with major School events, including invitations, programs, signage, email communications, web content, and photography/video coverage, in collaboration with the team members responsible for editorial and creative work.
  • Maintain a request-intake process and weekly status report; track production handoffs for Meetinghouse, Admissions and Advancement materials, and event communications. Flag missing assets, approval delays, and capacity conflicts for team decisions.
  • Oversee and maintain the School’s institutional calendar in Blackbaud and manage the annual calendar planning and reconciliation process.
  • Clerk and coordinate the School’s Calendar & Events Committee and serve as a liaison with New York Quarterly Meeting regarding scheduling and reservation of shared spaces.
  • Maintain the School’s annual communications calendar, working with the Director and Senior Associate Director of Communications to provide visibility into major communications across audiences, offices, and channels.
  • Coordinate day-to-day work with outside graphic design, video, print, and production vendors and contractors, including timelines, assets, proofs, revisions, deliverables, and related expenses.
  • Serve as an operational steward of the Communications Office’s digital systems and platforms, including project management, web, calendar, email, and asset-management systems.
  • Manage routine website maintenance and administration, including page and content updates, basic page creation, links, and other ongoing CMS needs.
  • Maintain constituent distribution lists and email templates across the School’s communications platforms.
  • Organize and maintain the Communications Office’s digital assets and archives, including logos, templates, photography, video, publications, and project files.
  • Support the Multimedia Producer by organizing incoming and selected photo/video files, recording available dates and subject information, locating assets for colleagues, and preserving approved exports alongside source files. Follow School procedures for access and image-use permissions.
  • Document recurring departmental workflows and processes to support consistency, efficiency, and continuity.
  • Administer routine departmental financial and operational processes, including expense reconciliation, invoices, vendor and contractor expenses, expenditure tracking, and office purchases.
  • Provide communications support as needed, including basic graphic design, social media posting, writing and editing, photography, and assistance with video production.
  • Collaborate with Communications colleagues and partners across the School to anticipate needs, coordinate projects, and support institutional priorities.
  • Participate in occasional evening and weekend work in support of School events and communications needs.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree and related professional experience.
  • Four or more years of relevant professional experience in communications, project management, creative operations, or a related field, or equivalent demonstrated experience.
  • Demonstrated project-management experience and exceptional organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines, stakeholders, and priorities simultaneously.
  • A proactive approach to work, with the ability to anticipate needs, identify potential challenges, and move projects forward with limited direction.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and the confidence and diplomacy to establish timelines, follow up with colleagues, and hold collaborators accountable for deliverables.
  • Excellent writing, editing, proofreading, and verbal communication skills; ability to apply School style, and prepare accurate community-facing communications.
  • Strong digital skills, including shared-drive organization, document and spreadsheet tools, calendars, and reliable use of communications platforms; ability to learn and manage school-specific systems and document repeatable processes.
  • Solid working knowledge of Trello, Asana, or a comparable project-management tool, including setting up workflows, assigning owners, tracking milestones and dependencies, and maintaining clear status reports.
  • Familiarity with website content-management systems and email communications platforms.
  • Experience organizing shared drives, digital assets, or publication archives, including folder structures, naming conventions, version control, and searchable records. Experience planning a phased organization project is preferred.
  • Working knowledge of Canva or a comparable design tool; ability to adapt approved templates, prepare routine materials, and follow brand standards. Advanced design or layout experience is a plus.
  • Photography and basic photo-editing skills are a plus, not required. Willingness to support campus coverage logistics and learn routine asset-handling procedures is required.
  • Video recording or editing experience is a plus, not required. The role supports multimedia logistics and may assist with routine capture after training, according to demonstrated skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively and flexibly in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
  • Sound judgment and discretion when working with sensitive or confidential information.
  • Experience in an independent school, educational institution, nonprofit organization, or other mission-driven environment is preferred but not required. Relevant transferable experience is welcome.

Compensation

The salary range for this position is $85,000–$120,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

Benefits

Friends Seminary offers excellent benefits including paid time off, health, dental, vision, 403(b) with a School-paid match; wide-ranging opportunities for professional development, including tuition support and summer grants; and a talented and dedicated team of teaching colleagues and supportive administrators. Successful candidates will join a dynamic and forward-thinking teaching community of over 150 educators.

To apply, please submit the following:

  1. CompletedFriends Seminary employment application
  2. Cover letter
  3. Resume
  4. Writing sample
  5. Contact information for three personal references

When submitting your materials, kindly be sure to reference your first and last name, the position for which you are applying, and where you heard about the position in the subject line. i.e. [last name], [first name] - Communications Operations Manager - Friends Seminary website. You will receive a confirmation email when you submit your application. No phone calls, please.

Submit all materials to: communicationsjobs@friendsseminary.org

Friends Seminary actively promotes diversity, equity, inclusion, and anti-racism in all its programs and operations, including admissions, financial aid, hiring, and all facets of the educational experience. To form a community which strives to reflect the world’s diversity, we do not discriminate on the basis of race or color, religion, nationality, ethnicity, economic background, physical ability, sex, gender identity or expression, or sexual orientation. Friends Seminary is an equal opportunity employer. Candidates of color and members of other underrepresented groups are strongly encouraged to apply. We urge all applicants to identify and express their individuality and the ways in which they might enrich and diversify the School community.

Moreover, all successful applicants, whether for a faculty or administrative staff post, must demonstrate an ongoing commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and anti-racism in their professional lives. Applicants for a faculty position should highlight ways their curriculum, pedagogy, and classroom culture may advance these goals. Applicants for an administrative staff position should highlight ways they seek to promote these goals in their office work, programming, or operational endeavors.

job.title: American International School of Johannesburg Elementary School Visual Arts Teac
job.description:
Position Description

CAMPUS: Johannesburg Campus | SUPERVISOR: ES Principal | START DATE: 1 August 2027 |

POSTING DATE: 05 October 2026| CLOSING DATE: 28 October 2026

Inspire Learning to Build Our Better World. At the American International School of Johannesburg (AISJ), we are committed to providing an exceptional education that empowers global citizens to fulfill their future purpose. Our vision is to inspire learning to build a better world. We seek a dedicated and passionate professional who aligns with our commitment to excellence and believes in the transformative power of education. Every team member is crucial in creating a supportive and nurturing learning environment. At AISJ, we value every employee as a learner and expect them to embody and support the AISJ Portrait of Learner (Resilience, Mindful, Thinker, Globally Connected, Curious, Contributor) through their work. We are dedicated to justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion within our school community.

_______________________________________________________________________________________

Position Overview

The Elementary School Visual Arts Teacher inspires creative expression, visual literacy, and socio-emotional growth across Pre-Kindergarten through Grade 5 in alignment with AISJ’s Vision to inspire learning and build a better world. Grounded in the IB Primary Years Programme (PYP) framework, the Visual Arts Teacher designs and delivers a dynamic, transdisciplinary arts curriculum that fosters student agency, conceptual inquiry, and artistic appreciation. Through studio-thinking models and play-based, inquiry-led experiences, this role nurtures each child's unique social, emotional, and learning profile within an inclusive, culturally responsive environment. Partnering collaboratively with grade-level and specialist teams, the Visual Arts Teacher leads divisional art celebrations, integrates visual arts across content areas, and empowers learners with the academic and dispositional competencies needed to thrive as global citizens.

Qualifications & Experience:

Required Educational Qualifications & Certification

  • Bachelor’s degree in Education, Fine Arts, Art Education, or a related field (Master’s degree preferred).
  • Valid teaching license or certification in K–5 Visual Arts or Elementary Education from an accredited body.

Required Professional Experience

  • Minimum of 3 years of full-time, successful Visual Arts teaching experience in an elementary school setting.
  • Demonstrated experience designing, delivering, and assessing art curricula aligned with the National Core Arts Standards (NCAS).
  • Demonstrated expertise in concept-driven inquiry, studio practices, and age-appropriate visual arts techniques.
  • Proven track record of planning and executing student art exhibitions, community showcases, and collaborative arts events.

Preferred Qualifications & Specialized Experience

  • Experience teaching within a multicultural, top-tier international elementary school with IB Primary Years Programme (PYP) training (Category 1 or 2 preferred).
  • Qualification or experience in Responsive Classroom practices and positive behavior support environments.
  • Professional familiarity with Adaptive Schools frameworks and the Seven Norms of Collaborative Work.Key Responsibilities:

Curriculum, Studio Instruction & Inquiry

  • Design and implement a rigorous, concept-driven Visual Arts curriculum grounded in the IB PYP framework, emphasizing inquiry, play, and conceptual transfer.
  • Create physical, temporal, and social learning spaces that honor diverse cultures, foster student agency, and support the socio-emotional well-being of every child.
  • Manage art studio resources, specialized equipment, digital media, and learning environments efficiently to support active, hands-on studio learning.

Assessment, Exhibition & Community Engagement

  • Systematically analyze, document, and share student learning and artistic growth through portfolios, rubrics, and developmental frameworks.
  • Lead, coordinate, and organize the annual Elementary Artsfest celebrations and ongoing divisional art exhibitions.
  • Collaborate with the creative arts team to support visual elements for community showcases, school gatherings, and the Elementary School Production.

Collaboration & Transdisciplinary Integration

  • Collaborate effectively with grade-level and specialist teams to integrate visual arts seamlessly into transdisciplinary units of inquiry.
  • Strictly adhere to the Seven Norms of Collaborative Work when co-planning, analyzing student work, and designing differentiated art experiences.
  • Take an active, collaborative role in the ongoing review, revision, and vertical alignment of the AISJ Visual Arts curriculum.

Professional & Operational Contributions

  • Model academic and dispositional competencies, upholding the AISJ Portrait of a Learner to equip students as successful global citizens.
  • Engage in continuous professional learning, reflective practice, peer observations, and professional coaching cycles to enhance pedagogical practice.
  • Develop positive, supportive relationships with families, colleagues, and the broader AISJ community to advocate for arts learning and well-being.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Chaperone and support students during the Elementary Classroom Without Walls (CWW) program and off-campus trips.
  • Sponsor or facilitate student service groups and lead/co-lead at least one Co-Curricular Activity (CCA) per academic year.
  • Perform assigned campus supervision duties during break times and recess.
  • Participate in and support school-wide weekend functions, community gatherings, and divisional events as required.

Teacher Competencies

Planning for Learning

  • Curriculum Design: Creates personalized, challenging learning sequences that build on prior knowledge while ensuring knowledge transfer and regular reflection opportunities.
  • Collaborative Planning: Partners across disciplines and specialties to create cohesive learning experiences

that connect global contexts while anticipating student needs.

  • Inquiry-Based Learning: Designs flexible conceptual units that honor student choice, pace, and multiple pathways to demonstrate understanding.

Maximizing Teacher Efficacy

  • Student Agency & Critical Thinking: Creates self-directed learners who think critically, set goals, and drive their own learning journey.
  • Research-Based Instructional Excellence: Implements proven teaching strategies that adapt to individual student needs through continuous assessment and adjustment.
  • Connected Learning Design: Weaves together global perspectives, real-world applications, and cross-disciplinary connections to create meaningful learning experiences.
  • Collaborative Leadership: Builds a learning community where students develop leadership skills through structured collaboration and personalized engagement.

Reflecting as Practitioners

  • Student Agency: Builds student capacity for self-assessment through modeling, tools, and targeted feedback that drives individual growth.
  • Data-Informed Practice: Analyzes student achievement data to align curriculum, refine teaching strategies, and measure instructional effectiveness.
  • Professional Growth: Engages in collaborative reflection and data analysis with colleagues to continuously improve teaching practices and student outcomes.

Promoting Relationships, Community, & Culture

  • Builds strong community-school partnerships and actively participates in community initiatives to enrich the learning environment.
  • Adapts teaching practices by staying informed of educational and societal changes while understanding each learner's unique cultural background, learning style, and needs.
  • Creates an inclusive learning environment that embraces diversity, challenges stereotypes, and connects learning to students' real-world experiences and cultural contexts.
  • Fosters a growth mindset by encouraging calculated risk-taking and developing students' autonomy, personal responsibility, and ownership of learning.

All community members are expected to be committed to the AISJ Community Principles.

  • We are better when we act together.
  • Our differences make us stronger.
  • Every voice counts. Every voice matters.
  • Every team needs individuals. Every individual needs a team.

Work

Number of Work Days: : Monday through Friday - 188 (one hundred and eighty-eight) days per school year.

Work Day: 7:10 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. daily on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday, and from 7:10 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on Wednesday.

Other Duties As Assigned: The Teacher will be expected to perform any work assigned to them that is within their skills and capabilities and to be flexible about changes to this function that may be required from time to time for operational reasons. This includes other duties as assigned by their supervisor from time to time.

APPLICATION PROCESS

To apply, please complete the electronic form [Click here]. Information captured will be securely stored and used for a reference check on the candidate's compatibility. AISJ reserves the right to appoint the strongest candidate before the closing date if required.

SAFEGUARDING & CHILD PROTECTION

AISJ maintains robust child protection policies to ensure a safe, secure, and caring environment for our students. All employees must undergo criminal background checks, attend annual training, and sign a safeguarding agreement.

_______________________________________________________________________________________

Position Overview

This is a full-time position teaching a combination of Middle School Mathematics and Science sections in Grades 6–8.

  • Mathematics: Our program is aligned to the Common Core State Standards for Mathematics. We want a teacher who builds strong conceptual understanding and procedural fluency, and who connects mathematics to real-world problems so students see its purpose. Students learn in a Multi-Tiered System of Supports (MTSS). Math teachers use data to plan targeted intervention and extension, including through our FLEX program.
  • Science: Our program is aligned to the Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS). The teacher designs hands-on, inquiry-driven learning built around the NGSS Science and Engineering Practices, Crosscutting Concepts and Disciplinary Core Ideas. The aim is for students to investigate, reason from evidence and communicate like scientists, while developing a lasting love of discovery.

The Middle School operates on an 8-period rotating block schedule, and teachers are assigned to teach 5 of 8 blocks. Each Middle School Teacher is also responsible for an Eagle Forum cohort, which is integral to the Middle School experience as well as participating in our CWW, FLEX and Club programmes.

  • Inquiry-based learning and concept-based curriculum design
  • Running safe, well-managed laboratory and practical work

job.title: American International School of Johannesburg High School Science Teacher
job.description:
Position Description

Job Description:High School Science (with IBDP Biology and IBDP ESS) Tentative

CAMPUS: Johannesburg Campus | SUPERVISOR: HS Principal | START DATE: 01 August 2027 |

POSTING DATE: 05 October 2026 | CLOSING DATE: 28 October 2026

Inspire Learning to Build Our Better World. At the American International School of Johannesburg (AISJ), we are committed to providing an exceptional education that empowers global citizens to fulfill their future purpose. Our vision is to inspire learning to build a better world. We seek a dedicated and passionate professional who aligns with our commitment to excellence and believes in the transformative power of education. Every team member is crucial in creating a supportive and nurturing learning environment. At AISJ, we value every employee as a learner and expect them to embody and support the AISJ Portrait of Learner (Resilience, Mindful, Thinker, Globally Connected, Curious, Contributor) through their work. Position overview

The successful candidate will create engaging, inclusive, and appropriately challenging learning experiences that foster scientific inquiry, curiosity, and evidence-based thinking. Through hands-on investigation, experimentation, and the exploration of authentic scientific questions, the teacher will support students in developing the knowledge, skills, and confidence to understand and engage with the world around them. As an active member of the High School community, the teacher will build strong relationships with students, collaborate with colleagues, and contribute to a culture of belonging, care, and continuous learning. The High School operates on an eight-period rotating block schedule, with teachers assigned to five teaching blocks and an Eagle Forum (advisory/homeroom), an integral part of our Well-Being Program and commitment to supporting the whole student.

  • Secondary license or certification for teaching Science, with a preference for a master’s degree

  • Minimum of 3 years of full-time, successful experience teaching Science in a high school setting.

  • Successful experiences with advisory (homeroom/Well-/Being) programming

job.description:

At the American International School of Johannesburg (AISJ), we are committed to providing an exceptional education that empowers global citizens to fulfill their future purpose. We seek a dedicated and passionate professional who aligns with our commitment to excellence and believes in the transformative power of education. Every team member is crucial in creating a supportive and nurturing learning environment. At AISJ, we value every employee as a learner and expect them to embody and support the AISJ Portrait of Learner (Resilience, Mindful, Thinker, Globally Connected, Curious, Contributor) through their work. We are dedicated to justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion within our school community.

_______________________________________________________________________________________

Position Overview

The Learning Support Teacher supports the academic, social and emotional needs of students with mild to moderate learning differences at the Johannesburg Middle School. The teacher manages a caseload of students across Grades 6–8, providing Tier 2 and Tier 3 support within our Multi-Tiered System of Supports (MTSS).

The Learning Support Teacher is a key member of the Middle School Student Success Team. They work closely with counselors, general education teachers, administrators and families to identify student needs and plan for them. Working with the K–12 Student Support Services team, they help build inclusive practices across the school and widen opportunities for every learner. The position also at times supports multilingual learners who are acquiring English, using WIDA data to guide instruction.

The Middle School operates on an 8-period rotating block schedule, and teachers teach 5 of the 8 blocks; the Learning Support teacher's schedule typically includes Learning Lab and co-taught classes. Like every Middle School teacher, they also lead an Eagle Forum (advisory) cohort, which is central to the Middle School experience, and take part in our CWW, FLEX and Clubs programs.

  • Implementing MTSS and planning and delivering Tier 2 and Tier 3 interventions
  • Interpreting psycho-educational reports and standardized assessment data, then writing and monitoring Individual Learning Plans (ILPs) with clear, measurable goals
  • Co-teaching and coaching general education teachers in accommodations, scaffolds and strategies for students with learning differences and English learners
  • Applying a Universal Design for Learning Framework to planning with general educators
  • Using WIDA English-language data to inform instruction

  • Knowledge of the CASEL SEL Framework

job.title: Friends School of Baltimore Upper School History Teacher (Interim)
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Salary Range:

$50,000.00 To $70,000.00 Annually

At a Glance:

Job Title: Upper School History teacher (Interim)

Location: Friends School of Baltimore - Baltimore, MD 21210

Reports To: Upper School Principal

Position Type: Full Time, Exempt

Pay rate: $50,000-$70,000

Friends School is a Quaker, co-educational, college preparatory school, Pre-K through Grade 12, in Baltimore City, enrolling 790 students, 44% of whom identify as children of color. We are guided by the Quaker ideals of simplicity, peace, integrity, community, equality, and stewardship. We strive to be a purposefully inclusive community that reflects the racial, ethnic, cultural, socioeconomic, and religious diversity of our city and our region.

Educators at Friends are expected to model and foster the habits of mind we believe are essential to an outstanding education: creativity, curiosity, empathy, reflection, and resilience. We seek educators whose teaching styles and experiences demonstrate:

  • A desire to understand diverse attitudes, beliefs, behaviors, and practices and to incorporate a culturally responsive lens into teaching and learning.
  • A record of successful collaboration with colleagues, families, and students.
  • A commitment to lifelong learning, and ongoing professional development.
  • An ability to infuse technology to enhance student learning.
  • An openness to interdisciplinary teaching.
  • An appreciation for and understanding of the social and emotional development of students.
  • Flexibility, optimism, and a sense of humor.

Context and Philosophy

Friends School of Baltimore has an immediate opening for an Upper School History Teacher. The position requires the successful candidate to be able to teach the following combination of courses in our core sequence: one Early World History (9th Grade) class, one History of the Modern World (10th) class, and two U.S. and the World (11th) classes. Of particular interest are candidates who have experience using technology in their teaching, collaborating with colleagues, teaching in a block schedule, and using a diversity of assessment techniques. All Upper School teachers participate in the full program of an independent school in addition to their classroom responsibilities.

Responsibilities:

  • Teach the core subject area(s) that honors the Quaker values and the Teaching and Learning Paradigm of Friends School.
  • Fulfill responsibility in the co-curricular or extra-curricular life of the school including clubs, coaching, special event planning, field trips, seminars, etc.
  • Attend All-School Professional Days, Department meetings, and Upper School faculty meetings.
  • Collaborate with teachers in their Department, within the division, and cross-divisionally.
  • Provide parents and administrators with written and oral reports that explain in detail how a child is progressing in the various areas of his/her educational experience.
  • Complete timely, detailed, and prescriptive progress reports, grades, and comments at regular intervals during the year for each student they teach.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree and experience preferred
  • Candidates should demonstrate a willingness to understand and incorporate Quaker Principles and Quaker education into their work.

In addition to a commitment to the fundamental ideals of Quaker education, Friends School faculty members are expected to model and foster the habits of mind, which we believe are essential to an outstanding 21st century education: creativity, curiosity, empathy, reflection, and resilience.

Review of resumes will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. Interested candidates should apply with their resume, cover letter, and supporting documents to the link on the School website. A search committee will review candidate information and will contact those candidates with whom they are interested in speaking.

Friends School of Baltimore actively promotes equity, diversity, and inclusion in all programs and operations, including admissions, financial aid, and hiring. To form a community which strives to reflect the world's diversity, we do not discriminate on the basis of race or color, religion, nationality, ethnicity, economic background, physical ability, sex, gender identity or expression, or sexual orientation. Friends School of Baltimore is an equal opportunity employer. Candidates of color and members of other underrepresented groups who might enrich and diversify the school community are strongly encouraged to apply.

Position overview

  • Experience delivering structured SEL programs, specifically the Second Step curriculum.
