job.title: The Hotchkiss School Office Administrator
job.description:
Position Description & Application

The Office Administrator supports the Facilities Department at The Hotchkiss School, ensuring the smooth and efficient operation of the Facilities Office. We are looking for a professional with strong administrative and organizational skills and experience in office operations. Prior experience in facilities is not required.

The Office Administrator provides administrative support to the Director of Facilities and the Facilities Team through a variety of tasks related to office management, scheduling, organization, and communication. The Office Administrator is responsible for the day-to-day operations of the Facilities Office, including coordinating work orders, assigning and prioritizing requests, maintaining records, and supporting compliance and safety processes.

The Office Administrator must be able to communicate effectively via phone, email, and online systems, manage multiple priorities, and ensure that administrative duties are completed accurately and in a timely manner. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, organized, and able to work independently, using sound judgment and problem-solving skills to support the department's operations.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

Provide overall operations management of the facilities office, including but not limited to:

  • Greet all Office guests and execute follow-up communications to deliver a high standard of customer service.
  • Act as liaison for the Facilities Department and build effective working relationships with internal and external customers using professionalism, discretion, and good judgment.
  • Receive all contractor/consultant invoices, review (or ensure proper School representative reviews) for accuracy, and process each for payment through the Business Office.
  • Maintain an environment that is welcoming and inclusive to persons of all backgrounds and roles.
  • Receive, screen, and direct phone calls, take messages, and answer questions.
  • Send out Facilities announcements and communications as needed or directed.
  • Persist in accomplishing objectives with excellent attention to detail.
  • Maintain the Director of Facilities’ calendar.
  • Prepare, coordinate, and organize meetings as required, including room reservations, attendee notifications/confirmations, and distribution of meeting materials when needed.
  • Maintain office supplies and equipment.
  • Maintain the uniform purchase and replacement process.
  • Establish and maintain electronic and hard copy filing systems. Maintains contractor and vendor files that are relevant to the Assistant’s routine contacts.
  • Sort and direct mail.

Efficiently utilize online tools to ensure facilities work assignments are designated to the appropriate person or area, including but not limited to:

  • Manage the online work order system (Brightly) for all community services and trades
  • Prioritize work requests, including emergencies, and distribute them to appropriate personnel or vendors.
  • Professionally communicate when a work request is not a priority, not within the budget, or is not an authorized service provided by facilities.

Manage compliance and risk management under facilities, including but not limited to:

  • Thoroughly and consistently monitor, review, and collect Certificates of Insurance from outside contractors, confirming proper limits against standard protocol, in-force (active) insurance coverage, and identifying questionable situations that may require additional insured clauses. Work collaboratively with the Business Office and the insurance company to support risk management.
  • Work collaboratively with facilities supervisors and vendors to provide annual energy usage reports to outside compliance consultants.
  • Maintain reports on fuel usage and generator testing. Quarterly submission of reports to CTDEEP and other government offices.
  • Prepare and maintain Excel worksheets, forms, tables, reports, questionnaires, and other documentation required to manage and track Environmental Protection Agency and Department of Energy and Environmental Protection Compliance data requirements for electric, oil, propane, fuel, waste, air, water, asbestos, lead, and radon. Provide this data on a demand basis to State Inspectors and community members as it relates to State Regulations and all safe workplace Provide monthly compliance data reports to the school consultants for use by the Chief Financial Officer.
  • Maintain records pertinent to facilities that are required by other local, state, and federal regulatory agencies, including but not limited to the Department of Health, Fire Marshal, Building Official, Conservation Commission, Planning and Zoning, State Elevator Inspector, etc.
  • Provide annual energy usage reports to outside compliance consultants to satisfy NOx compliance, Tier II compliance, Emissions and Heating Equipment Operations compliance.
  • Maintain MSDS sheets and required postings.
  • Create/Maintain Excel spreadsheets for planning and budgeting purposes that capture all building data, including material construction, square footage, room numbers and size, renovations, and replacement costs.

Additional duties as needed and assigned.

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

The Administrator must possess the knowledge and the following skills and abilities to perform the essential functions of the job:

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Two years of college or business school is preferred or any combination of education, training and experience that provides the knowledge, skills and abilities required for this position.
  • Experience in construction, facilities management, asset management, insurance or risk management, or a related field is preferred.
  • Applied computer skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite applications, Google Docs/ Sheets, Gmail, Google Calendar, CMMS Systems, and the ability to learn new software.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in business writing and oral communication using correct spelling and grammar.
  • Proficient and accurate typing skills.
  • Ability to plan, organize, and prioritize work to maintain workflow consistent with the pace of the office and in order to meet schedules and timelines.
  • Must be able to learn, interpret, and apply knowledge of facilities and general school operations.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to communicate with students, staff, parents, and the public using patience and courtesy, and in a manner that reflects positively on the department and the school.
  • Ability to independently, and with minimal instruction, perform all of the duties of the position efficiently and effectively.

PHYSICAL CONDITIONS:

  • Primarily an office environment.
  • Must be able to walk, stand, stoop, and navigate stairs.
  • Repetitive motion (use of computer keyboard); working for extended periods of time at a computer, requiring the ability to focus, comprehend, and process information.
  • Work is primarily indoors, but requires the incumbent to be outdoors when traveling between campus buildings.
  • The work environment described is representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

Compensation & How We Determine Your Pay

Pay Range: $28.00-$33.65 per hour/year

Your starting pay within the posted range is determined by an individualized assessment of your relevant experience, skills, abilities, and internal pay equity.

Your Health and Well-being Benefits

Comprehensive Healthcare: Medical, dental and vision coverage starts the first of the month following your start date.

Financial Future: 403(b) Retirement Plan with up to a 12.5% employer match.

100% Hotchkiss-paid Protection: Basic life insurance, short- and long-term disability plans are fully paid for by Hotchkiss.

Investing in Your Growth:

Tuition Assistance: Full-time staff with one or more years of service can apply for tuition support toward job-related accredited education, advanced degrees and specialized certifications.

Departmental PD Funding: Access to dedicated annual department funds for professional development opportunities such as workshops, conferences, and professional memberships.

Paid Time Off: 10 paid holidays, 1 floating holiday, ~12 PTO days accrued per year, 10 vacation days, plus 5 paid days off to use during school breaks.

Community Life: Work alongside engaged colleagues, share complimentary meals together in the dining hall during your shift, and take advantage of our athletic facilities, golf course, lakefront, trails, Fairfield Farm and vibrant calendar of arts and athletic events.

*The summary above provides an overview of the benefits and perks available at Hotchkiss. Specific health, retirement, and professional development programs are subject to eligibility criteria, waiting periods, application and approval processes and program limits. Full terms are defined in official plan documents and posted policies.

The essential functions and basic skills have been included in this description. It is not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all functions, responsibilities, skills and abilities. Additional functions and requirements may be assigned by supervisors as deemed appropriate. This position description is subject to change at any time.

The Hotchkiss School is an equal opportunity employer committed to basing judgments concerning the employment of individuals upon their qualifications and abilities. The School is firmly committed to equal employment and advancement opportunities for all employees and applicants in all phases of the employment process (including recruitment, hiring, assignment, terms and conditions of employment, compensation, benefits, training, promotion, transfer, discipline and termination).

In accordance with applicable law, the School does not discriminate against any individual based on age, ancestry, color, genetic information, learning disability, marital status, past or present history of mental disability, national origin, physical disability, race, religious creed, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

job.title: The San Francisco School Interim Director of Marketing and Communications
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Overview of Position

The San Francisco School seeks an Interim Director of Marketing and Communications who will advance the School's mission and strategic initiatives. This is an immediate opening with the potential to become permanent. The Interim Director of Marketing and Communications will articulate and communicate the school's identity and unique characteristics to key constituents, enhancing our messaging within the SFS community as well as strengthening our external marketing position. The communications and marketing efforts will ultimately contribute to admissions efforts and revenue growth, and help ensure SFS's position in the San Francisco independent school market. This role reports to the Head of School.

The Interim Director will serve as the school's chief storyteller and brand steward, balancing high-level strategic leadership with hands-on execution.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Advancement Partnership

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to the Head of School and the senior leadership team on communications, branding, and reputation management.
  • Engage as a member of the Advancement team, supporting work within the office.
  • Develop, refine, and manage the school's messaging priorities and written content.
  • Establish annual goals and reporting measures (e.g., readership/engagement on key channels) to evaluate communications and marketing effectiveness and its contribution to enrollment and retention.

Brand Stewardship & Style Standards

  • Maintain and implement the school's Style Guide, using consistent standards across all publications.
  • Apply the school's look and feel to all external materials, ensuring a consistent voice and visual identity across print, digital, and physical communications.
  • Lead institutional storytelling that highlights the school's progressive approach.
  • Collaborate with the School's administrative team, faculty, and staff to develop and execute initiatives, remain current on key issues, and cultivate positive relationships with the school's community members.

Website & Digital Platform Management

  • Manage and monitor the school's webpage and the school's communication platform, ParentSquare.
  • Train and support new and existing staff on communications platforms as necessary.
  • Liaise with outside vendors of web-based programs such as Morweb and Constant Contact.

Core Publications & Editorial Calendar

  • Craft and publish the Tuesday Note Home, an electronic communication sent via ParentSquare, by writing and editing content, coordinating with contributors, and sourcing appropriate photos and images.
  • Produce, in partnership with the office of Advancement, the bi-annual community magazine, The Gaven Street Gazette, which includes the Annual Report.
  • Collaborate to produce all publications and published materials, including Development and Enrollment Management collateral, ensuring visual and editorial consistency.

Photography, Video, & Events Documentation

  • Document, share, and archive campus activities and events.
  • Manage the collection of photographs and videos for the school's website, print publications, and archives.
  • Manage school photo day (MugsyClicks).
  • Create promotional signage for school events.
  • Attend and assist in the execution of major school events.

Social Media & Content Strategy

  • Design the school's social media strategy and maintain the school's social media presence, including but not limited to Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn.
  • Liaise with and guide faculty to highlight happenings in the classrooms through various mediums.
  • Oversee digital marketing efforts including SEO and paid advertising and content marketing to support enrollment and visibility goals.

Public Relations & Media Relations

  • Serve as the primary media contact for the school.
  • Build and maintain relationships with local, regional, and education-focused media outlets.
  • Develop press materials, announcements, and key institutional messaging.
  • Proactively manage the school's public image and external reputation.

Crisis and Strategic Communications

  • Develop and maintain a comprehensive crisis communications plan.
  • Serve as a key advisor to the Head of School and the Board of Trustees during crisis or emergency situations.
  • Ensure timely, accurate, and mission-aligned communication during sensitive situations.
  • Coordinate all communications during urgent events.

Qualifications

The Interim Director of Marketing and Communications will serve as the School's primary writer, editor, photographer, web-based communicator, production coordinator, and graphic designer. (Freelance writers and out-of-house design support may be available on an as-needed basis.) The successful candidate will have a wide cross-section of skills and professional experiences.

  • Bachelor's Degree in Marketing, Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, or related field, advanced degree preferred
  • Independent school/nonprofit experience preferred
  • Ability to communicate effectively with school representatives, parenting adults, students, alumni, and donors
  • Excellent writing and editing skills
  • Attention to detail and outstanding organizational skills
  • Excellent computer skills, including proficiency with Google Suite, Canva and other design platforms, and Microsoft Office applications; and comfort with databases, social media, and emergent technologies
  • Experience with digital photography, graphic design, and video production
  • Sound judgment relating to confidential projects, personnel, school, and student matters
  • Ability to be a self-starter and work independently
  • Ability to multitask, meet deadlines, and manage many different projects and timelines in a fast-paced environment
  • A cooperative team approach with colleagues and a willingness to take on responsibilities beyond those explicitly defined

The San Francisco School is an equal opportunity employer. We continually strive to build an inclusive culture in our diverse community. The San Francisco School encourages applications for employment from all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, marital status, citizenship, disability, and veteran status.

California Compliance Notice: In accordance with California law (Education Code §44939.5, as amended by SB 848), applicants for positions with educational institutions are required to disclose all current and former employment with educational institutions. Any offer of employment will be contingent upon the completion of required employment verifications.

job.title: San Francisco Friends School Interim 5th & 6th Grade Learning Specialist
job.description:
Position Description & Application

The San Francisco Friends School (SFFS), located in the heart of the Mission District in San Francisco, educates K-8 students in the tradition of Quaker learning. By example and commitment, we hope to inspire all connected with our school to work together toward a peaceful and caring society. For further information about San Francisco Friends School’s beginnings, mission, and philosophy, please visit our website at www.sffriendsschool.org.

The school seeks teachers and administrators who resonate with the Friends School mission, which provides an exemplary education in a community dedicated to problem-solving, service to others, simplicity, social justice, and quiet reflection. Our Quaker mission also compels us to create a diverse and inclusive community; we seek a person who will thrive and contribute to such a community, both within and beyond the walls of the school.

Job Summary

The Learning Specialist plays a pivotal role in ensuring that all students, regardless of their learning styles and backgrounds, can access the support and resources they need to succeed. This position calls for an advocate to ensure philosophical and pedagogical alignment, to help teachers design and support students' daily experiences to achieve their potential, and to work directly with students and their families in order to develop the strategies and approaches necessary to access the curriculum.

The 5th & 6th Grade Learning specialist operates at multiple levels within the middle school. They develop learning plans, coordinate student support, and oversee student support across two grade levels. They work directly with families as they navigate educational assessments and understand their student’s needs, and they communicate regularly with families throughout the year. They work directly with students, both individually and in small groups, sometimes within the classroom environment and also during open times throughout the week. The learning specialist also works closely with teachers to ensure that the teachers understand the student learning needs within their classroom and have the tools to support all learners. Additionally, the learning specialist collaborates with the entire SLS team (including another MS specialist), cultivates community connections and coordinates with outside specialists and programs.

Rooted in Quaker values, San Francisco Friends School honors the uniqueness of each student, and the learning specialist position requires someone who is deeply student-centered, mission-aligned, and committed to creating a meaningful and impactful student experience in and out of the classroom for every student. The Learning Specialist is a vocal and steady advocate for current trends in research, learning differences, and the inclusion of all students. They will commit to modeling cultural humility by mining resources, centering interventions that recognize the unique experiences of each child and family, and providing equitable access to resources.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Case manages students with learning profiles for two specific grades; relays relevant information to teachers, regularly communicates with families, and collaborates to support those students in the classroom.
  • Works individually with students and in small groups, both in the classroom and in separate meetings
  • Introduces and facilitates established accommodations for students in the classroom and during testing
  • Works with faculty to understand best practices in student support
  • Provides educational screenings as needed for students; makes referrals for outside evaluations and supports parents and teachers in understanding outside learning evaluations.
  • Coordinates with SLS team and Counseling and Wellness department to assess best support for individual students
  • Meets regularly with other learning specialists, the school counselor, teachers, parents, grade levels (twice weekly), MS Dean of Student Life and Head of Middle School
  • Maintains confidential electronic student learning profiles and intervention lists for students.
  • Supports scheduling and teacher-tutor communication with independent tutors for students in the case load
  • Participates in parent education program and provides community learning resources to parents
  • Attends weekly all-faculty and divisional meetings
  • Reviews quarterly reports for all students who are receiving support
  • Coordinates with outside specialists and programs
  • Supports MAP testing, analyzing and sharing relevant data at the assigned grade level

Qualifications

Required Skills & Experience

  • B.A. and a Teaching Credential (or equivalent)
  • Learning Specialist degree (or equivalent professional credentials) and/or Education Specialist degree required
  • Middle school teaching experience
  • Experience working with language-based learning differences
  • Demonstrated deep knowledge of learning differences, assessment techniques, and resources for supporting a wide range of learners both in and outside the classroom
  • Excellent communication and organizational/case management skills
  • Ability to communicate with teachers about learning differences
  • Ability to work with multiple constituencies with professionalism, empathy, humility, calm, and strategic direction--parents, teachers, students, outside specialists, and the administrative leadership team
  • Excellent interpersonal, communication, and presentation skills, including patience, discretion, clarity, follow-through, a sense of humor, good judgment, and a desire to find the light in each student
  • Personable, flexible, and adaptable; a learner and an expert teachers can count on, who is a motivated and collaborative team player
  • Understanding of the intersection between learning and behavior support and diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging

Preferred Skills & Experience:

  • Specialized knowledge in other areas of academic instruction, innovation, and learning differences-- Brain Frames, multi-sensory-based teaching approaches, gifted education, mathematics, sensory integration, executive function/attention, neurodivergence
  • Experience with public speaking, parent education, and professional development presentations
  • Database management, Google Suite experience

Compensation and Benefit Summary

Competitive, exempt salary based on experience and qualifications. Excellent benefits are offered, including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, and matching 403(b).

$2,916.67 to $6,407.50 semi-monthly pay period for 24 pay periods per year ($70,000 to $153,780 if annualized). Placement on the step scale based on relevant teaching experience.

EEO Commitment

The San Francisco Friends School is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability, age, military or veteran status, marital status or any other category protected by law. The school also makes reasonable accommodations for qualified applicants with disabilities; candidates who need accommodations in order to apply for this position should request an accommodation as part of the submission of interest.

Employment Clearances required

  • SB 848 Authorization and Reference Checking
  • Livescan Background
  • US Employment Eligibility
  • TB Clearance certificate

For more information about San Francisco Friends School or Quaker education, please visit our website at www.sffriendsschool.org or the Friends Council on Education at www.friendscouncil.org.

job.title: The Shipley School Director of Advancement Services
job.description:
Position Description & Application

The Shipley School seeks a fundraising data professional with 2 to 3 years of experience to manage a Raiser's Edge NXT database, prospect research, and stewardship in the Alumni and Development office. The role is a full-time salaried and onsite position with one direct report. Experience with Raiser's Edge NXT is strongly preferred.Working as a member of the Development Office and reporting to the Director of Development, the Director of Advancement Services supports the fundraising work of the Development Office, maintaining close working relationships with constituent-based gift officers, the Development Administrative Coordinator, and the Directors of Data Operations and Finance. The position supervises the Advancement Services Coordinator. The Director is responsible for three major program areas: database management, prospect research and management, and stewardship support for all constituencies.

Key Responsibilities

Database Management & Reporting:

  • Manage the Raiser's Edge CRM database to ensure the integrity and accuracy of information entered in the database and that all protocols have been followed. Authorize and record security permissions.
  • In collaboration with various constituents, oversee the continued evolution or enhancement and implementation of policies, such as gift acceptance, database and gift entry, and gift counting and reporting.
  • Develop and maintain procedures for use of Raiser's Edge database. Train staff on policies and processes, as well as the use of the database. Update and maintain a written procedures manual to ensure data processing and business continuity. Review the procedures manual with the Director of Development on an annual basis.
  • Stay informed of the latest product updates from Blackbaud and other vendors in order to implement new data processing and other procedures as needed to keep systems and processes up to date.
  • Serve as the integration liaison between Raiser's Edge and onCore and work closely with Director of Data Operations to ensure ongoing communication and smooth interface between the two databases. This includes managing ongoing database maintenance and procedures to ensure accuracy, consistency, and integrity.
  • Supervise the Advancement Services Coordinator, ensuring the accurate and timely processing and acknowledgment of gifts, pledges, pledge payments, matching claims, memorial gifts, in honor gifts, and other contributions to Shipley. Monitor the timeliness and efficiency of processing and ensure that all corresponding links in the database are updated and maintained as gifts are processed. Record links may include but will not be limited to spouses and other family members; other alumni and friends; corporations/foundations to employees/owners, etc.
  • Fulfill data requests for the Head of School, the Assistant Head of School for Community Engagement, the Director of Development, the Development Office, and the Communications & Marketing Office by querying and exporting information from Raiser's Edge, as well as produce reports as requested, including monthly gift reports for the Business Office and annual reporting for NAIS.
  • Oversee the generation of donor lists for annual Gratitude Report and ensure their accuracy.
  • Manage summer database changes and coordinate changes with gift officers.

Prospect Research & Management:

  • Identify and conduct ongoing research of major prospects and donors.
  • Write and maintain major prospect and donor profiles.
  • Process Call Reports written by a prospect's Prospect Manager (PM). This includes gathering new information on prospect, updating prospect profile, doing more research if necessary, and filing documentation in Raiser's Edge.
  • Generate and analyze Pipeline reports and Prospect Manager reports. Add alerts on database records of Pipeline prospects.
  • With the Director of Development, perform a periodic review of the Moves Management System and identify and recommend a course of action for improvement.
  • Co-lead monthly Prospect Managers meetings with the Director of Development.

Stewardship:

  • Collaborate with gift officers to devise and execute annual personalized stewardship plans for all donor constituencies. Maintain and ensure adherence to a set schedule and proactively gather examples of philanthropic impact across campus.
  • Manage ongoing stewardship of constituents connected to named endowment funds, coordinating efforts with PMs, where applicable. This includes gathering student scholarship recipient information, student-authored letters to donors, and endowment values, and incorporating the information into donor correspondence.
  • Manage ongoing stewardship of constituents connected to student awards, coordinating efforts with PMs, where applicable. This includes invitations to yearly awards ceremonies and follow-up correspondence with information about award recipients.
  • Collaborate with PMs in devising and implementing stewardship strategies for Centennial Society members and donors connected to restricted operating funds.
  • Maintain gift acknowledgement letter templates.
  • Manage pledge reminder process.
  • Maintain an inventory of donor recognition signage across campus and update annually as necessary. Coordinate signage generation on an ongoing basis.

General Responsibilities

  • Manage in coordination with the Director of Data Operations relationships with vendors, such as providers of database, online giving, and prospect research services. Manage subscriptions and conduct an annual review to determine potential renewals, cancellations, or alternatives.
  • Process all department invoices and check requests. Support reconciliation of budget sections with the Business Office.
  • Manage end of year financial reconciliation with Business Office and auditors.
  • Participate in the development of a Document Retention Policy for the School.
  • Support and staff events run by the Development Office, including but not limited to Secret Gardens and Alumni Weekend, and other events as needed.

Qualifications and Expectations

  • Familiarity with and endorsement of Shipley's mission, culture, and values
  • Personal and professional integrity as well as respect for the confidentiality of colleagues and constituents
  • Self-motivation, flexibility, problem-solving, commitment to innovation, and a proactive approach to managing both professional responsibilities and team members
  • Cooperation, collegiality, and commitment to teamwork
  • Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills
  • Excellent quantity, quality, accuracy, and timeliness of work produced
  • Excellent planning, prioritization, organization, multitasking, efficiency, and follow-through in execution of responsibilities
  • Dependability, punctuality, and attendance at all required and some optional meetings and events
  • Professional appearance and demeanor
  • Commitment to professional development and self-improvement
  • Proficiency in technology use: Raiser's Edge database, Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, and Power Point).
  • Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends

Shipley and Its Commitment to Equity

The Shipley School, founded in 1894, is a co-educational, college preparatory, independent day school currently enrolling over 700 students in grades Pre-K through 12. Located in the western suburbs of Philadelphia, the school is committed to educational excellence and dedicated to developing in each student a love of learning and compassionate participation in the world.

The Shipley School is committed to equal employment opportunities for all individuals. The school will make all employment decisions for employees and applicants without unlawful discrimination as to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship, disability, pregnancy, age, marital status, military or veteran status, gender identity and expression, creed, genetic predisposition, victim of domestic violence or any other basis protected by law

How to apply

Interested candidates should complete the online application.Please note that clearances are not required at the time of application but will be required for employment. No phone calls, please.

job.title: Northfield Mount Hermon Executive Director of Summer Lab and Auxiliary
job.description:
Position Description

Northfield Mount Hermon (NMH), a coeducational boarding and day school for grades 9 to 12, plus a postgraduate year, in western Massachusetts near the borders of New Hampshire and Vermont, seeks an entrepreneurial and creative leader and manager to serve as Executive Director of NMH Summer Lab and Auxiliary Initiatives. The Executive Director will lead the continued evolution and growth of NMH’s summer and auxiliary programs, developing innovative ways to extend the school’s educational mission, introduce new audiences to NMH, make thoughtful use of the school’s extraordinary campus and resources, and generate meaningful revenue in support of the institution.

Located on the banks of the Connecticut River on a 746-acre wooded campus in western Massachusetts, NMH is a coeducational, secular boarding school serving 620 students in grades 9 through 12, plus a postgraduate year, from 50 countries and 30 U.S. states. The school offers an advanced educational experience – the College-Model Academic Program – that empowers students to shape deep learning experiences, follow their passions, and balance rigorous academics with wide-ranging artistic and athletic pursuits. The robust curriculum offers more than 160 courses, including signature programs in environmental studies, the humanities, and social entrepreneurship. NMH’s mission to educate students’ heads, hearts, and hands ensures that they possess the skills, resources, and convictions to serve and lead with humanity and purpose.

Reporting to the Head of School, the Executive Director provides strategic, entrepreneurial, financial, and operational leadership for NMH’s portfolio of summer and auxiliary programs. The role carries responsibility for approximately $1.8 million in annual program activity and for the overall profit and loss associated with these programs. The Executive Director will continually assess the performance of current offerings; identify opportunities for growth, improvement, partnership, and new program development; and ensure that NMH’s programs deliver educational value, an exceptional participant experience, and appropriate financial returns to the school.

The Executive Director will also be a member of the broader NMH community. During the academic year, the position will include limited faculty or community responsibilities, which may include advising, dormitory duty, coaching, teaching, or administrative support as appropriate. This connection to the daily life of the school is important: the strongest summer and auxiliary programs will grow from a deep understanding of NMH, its students, its educational philosophy, and the community and culture that distinguish it.

This is a rare opportunity for a creative and commercially-minded educational leader to build something distinctive at one of the country’s leading boarding schools. NMH is looking for someone who can imagine what is possible, determine what is viable, bring people together around a compelling vision, and then execute with excellence. The successful candidate will combine entrepreneurial energy with sound business judgment, strategic thinking with operational discipline, and ambition with a genuine commitment to NMH’s mission and community.

To see the full job description details, please click here.

Salary and Benefits:

Salary range is $110,000-$125,000 commensurate with experience. NMH offers a generous benefits package as well, including tuition remission and on-campus housing.

How to Apply:

Please e-mail your cover letter, resume, and contact information for three professional references to:

Human Resources

Northfield Mount Hermon

One Lamplighter Way, Mount Hermon, MA 01354

Phone: (413) 498-3229

HR@nmhschool.org

Application Timeline:

Applications will be accepted through 10/28/2026. To ensure full consideration, candidates should submit their application materials by the deadline. The search committee will begin reviewing applications following the close of the application window and will consider candidates based on the materials received by that time. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

job.title: Northfield Mount Hermon Advancement Special Projects Coordinator
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Northfield Mount Hermon (NMH) seeks an Advancement Special Projects Coordinator to support donor stewardship, communications, and strategic initiatives within the Office of Advancement. You are the right person for this job if you enjoy taking a project from an idea to a finished product, bringing people and details together to make things happen, and creating thoughtful experiences for donors and guests. Working directly with the Director of Donor Relations and Advancement Special Projects, you’ll be part of a collaborative team with the opportunity to contribute to a variety of projects and see your work make an impact. You’ll find satisfaction in knowing that the work you coordinate helps strengthen the relationships that support NMH’s mission and the students we serve.

Why NMH

  • Comprehensive insurances, including medical, dental, vision, life, and disability
  • A robust 11% 403(b) contribution (with a 3% employee contribution)
  • Generous paid time off, including three weeks of annual paid vacation
  • Tired of packing lunch? Enjoy meals in our dining hall while on duty and save an average of $2,700 a year.
  • Tuition remission for dependent children of high school age who meet the acceptance requirements of the school

About NMH

Northfield Mount Hermon, an independent boarding and day school located in the beautiful Connecticut River Valley of Massachusetts, was founded on the principles of inclusivity and community — values that have been central to the school’s mission since 1879. NMH engages the intellect, compassion, and talents of its students, empowering them to act with humanity and purpose.

A Day in the Life

The Advancement Special Projects Coordinator helps bring donor stewardship and advancement initiatives to life through project coordination, cross-functional collaboration, communications, and event support. This is a dynamic role for someone who enjoys managing details while working across teams to move meaningful projects forward. A typical day may include coordinating timelines and deliverables for priority projects, preparing stewardship materials, gathering information to support strategic initiatives, and working with colleagues across departments, external vendors, and partners. The Coordinator also supports donor recognition, stewardship, and cultivation events through tasks such as managing guest lists and RSVPs, coordinating vendors and materials, and assisting with on-site setup. The successful candidate will be highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable balancing multiple priorities while collaborating with a range of internal and external partners.

Required Skills and Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; Associate’s degree preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and professional experience.
  • Administrative, project management, or communications experience.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and a high degree of accuracy.
  • Strong writing, editing, and proofreading skills, with excellent command of grammar.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple tasks, prioritize deadlines, and stay organized in a dynamic environment.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills, sound judgment, and the ability to handle confidential donor information with discretion and professionalism while working collaboratively across departments
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and Google Workspace applications. Experience with database software preferred.
  • Ability and willingness to learn new software and use technology to support donor relations, communications, and event coordination.
  • Reliable transportation, this is a fully on-site position in Gill, MA.

Schedule

This is a full-time, 37.5-hour-per-week position. Occasional evening or weekend work may be required to support donor events and other Advancement initiatives.

Application Timeline

Applications will be accepted through 10/25/2026. To ensure full consideration, candidates should submit their application materials by the deadline. The search committee will begin reviewing applications following the close of the application window and will consider candidates based on the materials received by that time. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

Northfield Mount Hermon School is an Equal Opportunity Employer

job.title: Prep for Prep Director of the PREP 9 Preparatory Component
job.description:
Position Description

Organization Summary: Prep for Prep is a premier educational and leadership development program that develops ethical and effective leaders who reflect our society. Prep is approaching its 50th anniversary and setting a bold vision for its future. Prep identifies New York City’s most promising students, prepares them to excel at the nation’s top independent schools, and supports their academic, professional, and personal growth through middle school, high school, college graduation, and beyond.

Learn more at prepforprep.org.

Position Summary: The Director of the PREP 9 Preparatory Component reports to the Director of Academic Programs.

Tasks as Director of the PREP 9 Preparatory Component:

Note: It is understood that some of these tasks (as determined by the Director) will be delegated by the Director to the Dean of Students, and that it will remain the responsibility of the Director to supervise the Dean of Students in the carrying out of such tasks.

  • Talent Search: when asked, interview candidates for admission to PREP 9 and consult on select Admissions Folders.
  • Preparatory Component: in conjunction with the Director of Academic Programs, developing the curriculum; hiring and supervising faculty and staff, with hiring subject to the final approval of the Director of Academic Programs; working with the counseling staff for the Preparatory Component; creating, enforcing, and evaluating rules, regulations, and academic policies, and determining the status of each student in the program; scheduling classes and assigning students to specific courses and sections; assigning tutorials for students, when necessary, and submitting annual reports to the Director of Academic Programs regarding the overall status of the PREP 9 Preparatory Component, especially noting the current numbers of enrolled students. Lead, attend, and stay on campus for the two-week PREP 9 boarding school immersion-in-residence program.
  • Placement: Oversee the entire PREP 9 placement process, including school presentations, school visits, and selecting the schools to which students will apply. Guide students and parents through the selection and application process, ensuring the quality and integrity of each boarding school application, and aim to place all students first in boarding schools in the PREP 9 Consortium and second in other boarding schools. Supervise the Dean of Students in managing the financial aid process and coordinate with the Director of Academic Programs throughout the process, updating and discussing placement strategy. Travel for in-person visits to Prep’s Consortium and affiliated schools to cultivate and maintain PREP 9’s placement relationships is required.
  • School Relations: Maintain communication and strong relationships with sending schools; the Consortium Operations Committee and boarding schools; parents of PREP 9 students; and the schools whose facilities we require.
  • Participate in all Prep for Prep staff meetings as determined by the Director of Academic Programs.
  • The following positions report to the Director of the PREP 9 Preparatory Component: the Dean of Students, the PREP 9 Faculty, Advisors, and the Administrative Assistant for the PREP 9 Preparatory Component.
  • Review all communication sent to families, faculty, and schools, or designate someone to ensure all materials are accurate, up to date, and reflect Prep for Prep in a positive light.
  • Manage semi-monthly payroll for faculty, advisors, and the Clinical Social Worker, ensuring accuracy and timely submission.

Qualifications:

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree in education, social work, or psychology preferred.
  • 3+ years of education leadership experience, with a demonstrable track record of managing high-performing teams.
  • Exceptional interpersonal and written communication skills, with the ability to inspire and engage diverse audiences.

Preferred

  • Familiarity with the New England and Mid-Atlantic independent boarding school landscape.
  • Experience with Salesforce or a comparable student information system.
  • Valid driver’s license and travel to various schools for visits as needed.

Working Conditions:

This is a hybrid position, with three days in the office and two days remote. However, depending on the department’s needs, this role may be required to work in-person more than three days per week. Evening or weekend work may be required around student events, school cultivation activities, and major organizational events. During summer classes, this position is required to be in-person five days a week.

All employees of the organization should see their roles as: one, contributing to achieving this goal in the highest possible quality, and two, working in conjunction with all other members of the staff. In light of this, the tasks listed above serve as a general framework for this position's responsibilities. Flexibility and continued quality improvement are necessary for this institution and require individuals not to perceive any job description as fixed.

Compensation Range: $120K to 130K

To apply, interested candidates should send their resume and cover letter, with the subject line “Director of PREP 9,” to personnel@prepforprep.org, nsmith@prepforprep.org, and jcollins@prepforprep.org.

job.title: Prep for Prep Executive Assistant to Chief Executive Officer
job.description:
School Career Site

Organization Summary:

Prep for Prep is a premier educational and leadership development program that develops ethical and effective leaders who reflect our society. Prep is approaching its 50th anniversary and setting a bold vision for its future. Prep identifies New York City’s most promising students, prepares them to excel at the nation’s top independent schools, and supports their academic, professional, and personal growth through middle school, high school, college graduation, and beyond.

The Executive Assistant to the CEO is a skilled professional who provides high-level administrative support to the CEO and the Executive Office. Key responsibilities include scheduling support, limited event planning, managing special projects, and contributing to the executive office's overall efficiency and success. The ideal candidate is proactive and detail-oriented, able to manage complex tasks and work at a brisk pace while maintaining a high level of professionalism, collaboration, and confidentiality. Additionally, the candidate must have an appreciation for how their work contributes to the strategic goals of the organization.

Responsibilities for this role include, but are not limited to, these primary areas:

CEO Administrative Support

  • Oversee the CEO’s calendar by prioritizing appointments, meetings, and engagements aligned with Prep’s broader organizational priorities, and ensure the CEO has the necessary materials for meetings and events.
  • Anticipate, manage, and facilitate CEO meetings. This includes but is not limited to creating agendas, preparing briefing documents, providing technical support, and ensuring documents are ready.
  • Manage incoming requests for CEO involvement, engagement, or activities to prioritize and recommend appropriate responses and actions.
  • Arrange and coordinate travel, including but not limited to flights, hotel accommodations, and itineraries, ensuring all arrangements are seamless and aligned with the executive’s schedule and preferences
  • Record Keeping - Ensure that appropriate files are maintained, updated, and organized.
  • Oversee clerical and technology support for preparing mailings and mass communications.

Liaison between the Executive Staff and the Chief Executive

  • Coordinate regular meetings with Executive Staff members.
  • Assist the Executive Director, Chief Operating Officer, and Director of Advancement with tasks related to the CEO.
  • Collaborate across departments to coordinate and plan special events for Staff, Board members, Alumni, and school partners.

Skills, Experience, and Competencies

  • Bachelor’s degree is preferred.
  • 2+ years of proven experience in a complex administrative or fundraising role, preferably supporting senior leadership in a nonprofit or corporate setting.
  • Knowledge of New York City independent schools, elite colleges, and the business community is a plus.
  • Strong background in supporting leadership teams with project management, process improvement, and strategic execution is a plus.
  • Exceptional organization, meticulous attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously and meet deadlines.
  • Proficiency and comfort with technology and software platforms, including the Microsoft Suite, Salesforce, Google Suite, social networking sites, Mailchimp, and other project management tools.
  • Ability to work independently, take initiative, and maintain a high level of confidentiality and professionalism.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with an ability to create clear, concise, and professional documents and presentations.
  • Works well with a range of leadership, from board chairs and members to senior executives and managers.
  • Passion for the education, professional advancement, and leadership development work of the organization.

All employees should see their roles as contributing to Prep for Prep's mission with the highest possible quality and working in conjunction with all other staff members. With this in mind, we designed the tasks above as a general framework for this position's responsibilities. Flexibility and continued quality improvement are necessary for this institution and require that individuals not perceive any job description as fixed.

This is a hybrid, full-time position that requires the employee to be in the office at least three days each week and, as needed, based on the needs of the CEO and/or the organization. The role also requires some evening and infrequent weekend work.

Salary Range: $66,500 - $70,000

How to Apply: Please email a cover letter and resume with the subject line “Executive Assistant to Chief Executive Officer” to personnel@prepforprep.org

job.title: Children's Day School Third Grade Teacher - Temporary Long Term Sub
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Time Frame: January - April 2027.

At Children’s Day School, what you learn and who you become are equally important.

Children’s Day School (CDS) is a welcoming community in the big city, a farm and garden among urban streets, an advocate for change and uplifting progressive values, an independent school with down-to-earth values, and an institution that is always asking how we can do this better.

We strive for balance so students become both academically successful and grounded. They leave CDS confident, with the humility to listen and the resolve to speak up for what they see as right.

CDS is a co-educational preschool through eighth grade school serving over 450 students in the Mission Dolores neighborhood of San Francisco with two campuses, two sheep, and lovely people.

To learn more about CDS, visit our website at www.cds-sf.org.

Job Summary

Lower School Teachers at CDS work as a co-teacher in their classroom. In this partnership, teachers work together to implement curriculum and best support the needs of the learners in the class. Lower School Teachers also work as part of a grade level team to ensure the continuous development of grade-level curriculum in alignment with the school’s mission and core learning beliefs. Lower School Teachers root their practice in inquiry at CDS. Students will develop agency over their own learning and teachers will help to facilitate the integration of topics and concepts throughout the curriculum to best develop skills as competent learners through the years.

Our Lower School Teachers engage in rigorous discussion and developments that align to the initiatives and goals of the school and division. They bring a critical lens to discussions and are collaborative and solutions-orientated. Our Lower School Teachers are proactive in their approach to learners, families, and team dynamics. Collaboration is key in our co-teaching model so robust communication skills, curiosity, and a dedication to building a productive team are essential.

Primary Responsibilities

Essential Practices of a CDS Educator

CDS Educators have identified and aligned on these five essential teaching practices to guide instruction and learning in the classroom. Applications should excel in using these practices and be able to apply them to curriculum and unit design across all content areas they are responsible for.

Classroom Leader and Curriculum Thought Partner

  • Co-Lead the development and implementation of grade-level curriculum so that it is both accessible to a diverse population of students and meets the intended learning goals of the division.
  • Provide a hands-on, inquiry-based learning with an integrated approach to creatively embed concepts and themes into the curriculum.
  • Work alongside a partner teacher, and grade-level teaching team, to plan and develop curriculum and learning opportunities for students. This can occur through frequent and open communication as well as planned weekly collaboration meetings.
  • Manage collaborative learning groups and demonstrate effective and proactive differentiation strategies to meet the needs of a diverse learning population.
  • Provides coaching and feedback to a diverse population of students with conferences and with individualized support for learners.
  • Nurture a culture of social justice, inclusion, and action in the classroom through the curriculum, conversations, and community-based learning.
  • Develop and implement formative and summative learning assessments and approaches that will consistently and continuously provide a basis for giving students feedback and reporting student progress.
  • Design purposeful assessments and performance tasks to best understand student learning track progress and student’s development of competencies and share learning goals throughout projects.
  • Keep track of assessment data and critically analyze data collected to understand student learning, and be able to adapt instructional practice using assessment data collected throughout the school year.
  • Facilitate the social, emotional, and academic growth of students.
  • Demonstrate and model cultural competence; proactively address mistakes and misunderstandings with curiosity and a learner stance; continue ongoing learning about how racism, stereotypes, and bias continue to shape children's lives and experiences.
  • Co-lead and provide parent education opportunities, including Back to School Night, weekly classroom blogs, family conferences, and learning celebrations.
  • Manage the day to day operations of the classroom and keep curriculum documentation up to date.
  • Ensure timely communication with parents/guardians through calls, emails, classroom blogs, and conferences.
  • Pursue professional development that is aligned with professional goals and school wide initiatives to model and practice continued learning.

Division Wide Collaboration

  • Partner with the Lower School Division Head, Grade Level Team, Learning Specialists and Counselors to advocate for student learning and well being.
  • Partner with the Lower School Division Head, Director of Curriculum and Innovation, Team Leads and other leaders on campus to set goals, respond to feedback, and focus on professional growth and development.
  • Attend weekly division meetings, grade level team meetings, and as needed meetings with families to update or check in on student progress and development.
  • Support the division with lunch duties, recess coverage, and various other division wide student supervision needs.
  • Build strong collaborative partnerships with specialist teachers to integrate curriculum and support student learning inside and outside of the classroom.

Whole School - CDS Team

  • Engage actively in the CDS professional learning community by forwarding schoolwide initiatives and strategic priorities.
  • Partner with admissions and advancement as needed to promote the CDS program and mission.
  • Find opportunities to lead and contribute by joining committees, leading affinity groups, and collaborating with colleagues to sustain our commitment to innovation and ongoing learning

Position Requirements

  • BS/BA (required)
  • Demonstrated successful experience with inquiry-based models of elementary teaching.
  • Demonstrated experience with curriculum development and/or oversight.
  • Acumen in 21st-century learning skills and issues of diversity, equity, and inclusion.
  • Demonstrated knowledge, skills and habits within whole child learning practices - a focus on core academics and SEL development.
  • Strong communication skills and solutions-oriented mindset.
  • Proficiency in use of technology, google suite and managing multiple platforms for the purpose of organization and curriculum implementation.

Schedule

  • January - April 2027
  • Hours: Monday - Friday from 7:45 am-3:45pm.
  • Division Meetings take place on Wednesdays from 3:45 pm - 5:00 pm.

Compensation

Pro-rated salary up $24,220 - $53,162 for 4 months of employment. Salary is based on qualifications, teaching experience, and the number of weeks worked. School holidays will be paid days off. Temporary/Non-benefited position.

CDS is an equal opportunity employer. Our community is diverse in many ways, inclusive of race/ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender spectrum, age, ability, and more. We welcome and value the same in our faculty and staff.

Clearance Requirements

job.title: The Dalton School High School Psychologist Leave Replacement
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Salary Range: $63,000 - $77,000. Placement in the range is commensurate with experience.

Exemption Status: Exempt

The Dalton School, a progressive K-12 gender-inclusive school in Manhattan’s Upper East Side, is consistently recognized as one of the preeminent independent day schools in the nation. Known for its child-centered approach and an exceptional, inspiring faculty, Dalton enrolls over 1,300 students with approximately 350 faculty and staff. Guided by the Dalton Plan, the foundation of a Dalton education, our faculty meets each student’s evolving needs, interests, and abilities. Dalton challenges each student to develop intellectual independence, creativity, curiosity, and a sense of responsibility toward others both within the School and in the broader community.

Dalton seeks a full-time High School Psychologist (Psy.D., Ph.D.) or Master Level Clinician, LCSW, LPC or Ed.D. for a leave replacement from November 2026 through June 2027. The psychologist/counselor will provide clinical counseling and consultation to support the mental health, emotional well-being, and healthy development of high school students. This is a full-time, in-person position reporting to the Director of Health & Wellness.

Responsibilities

Clinical Counseling & Student Support:

  • Provide short-term individual counseling to high school students presenting with a range of social, emotional, behavioral, and mental health concerns.
  • Conduct clinical and risk assessments; respond to mental health crises and develop safety plans when clinically indicated.
  • Develop and implement appropriate short-term interventions and coping strategies.
  • Support students navigating anxiety, depression, stress, relationships, identity development, family concerns, substance use, grief and loss, and other adolescent mental health concerns.
  • Determine when additional evaluation, outside treatment, or higher levels of care are warranted and facilitate appropriate referrals.
  • Maintain appropriate clinical boundaries, confidentiality, and documentation in accordance with professional standards and school policies.

Consultation & Care Coordination:

  • Collaborate closely with students, parents/guardians, teachers, administrators, learning support professionals, and the High School Clinical Team to coordinate student support.
  • Communicate with outside therapists, psychiatrists, psychologists, and other providers, as appropriate and with appropriate releases of information.
  • Coordinate school-based and community-based mental health services and support continuity of care.
  • Participate in multidisciplinary case consultation and contribute clinical expertise to discussions regarding students of concern.

Evaluations & Student Support Meetings:

  • Review neuropsychological, psychoeducational, psychological, and other relevant clinical evaluations and communicate clinically relevant findings and recommendations to appropriate school professionals.
  • Collaborate with the Learning Support Team to understand and implement recommendations related to students’ emotional, behavioral, and academic functioning.
  • Participate in High School guidance and student support meetings, contributing relevant clinical information and identifying students who may benefit from additional intervention or referral.

Parent/Guardian Consultation:

  • Provide clinical consultation to parents/guardians regarding adolescent mental health, emotional development, family dynamics, and school-related concerns.
  • Help families understand and respond to emerging mental health or behavioral concerns.
  • Provide referrals and resources to outside clinicians, treatment programs, and other community-based services when appropriate.
  • Facilitate communication among students, families, school professionals, and outside providers when clinically appropriate.

Documentation & Confidentiality:

  • Maintain timely, accurate, and clinically appropriate documentation of counseling sessions, consultations, referrals, and relevant student concerns in the school’s confidential August Schools database.
  • Maintain student confidentiality while appropriately communicating information necessary to ensure student safety and coordinate care.

Qualifications

  • Must have a doctoral degree in a mental health field and current clinical licensure.
  • Demonstrated clinical experience providing counseling or psychotherapy to adolescents; experience with high school-aged students required.
  • Experience with clinical assessment, risk assessment, crisis intervention, and/or care coordination preferred.
  • Experience working in a school, particularly an independent school setting, strongly preferred.
  • Strong understanding of adolescent development and contemporary mental health concerns.
  • Excellent communication, collaboration, organizational, and interpersonal skills.
  • Sound clinical judgment, strong professional boundaries, and ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary team.
  • Commitment to supporting students within an inclusive school community.

The Dalton School does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, ethnic origin, age, physical disability, sexual orientation, or any other category protected by applicable law in the administration of our educational policies, hiring policies, admissions policies, financial aid programs, athletics, and other school-administered programs.

Application Instructions

Candidates must be authorized to work in the US without needing sponsorship. To apply, please submit a resume and cover letter to the employment portal using the following link - https://www.dalton.org/employment

job.title: The Harker School Assistant to Upper School Division Head
job.description:
Position Description & Application

The Harker School seeks an experienced, highly organized, and personable Administrative Assistant to the Head of Upper School, preferably with prior school experience, to provide high-level administrative and operational support to the Upper School Division Head.

This full-time, 12-month position serves as an important liaison between the Upper School office and the Harker community.

Work Schedule: Monday–Friday, 7:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m., with a one-hour unpaid lunch break.

The Administrative Assistant provides direct support to the Head of Upper School while overseeing the multifaceted administrative functions and daily operations of a thriving Upper School campus. Responsibilities include executive scheduling, communications, event and project coordination, financial administration, calendar management, and general office operations. As a central point of contact for students, parents, faculty, staff, and administrators, the Administrative Assistant plays an essential role in fostering an organized, welcoming, and efficient office environment.

Each day brings new opportunities to learn, collaborate, and engage in creative and innovative ways within our diverse school community. Success in this role requires the ability to develop positive, professional, and friendly relationships with students, parents, faculty, and staff.

The ideal candidate combines a proactive, problem-solving mindset with exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and a demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities. This individual enjoys working with students and educators, anticipates needs, exercises sound judgment, and brings professionalism, warmth, and enthusiasm to their daily interactions.

We are guided by our institutional Values in Action:

  • Greet cheerfully
  • Seek to understand
  • Lean in
  • Discover daily
  • Make a difference

All with honor and integrity.

Qualifications

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
  • 3–5 years of progressively responsible administrative experience, preferably supporting a senior-level leader.
  • Experience coordinating projects, events, programs, or administrative operations.
  • Previous experience working in a school or educational environment strongly preferred.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
  • Strong project management, planning, and problem-solving abilities.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Demonstrated professionalism, discretion, and sound judgment when managing sensitive or confidential information.
  • Ability to anticipate needs, take initiative, and work independently while contributing effectively to a collaborative team.
  • Ability to prioritize and manage multiple responsibilities in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.
  • Flexibility, adaptability, and composure when responding to changing priorities and unexpected situations.
  • Ability to establish and maintain positive, professional, and friendly relationships with students, parents, faculty, staff, and administrators.
  • Proven ability to balance independent problem-solving with accurate, detail-oriented work.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and other productivity and collaboration tools.
  • Ability to quickly learn and effectively utilize school-specific systems and technology platforms.
  • Genuine interest in working with and supporting students, educators, and the broader school community.
  • Demonstrated commitment to supporting The Harker School's mission of equity, diversity, and inclusion.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Executive and Administrative Support

  • Provide comprehensive administrative support to the Head of Upper School, including calendar management, scheduling, meeting coordination, and correspondence.
  • Organize priorities, track deadlines, coordinate follow-up items, and manage recurring administrative responsibilities.
  • Prepare presentations, meeting materials, reports, correspondence, and other documents.
  • Respond to requests and correspondence in a timely and professional manner.
  • Exercise discretion and sound judgment when handling confidential or sensitive information.
  • Anticipate needs, troubleshoot challenges, and independently resolve routine administrative and logistical matters.

Upper School Operations and Communications

  • Serve as a primary point of contact and liaison for students, parents, faculty, staff, administrators, and visitors, providing information and assistance in a welcoming and professional manner.
  • Support daily office operations and maintain efficient administrative processes.
  • Draft, prepare, and distribute communications to students, parents, faculty, and staff.
  • Maintain accurate and current information across Upper School schedules, webpages, shared resources, and internal systems.
  • Collaborate with other departments and administrative teams on school-wide initiatives and operational needs.
  • Foster a positive, organized, and welcoming environment within the Upper School office.

Event and Project Coordination

  • Plan and coordinate major Upper School events, including Back to School Day, conferences, faculty and parent events, senior activities, awards ceremonies, Baccalaureate, and graduation.
  • Oversee event logistics, schedules, timelines, materials, communications, and coordination with participating departments.
  • Develop and maintain project plans, timelines, and organizational systems to ensure successful execution of events and initiatives.
  • Track project progress, deadlines, and responsibilities to ensure tasks are completed accurately and on time.
  • Support additional Upper School programs, events, and special projects as assigned.

Calendar and Scheduling Management

  • Manage and maintain the Upper School calendar, bell schedules, special schedules, and long-range event planning.
  • Communicate calendar and scheduling information accurately and effectively to the school community.
  • Participate in school-wide calendaring efforts and collaborate with other divisions and departments to identify and resolve scheduling conflicts.
  • Maintain long-range planning information for recurring Upper School events and programs.

Financial Administration

  • Manage routine financial processes, including credit card reconciliation, invoices, purchase orders, and reimbursements.
  • Maintain and monitor the Upper School office budget and related documentation.
  • Support financial administration for Upper School programs, events, and activities.
  • Ensure financial records and transactions are accurate, organized, and processed in accordance with school procedures.

Additional Duties and Responsibilities

  • Collaborate with other departments to support school-wide programs and initiatives.
  • Participate in meetings, planning activities, and special projects related to Upper School operations.
  • Provide additional administrative and operational support as needed.
  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned by the Head of Upper School.

Working Conditions

The position is primarily office-based and requires frequent computer use and regular interaction with students, faculty, staff, parents, and visitors. The Upper School office is an open and active environment where individuals frequently seek information and assistance. The successful candidate must be comfortable managing interruptions, responding to changing priorities, and maintaining professionalism in a busy school setting.

Occasional evening and weekend work may be required to support school events and activities, including graduation, Baccalaureate, and other Upper School programs. Overtime will be compensated in accordance with applicable wage and hour laws.

Our Mission

Our mission is to educate students for success at college and beyond and to foster kindness, respect and integrity within a safe and nurturing environment. We achieve academic excellence through the development of intellectual curiosity, personal accountability and a love of learning. Our comprehensive program and exceptional faculty and staff help students discover, develop and enjoy their unique talents. We honor individuality, embrace diversity, and promote leadership and service, preparing students to take their place as global citizens.

Compensation

Pay for this position is determined according to The Harker School's established pay scale and is based on relevant education and experience, as evaluated by the Human Resources Department. The posted pay range reflects the full pay scale for this position. While the maximum rate is included for transparency, most new hires can expect to fall within the lower to middle portion of the pay scale based on their qualifications and experience.

San Domenico is an independent, K-12 day and boarding school with a tradition of innovation and academic excellence since 1850. We foster a community where students are encouraged to discover their passions; lead with courage, wisdom, and kindness; and make a meaningful impact in their immediate and extended environments.

As a welcoming and trusted presence, the Office Manager helps create an environment where children and adults feel known, respected, and cared for, bringing warmth, kindness, and sound judgment to daily interactions.
