job.title: San Domenico School Director of Residential Life
job.description:
Position Description

Full-time, twelve-month leadership position | Start date: July 1, 2027

About San Domenico

San Domenico School is an independent K-12 day and boarding school in Marin County, California, approximately 30 minutes north of San Francisco. Founded in 1850, it is the oldest independent school in California. The School serves approximately 680 students on a picturesque 515-acre campus, including about 140 boarding students from the Bay Area, elsewhere in the United States, and around the world, together representing more than 20 countries.

San Domenico provides a distinctive boarding experience rooted in rigorous academics, meaningful relationships, intercultural understanding, personal growth, and connection to the cultural and educational resources of the Bay Area.

The Opportunity

San Domenico seeks a highly capable, compassionate, and experienced Director of Residential Life to provide strategic and operational leadership for our boarding program. Reporting to the Director of Upper School, the Director leads approximately twelve residential staff members and is responsible for the quality, safety, consistency, and ongoing development of the residential student experience. The new Director will join a stable, well-enrolled program with strong established programming and the opportunity to build on this foundation as the needs of our students and community continue to evolve.

Residential Life is an extension of the School’s educational mission. The program helps students develop intellectual curiosity, personal accountability, independence, self-awareness, integrity, respect for self and others, intercultural understanding, and a commitment to community involvement and service.

The Director will be a visible, relationship-centered leader who understands that strong boarding communities are built through consistency, presence, trust, clear expectations, and everyday interactions. The ideal candidate will be energized by the pace and complexity of residential life, able to respond calmly in challenging moments, and committed to helping adolescents grow in confidence, responsibility, belonging, and purpose.

This is a full-time, twelve-month, exempt position that requires residence in school-provided housing on campus. The role includes active dorm duty and afternoon, evening, weekend, school-break, holiday, and on-call responsibilities when students are present.

Primary Responsibilities

Lead the Program

  • Set the vision, goals, and improvement priorities for Residential Life in alignment with the mission of San Domenico and the educational priorities of the Upper School.
  • Develop and maintain clear policies, procedures, handbooks, schedules, records, and operational systems.
  • Oversee the residential budget and advocate for the resources needed to support students, staff, and facilities.
  • Develop community traditions, student leadership opportunities, activities, and educational programming that support students’ intellectual, social, emotional, physical, and intercultural growth.
  • Develop a purposeful off-campus learning and enrichment program that draws on Marin County and the Bay Area’s cultural, educational, service, professional, recreational, and outdoor opportunities.

Develop and Support Staff

  • Recruit, hire, onboard, supervise, evaluate, coach, and retain a strong team of residential staff.
  • Ensure that residential staff understand students’ goals and help them develop the habits, discipline, and follow-through that can help them experience success.
  • Create staff schedules, duty assignments, coverage plans, and accountability structures while coordinating with staff members’ other school responsibilities.
  • Lead orientation, August training, regular staff meetings, ongoing professional learning, and formal performance-review cycles.
  • Build a team culture grounded in collaboration, reliability, professional boundaries, consistent practice, and shared responsibility for student well-being.

Support Students and Families

  • Maintain a visible and engaged presence in the residential community and ensure that students experience a safe, inclusive, supportive, and developmentally appropriate living environment.
  • Support students in pursuing and achieving goals across academics, the arts, athletics, service, leadership, and other areas of interest.
  • Coordinate responses to student concerns and crises, including supervision, communication, documentation, referral, and follow-up.
  • Partner with the Dean of Students on residential expectations, discipline, restorative responses, and student accountability.
  • Communicate proactively and sensitively with families across cultures and time zones.
  • Supervise the staff member responsible for training and supporting student prefects and other residential student leaders.

Coordinate Across the School

  • Serve as an active member of the Upper School leadership team and collaborate closely with Counseling, Health Services, Admissions, Auxiliary Programs, Campus Security, Athletics, Facilities, Food Services, and Upper School faculty and staff.
  • Build strong relationships with day students and create meaningful opportunities for day and boarding students to participate together in community.
  • Partner with emergency preparedness and operations leaders to implement safety procedures and coordinate effective responses to emergencies.
  • Monitor residential facilities, communicate needs, and ensure appropriate follow-up with Facilities and Maintenance.
  • Represent the residential program at Admissions and enrollment events.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in education, student development, counseling, social work, or a related field.
  • Progressively responsible experience in residential life, student life, education, youth development, or a related setting, including meaningful supervisory experience.
  • Strong understanding of adolescent development and experience supporting high-school students.
  • Demonstrated skill in staff leadership, conflict resolution, crisis response, organization, communication, and sound decision-making.
  • Ability to build trusting relationships across cultures while maintaining clear expectations, confidentiality, and professional boundaries.
  • Willingness and ability to reside on campus and fulfill the active-duty, variable-schedule, and on-call responsibilities of the position.
  • Valid California driver’s license and ability to receive and maintain clearance to operate school vehicles through the School’s insurance provider.
  • Current CPR and First Aid certification, or ability to obtain certification by the start of employment.

Preferred

  • Master’s degree in a related field.
  • Leadership experience in a boarding school or residential program, preferably within an internationally diverse school community.
  • Demonstrated experience in staff development, restorative practices, trauma-informed care, budget management, and residential programming.
  • Substantial experience supporting international students and families through the transition to boarding school in the United States, including communicating effectively across languages, cultures, and time zones.
  • A record of fostering a vibrant, inclusive residential community in which international students and students from the United States form meaningful relationships and learn from one another.
  • Proficiency in a language other than English, particularly one spoken by families in our boarding community.

Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this position is $120,000–$165,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications. School-provided on-campus housing is included as a condition of the role. This position offers a competitive benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a matching 403(b) retirement plan, and meals whenever the campus dining hall is open.

Housing consists of an attractive two- or three-bedroom apartment within the residential community, depending on the needs of the Director and their family.

How to Apply

Please submit a cover letter describing how your experience and skills will contribute to San Domenico’s residential community, along with your resume and salary requirements, to hr@sandomenico.org by November 2, 2026. Early applications are encouraged, as we will begin reviewing materials in October and continue throughout the application period.

Or mail to:

San Domenico School

1500 Butterfield Road

San Anselmo, CA 94960

Attn: Director of Residential Life Search

job.title: International School Bangkok School Speech Language Pathologist
job.description:
Position Description

The ISB Educator Profile

ISB educators embody key attributes integrated with our core values to create a vibrant, inclusive learning community. They are adaptable professionals who thrive in dynamic environments, remaining flexible and ready to pivot to meet the evolving needs of our students. As true collaborators, they view education as a shared endeavor—actively co-planning, co-teaching, and building strong relationships with colleagues and families. They serve as optimistic problem solvers who approach every challenge with a positive outlook, turning obstacles into opportunities for innovation and growth. Above all, their practice is student-centered, ensuring that all pedagogical and design choices are rooted in student learning and well-being. Ultimately, ISB educators embody our mission by demonstrating curiosity, courage, and empowerment in their lives, work, and professional growth.

ISB’s ideal team player combines deep subject expertise and strong pedagogy with humility, drive, and a positive disposition for supporting young learners.

We believe

At ISB, we believe that education is a dynamic, creative, and collaborative human endeavor. We are seeking a passionate Speech-Language Pathologist to join our faculty to foster student independence, effective communication, and meaningful participation across school and community settings.

Our vibrant school environment thrives on the energy and dedication of our faculty. We seek educators who navigate diverse teaching responsibilities with ease and work closely with students, families, counselors, and administrators to foster a rich community of inquiry. Our teachers bring curiosity, creativity, and a commitment to collaboration to their work, designing meaningful learning experiences that support students' academic, social, and emotional growth.

Beyond the classroom, our educators support students in co-curricular programming, trips, activities, performances, and are available to support and celebrate their growth and development as they strive to reach their full potential

Position Overview

The Speech and Language Pathologist provides high-quality, evidence-based assessment, intervention, and consultation services across ISB, with a primary focus on supporting students in Secondary (middle school and high school) and the Life Centered Education (LCE) program. The SLP works collaboratively with students, families, teachers, administrators, and other specialists to support communication, participation, independence, well-being, and meaningful learning.

The SLP will provide specialized support for students with communication and learning needs, with an emphasis on functional communication, social pragmatics, and the application of skills across classroom, school, and community environments.

Core Responsibilities

● Provide comprehensive speech and language screenings, assessments, and evidence-based intervention using formal and informal measures.

● Develop, implement, and monitor individualized treatment plans and ILPs based on student strengths, needs, and goals.

● Provide individual and small-group speech and language therapy, including within the classroom, in community spaces, and in LCE environments, as appropriate.

● Work closely with the LCE Coordinator, LCE teachers, families, and other specialists to provide integrated support for students with intensive communication needs, leading classes such as wellbeing and learning needs as best fits.

● Support families in a specific understanding of their child’s speech goals as well as how

● to train on the use of different communication tools, strategies, or devices (such as AAC), support functional communication, independence, participation, and the generalization of communication skills across classrooms, the middle and high school, and community settings.

● Collect, analyze, and interpret data to monitor student progress, evaluate services, and inform recommendations and future programming.

● Conduct classroom observations and provide practical communication strategies, accommodations, and supports across settings.

● Collaborate with teachers, families, administrators, and multidisciplinary teams to support student learning, communication, participation, and well-being.

● Provide consultation, coaching, and professional learning for teachers, families, and school personnel to build capacity and support student communication.

● Participate in Student Support Team, grade-level, LCE, transition, and other relevant meetings.

● Maintain accurate, timely, and confidential student records and documentation.

● Contribute to admissions processes, including assessment, consultation, and recommendations when appropriate

● Collaborate with external therapists, agencies, and service providers to promote continuity of support when needed.

● Engage in professional reflection, peer collaboration, supervision, and continuing professional development.

● Contribute to innovative practices, program development, and broader ISB Student Services initiatives.

Required Qualifications

● Master’s degree in Speech-Language Pathology/Communication Disorders and appropriate professional credentials (e.g., CCC-SLP and/or applicable license)

● Experience assessing and treating speech, language, fluency, voice, cognitive-communication, and social communication needs

● Experience with PEERS or a similar type of social communication research-based program

● Experience working with children in a school or pediatric setting; familiarity with MTSS/RTI preferred

● Experience supporting students with a range of communication needs, including students who use Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) systems and devices, oral motor plans, and be able to support parents and community understanding

● Strong knowledge of evidence-based practices and current research

● Excellent communication, organization, collaboration, and time-management skills

● Flexible, adaptable, culturally responsive, and committed to inclusive practice

● Warm, ethical, professional, and committed to ISB’s values and Culture of Care

● Commitment to ongoing professional learning and development

Personal Attributes

● Committed to meeting the needs of diverse learners in a multicultural school setting

● Committed to lifelong learning; professional growth in the fields of speech-language pathology and education (conferences, workshops, coursework)

● Organized and efficient; excellent time management skills

Application Details

Interested candidates should complete the online application (www.isb.ac.th/job-opportunities) at the earliest opportunity and before the deadline of February 1, 2027. Search Associates candidates need only apply through the Search Associates platform, and finalists will be invited to complete the secondary screening via TruFit Talent. All other applicants can apply directly through TruFit Talent using the link provided in the vacancy announcement on the school website.

Please note that if an outstanding applicant is identified early in the search process, ISB reserves the right to make an appointment prior to the deadline.

Compensation and Benefits

ISB provides a competitive compensation and benefits package that is commensurate with the candidate’s experience and aligned with global international school standards. Benefits provided to the employee and up to two dependent children.

Teaching and Learning

● Partner with Middle School teachers to integrate research, media literacy, digital citizenship, and inquiry into unit designs.

● Provide targeted instruction on research strategies, source evaluation, ethical information use, and digital tool navigation.

● Guide students to become independent, critical, and ethical creators and consumers of information.

● Co-design and co-teach interdisciplinary projects utilizing varied print, digital, and multimedia resources.

● Cultivate a school-wide culture of reading for personal enjoyment and intellectual growth.

● Differentiate learning opportunities to challenge and support students of diverse abilities, interests, and backgrounds.

Library Program Development

● Manage a student-centered Middle School Library program aligned with ISB learning goals.

● Provide equitable access to library facilities, collections, and educational programs

● Organize literary events, displays, and initiatives that spark curiosity and foster community belonging.

● Assess and continuously refine library services based on student feedback, curriculum needs, and data.

Collection Development and Resource Management

● Curate and maintain a balanced, current collection of print and digital resources supporting the curriculum.

● Select materials that reflect diverse student backgrounds, interests, reading levels, and global perspectives.

● Regularly evaluate, promote, and weed resources to keep the collection engaging and relevant.

Collaboration and Professional Community

job.title: International School Bangkok Director of Learning
job.description:
Position Description

The ISB Educator Profile

ISB educators embody key attributes integrated with our core values to create a vibrant, inclusive learning community. They are adaptable professionals who thrive in dynamic environments, remaining flexible and ready to pivot to meet the evolving needs of our students. As true collaborators, they view education as a shared endeavor—actively co-planning, co-teaching, and building strong relationships with colleagues and families. They serve as optimistic problem solvers who approach every challenge with a positive outlook, turning obstacles into opportunities for innovation and growth. Above all, their practice is student-centered, ensuring that all pedagogical and design choices are rooted in student learning and well-being. Ultimately, ISB educators embody our mission by demonstrating curiosity, courage, and empowerment in their lives, work, and professional growth.

ISB’s ideal candidate combines deep subject expertise and strong pedagogy with humility, drive, and a positive disposition for supporting young learners.

We Believe

At ISB, we believe that education is a dynamic, creative, and collaborative human endeavor. Beyond the classroom, our educators support students in co-curricular programming, trips, activities, performances and are available to support and celebrate their growth and development as they strive to reach their full-potential.

Our ideal learning leader is someone who can see what needs to be done and act, who can collaborate effectively, manage people and navigate difficult conversations directly, and who believes deeply in every professional's capacity to grow, while never losing sight of student learning as the top priority. Joining ISB is a unique and exciting opportunity.

Our Learning Program

This is fundamentally a systems role: clarifying what exists, building what's missing, and working in close collaboration with PK–12 leaders to support and codify robust faculty support and development and move ISB toward a genuine one-school experience for students. This work ensures that the ISB learning experience is a true PK–12 continuum: coherent, developmentally appropriate, and responsive, providing support when needed and challenge when needed, all in service of ISB's mission to develop thinkers and doers who are curious, courageous, and empowered to shape what comes next. The Director of Learning improves foundational teaching practices with a clear-eyed recognition that students are dynamic learners and that ISB's faculty care deeply about meeting their needs.

The Director of Learning Position

The Director of Learning reports to the Head of School and sits on the Leadership Team. The role oversees and tracks the schoolwide professional development fund and leads the Learning Design Center (LDC) as ISB's central hub for professional learning, coaching, and data-informed practice, supporting ISB as a professional learning community. Within the LDC sit four core pillars: faculty growth and evaluation, PK–12 curriculum articulation and coherence, a PK–12 coaching model, and research and innovation.

1. Faculty Growth and Evaluation

● Finalize and implement a learning progression for leadership, teacher leadership, and teachers around the new Professional Growth and Evaluation System (year one full roll out to begin January 2028) that deepens understanding, maximizes connection to existing work, and empowers teachers to own their professional growth.

● Hold the PK–12 Professional Growth and Evaluation System accountable for improvement in teaching practice and student learning, not just compliance.

● Ensure the Professional Growth and Evaluation System generates timely, actionable, helpful, and iterative feedback between evaluators, coaches, and faculty

2. PK–12 Curriculum Articulation and Coherence

● Develop clearly articulated scope and sequence, assessment, and measurable PK–12 learning outcomes.

● Use learning data to identify gaps and redundancies and prioritize where curriculum should evolve.

3. PK–12 Coaching and Professional Growth Culture

● Lead the coaching model to full, consistent implementation across all divisions.

● Use coaching data and faculty feedback to refine the model and sustain a lasting coaching culture with the goal of improving teaching for learning.

4. Research & Innovation

● Develop a culture of research-informed practice across the school, ensuring pedagogical innovation is grounded in evidence and connected to the science of learning.

● Support and document ongoing action research among faculty and teams, providing structure (protocols, time, coaching support) for staff to test new practices in their own classrooms.

● Establish a pipeline for promising pilots so innovation isn't a side project, it's how the LDC's other pillars evolve.

● Collaborate with key partners to explore innovation and continuous improvement, keeping ownership and accountability inside the LDC.

Required Qualifications

● A master's or doctoral level (Ed.D. or Ph.D.) degree in a relevant educational field.

● Minimum 3 years of administrative experience (Principal/Division Director, Learning Leader, or Curriculum Director preferred).

● Proven track record in international and/or independent schools, with a background in teaching, evaluation, and curriculum design.

● Deep knowledge of curriculum and teaching practices grounded in the science of learning.

● Understanding of how student support functions as a vital partner to teaching and learning, ensuring students can access the curriculum and thrive.

Personal Attributes

● Action-Oriented: Able to see what needs to be done and acts without waiting to be told.

● People Management: Skilled at managing others and having direct, difficult conversations when needed.

● Growth Mindset: Believes in a professional's capacity to grow, while keeping student learning at the forefront.

● Collaborative: Works closely and effectively with PK–12 leaders and Division Directors as true partners.

● Flexible & Insightful: Adapts to shifting needs and reads situations with sound judgment.

● Curious & Creative: Brings fresh thinking and genuine curiosity to problems of teaching and learning.

● Passion: Loves the work, and brings energy and enthusiasm to a role built for the right person.

● Future-Ready: Prepared to lead ISB's research and innovation efforts as they grow and evolve over the coming years.

● Research-to-Practice: Able to translate research into practice as a critical consumer of research, and to guide action research within the school.

Application Details

International School Bangkok (ISB) is partnering with TruFit Talent for this leadership search. Interested candidates are invited to apply through TruFit Talent directly by clicking the link below by October 30, 2026. Search Associates candidates need only apply through Search. Only finalists will be invited to complete TruFit's secondary screening process. Through TruFit Talent’s secondary screening process, applicants will be completing a free profile and leadership scenarios.

To apply, click: me.trufittalent.com/assess/apply/isb-director-of-learning

Compensation and Benefits

ISB provides a highly competitive compensation and benefits package that is commensurate with the candidate’s experience and aligned with global international school standards.

job.title: Flint Hill School Upper School History and Social Sciences Teacher
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Flint Hill School provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, pregnancy, national origin, ethnic origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

Description

When passion and impact come together, an institution becomes more than a place to work. As many of our teachers and staff will tell you, Flint Hill is a place where they are challenged and inspired, and yet it still feels like home.

At Flint Hill, we believe in redefining what educational excellence looks like. Always curious, every day, we ask questions like, “Imagine if?” and “What’s possible?” And we encourage our students to do the same.

Our teachers’ expertise and commitment to innovative teaching are complemented by a personal approach that emphasizes respect and communication.

With our rigorous academic program and extracurricular opportunities, Flint Hill students can do it all. We inspire our students to reach their greatest potential while maintaining balance and wellbeing. Our Upper School, grades 9-12, academic program is both challenging and supportive — allowing all students to be successful. We cultivate deep learning and encourage students to pursue all of their interests. We believe that learning led by curiosity inspires students to develop passion and purpose. Always innovating to set new standards of excellence, we don’t let resources or schedules limit our students’ experience. Our culture of support and inclusion allows students to feel welcome and connected from day one — whether they’re a lifer or transferring from another school. Preparing for college, our four full-time college counselors focus on truly getting to know students and guiding them to “right-fit” schools. Students graduate as confident self-advocates with the skills and maturity to excel in college and blaze their own trail in life.

The Upper School History and Social Sciences Teacher supports the experience of Flint Hill students and faculty and embraces the mission, vision, and core values of the school, the Flint Hill Statement of Institutional Equity and Inclusion and the Portrait of the Flint Hill Student.

The salary range for this position is $65,000 to $115,000. The pay range represents a good-faith estimate of the salary the school reasonably expects to pay for the position upon hire. The pay offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on a range of factors unique to each candidate, including, but not limited to, knowledge, skills, and abilities; relevant education; length, depth, and breadth of related experience; and any advanced skills the candidate may possess.

job.title: International School Bangkok High School English/Social Studies Teacher
job.description:
Position Description

The ISB Educator Profile

ISB educators embody key attributes integrated with our core values to create a vibrant, inclusive learning community. They are adaptable professionals who thrive in dynamic environments, remaining flexible and ready to pivot to meet the evolving needs of our students. As true collaborators, they view education as a shared endeavor—actively co-planning, co-teaching, and building strong relationships with colleagues and families. They serve as optimistic problem solvers who approach every challenge with a positive outlook, turning obstacles into opportunities for innovation and growth. Above all, their practice is student-centered, ensuring that all pedagogical and design choices are rooted in student learning and well-being. Ultimately, ISB educators embody our mission by demonstrating curiosity, courage, and empowerment in their lives, work, and professional growth.

ISB’s ideal candidate combines deep subject expertise and strong pedagogy with humility, drive, and a positive disposition for supporting young learners.

We believe

At ISB, we believe that education is a dynamic, creative, and collaborative human endeavor. We are seeking a passionate High School English/Social Studies teacher to join our faculty and help students explore, investigate, and make sense of the world.

Our vibrant school environment thrives on the energy and dedication of our faculty. We seek educators who navigate diverse teaching responsibilities with ease and work closely with students, families, counselors, and administrators to foster a rich community of inquiry. Our teachers bring curiosity, creativity, and a commitment to collaboration to their work, designing meaningful learning experiences that support students' academic, social, and emotional growth.

Beyond the classroom, our educators support students in co-curricular programming, trips, activities, performances and are available to support and celebrate their growth and development as they strive to reach their full-potential.

Position Overview

ISB seeks an experienced High School English/Social Studies Teacher who is passionate about creating engaging, inquiry-driven learning experiences for students.

The ideal candidate will have strong subject knowledge in English and Social Studies and the ability to design meaningful learning experiences that develop students' communication, critical thinking, inquiry, research, and disciplinary thinking skills. The successful candidate will be student-centered, collaborative, adaptable, and committed to using current and research-supported pedagogical practices.

The candidate will contribute to a Professional Learning Community (PLC), work collaboratively with colleagues, and use student evidence and data to inform instructional decisions. Experience teaching IB and/or AP courses is valued. Experience with inquiry-based approaches and, for Social Studies, the C3 Framework is preferred.

This position may also provide opportunities to contribute to innovative programming and authentic learning experiences that connect students with mentors, real-world contexts, and opportunities to apply their learning beyond the classroom.

Required Qualifications and Experience

● A valid teaching license or certification in a related field.

● At least three years of relevant and recent High School teaching experience.

● Experience with, and a belief in, an inquiry approach to teaching and learning.

● Experience teaching English Language Learners.

● Experience using data to inform instruction through a Professional Learning Community (PLC).

● Strong subject knowledge and teaching experience in English and/or Social Studies.

Preferred Qualifications

● Experience teaching IB and/or AP courses.

● Experience teaching a standards-based curriculum, such as the Common Core Standards for English or the C3 Framework for Social Studies.

● Experience teaching English and/or Social Studies within an international school setting.

● Experience developing interdisciplinary learning opportunities.

Pedagogical Practice requirements

● Has an Inquiry-based approach to teaching and learning

● Ability to adapt teaching to the context

● Highly Skilled in using a varied pedagogical and assessment toolkit

● Can challenge and extend all learners

● Can integrate the teaching of skills to prepare students for life beyond the classroom

● Identifies, selects, and utilizes instructional resources to meet the needs of students with varying backgrounds, learning styles, and special needs.

● Uses data to improve learning

Mindsets and Dispositions

● Cares for students

● Commitment to the Social and Emotional Learning (SEL) of students.

● Strong work ethic

● Contributes positively to the culture of the school

● Strong and effective communication skills

● Open-minded and adaptable

● Demonstrates growth-mindset and passion for lifelong learning

● Culturally competent

● Reflective on their practice

Core Responsibilities

● Teach assigned High School English/Social Studies courses.

● Develop students' disciplinary thinking, critical inquiry, research, analysis, problem-solving, and communication skills.

● Utilize varied assessments and student data to monitor progress, adapt instruction, and provide timely, actionable feedback.

● Integrate appropriate technology and contemporary resources to enhance learning and connect classroom concepts with real-world contexts.

● Partner with counselors, administrators, and parents to support students' academic achievement and social-emotional well-being.

● Chaperone local/international trips, including DELVE experiential learning week, and. fulfill assigned supervision duties.

● Maintain professional obligations, meeting deadlines, and honoring schedules.

● Strictly uphold ISB standards of integrity, respect, and care.

● Serves as an Advisor in the High School Advisory Program.

● Collaborate as an effective member of high school teams (PLC, Department, Grade Level, etc.)

● Positively contribute to school culture through the support and sponsorship of a student club or non-stipended extracurricular activity.

● Participates in professional development training and attends required presentations.

● Meets professional obligations through efficient work habits such as meeting deadlines, honoring schedules, and working with colleagues.

● Ensures student growth and achievement is continuous and appropriate for age group, subject area, and /or program classification.

● Provides a positive and safe environment in which students are encouraged to actively engage in the learning process.

● Strictly uphold ISB expectations for child safeguarding and student well-being.

● Performs other duties and responsibilities as assigned by the supervisor.

Application Details

Interested candidates should complete the online application (www.isb.ac.th/job-opportunities) at the earliest opportunity and before the deadline of February 1, 2027. Search Associates candidates need only apply through the Search Associates platform, and finalists will be invited to complete the secondary screening via TruFit Talent. All other applicants can apply directly through TruFit Talent using the link provided in the vacancy announcement on the school website.

Please note that if an outstanding applicant is identified early in the search process, ISB reserves the right to make an appointment prior to the deadline.

Compensation and Benefits

ISB provides a competitive compensation and benefits package that is commensurate with the candidate’s experience and aligned with global international school standards. Benefits provided to the employee and up to two dependent children.

● Ability to adapt teaching to the context

● Highly Skilled in using a varied pedagogical and assessment toolkit

● Provide targeted instruction on research strategies, source evaluation, ethical information use, and digital tool navigation.

● Guide students to become independent, critical, and ethical creators and consumers of information.

job.title: The Calhoun School Upper School Assistant Director
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Job title: Upper School Assistant Director Department/Division: Upper School

Direct report: Upper School Director FLSA status: Exempt

Position status: Full-time Classification: Administration Salary range: $100,000-$130,000

POSITION SUMMARY

The Upper School Assistant Director works with the Upper School Director, providing leadership to the Upper School faculty and supporting the division's daily operations and programs. In partnership with the Upper School Director, the Assistant Director examines curriculum and pedagogical practice. They collaborate with faculty, partner with parents, and interact with students. The Assistant Director supports the Director in creating a joyful community of learners. They are actively engaged in student life, providing a healthy structure for Upper School students and encouraging personal development and social responsibility. In partnership with the Director, they oversee disciplinary matters and work closely with US advisors, grade deans, the US counselor, the learning specialists, and faculty to support students' progress and well-being.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS/RESPONSIBILITIES/DUTIES/TASKS

  • Uphold the school's mission statement, inclusive practices, commitment to social justice, and all activities of Calhoun’s Upper School
  • Support the Upper School Director as an instructional leader in the Upper School, responsible for its day-to-day life and program; support the work of upper school faculty members in the performance of their work; support the Upper School Director in all aspects of the upper school division
  • Work in partnership with the Director in articulating the Upper School curriculum, programs, expectations, behavioral guidelines, and other information necessary to ensure faculty and students are fully informed, consistent with their roles
  • Serve on the Upper School Leadership Team to support the individual needs of upper school students
  • Work with parents and children in the upper school to develop effective relationships and provide effective feedback
  • Support the hiring process and professional development work of upper school faculty
  • Work with admissions to increase and maintain enrollment
  • Maintain a healthy and safe upper school atmosphere for children
  • Support regular meetings with upper school faculty, on both routine school matters and with the exchange of ideas on issues of educational/philosophical interest and concern
  • Show respect and empower upper school faculty to meet their full potential, and encourage respectful interactions

COLLABORATION & COMMUNICATION

  • Collaborate with colleagues intra- and cross-divisionally to ensure alignment and student progress.
  • Attend faculty meetings and conferences.
  • Maintain consistent and clear communication with faculty and families.
  • Engage fully in the wider life of the School.
  • Demonstrate strong commitment to and alignment with Calhoun’s mission and values.

SKILLS & COMPETENCIES

  • Strong affinity for, and commitment to, progressive, humanistic education.
  • Interest in teaching and working with Upper School students.
  • Ability to organize and manage multiple priorities.
  • Demonstrated enthusiasm and strong interpersonal skills to relate well with students, staff, administration, parents, and the community.
  • Flexibility and ability to navigate a dynamic school environment.
  • Systems-oriented mindset with attention to operational detail.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS/WORK REQUIREMENTS

The employee is required to stand, sit, and navigate the classroom continuously for extended durations, including the lifting and transportation of classroom materials and equipment as necessary.

COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY WORK

Calhoun is committed to addressing issues of social justice, diversity, equity, and anti-bias education in our curriculum and in our community. Employees must be willing learners and participants in supporting this work.

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY POLICY

Calhoun is committed to recruiting, hiring, and supporting a diverse staff and welcomes applicants of all gender, sexuality, religious, ethnic, racial, and cultural identities. Calhoun does not unlawfully discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of one’s actual or perceived race; color; religion; sex/gender (including gender identity); creed; sexual orientation; marital status; pregnancy; ethnicity; national origin; ancestry; age; disability.

Qualifications

QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED

  • Experience in school leadership, instructional coaching, or grade-level leadership.
  • Commitment to diversity, collegiality, and school mission.
  • A solid understanding of children’s academic, social, and emotional development.
  • Prior experience as a teacher and/or administrator of upper school-age children.
  • Deep appreciation for student-centered, engaging, and innovative teaching practices.
  • A desire to work collaboratively with a group of talented colleagues
  • Strong organization and communication skills

QUALIFICATIONS DESIRED

  • Master’s Degree in Education or related field.
  • Experience working in a progressive school environment.
  • Experience supporting student behavior systems and restorative practices.
