job.title: Columbus School for Girls After School Teaching Aide
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Columbus School for Girls (CSG) is an independent day school in Columbus, Ohio, founded in 1898, serving diverse students in pre-k through grade 12. CSG empowers girls to discover their distinct potential as learners and leaders. As a leader in the education of girls and young women, CSG is a vibrant community of more than 560 students, 135 faculty and staff, and 2,500 active alumnae. CSG’s 8-acre academic campus in the beautiful Bexley neighborhood is a ten-minute drive from downtown Columbus, a city bustling with artistic, civic, and shopping experiences. Having just completed a strategic plan to guide the School’s direction over the next several years, CSG offers an exceptional, student-centered academic experience with strong offerings in the arts, an impressive athletic program, and a health and wellness curriculum that is unique in Central Ohio. This combination of academics and skills ensures that CSG students will be well prepared for life beyond CSG.

Columbus School for Girls seeks to hire an energetic and creative After School Teaching Aide effective in January 2027. This position is a 10 month position, following the faculty calendar, working 2:30p-6:00p. CSG offers a competitive salary, generous benefits and professional opportunities. CSG welcomes candidates who add to the racial, cultural, religious, and gender diversity of the school community.

Characteristics, Qualities, Values & Competencies

  • A belief in the endless capacity and promise of girls with a commitment to the mission of CSG.
  • A student-centered educator who emphasizes inquiry, innovation, and balances the importance of depth and breadth of knowledge.
  • Dedicated to motivating and inspiring students to achieve their highest potential and building strong home and school partnerships.
  • An individual with a growth mindset and a joy and passion for learning and education.
  • Eager to work collaboratively with colleagues; committed to developing an equitable and inclusive classroom and community, and dedicated to making positive contributions to the student experience both inside and outside the classroom.
  • Ability to navigate a fast-paced environment, agility, and the capacity to pivot as needed.
  • High emotional intelligence, strong cultural competence, and a demonstrated belief in the value of a diverse and multicultural community.

Major Functions and Responsibilities:

  • Work collaboratively with teachers in the classroom to provide the highest quality education and care for the children.
  • Supervise students to ensure their safety and well-being.
  • Support and extend student work in the classroom in a questioning and reflecting manner

Additional responsibilities may include:

  • Prepare snacks.
  • Help maintain the classroom, materials, Columbia House and the playground.
  • Take and type notes and photographs for documentation.
  • Attend parent meetings when requested.

Experience

  • Associate’s degree required; Bachelor’s or Master’s degree preferred; preferably with background in early childhood; Strong candidates will have classroom experience
  • An understanding of the value of an all-girls education and the eagerness to learn about the best ways to help young women of promise to reach their full potential as learners and leaders
  • Excellent communication skills, a genuine appreciation for and an understanding of the development of young children, a sense of humor, and the ability to work well within a diverse, collaborative environment

Other Requirements

  • Ability to lift or run after a child
  • Go outside in inclement weather
  • Travel throughout the campus to complete their duties

Physical Demands:

The physical demands include being able to sit, talk, hear, stand; use hand to finger, handle, or feel; and reach hands and arms. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required for this job include close and distance vision.

Interested candidates should apply on the Career page of our website at: https://www.columbusschoolforgirls.org/about/careers and submit a cover letter outlining their interest in and qualifications for this specific position including a resume

Columbus School for Girls is an Equal Opportunity Employer and as such, does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, sex, age, religion, national origin, ancestry, sexual orientation, disability, veteran status, marital status, or any other status protected by law.

job.title: Waldorf School of the Peninsula Preschool Teaching Assistant
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Waldorf School of the Peninsula (Preschool - Grade 12) is celebrating it's 41st year of bringing Waldorf education to Northern California. Our school has two beautiful campuses: Preschool through grade 5 in Los Altos and a few miles away in Mountain View are grades 6-12. Our school is a full member of and accredited by the Association of Waldorf Schools of North America and fully accredited by the Western Association of Schools and Colleges. WSP is dedicated to hiring dedicated and highly capable faculty and administration. We invest in our learning and growth to best serve the needs of our students, teachers, community, and each other.

We are seeking a dedicated full-time preschool teaching assistant for our preschool program at the Los Altos, CA campus for the upcoming school year. This role is an hourly, full-time position supporting one of our preschool classrooms, with possible work opportunities during school breaks and summers, when camps are offered. Availability Monday through Friday 8 am - 3 pm is required.

Excellent, professional interpersonal skills are required as well as the ability to multitask and take ownership of a wide range of children’s needs, indoor and outdoor activities, and housekeeping duties. Areas of responsibility include tracking student arrivals and departures, supervision and support of student activities and social interactions, communication with parents, and a variety of daily housekeeping duties including organization and management of materials and classroom space, food preparation, laundry and cleaning tasks.

The ideal candidate will have a loving and playful, yet authoritative presence with children. This person will be fluid and flexible in an ever-changing landscape, yet able and willing to maintain the rhythms and routines that are in place to support this fluidity for the children. Experience working with early childhood children is required, as is the ability to be in physical movement such as walking, bending, lifting approximately 25lbs, squatting, and playing for the majority of the work day. Staff are expected to be safety conscious and able to solve problems with discernment, while maintaining confidentiality of student, familial and organizational information.

Responsibilities:

Each employee is responsible for exhibiting good communication, problem solving and priority setting skills as well as maintaining an overall positive attitude. In collaboration with Waldorf School of the Peninsula administrative staff and early childhood faculty:

  • Promote positive relationships with all children and adults
  • Create a nurturing environment for young children and families
  • Develop partnerships with colleagues to establish a cohesive early childhood community
  • Assist Lead Teachers and Extended Care Director as informed
  • Perform light housekeeping and child maintenance duties

Minimum Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma required ; Bachelors degree preferred
  • 6 ECE Units or enrolled in an ECE course preferred
  • Minimum age: 18 years old
  • Must be able to perform and meet the physical demands required in this capacity (ability to sit on the floor, bend at the waist, kneel and/or stop most of the time)
  • Complete a health screening (no more than 60 days prior to hire date) and negative Tuberculosis test (no more than 1 year prior to hire date)
  • Meet the immunization requirements required by the state of CA for early childhood employees
  • Must have a current Pediatric CPR and First Aid certification or ability to obtain
  • Complete a California criminal record clearance via DOJ, FBI, and CACI clearance
  • Extended Care staff enjoy a supportive and collaborative environment, frequent interactions with parents, teachers, and students, as well as an interesting variety of daily challenges.

The role is ideal for an individual with strong leadership capacities who has an interest in teaching and Waldorf Education.

Actual weekly schedules are determined by the Pedagogical Administrator based upon program needs in consultation with staff.

Compensation for this position is $24-$25 an hour.

We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, age, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

job.title: International School Bangkok High School PE/Health Teacher
job.description:
Position Description

The ISB Educator Profile

ISB educators embody key attributes integrated with our core values to create a vibrant, inclusive learning community. They are adaptable professionals who thrive in dynamic environments, remaining flexible and ready to pivot to meet the evolving needs of our students. As true collaborators, they view education as a shared endeavor—actively co-planning, co-teaching, and building strong relationships with colleagues and families. They serve as optimistic problem solvers who approach every challenge with a positive outlook, turning obstacles into opportunities for innovation and growth. Above all, their practice is student-centered, ensuring that all pedagogical and design choices are rooted in student learning and well-being. Ultimately, ISB educators embody our mission by demonstrating curiosity, courage, and empowerment in their lives, work, and professional growth.

ISB’s ideal candidate combines deep subject expertise and strong pedagogy with humility, drive, and a positive disposition for supporting young learners.

We Believe

At ISB, we believe that education is a dynamic, creative, and collaborative human endeavor. We are seeking a passionate High School PE/Health teacher to join our faculty and help students explore, investigate, and make sense of the world.

Our vibrant school environment thrives on the energy and dedication of our faculty. We seek educators who navigate diverse teaching responsibilities with ease and work closely with students, families, counselors, and administrators to foster a rich community of inquiry. Our teachers bring curiosity, creativity, and a commitment to collaboration to their work, designing meaningful learning experiences that support students' academic, social, and emotional growth.

Beyond the classroom, our educators support students in co-curricular programming, trips, activities, performances and are available to support and celebrate their growth and development as they strive to reach their full-potential.

Position Overview

ISB seeks an experienced Physical and Health Education teacher who excels at designing standards-based, hands-on learning experiences that promote physical literacy, personal growth, health, and lifelong wellness. The ideal candidate will foster student agency through inquiry, reflection, and skill development in both individual and team contexts.

Additionally, the ideal candidate will have experience teaching a variety of high school courses with the ability to connect classroom learning to authentic, real-world applications.

The successful candidate will be a collaborative educator who contributes to the department and continuously seeks to inspire students to pursue healthy, active lifestyles. They will also be expected to coach in one or more athletic seasons as part of ISB’s vibrant co-curricular program.

Required Qualifications and Experience

● Hold a valid teaching license or certification

● Have at least three years of relevant and recent teaching experience

● Have experience coaching in high school

● Have experience with, and a belief in, an inquiry approach to teaching and learning

● Have experience teaching English Language Learners

● Have experience using data to inform instruction through a Professional Learning Community (PLC)

Preferred Qualifications

● Have experience teaching a standards-based curriculum

● Experience with IB Sport, Exercise and Health Science

Pedagogical Practice requirements

● Has an Inquiry-based approach to teaching and learning

● Ability to adapt teaching to the context

● Highly Skilled in using a varied pedagogical and assessment toolkit

● Can challenge and extend all learners

● Can integrate the teaching of skills to prepare students for life beyond the classroom

● Identifies, selects, and utilizes instructional resources to meet the needs of students with varying backgrounds, learning styles, and special needs.

● Uses data to improve learning

Mindsets and Dispositions

● Cares for students

● Commitment to the Social and Emotional Learning (SEL) of students.

● Strong work ethic

● Contributes positively to the culture of the school

● Strong and effective communication skills

● Open-minded and adaptable

● Demonstrates growth-mindset and passion for lifelong learning

● Culturally competent

● Reflective on their practice

Core Responsibilities

● Teach assigned High School PE/Health courses.

● Develop students' disciplinary thinking, critical inquiry, research, analysis, problem-solving, and communication skills.

● Utilize varied assessments and student data to monitor progress, adapt instruction, and provide timely, actionable feedback.

● Integrate appropriate technology and contemporary resources to enhance learning and connect classroom concepts with real-world contexts.

● Partner with counselors, administrators, and parents to support students' academic achievement and social-emotional well-being.

● Chaperone local/international trips, including DELVE experiential learning week, and fulfill assigned supervision duties.

● Maintain professional obligations, meeting deadlines, and honoring schedules.

● Strictly uphold ISB standards of integrity, respect, and care.

● Serves as an Advisor in the High School Advisory Program.

● Collaborate as an effective member of high school teams (PLC, Department, Grade Level, etc.)

● Positively contribute to school culture through the support and sponsorship of a student club or non-stipended extracurricular activity.

● Participates in professional development training and attends required presentations.

● Meets professional obligations through efficient work habits such as meeting deadlines, honoring schedules, and working with colleagues.

● Ensures student growth and achievement is continuous and appropriate for age group, subject area, and /or program classification.

● Provides a positive and safe environment in which students are encouraged to actively engage in the learning process.

● Strictly uphold ISB expectations for child safeguarding and student well-being.

● Performs other duties and responsibilities as assigned by the supervisor.

Application Details

Interested candidates should complete the online application (www.isb.ac.th/job-opportunities) at the earliest opportunity and before the deadline of February 1, 2027. Search Associates candidates need only apply through the Search Associates platform, and finalists will be invited to complete the secondary screening via TruFit Talent. All other applicants can apply directly through TruFit Talent using the link provided in the vacancy announcement on the school website.

Please note that if an outstanding applicant is identified early in the search process, ISB reserves the right to make an appointment prior to the deadline.

Compensation and Benefits

ISB provides a competitive compensation and benefits package commensurate with the

candidate’s experience and aligned with international school standards. Benefits are provided to the employee and up to two dependent children.

job.title: The Buckley School Head of Middle School
job.description:
Position Description & Application

The Buckley School is a dynamic, nurturing learning community committed to equity and inclusion, and as such, seeks to hire talented employees with diverse backgrounds.

Head of Middle School

The Buckley School is seeking a Head of Middle School who will create a dynamic and nurturing

environment for Middle School students, faculty, and families in a 93-year-old, all gender K-12 school in Los Angeles that is committed to being both true to its roots and relevant for the times. Nestled in a canyon in the Santa Monica Mountains, Buckley is a nationally recognized college preparatory school with a bold mission, a clear vision, and forward momentum.

with a bold mission, a clear vision, and forward momentum

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Culture & Program

  • Lead the Middle School faculty, staff and administrators in modeling strong, collaborative teamwork and creating a warm, uplifting, and affirmational culture for students and families that creates belonging for all.
  • Oversee all aspects of the academic program, ensuring that curriculum and instruction spark intellectual curiosity and skill development, and are experienced by students as engaging, culturally responsive, and relevant for the times.
  • Design and implement programs to retain current students and families (e.g. the Griffin Family Open
  • House events for current third, fourth, and fifth grade students and families, parent education, systems for communicating with individual families, etc.) and collaborate with the admission team to design and
  • implement programs and materials to attract and yield new students and families.
  • Support the Director of DEI, deans, and other relevant adults to create and implement a robust co-curricular program, including advisory, assemblies, community times, service learning, clubs, internships, crossdivisional buddies, after-school programming for Lower and Middle School, Outdoor Ed, G-Term, trips and travel, and public-private partnerships to create belonging and engagement, and ensure students are developing the skills and attributes in Buckley's Portrait of a Graduate.
  • Collaborate with the Chief of Strategic Initiatives to develop systems to collect and analyze relevant data
  • in order to inform ongoing program growth.
  • Collaborate with the heads of Lower School and Upper School to facilitate K-12 alignment in program,
  • practice, and culture while honoring the developmental needs of each age group.

Faculty & Staff

  • Lead the Middle School faculty, staff, and administrators in fostering an educational program that fulfills the school's mission, vision and values.
  • Observe, evaluate, support, coach, and assign responsibilities and duties to Middle School instructional and non-instructional faculty, staff, and administrators, in conjunction, as applicable, with department chairs and other senior administrators.
  • Lead, with support from department chairs and other senior administrators, retention, recruitment, hiring, and managing faculty and staff.
  • Design, with other senior administrators and department chairs, professional development experiences for faculty and staff.
  • Support faculty in their communication with families in their role as advisor, teacher, coach, etc.

Families

  • Create supportive relationships with parents, helping them navigate the joys and challenges of raising
  • middle school students.
  • Provide timely communication about school operations/schedules, and issues related to adolescence and parenting.

Students

  • Create supportive relationships with students, helping them develop the skills needed as scholars, athletes, artists, and community members.
  • Set and maintain clear expectations for behaviors, oversee investigations, and manage discipline.
  • Organize the Middle School academic advising process.
  • Serve on the admission committee and assist in the admission process for the testing, interviewing, and
  • evaluation of Middle School applicants.
  • Lead student retention efforts and take a key role in yield efforts.

EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE

  • A. or other advanced degree preferred.
  • Prefer minimum of five years' experience in an academic environment, preferably with experience as a middle school teacher and administrator in independent schools.

SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE, & Other Qualifications

  • Model high standards of professionalism and create warm, uplifting, and trusting working relationships marked by humor, optimism, humility, excellent emotional intelligence, extraordinary interpersonal skills, and collaboration.
  • Relish the joys and challenges of working with students ages 9-15, and possess a deep understanding of human development, including a particularly strong understanding of the intellectual, social, emotional, and physical development of Middle School students.
  • Possess deep appreciation and passion for education, particularly in an independent school environment conveyed by a solid understanding of educational practice and philosophy, and the ability to share the school's philosophy and practice to prospective families.
  • Model a growth mindset and believe in the capacity for adult growth.
  • Demonstrate strong communication skills in person, in writing, by phone and through other electronic means (such as Zoom).
  • Demonstrate great individual integrity, initiative, self-awareness, commitment to personal and professional growth, ability to receive and apply feedback, and the ability to advance multiple strategic and operational priorities simultaneously.
  • Possess and utilize leadership skills, specifically the ability to motivate, educate and excite faculty.
  • Think and act strategically.
  • Organize and lead routine and special events.
  • Offer evidence of a successful track record in meeting or exceeding stated goals.
  • Possess knowledge of Microsoft Office, Google Suite, Blackbaud/Education Edge, and the ability to learn new and evolving technology.
  • This position requires adaptability, analyzing, assessing, calculating, decision making, dependability, good judgment, reading, memorizing, social skills, speaking, multitasking, and writing.

COMPENSATION

$190,000 – 225,000 per hour

The base salary is separate from fringe benefits, such as retirement contributions, daily lunch, on-site parking, contributions to medical, dental, vision, life/AD&D plans, our generous time off policy, or potential stipends (for eligible employees). Our pay ranges are reasonable estimates of what the School anticipates paying for a role but are not guaranteed. If hired at The Buckley School, your actual base salary will be determined by your education and experience.

TO APPLY

Visit https://buckley.isolvedhire.com/jobs/

Applications received by November 10 will be given priority; the position will be open until filled.

Please submit a single PDF that includes:

  • A cover letter introducing yourself
  • Your résumé
  • A writing sample, which could be a personal statement, educational philosophy, newsletter article, speech, letter to the community, etc.
  • Names, contact info, and your relationship to five references (we will not contact references without

Start date: July 1, 2027

ABOUT THE SCHOOL

The Buckley School proudly carries on the mission of its founder, Dr. Isabelle Buckley, who in 1933 set out to provide students with an education characterized not only by academic excellence, but also a sense of self-esteem, responsibility, and character. An independent, all-gender day school for students in kindergarten through grade 12, providing students with a program based on critical thinking, creative self-expression through arts, physical development, and moral education lies at the heart of Buckley's ethos.

At The Buckley School, faculty and staff believe in their students, see their capacity for growth, and nurture their ability to create and evaluate. Students are honored for their diverse backgrounds and admired for their ability to lead with empathy and courage. Inspired by its mission, the Portrait of a Graduate, Dr. Buckley's Four-Fold Plan - education with equal emphasis on Academics, the Arts, Athletics, and Moral Education - and the Buckley Commitment of Honesty, Loyalty, Respect, Kindness, Self-Reliance, and Self-Discipline, faculty uplift students, partner with parents, and build community every day.

job.title: Children's Community School Transitional Kindergarten Associate Teacher
job.description:
Position Description

Position Overview

Children’s Community School seeks a warm, reflective, and collaborative Transitional Kindergarten Associate Teacher to help create a joyful, inclusive classroom where young children learn through play, inquiry, relationships, and meaningful participation in their community. Working in close partnership with the Lead Teacher, the Associate Teacher supports the academic, social-emotional, physical, and creative development of each child while contributing to a responsive and engaging classroom environment.

This role requires prior experience in early childhood development and previous work with children in a classroom or other group setting. The successful candidate understands that young children are capable thinkers, communicators, problem-solvers, and community members whose ideas and identities should shape their learning.

Our Progressive Approach

Our program centers the whole child. Teachers observe closely, listen carefully, and design experiences that grow from children’s questions, interests, developmental needs, and lived experiences. Learning is active and connected across subject areas. Classrooms value collaboration, curiosity, creativity, reflection, social justice, and the many ways children express what they know.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Partner with the Lead Teacher to plan and facilitate developmentally appropriate, play-based, inquiry-driven learning experiences.
  • Support a classroom culture in which children feel known, respected, safe, and empowered to participate.
  • Guide individuals and small groups through hands-on learning in early literacy, mathematics, science, social studies, art, movement, and outdoor exploration.
  • Use observation, documentation, and reflection to understand children’s development, inform instruction, and contribute to student assessment.
  • Support children’s social-emotional growth, including self-regulation, communication, conflict resolution, independence, and collaborative problem-solving.
  • Use positive, respectful guidance and developmentally responsive classroom-management practices.
  • Prepare materials, organize learning spaces, and help maintain a welcoming, accessible, and engaging classroom environment.
  • Provide active supervision and attend to children’s health, safety, and well-being during classroom activities, transitions, meals, rest, outdoor play, and field experiences.
  • Recognize and respond to varied learning styles, strengths, identities, languages, cultures, family structures, and support needs.
  • Communicate professionally and respectfully with colleagues and families while maintaining confidentiality and appropriate boundaries.
  • Participate in staff meetings, professional learning, school events, and the shared work of the CCS community.
  • Receive feedback with openness, reflect on practice, and contribute ideas as an engaged member of the teaching team.
  • Perform other duties that support the classroom and school program as assigned.

Required Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience or training in early childhood development, early childhood education, child development, or a closely related field.
  • Previous experience working with young children in a classroom, preschool, childcare, camp, after-school program, or comparable group setting.
  • A clear understanding of developmentally appropriate practice for children in Transitional Kindergarten.
  • Ability to build caring, respectful relationships with children and support a diverse community of learners.
  • Strong collaboration, communication, organization, reliability, and follow-through.
  • Ability to remain attentive and engaged while supervising children throughout the school day.
  • Commitment to equity, inclusion, anti-bias education, and ongoing professional growth.
  • Ability to meet all applicable school, licensing, background-check, health, and safety requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • College coursework, certificate, or degree in early childhood education, child development, education, or a related field.
  • Experience in a progressive, inquiry-based, play-based, constructivist, or project-based learning environment.
  • Experience using observation and documentation to make children’s thinking and learning visible.
  • Current pediatric first aid and CPR certification, or willingness to obtain certification.

Professional Qualities

The ideal candidate is patient, playful, observant, flexible, and grounded. They approach children with genuine curiosity, communicate with care, value teamwork, and understand that teaching young children requires both thoughtful planning and responsiveness in the moment.

Physical and Work Environment Expectations

The position involves frequent movement throughout indoor and outdoor learning spaces; sitting on the floor; standing, bending, and kneeling; assisting children with classroom routines; and lifting or carrying classroom materials. Reasonable accommodations may be made for qualified individuals in accordance with applicable law.

Compensation and Benefits

$34-$37 per hour. Working hours will be from 8:30 a.m. – 2:20 p.m. and on Thursdays 8:30 a.m. – 2:00 p.m.

September – June.

How to Apply

Please submit a resume and brief letter of interest describing your experience with young children, your work in classroom or group settings, and your interest in progressive education to careers@ccsteaches.org.

Equal Opportunity

Children’s Community School is committed to building an inclusive community and providing equal employment opportunities. We welcome applicants whose identities, experiences, and perspectives strengthen our school community.

job.title: Deerfield Academy Systems Administrator
job.description:
Position Description & Application

**SIGN-ON BONUS**

The successful candidate will receive a $1,000 sign-on bonus ($500 paid at time of hire and $500 paid at the end of 90 days of employment.

Reporting to the Assistant Director of Infrastructure and Security, the Systems Administrator manages and secures the Academy’s infrastructure, identity, and cloud environments through automation, identity and access management, vulnerability and patch management, and the integration of cloud and on-premises systems to ensure reliable technology services.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities

  • Administer and maintain the Academy's on-premises and cloud-based server infrastructure, including Windows and Linux systems, virtualization platforms, storage systems, and associated services.
  • Lead the Academy's vulnerability management program by conducting vulnerability assessments, coordinating remediation efforts, tracking risk reduction activities, and ensuring timely resolution of identified issues.
  • Manage and maintain patch management processes for server operating systems, infrastructure services, virtualization platforms, and third-party server applications to ensure security and compliance.
  • Develop and maintain automation solutions using scripting and systems management tools to improve operational efficiency, standardization, and service reliability.
  • Administer identity and access management systems, including Hybrid Active Directory, Entra ID, single sign-on (SSO), multi-factor authentication (MFA), role-based access controls, and user lifecycle management.
  • Configure and support Microsoft 365 services, including Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, and related collaboration technologies.
  • Collaborate with Infrastructure and Security staff to manage DNS, DHCP, certificate services, authentication systems, and device registration processes.
  • Monitor system performance, availability, capacity, and security using centralized monitoring, logging, and alerting tools.
  • Research, evaluate, recommend, and implement infrastructure technologies that improve reliability, security, operational efficiency, and user experience.
  • Support incident response activities, digital record retention requirements, eDiscovery processes, and security investigations as needed.
  • Develop and maintain backup, recovery, and disaster recovery solutions to ensure institutional resilience.
  • Create and maintain accurate technical documentation, system standards, operational procedures, and configuration records.
  • Participate in infrastructure projects, technology upgrades, and strategic initiatives led by Information Technology Services.
  • Participate in the ITS technical on-call rotation and provide after-hours support when necessary.
  • Provide Tier 2 technical support and escalation assistance for complex workstations, operating system, application, identity, and account-related issues.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Job Specifications

  • This position requires a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, or a related field; or mastery of the required skills listed below.
  • 5-7 years of experience administering enterprise systems, servers, and infrastructure in a complex environment required
  • Experience in educational, nonprofit, or similar mission-driven organizations preferred.
  • Industry certifications such as Microsoft, VMware, CompTIA Server+, Security+, AZ-104, VCP, CISSP, or comparable certifications are preferred.
  • Strong experience administering Windows Server and Linux operating systems in on-premises and cloud environments.
  • Experience managing virtualization platforms such as VMware vSphere, Hyper-V, Nutanix, Proxmox or KVM.
  • Demonstrated experience with systems automation and scripting using PowerShell, Python, Bash, or similar technologies.
  • Knowledge of patch management, vulnerability management, configuration management, and security remediation processes.
  • Strong understanding of Microsoft 365, Entra ID (Azure AD), Active Directory, Group Policy, multi-factor authentication, and identity management technologies.
  • Experience administering Microsoft 365 services, including Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, and Entra ID required
  • Experience with enterprise systems management, monitoring, logging, backup, recovery, and disaster recovery platforms.
  • Familiarity with cybersecurity frameworks, security best practices, vulnerability management methodologies, and security hardening standards.
  • Working knowledge of DNS, DHCP, certificate services, networking fundamentals, and authentication technologies.
  • Experience troubleshooting and resolving complex Windows, macOS, Microsoft 365, authentication, and endpoint-related issues.
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects and operational responsibilities simultaneously.
  • Demonstrated commitment to continuous improvement through automation and process optimization.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Excellent organizational and documentation skills.
  • Strong customer service orientation and commitment to supporting the institution's mission.
  • Demonstrated commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging.
  • Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion and professionalism.

Physical Job Demands

  • Close visual acuity to analyze data and figures and view a computer monitor
  • Ability to sustain substantial movements of the wrists, hands and/or fingers; or to dictate instructions to a computer
  • Ability to sit or stand at a desk or table for extended periods of time
  • Light Physical Requirements, which include exerting up to 20 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 10 pounds of force frequently, and/or a negligible amount of force constantly to move objects

Working Conditions

The worker is mainly in an office environment and is not substantially exposed to adverse environmental conditions.

Special Instructions for Applicants

Application materials must include:

  • A cover letter summarizing interests and qualifications
  • A complete resume or curriculum vitae

Compensation & Benefits

Deerfield Academy offers a competitive total compensation package, where base compensation or salary is just one component. Pay within the published range is determined by factors such as qualifications, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience, allowing for growth and progression within the role.

We also offer a comprehensive suite of benefits to eligible employees, including:

  • Health & Financial: Medical, dental, and vision insurance; a 403(b)-retirement plan; and employer-paid life and disability plans.
  • Time Off: Generous paid time off and paid holidays.
  • Campus Perks: Tuition remission, fitness center access and complimentary dining hall meals

job.title: Burgundy Farm Country Day School Middle School Science and Math Teacher
job.description:
Position Description

This Middle School teaching position combines math and science, with one section of math and three sections of science. The math section is for 7th grade, and the science sections are for 6th, 7th, and 8th grades.

Math is taught primarily using the Math in Focus program, supplemented with additional resources. Science is interdisciplinary, combining Earth, Life, Space, Physical, and Engineering into a thematic approach.

The Middle School Science and Math teacher will also serve as a grade-level advisor, meeting with a group of advisees each morning to start the day and at periodic points throughout the week.

The qualified candidate will have:

  • An appreciation for and desire to work with Middle School students
  • Genuine appreciation for math and science ideas
  • Experience and expertise teaching math and science concepts
  • A collaborative spirit, interest in team-teaching, and planning
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills
  • Proven commitment to meeting students where they are, a developmental mindset, and an ability to differentiate for varying learning styles and abilities
  • Demonstrated commitment to supporting diversity, equity, and inclusivity
  • Interest in outdoor, hands-on, and environmental education

Details and Hours:

  • This is a full-time, 10-month teaching position
  • The workday runs from 8:00 am to 3:45 pm, Monday through Friday (note: Faculty meetings are held on Wednesdays from 2:45 pm to 5:00 pm)
  • Some after-school clubs or coaching may be required
  • School is closed for most national holidays and Winter and Spring Break

Compensation: Salary is competitive and commensurate with experience. The school offers a generous benefits package, including professional development opportunities.

How to Apply: Please submit a letter of interest and résumé to Jared Givarz, Middle School Head and Assistant Head of School, at hiring@burgundyfarm.org.

Burgundy Farm Country Day School actively maintains its commitment to equal opportunity for all employees. To fulfill this commitment, we recruit, hire, promote, and retain individuals in all job titles without regard to race, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, and related medical conditions), religion, age, national origin, sexual orientation, military status, or disability.

job.title: Deerfield Academy Director of Music
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Reporting to the Director of Arts and the Dean of Faculty, the Director of Music teaches music classes and works collaboratively with music faculty, adjunct instructors, and other visual and performing arts colleagues to support and administer a music program characterized by excellence, strong student participation, and meaningful community engagement.

Responsibilities

Program Leadership

  • Set and maintain the mission and vision of the Music Program, in alignment with Deerfield Academy’s core values, and in the best interests of students;
  • Promote, organize, and facilitate public demonstrations of the Music Program, including on-campus, domestic, and international performances, and with the Director of Arts, ensure cohesion of those events with other campus events by effectively communicating about schedules and content;
  • Effectively collaborate with colleagues within the Visual and Performing Arts Department, and across campus, to create and promote a spirit of collegiality and respect;
  • Support Music performances for major campus events, including Commencement, Baccalaureate, Convocation, MLK Day, and other Academy events as needed;
  • Produce and coordinate the guest artist series, including communication with artists and collaboration with the Director of Arts and relevant Academy offices;
  • Prioritize the well-being of students within the Music Program, and communicate effectively and urgently about student health and well-being with advisors, class deans, and Deerfield’s health and medical professionals;
  • Steward the Academy’s budgetary resources devoted to the Music Program by carefully tracking program spending to ensure it fits within budgeted totals, participating in yearly budget planning, and making capital requests when needed;
  • Ensure proper management and storage of materials and equipment used by the Arts Program, in collaboration with campus partners;
  • Communicate with prospective and current families of Deerfield students, and effectively share information about opportunities for families to engage with the Arts Program through performances, exhibitions, and more.

Teaching

  • Teach two music courses every term in subject areas of expertise, including one in an instrumental performance music class (like Band or Chamber Music), and one in Music Production, Composition, or Analysis;
  • Conduct the Deerfield community Orchestra, made up of students, faculty, staff, and select professional musicians, in Monday evening rehearsals and in two major performances per year, with brief showcases on family weekends;
  • Serve as Head Coach of the Music Co-curricular for three terms (Fall, Winter, and Spring) during the week, including leadership of The Other Doors house band at School Meetings, and the organization of service performances once per term;
  • Support other teachers in the Music Program in reviewing and updating their courses’ curriculum and repertoire as needed;
  • With the Director of Arts, schedule and manage public presentations of the Music Program, including performances, exhibitions, and more;
  • Collaborate with other Arts program leaders in Dance, Theater, and Visual Arts on interdisciplinary projects in the academic, cocurricular, and extracurricular realms;
  • Keep students and faculty advisors informed about registering for appropriate classes offered in the Music Program;
  • With program colleagues, maintain and update the Music Program’s online content;
  • Provide extra help for students in the Music Program’s academic, cocurricular, and extracurricular realms, during Deerfield’s weekly Extra Help time, and at other times as arranged.

Recruitment, Admissions, and Yield

  • Develop Program strategies for recruitment, retention, and yield of prospective students, including the presentation of Arts at Open Houses, Spring Visit Days, and other public events;
  • Collaborate with the Admissions Office to attract prospective students, meet applicants, and maintain communications with students who express a strong interest in Music at Deerfield;
  • Review video recordings from prospective applicants, submitted via SlideRoom, to identify students who would make a verified impact on our Music Program;
  • Collaboratively review and approve Program promotional materials designed by the Admissions Office and Communications;
  • Actively encourage new and current students and adult members of the community to join the program’s activities, and provide extra support for students trying the Program for the first time, and those with less experience.

Staff Supervision

  • Manage Deerfield’s adjunct Music Faculty, including overseeing coordination, communication, support, and program alignment;
  • Assess staffing needs to anticipate timely hiring of part-time and intermittent Music Lesson Instructors and Coaches;
  • Coordinate recruitment and orientation through Human Resources, according to the Academy’s stated Best Practices in Hiring;
  • Approve accurate time and attendance of all work performed by Music Lesson Instructors and Coaches to ensure timely payment of wages.

Advising:

  • Advise 6 - 8 students to assist them with their academic and personal challenges and liaise with parents in an effective and timely way;
  • Meet individually and regularly with each of their advisees to help them adapt to and thrive in Deerfield life;
  • Monitor advisees’ academic progress, direct them to additional support if necessary, and guide them through the course selection process;
  • Encourage advisees to stretch themselves and take advantage of Deerfield’s co-curricular program, extra-curricular activities and leadership opportunities;
  • Meet with their advisees for lunch once a week and generally engage in meetings with them once every two weeks;
  • Write two advisor reports per year, one in January and the other in June, to record the personal and academic progress of each one of their advisees.

Other:

  • Supervise a table in the dining hall four-to-five times per week to engage students in family-style meals, promoting civil conversation and small group interactions;
  • Attend department and.or faculty meetings once a week;
  • Participate on faculty committees as needed;
  • Write college recommendations letters for students who make such a request;
  • Monitor student progress and stay abreast of regular updates about schedules, programs and policies by reading school emails and the Employee FYIs;
  • Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

We are looking for candidates who exhibit excellence in the classroom and who can help develop in students the fundamental learning traits outlined in The Deerfield Student and A Framework For Schools. Beyond the classroom, candidates must be prepared to fully engage in the activities and less formal spaces that help define a strong residential educational community. Additionally, candidates for this position will possess the following specific attributes/qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree required, advance degree preferred;
  • 3-5 years of leadership experience within a musical organization or school music program;
  • Demonstrated expertise as a conductor of musical ensembles;
  • Proficiency with and ability to instruct students in Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) tools;
  • Significant experience using Sibelius, or similar music notation software;
  • Excellent communication skills;
  • High level of patience and diplomacy;
  • Excellent office, computer and data-entry skills;
  • Excellent organization, oral and written communication skills;
  • Ability to multi-task effectively;
  • Ability to handle highly confidential information;
  • Ability to work independently as well as part of a team;
  • Detail-oriented;
  • A sense of humor;
  • Demonstrated commitment to diversity and inclusion and to serving the needs of a diverse community.

Physical Job Demands

  • Close visual acuity to view a computer terminal, analyze text, data and/or figures, and to read for 2-5 hours at a time;
  • Ability to frequently stand and/or sit for sustained periods of time;
  • Ability to frequently reach items and paperwork;
  • Ability to frequently sustain substantial movements of the wrists, hands and/or fingers;
  • Ability to frequently receive and communicate information;
  • Ability to occasionally stoop or kneel;
  • Ability to occasionally lift/carry/push up to 25 pounds.

Working Conditions

The worker is typically in an office environment and not substantially exposed to adverse environmental conditions.

Disclaimer

The above job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this classification. This job description is not intended to be construed as a comprehensive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required of personnel so classified. It is expected that job duties and responsibilities will develop over time commensurate with performance.

Application materials must include a cover letter (specific to this position) and a resume. Candidates may also submit a brief statement of educational philosophy.

Compensation & Benefits

Deerfield Academy offers a competitive total compensation package, where base compensation or salary is just one component. Pay within the published range is determined by factors such as qualifications, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience, allowing for growth and progression within the role.

We also offer a comprehensive suite of benefits to eligible employees, including:

  • Health & Financial: Medical, dental, and vision insurance; a 403(b)-retirement plan; and employer-paid life and disability plans.
  • Time Off: Generous paid time off and paid holidays.
  • Campus Perks: Tuition remission, fitness center access and complimentary dining hall meals

job.title: International School Bangkok Outdoor Education Specialist
job.description:
Position Description

The ISB Educator Profile

ISB educators embody key attributes integrated with our core values to create a vibrant, inclusive learning community. They are adaptable professionals who thrive in dynamic environments, remaining flexible and ready to pivot to meet the evolving needs of our students. As true collaborators, they view education as a shared endeavor—actively co-planning, co-teaching, and building strong relationships with colleagues and families. They serve as optimistic problem solvers who approach every challenge with a positive outlook, turning obstacles into opportunities for innovation and growth. Above all, their practice is student-centered, ensuring that all pedagogical and design choices are rooted in student learning and well-being. Ultimately, ISB educators embody our mission by demonstrating curiosity, courage, and empowerment in their lives, work, and professional growth.

ISB’s ideal candidate combines deep subject expertise and strong pedagogy with humility, drive, and a positive disposition for supporting young learners.

Position Overview

At ISB, we believe that education is a dynamic, creative, and collaborative human endeavor. We are seeking a passionate Outdoor Education Specialist to join our faculty and help students in Grades 5 - 12 explore, investigate, and make sense of the world.

The Outdoor Education Safety & Program Coordinator ensures that all outdoor education programs are thoughtfully structured and operate according to the highest international industry standards.

This role leads the outdoor education team of teachers and instructors, ensuring team members maintain relevant qualifications and remain fully prepared for both daily operations and emergency situations.

Required Qualifications

● Valid teaching license/certification and at least 3 years of relevant teaching experience.

● Experience with inquiry-based learning, ELL instruction, and using PLC data to inform instruction.

● Valid driver's license, with the ability to obtain and maintain a Thai driver's license

● Valid certifications in:

○ Advanced First Aid, AED, and emergency oxygen administration

○ Rock climbing instruction (auto-belay, top-rope, and single-pitch rappelling)

○ Kayaking and canoeing (instruction and water rescue)

○ Pool lifeguarding

○ Physical fitness required to fulfill all field and instructional duties

● Strong expertise in safety systems, risk assessment, emergency response, staff leadership, and program design.

● Proven skills in logistics, budgeting, procurement, and cross-departmental communication.

Mindsets and Dispositions

● Dedicated to student care and Social and Emotional Learning (SEL).

● Strong work ethic, effective communicator, and positive contributor to school culture.

● Adaptable, open-minded, growth-oriented, culturally competent, and reflective.

Core Responsibilities

Operational and instructional Programming::

● Maintaining safety documentation, staff training, and Ready For Operation (RFO) testing.

● Developing and updating Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for generic, rock, and water activities.

● Establishing and updating Emergency Action Plans (EAPs).

● Conducting comprehensive risk assessments.

● Creating and maintaining Activity Safety Cards.

● Managing staff training, official certifications, and annual competency assessments (lifeguarding, rock climbing, kayaking/canoeing, and first aid), maintaining documentation on-site at EWC.

● Performing safety audits on all land, water, and rock climbing equipment, maintaining records at EWC.

● Inspecting and maintaining field first aid kits and emergency response equipment (lightning detectors, AEDs, oxygen units, stretchers).

● Planning, conducting, and reviewing Ready For Operation (RFO) testing, reporting findings to the ISB Leadership Team.

External Safety Audit

● Commissioning and preparing documentation for external desk audits.

● Planning on-site trip audits to align with current international industry standards.

Curriculum & planning

● Coordinating program calendars with Middle and Elementary School Administrators

● Developing and refining Outdoor Education curriculum for Grades 5 through 8.

● Delivering comprehensive safety briefings for all student and staff groups.

ISB Climbing Wall

● Managing climbing wall safety procedures, staff training, curriculum integration, instructor qualifications, and facility access.

● Conducting safety audits for the climbing wall and maintaining inspection records at EWC.

Trip Leadership

● Serving as Administrator-in-Charge on outdoor education trips and providing direct group

supervision as needed.

● Acting as Incident Commander for emergency response across all outdoor education trips.

● Supervising and managing performance for assigned program staff.

Procurement & Budget

● Procuring replacement and supplemental equipment based on safety audit findings and

program needs.

● Preparing the Middle School Outdoor Education budget and submitting proposals to the CFO.

● Managing inventory and procurement for field first aid kits and emergency response equipment.

● Managing Wild Panthers team uniforms and apparel procurement.

● Overseeing the maintenance, servicing, and official use of the program fleet vehicle.

Other

● Create a safe, inclusive environment, differentiating instruction and selecting resources to meet diverse learner needs and backgrounds.

● Utilize varied assessments and student data to monitor progress, adapt instruction, and provide timely, actionable feedback.

● Integrate appropriate technology and contemporary resources to enhance learning and connect classroom concepts with real-world contexts.

● Partner with counselors, administrators, and parents to support students' academic achievement and social-emotional well-being.

● Engage in continuous professional learning, self-reflection, and contribute positively to the school culture.

● Maintain professional obligations, meeting deadlines, honoring schedules, and upholding ISB standards of integrity, respect, and care.

● Strictly uphold ISB expectations for child safeguarding and student well-being.

● Other duties as assigned by the supervisor.

Application Details

Interested candidates should complete the online application (www.isb.ac.th/job-opportunities) at the earliest opportunity and before the deadline of February 1, 2027. Search Associates candidates need only apply through the Search Associates platform, and finalists will be invited to complete the secondary screening via TruFit Talent. All other applicants can apply directly through TruFit Talent using the link provided in the vacancy announcement on the school website.

Please note that if an outstanding applicant is identified early in the search process, ISB reserves the right to make an appointment prior to the deadline.

Compensation and Benefits

ISB provides a competitive compensation and benefits package that is commensurate with the candidate’s experience and aligned with global international school standards. Benefits for this faculty leadership position provided to the employee and up to two dependent children.

job.title: Hong Kong International School Choir Teacher (Grade 6-8)
job.description:
Position Description & Application

In support of the HKIS Mission and Vision, and to meet HKIS Student Learning Results and appropriate grade level and subject area expectations, the Secondary School teacher will carry out broad and specific responsibilities across the following domains: Knowledge of Content, Pedagogy and Students; Instructional Strategies; Management; Assessment; Communication; Collaboration and Professional Practice.

KEY AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY:

KNOWLEDGE OF CONTENT, PEDAGOGY AND STUDENTS:

This describes the breadth and depth of knowledge of the discipline(s) and understanding of HKIS’ Shared Philosophy of Education. For educators this includes planning for instruction, reflection on curriculum content, knowledge of tools and resources, developmental characteristics of students and current pedagogy.

  • Demonstrates a sound knowledge of curricular standards; plans with student awareness and understanding of curricular standards and continually updates professional content knowledge
  • Demonstrates an understanding of levels of cognitive development and learning needs of diverse students through planning and instruction that reflect academic, cultural, spiritual and individual diversity of students.
  • Designs instructional and assessment opportunities that align with overall learning outcomes and match content appropriately

INSTRUCTIONAL STRATEGIES:

This describes the means by which classroom teachers establish a culture for learning, engage students in learning and deliver content. This includes flexibility in the choice of materials, use of appropriate technology and a variety of presentation, grouping and pacing techniques in response to student learning needs.

  • Utilizes a variety of questioning, discussion and reflection techniques that establishes a positive culture for learning in the classroom
  • Demonstrates and encourages a growth mindset in students that promotes accountability for high quality student work
  • Engages students in learning opportunities that build procedural and conceptual understanding
  • Uses a wide variety of digital and non-digital tools and resources for instruction and application activities

MANAGEMENT

This describes how time and resources are prioritized, organized and allocated to provide an effective learning environment. This involves organizing one's own work, planning work for others, anticipating needs and adjusting resources accordingly. For educators, this includes classroom management.

  • Organizes, adapts and maintains student learning data and resources to inform instructional practice.
  • Maintains a safe, accessible learning environment in the classroom and is able to accommodate a range of physical and social needs
  • Establishes and maintains clear classroom expectations and procedures that promote respect and positive relationships
  • Maintains student learning data to support instruction and assessment

ASSESSMENT

This describes the monitoring of student understanding through a balanced program of developmentally appropriate formative and summative assessments aligned to UbD elements (including articulated standards, enduring understandings, knowledge and skills, misunderstandings and academic vocabulary). This includes providing feedback to students and parents to promote learning and the use of assessment results in planning and instruction.

  • Designs and implements a variety of high quality assessments that are aligned with learning outcomes; this includes the use of rubrics and exemplars consistent with our HKIS Assessment Agreements (Secondary)
  • Collaborates with colleagues across the department and division to align assessment expectations that are clear and developmentally appropriate for students in each course and grade level
  • Is able to provide rich feedback on assessment to students in a timely fashion that furthers the next steps in learning
  • Models and explicitly teaches how students can constructively use feedback from the teacher and/or peers and self-assess to inform their learning.
  • Keeps students and families up to date about assessment feedback and a student’s progress through the learning objectives of a course

Communication

This describes the verbal and non-verbal articulation of messages within the HKIS community (students, parents, colleagues) both in formal and informal situations. This includes clarity and accuracy of information, the choice of the most appropriate medium and active listening to facilitate a mutual understanding of needs, issues and concerns.

  • Provides clear, accurate and timely feedback to stakeholders
  • Maintains respectful dialogue that demonstrates care, respect for others and sensitivity to diversity
  • Proactively communicates with students, parents, colleagues, administrators and school staff as appropriate

Collaboration and Professional Practice

This describes the manner in which individuals build, promote and maintain strong learning communities. This includes building professional and reciprocal relationships, sharing information about students, curriculum and resources that enhance the success of the HKIS community.

  • Demonstrates a high degree of professionalism at all times and strives to uphold HKIS’s core values
  • Is a reflective practitioner and works in collaboration with colleagues, administrators and students in positive ways
  • Upholds the highest standards with regard to student and adult safety and safeguarding; this includes adherence to privacy and acceptable use of data and technology guidelines
  • Demonstrates initiative in professional learning and seeks out opportunities for professional development to enhance knowledge and pedagogical skills

Other

  • Undertake other duties and functions as required that will impact and strengthen the contributions of the department and overall operations of the school.

Minimum requirements and qualifications:

Education:

  • Bachelors degree in relevant subject area, Masters Degree preferred
  • Qualified Teacher Certification

Experience:

  • Minimum 5 years of full time teaching in the subject area
  • Experience in a leading international school with an American-style education preferred
  • Experience in Understanding by Design, Inquiry models and strategies preferred
  • Experience and ability to collaborate with diverse teams of educators preferred

Required skills:

  • Excellent knowledge of the subject content and current pedagogy
  • Excellent knowledge of the developmental needs of students in Grades 6-8
  • Strong grounding in understanding and practice of Standards Based Approaches to instruction and assessment
  • Strong communication skills; ability to communicate effectively (written and verbal) with a diverse community
  • Adept at using educational and classroom technology
  • Strong organizational and time management skills
  • HKIS seeks to hire candidates who are interested in the complex questions of faith and spirituality and who are keen to learn and interact with others of different faith traditions.

Child Protection Statement:

  • At HKIS, each child’s welfare is paramount. We act to ensure that our students enjoy the right to be protected from harm and exploitation and have their welfare safeguarded.

TO APPLY

Interested candidates, please forward your updated resume together with a cover letter and references to recruitment@hkis.edu.hk

  • Minimum 5 years of full time teaching in the subject area
  • Experience in a leading international school with an American-style education preferred
  • Experience in Understanding by Design, Inquiry models and strategies preferred
  • Experience and ability to collaborate with diverse teams of educators preferred

Required skills:

  • Excellent knowledge of the subject content and current pedagogy
  • Excellent knowledge of the developmental needs of students in Grades 6-8
  • Strong grounding in understanding and practice of Standards Based Approaches to instruction and assessment
  • Strong communication skills; ability to communicate effectively (written and verbal) with a diverse community
  • Adept at using educational and classroom technology
  • Strong organizational and time management skills
  • HKIS seeks to hire candidates who are interested in the complex questions of faith and spirituality and who are keen to learn and interact with others of different faith traditions.

Child Protection Statement:

  • At HKIS, each child’s welfare is paramount. We act to ensure that our students enjoy the right to be protected from harm and exploitation and have their welfare safeguarded.

TO APPLY

Interested candidates, please forward your updated resume together with a cover letter and references to recruitment@hkis.edu.hk

job.title: Hong Kong International School Comprehensive Counselor (Grade 9-12)
job.description:
Position Description & Application

HKIS school counselors provide a comprehensive, developmentally appropriate guidance program that promotes students’ personal, social, spiritual, and educational development in accordance with recognized standard of practice for international school counselors.

KEY AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY:

Professional Knowledge

  • Apply knowledge of Social‑Emotional Learning (SEL) competencies (e.g., CASEL framework, ISCA standards), as well as academic and career exploration curricula, to support existing HKIS programs and inform individual counseling practice.
  • Implement current child safeguarding policies, protocols, and standards, and apply appropriate strategies to protect the wellbeing and safety of all students.
  • Incorporate an understanding of the diverse interests, cultural backgrounds, assets, talents, and spiritual identities of students and families into individual counseling, small‑group work, and seminar planning and delivery.
  • Apply current research related to adolescent development (typical and atypical), learning, and key life transitions to counseling practice and student support.

Collaborative Student Support & Responsive Counseling

  • Work closely with a multidisciplinary team that includes classroom teachers, administrators, learning specialists, parents, and outside providers to support the academic, social, and emotional wellbeing of students.
  • Provide responsive services such as child protection and trauma‑informed crisis support.
  • Deliver individual and small‑group, solution‑focused counseling tailored to student needs.

Family Partnership, Faculty Support, and Professional Learning

  • Build strong partnerships with families through parent education and engagement opportunities, such as coffee mornings and parenting workshops.
  • Provide consultation and guidance to faculty and contribute to faculty professional development, particularly in areas such as child protection, student mental health, and wellbeing.

Social‑Emotional Learning & Student Transitions

  • Deliver Social‑Emotional Learning (SEL) and mental health and wellbeing lessons, working in partnership with divisional colleagues.
  • Closely collaborate with administration to support smooth transitions for students joining HKIS and for those departing, ensuring continuity of care and clear communication.

High School Counseling Model & Specialized Experience

The High School counseling program is intentionally designed around a community model. The division is organized into four communities, each served by two counselors, with approximately 50 students per grade level per community.

  • Work collaboratively with a counseling colleague to advise, advocate, and support students across social‑emotional, academic, and college/career domains.
  • Guide families through the full university application process.
  • Teach Counseling Seminars (Grades 9–12) within the Wellbeing Block is essential.
  • Identify and leverage individual and team strengths within a shared leadership model.

Other

  • Undertake other duties and functions as required that will impact and strengthen the contributions of the department and overall operations of the school.

Minimum requirements and qualifications:

Education:

  • Master’s or advanced degree in Counseling or equivalent (School Counseling preferred)
  • Minimum of five years experience as a counselor in a school context at the relevant grade/age level.
  • Experience leading and facilitating parent and student groups within a culturally diverse setting

Experience:

  • Experience working within an evidence-based secondary counseling model
  • Experience of counseling in diverse, multicultural setting
  • Experience working with U.S., U.K., and international university admissions representatives
  • Familiarity with global admissions practices and application platforms

Required skills:

  • Excellent interpersonal skills to collaborate with faculty, parents, students, and administrators
  • Strong written and oral communication skills
  • Working understanding of the ISCA and/ or ASCA counseling framework
  • Interest and experience in curriculum development and delivery, preferably in counseling curriculum
  • Ability to collect and interpret individual and group data
  • Skilled in the use of technology for student planning, documentation, and the virtual delivery of counseling program
  • Enthusiastic about collaboration and professional development

Child Protection Statement:

  • At HKIS, each child’s welfare is paramount. We act to ensure that our students enjoy the right to be protected from harm and exploitation and have their welfare safeguarded.

TO APPLY

Interested candidates, please forward your updated resume together with a cover letter and references to recruitment@hkis.edu.hk
