job.title: Alcuin School Early Childhood Support Specialist
job.description:
Position Description & Application

GENERAL POSITION SUMMARY

The Early Childhood Support Specialist strengthens the daily operation of Alcuin School's Early Childhood programs through reliable classroom coverage and disciplined program support. Reporting to the Director of Early Childhood, the position serves as a qualified substitute teacher in Toddler and Primary classrooms and maintains the records, calendars, and follow-up systems that support Toddler licensing, Montessori recognition, accreditation, and Early Childhood operations.

JOB SCOPE

This is a full-time, 10-month, non-supervisory position supporting approximately 239 Early Childhood students, including 57 Toddler students and 182 Primary students, with an anticipated addition of 20 students during the school year. Weekly priorities shift based on classroom coverage, student needs, recordkeeping deadlines, licensing requirements, and Early Childhood program activities.

The Director of Early Childhood remains the designated child-care center director and retains responsibility for program decisions, employee supervision, policy interpretation, and regulatory compliance. This position does not supervise employees, direct the work of Guides or Assistants, or independently commit the School to a regulatory response.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Early Childhood Classroom Support

  • Provide planned and short notice substitute coverage in Toddler, Primary and MPC/ASE classrooms as assigned by the Director of Early Childhood.
  • Follow the classroom Guide's plans, routines, Montessori practices, and established expectations so students experience continuity, consistency, and a well-prepared environment.
  • Maintain active supervision, required staff-to-child ratios, attendance accountability, health and safety practices, and positive guidance throughout classroom activities, transitions, meals, rest, arrival, dismissal, and outdoor time.
  • Present or support developmentally appropriate Montessori activities within the employee's training and assigned responsibilities; seek direction before modifying classroom plans or established practices.
  • Observe students carefully, document relevant information, and communicate classroom events, injuries, behavioral concerns, or family questions promptly through established reporting channels.
  • Build respectful, professional relationships with children, families, Guides, Assistants, and colleagues while maintaining appropriate confidentiality and role boundaries.
  • Help prepare, restore, and maintain orderly classroom environments and shared materials before, during, and after coverage assignments.

Records, Licensing, Recognition, and Accreditation Support

  • Maintain organized, accurate, and current files for Early Childhood departments, Toddler licensing, Montessori recognition, and school accreditation, including required staff, child, training, health and safety, and operational records.
  • Follow up with parents and guardians to obtain missing or updated student health forms and route questions requiring clinical or administrative judgment to the appropriate school contact.
  • Prepare professional development certificates and maintain supporting training documentation for licensing, recognition, accreditation, and school records.
  • Track recurring compliance deadlines, required postings, permits, certifications, training, drills, inspections, renewals, and follow-up items; notify the Director of Early Childhood of upcoming requirements and unresolved concerns.
  • Review routine records for completeness and consistency, identify gaps or potential deficiencies, and promptly escalate them to the Director of Early Childhood for direction and resolution.
  • Prepare documentation and facilities for licensing visits, assist during inspections as directed, and maintain records of findings, corrective actions, and completion dates.
  • Monitor updates to Texas HHSC Child Care Regulation standards and related school procedures, summarize operational changes for the Director, and support approved implementation and staff communication.
  • Support accurate staff onboarding and annual compliance processes by collecting required documents and coordinating with Human Resources and program leadership.
  • Maintain appropriate confidentiality and records security when handling student, family, employee, medical, background-check, or regulatory information.
  • Provide administrative support for Toddler program safety and compliance systems without independently setting policy, directing employees, or representing the School as its designated child-care center director.

Early Childhood Program Support

  • Supervise the Toddler gate during assigned carpool periods and follow established arrival, dismissal, security, and student-release procedures.
  • Assist with planning, logistics, and ordering for Parent Education programs, staff events, and speech-language programming.
  • Support Early Childhood purchasing throughout the school year, including maintaining and processing approved Amazon wish lists and routing requests for authorization.
  • Support substitute orientation by preparing materials, reviewing established classroom and operational procedures, and directing policy or performance questions to the Director of Early Childhood.

Program Collaboration and Communication

  • Work closely with the Director of Early Childhood to prioritize classroom coverage and licensing work when needs compete.
  • Coordinate documentation and process support with Human Resources, Health Services, Facilities, and other departments while keeping program decisions with the Director.
  • Participate in required training, faculty meetings, emergency drills, and professional learning scheduled during regular working hours.
  • Contribute accurate information and practical recommendations that strengthen consistent practices across Toddler and Primary programs.

MARGINAL FUNCTIONS

  • Provide limited clerical or program support related to Early Childhood operations when classroom coverage and licensing priorities permit.
  • Perform other closely related duties assigned by the Director of Early Childhood that are consistent with the purpose and level of the position.

Qualifications

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES, AND OTHER REQUIREMENTS

Required

  • Ability to provide documents verifying authorization to work in the U.S.
  • Must pass Criminal Background Checks and Drug Testing
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • AMI Assistants to Infancy diploma
  • At least three years of successful Montessori classroom experience.
  • Experience maintaining child-care licensing documentation and the ability to learn, interpret, track, and apply current Texas HHSC Child Care Regulation requirements and Alcuin policies under the direction of the Director of Early Childhood.
  • Working knowledge of Montessori theory and practice for children from approximately 18 months through age three.
  • Current pediatric first aid and CPR certification, or ability to obtain required certification before working independently with children, and satisfactory completion and maintenance of all background checks, training, and other qualifications required by Alcuin and applicable child-care regulations.
  • Intermediate proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint.
  • Basic proficiency with Canva and the ability to create or update simple certificates, signs, and event materials.

Preferred

  • AMI Primary diploma in addition to the required AMI Assistants to Infancy diploma.
  • Bachelor's degree in early childhood education, child development, education, or a related field.
  • At least three years of successful Toddler classroom experience.
  • Experience in an independent school or an AMI-recognized Montessori program.
  • Experience preparing for Texas child-care licensing inspections or maintaining corrective-action documentation.
  • Experience in administration.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY

None. The position may support consistent implementation of established licensing and classroom procedures but does not assign work, evaluate performance, approve leave, discipline employees, or exercise delegated supervisory authority over Guides, Assistants, substitutes, or other employees.

INTERNAL CONTACTS

  • Director of Early Childhood; Toddler and Primary Guides and Assistants; Early Childhood substitutes.
  • Human Resources, Health Services, Facilities, Admissions, and other school departments involved in records, safety, staffing, or student services.

EXTERNAL CONTACTS

  • Texas HHSC Child Care Regulation representatives, Montessori recognition and accreditation contacts, training providers, service vendors, and other external parties, as authorized by the Director of Early Childhood.
  • Parents and guardians in connection with assigned classroom responsibilities and within established communication protocols.

EQUIPMENT AND TECHNOLOGY USED

  • Standard office and classroom equipment, Montessori classroom materials, Microsoft Office, Canva, and school-approved communication, student information, purchasing, and electronic recordkeeping systems.

JOB AND WORKING CONDITIONS

  • Works on campus during Alcuin's regular school-day hours in classroom, office, and indoor and outdoor school environments.
  • Must be available to move between planned licensing work and classroom coverage, including short-notice substitute assignments during the regular workday.
  • Accurately records all hours worked and follows Alcuin procedures for schedule changes and advance approval of overtime; overtime is compensated in accordance with applicable law.

ABOUT ALCUIN SCHOOL

Alcuin School, one of the largest accredited Montessori schools in the U.S., along with the International Baccalaureate Middle Years and Diploma Programs, provides an ideal learning environment that guides and nurtures the full development of the child from 18 months to 18 years of age. Alcuin School is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All persons will receive consideration for employment without regard to gender (including gender identity, gender expression and gender reassignment), race (including color, nationality, ethnic or national origin), religion or belief, marital or civil partnership status, disability, age, sexual orientation, pregnancy or maternity, trade union membership or membership in any other legally protected category. We strive to create an inclusive environment, empower employees, and embrace diversity. We encourage everyone to respond.

job.title: American International School of Johannesburg Director of Student Support Serv.
job.description:
Position Description & Application

CAMPUS: Johannesburg Campus | SUPERVISOR: School Director | START DATE: 1 August 2027

POSTING DATE: 29 September 2027 | CLOSING DATE: 16 October 2026

Inspire Learning to Build Our Better World. At the American International School of Johannesburg (AISJ), we are committed to providing an exceptional education that empowers global citizens to fulfill their future purpose. Our vision is to inspire learning to build a better world. We seek a dedicated and passionate professional who aligns with our commitment to excellence and believes in the transformative power of education. Every team member is crucial in creating a supportive and nurturing learning environment. At AISJ, we value every employee as a learner and expect them to embody and support the AISJ Portrait of Learner (Resilience, Mindful, Thinker, Globally Connected, Curious, Contributor) through their work. We are dedicated to justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion within our school community.

POSITION OVERVIEW

The Director of Student Support Services (DSSS) is a mission-critical executive leader responsible for the strategic vision, alignment, and oversight of inclusive practices across the Pre-K through Grade 12 continuum. This role integrates the leadership of Learning Support, English Language Acquisition (ELA/ELL), Counseling, and Life-Centered Education Services.

The Director will champion a Multi-Tiered System of Support (MTSS) and Universal Design for Learning (UDL) framework to ensure that every student—including those requiring high-ability challenge or intensive intervention—experiences a sense of belonging and academic success. As a key member of the Child Safeguarding Team, the Director ensures that safety, well-being, and equity are at the heart of the AISJ experience.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Education: Master’s Degree in Special Education and/or Educational Leadership or related field
  • Certification: Valid K-12 Teaching and/or Administrative license or certification from a recognized educational authority.
  • Minimum of 8 years in education
  • Successful experience working collaboratively with school leaders, teachers, and outside service providers.
  • Experience working in an American system within special education or student support services
  • Successful experience in working collaboratively with parents of children with learning challenges.
  • Emotional Intelligence: Exhibits patience, empathy, and the ability to balance ambition with humility.
  • Communication: Exceptional command of written and spoken English; ability to present complex data clearly to diverse stakeholders.
  • Collaborative Spirit: A "team-first" mentality that values diverse perspectives and builds trusting relationships with Principals, parents, teachers, and students.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • Technical Expertise: Deep knowledge of WIDA assessments, IEP development, Life-Centered Education Services, and instructional coaching models.
  • Two or more years in a leadership role and/or a role that has campus/district-wide responsibility.
  • Proven track record in implementing complex change initiatives and MTSS frameworks.
  • Comprehensive understanding and work within a program providing
  • Support services for exceptional learners
  • In Learning Support
  • For students with significant cognitive or functional support needs

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Strategic Leadership & Vision

  • Execute a clear vision for Student Support Services (SSS) that aligns with the AISJ Vision- Purpose and Community Principles.
  • Provide cross-campus guidance to ensure consistent, equitable, and aligned programming from Early Years through High School.
  • Lead the development of a coherent approach to Inclusion and Challenge, ensuring high-ability learners are stretched within an inclusive framework
  • Lead the coordination of services for students with high support needs

2. Multi-Tiered System of Support (MTSS) & Data

  • Oversee Tier 1–3 practices across academic, behavioral, and social-emotional domains.
  • Design and implement school-wide data systems to gather and analyze evidence of learning, ensuring that interventions are timely, ethical, and effective.
  • Collaborate with the Teaching and Learning Team to implement universal screening tools to gather early intervention data.

3. Admissions & Enrollment

  • Collaborate with the Director of Advancement and the Admissions Team to review student applications and make data-informed decisions regarding placement and support capacity.
  • Ensure the school can fulfill its promise of support for students with identified learning variations upon entry.
  • Work with the Advancement Team to ensure the program's long-term sustainability through consistent enrollment and client satisfaction.

4. Personnel & Resource Management

  • Supervise, in conjunction with Divisional principals, SSS faculty and program leaders across all divisions.
  • Coordinate workload calibration and caseload management, ensuring resources are balanced between campuses and departments.
  • Manage the departmental budget and identify external consultants and specialists to enhance internal services.

5. Child Safeguarding & Well-being

  • Serve as a member of the Schoolwide Child Safeguarding Team, coordinating protocols, reporting incidents, and ensuring compliance with international best practices.
  • Collaborate with crisis management and counseling teams, fostering a holistic approach to student safety and mental health.

6. Professional Development & Advocacy

  • Design and facilitate professional learning for all faculty on asset-based language acquisition, differentiated instruction, and socio-emotional well-being.
  • Advocate for students with diverse needs, ensuring their voices are represented in school-wide strategic initiatives.

APPLICATION PROCESS

To apply, please complete the electronic form [Click here]. Information captured will be securely stored and used for a reference check on the candidate's compatibility. AISJ reserves the right to appoint the strongest candidate before the closing date if required.

SAFEGUARDING & CHILD PROTECTION

AISJ maintains robust child protection policies to ensure a safe, secure, and caring environment for our students. All employees must undergo criminal background checks, attend annual training, and sign a safeguarding agreement.

PRIVACY

By submitting your CV, you consent to AISJ processing your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy, accessible at AISJ Privacy Policy, and under the Protection of Personal Information Act of 2013.

OTHER INFORMATION

  • The first contract is for two years and then extended each year based on an annual review.
  • The package for this Administrative position is competitive with others like international schools around the world.

job.title: Northfield Mount Hermon Mathematics Teacher
job.description:

Northfield Mount Hermon, an independent co-educational boarding school in western Massachusetts, seeks a dynamic individual to teach in a challenging secondary level mathematics program. This position begins with the fall semester of the 2027-2028 academic year.

The successful applicant will have at least a bachelor’s degree in mathematics or a related field (master’s preferred) with a background sufficient to teach Algebra 1 through Calculus and experience teaching mathematics. Knowledge of and experience with curricular design and development are preferred. Additional qualifications include strong interpersonal and communication skills, including a demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with colleagues, and experience using technology in the classroom, including graphing calculators, computer-based math applications and Google Apps for Education. Experience teaching computer science and statistics will be a plus for this position.

Candidates must be familiar with boarding school life and have an interest in making a positive impact on the lives of adolescents. They will demonstrate experience in equity and inclusion work that promotes a diverse community environment and a clear understanding of anti-bias education.

Responsibilities of the position include a combination of classroom teaching, student advising, resident dormitory supervision, and coaching or equivalents. Candidates are encouraged to include in their application experiences that may support our athletic and student life program.

job.title: Francis Parker School Upper School Learning Specialist
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Job Type

Full-time

Description

Exciting Opportunity at Francis Parker School in San Diego, California

Francis Parker School (Parker) is seeking an enthusiastic, dedicated, and passionate educator who shares its core values: Students First, Academic Excellence, Global Perspective, Strength of Character, Inclusive Community, and No Limit to Better. Collegial and collaborative, Parker faculty create a learning environment that is dynamic and engaging. Parker faculty are content and pedagogical experts who invest in professional growth generously supported by the School. Importantly, Parker’s unswerving commitment to being a diverse, equitable, and inclusive community creates a culture of respect for all.

If Parker’s values and school culture resonate with you, we encourage you to consider this opportunity.

About Parker:

Parker is a coeducational independent day school in San Diego, California with 1,330 students in Junior Kindergarten through Grade 12. Founded in 1912, the school’s mission is “to create and inspire a diverse community of independent thinkers whose academic excellence, global perspective, and strength of character prepare them to make a meaningful difference in the world.” Parker has two campuses: one in Mission Hills (Lower School, Junior Kindergarten - Grade 5) and a second in Linda Vista (Middle and Upper School, Grades 6 - 12).

Job Description:

The Upper School Learning Specialist serves our Upper School population and supports students with identified learning differences by providing appropriate interventions; supports teachers in their efforts to advance students with different learning needs within the classroom; and works with parents, students, and outside professionals in order to better support academic progress. This role focuses on the provision of targeted instructional and literacy support to students in grades 9-12 through individual and small group instruction. The learning specialist works to close achievement gaps, reinforce core concepts, and build student confidence. This role also involves close collaboration with classroom teachers to help students meet grade-level academic standards. The specialist’s broad area of responsibility is to ensure that each student may learn and flourish academically, socially, and emotionally, and upon graduation is prepared for a successful transition to college.

The Upper School Learning Specialist reports to the Head of Student Success and Wellness.

Requirements

Essential Duties/Responsibilities:

  • Provides small-group or one-on-one instruction to students performing below expectations in reading comprehension, written expression and other literacy skills.
  • Uses diagnostic and formative assessments to identify learning needs, inform instruction, monitor progress and adjust intervention strategies.
  • Develops solid knowledge of the Scope and Sequence and all other grade-level curricula in each content area taught in the upper school, including the essential information, concepts and skills, so as to better support students and assist classroom teachers.
  • Differentiates instruction as needed (in content, process, product, and environment).
  • In collaboration with the Head of Student Success and Wellness, creates an individualized learning profile (LP) for each student requiring specialized instructional support.
  • Delivers targeted interventions aligned with the student’s learning profile, classroom instruction, state, national, and content area standards.
  • Serves as case manager and oversees the implementation of each student’s learning profile, collaborating with classroom teachers, counselors, and other faculty.
  • Holds annual meetings for all students with LPs.
  • Assists teachers in classrooms to help adjust and enrich curricular approaches and improve pedagogy.
  • Establishes and maintains frequent communication with parents about their child’s academic, social and emotional progress and needs. This includes discussing grades, phone calls, learning management systems, email blasts, etc.
  • In collaboration with the Head of Upper School, the Head of Student Success and Wellness, and the other upper school learning specialist, co-facilitates the US Student Support Team meetings and implements protocols for determining who will receive additional support.
  • Communicates student progress with the Student Success Team, teachers, and advisors
  • Provides support to students referred by the Student Success Team who are struggling academically due to concussions or extended absences.
  • Works collaboratively with Deans, Department Chairs and the Middle and Lower School learning specialists.
  • Works in conjunction with the Head of Student Success and Wellness to recommend tutors, psycho-educational referrals, etc.
  • Consults with outside specialists attending to students’ needs.
  • Coordinates scheduling for student observations, evaluations, meetings, and other required activities with outside providers when approved by the Head of Upper School and Head of Student Success and Wellness.
  • Proctors and supervises students utilizing accommodations in the Center for Academic Success testing room
  • Seeks out new and innovative curricula, texts, and technological applications for implementation in our classrooms.
  • When necessary, meets with the appropriate teacher(s) and department heads to ensure the easy and comfortable assimilation of all new students.
  • Remains current with accepted and appropriate instructional theory, practice and research. Including engaging in regular and strategic professional development to advance the role of the Learning Specialist (including local and national seminars and conferences).
  • Provides skillful classroom management practices (routines and procedures) to ensure a safe, orderly, positive, enjoyable, and productive learning environment.
  • Collaborates with the College Counseling Department and families to provide college transition guidance for students with identified learning support needs.
  • Provides professional development for faculty.
  • Attends and participates in faculty meetings, committee meetings, school functions, and professional development activities during and after school hours as needed, appropriate and assigned.
  • Upholds the philosophy, principles, policies, and procedures of Francis Parker School.
  • Represents Francis Parker School positively in the school community and the wider community.
  • Adheres to strict student confidentiality.
  • Demonstrated knowledge and experience with record keeping and documentation of service provision.
  • Performs other tasks as deemed necessary and appropriate by the Head of Student Success and Wellness.

Qualifications:

  • Has significant experience within a thriving Learning Specialist Program and/or experience building a Learning Specialist program.
  • Bachelor’s degree or higher from an accredited institution, (Master’s degree preferred)
  • Professional Teacher Certification (including special education).
  • Minimum of 3 years of teaching experience, with a literacy focus
  • Extensive coursework and experience in special education or educational therapy.
  • Knowledge of intervention strategies, differentiated instruction, and data-driven teaching.
  • Experience interpreting psychoeducational evaluations and translating results into accommodations and interventions that reflect empirically based best practices.
  • Experience working with High School students both individually and in groups.
  • Knowledge of relevant technology.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to implement formal and informal assessment programs.
  • Multicultural curriculum development and culturally responsive teaching experience
  • Strong interpersonal and cultural competency skills when working with students, parents, faculty, and School leadership.
  • High standards and high expectations for students.
  • Commitment to being a positive and contributing member of the professional community.
  • A love of children, a passionate commitment to secondary education, and a desire to work with all types of learners.
  • Extraordinary communication and presentation skills.

Salary and Benefits:

Parker is committed to attracting and retaining the highest quality faculty and staff through a substantial compensation plan, including competitive salary, TIAA retirement benefits, and full medical/dental coverage. Individual salary is negotiable depending on years of experience and educational background.

Salary Range: $82,000 - $120,000 per year

The actual salary will be determined by the candidate’s educational degree and their years of full-time teaching experience. The starting salary listed reflects this position’s minimum experience and educational requirements; the ending salary listed represents the top of the salary structure for this position. Most candidates can expect to enter in the lower to middle section of this salary range, depending on their specific experience and education.

Non-Discrimination:

Parker values diversity and seeks talented students, faculty, and staff from different backgrounds. All employment decisions are made without regard to unlawful considerations of race, color, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and related medical conditions), gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, religion, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, creed, age, mental or physical disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other basis prohibited by federal, state, or local law.

job.title: Francis Parker School Director of Transportation
job.description:
Position Description & Application

About Francis Parker School:

Parker is a coeducational independent day school in San Diego, California, with 1,330 students in Junior Kindergarten through Grade 12. Founded in 1912, the school’s mission is “to create and inspire a diverse community of independent thinkers whose academic excellence, global perspective, and strength of character prepare them to make a meaningful difference in the world.” Parker has two campuses: one in Mission Hills (Lower School, Junior Kindergarten - Grade 5) and a second in Linda Vista (Middle and Upper School, Grades 6 - 12).

Job Description:

The Director of Transportation provides strategic and operational leadership for Parker’s student transportation program and fleet of approximately 14 buses and 8 passenger vans. The Director is responsible for ensuring that all transportation services are safe, dependable, efficient, compliant, and responsive to the needs of students, families, faculty, and school programs.

The Director of Transportation oversees daily transportation operations, including home-to-school services, athletics, and field trips; driver staffing and training; vehicle maintenance; regulatory compliance; transportation scheduling; fleet replacement planning; and emergency response preparedness. The Director of Transportation works closely with Parker leadership, division administrators, athletics, summer and extended-day programs, security, and other departments to ensure that transportation supports Parker’s educational mission.

The successful candidate will combine strong organizational and supervisory skills with a highly visible, service-oriented approach and a deep commitment to student safety.

Requirements

Essential Duties/Responsibilities:

Transportation Operations

  • Direct Parker’s daily transportation operations for approximately 14 buses and 8 vans.
  • Develop, maintain, and optimize student transportation routes and schedules.
  • Coordinate morning, afternoon, athletic, field trip, summer, and special event transportation.
  • Ensure buses and vans are available, properly staffed, and maintained according to established schedules.
  • Monitor transportation operations and respond promptly to delays, breakdowns, route changes, weather events, and other disruptions.
  • Establish procedures for student loading, unloading, supervision, bus stops, field trips, and transportation-related emergencies.
  • Coordinate transportation needs with the three academic divisions, athletics, and summer and extended day programs.
  • Maintain effective communication with families regarding transportation schedules, procedures, changes, and significant service interruptions.

Student Safety

  • Make student safety the highest priority in all transportation decisions and practices.
  • Establish and enforce comprehensive transportation safety procedures.
  • Ensure appropriate supervision and accountability of students while boarding, riding, and exiting vehicles.
  • Develop and maintain a comprehensive transportation safety plan, including procedures for emergencies (e.g., evacuations).
  • Conduct or coordinate regular safety inspections, drills, and training.
  • Investigate transportation-related accidents, incidents, complaints, and safety concerns and recommend corrective actions.
  • Maintain appropriate records and documentation of accidents, incidents, inspections, training, and corrective actions.
  • Partner with security and risk management personnel on transportation security.

Driver Management and Training

  • Recruit, interview, hire, onboard, supervise, and evaluate transportation personnel.
  • Establish driver qualification and onboarding procedures.
  • Verify required licenses, certifications, medical clearances, driving records, and other qualifications.
  • Maintain accurate records of driver credentials, training, certifications, and other compliance requirements.
  • Develop and administer ongoing driver training and professional development programs.
  • Monitor driver performance, attendance, safety practices, and adherence to Parker policies.
  • Establish clear expectations for professional conduct, student interactions, appearance, vehicle cleanliness, and customer service.
  • Develop staffing plans and contingency coverage for absences, vacations, field trips, and other operational needs.
  • Address performance and disciplinary matters in accordance with Parker policies and Human Resources guidance.

Fleet Management and Maintenance

  • Oversee Parker’s in-house mechanic to ensure that the buses and vans are maintained according to the highest safety and reliability standards.
  • Establish preventive maintenance schedules based on manufacturer recommendations, regulatory requirements, mileage, vehicle age, and operating conditions.
  • Coordinate inspections, repairs, preventative maintenance, registration, and required certifications.
  • Maintain accurate vehicle maintenance and inspection records.
  • Develop procedures for daily vehicle inspections and prompt reporting of mechanical issues.
  • Establish and maintain business relationships with qualified bus suppliers, repair facilities, vendors, and other service providers.
  • Monitor vehicle downtime and develop contingency plans for transportation disruptions.
  • Maintain appropriate standards for vehicle cleanliness, appearance, accessibility, and passenger comfort.
  • Develop and maintain a long-term fleet replacement plan based on age, mileage, condition, reliability, safety, operating costs, and anticipated transportation needs.

Compliance and Risk Management

  • Ensure transportation operations comply with applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, licensing requirements, and Parker policies.
  • Maintain required transportation records and documentation.
  • Monitor changes in transportation laws and regulations and recommend policy or operational changes as appropriate.
  • Coordinate required inspections, registrations, permits, certifications, and reporting.
  • Work closely with Parker leadership regarding safety, liability, and compliance matters.
  • Ensure appropriate procedures are in place for transportation accidents and insurance claims.
  • Participate in Parker’s emergency preparedness and business continuity planning.

Scheduling, Systems, and Administration

  • Manage Parker’s transportation calendar and vehicle scheduling system.
  • Establish processes that minimize scheduling conflicts and maximize efficient use of the fleet.
  • Maintain accurate transportation databases, route information, vehicle records, driver records, and student transportation information.
  • Utilize routing, fleet management, GPS, communications, and other technology to improve safety, efficiency, and service.
  • Develop operating procedures and documentation for transportation services.
  • Prepare reports for Parker leadership regarding fleet condition, safety, staffing, utilization, incidents, and operational performance.

Budget and Financial Management

  • Develop and manage the annual transportation operating budget.
  • Monitor expenditures for fuel, maintenance, repairs, parts, insurance, training, licensing, equipment, and contracted services.
  • Review transportation costs and identify opportunities for operational efficiencies without compromising safety or service.
  • Develop capital requests and long-range financial plans for vehicle replacement and transportation-related equipment.
  • Solicit and evaluate bids and proposals from transportation vendors and service providers in accordance with Parker's purchasing policies.
  • Maintain appropriate controls for fuel, parts, supplies, and transportation equipment.

Communication and Customer Service

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for transportation operations.
  • Establish a high standard of customer service for students, parents, faculty, and staff.
  • Communicate proactively regarding route changes, delays, cancellations, vehicle issues, and other transportation matters.
  • Respond professionally and promptly to transportation-related questions and concerns.
  • Build strong working relationships with Parker administrators, faculty, staff, families, students, and external service providers.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business administration, operations management, logistics, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 5 or more years of experience managing a transportation operation, or a comparable safety-sensitive operation.
  • Experience managing transportation operations at an independent school, public school, college, university, camp, or other educational environment preferred.
  • Proven history of successfully supervising and developing employees.
  • Commercial Driver License (CDL) with applicable passenger and school-bus endorsements.
  • Experience with GPS-based fleet tracking and transportation routing software.
  • Familiarity with California student transportation regulations and school transportation requirements.
  • Strong knowledge of fleet maintenance, vehicle safety, scheduling, and other transportation operations.
  • Experience developing fleet replacement and capital improvement plans preferred.
  • Excellent organizational, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Uncompromising commitment to student safety and service.
  • Ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment in emergency and time-sensitive situations.
  • Proficiency with office applications (e.g., Microsoft Office, Google Suite) and transportation/fleet management technology.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

  • Safety leadership: An uncompromising commitment to student and employee safety.
  • Operational excellence: Ability to develop systems that produce reliable, efficient transportation services.
  • Leadership: Ability to recruit, develop, motivate, and hold employees accountable.
  • Judgment: Ability to make sound decisions under pressure and respond effectively to emergencies.
  • Communication: Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.
  • Organization: Exceptional attention to detail and ability to manage complex schedules and competing priorities.
  • Technology: Ability to effectively use routing, GPS, fleet-management, scheduling, and administrative systems.
  • Customer service: A collaborative and service-oriented approach to students, families, and colleagues.
  • Financial management: Ability to manage budgets and evaluate operating and capital costs.
  • Continuous improvement: Willingness to evaluate transportation operations and implement improvements in safety, efficiency, and service.

Physical and Work Environment Requirements

The position requires the ability to:

  • Regularly walk through parking areas, transportation facilities, and vehicle staging areas.
  • Inspect buses and vans and enter/exit vehicles, as necessary.
  • Work outdoors in varying weather conditions.
  • Respond to transportation incidents and emergencies outside normal business hours when necessary.
  • Work early mornings, evenings, weekends, and occasional holidays based on Parker’s transportation requirements and special events.
  • Occasionally lift, carry, or move transportation-related equipment and supplies.
  • Maintain a professional and calm demeanor during high-pressure situations.

Salary and Benefits:

Parker is committed to attracting and retaining the highest-quality faculty and staff through a substantial compensation plan, including competitive salary, TIAA retirement benefits, and full medical/dental coverage.

Salary Range: $115,000 - $125,000 per year, based on experience.

Non-Discrimination:

Francis Parker School values diversity and seeks talented students, faculty, and staff from different backgrounds. All employment decisions are made without regard to unlawful considerations of race, color, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and related medical conditions), gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, religion, national origin, ancestry, age, mental or physical disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other basis prohibited by federal, state, or local law.

Application Process:

To be considered, interested candidates must submit the following:

  • Online employment application.
  • Cover Letter
  • Resume

Your application will be considered incomplete if you do not include all required information, including completion of the Employment History, Education, and References sections of the online application, required attachments, and responses to all application questions.

Salary Description

$115,000 - $125,000

job.title: American International School of Johannesburg Elementary School Learner
job.description:
Position Description & Application

CAMPUS: Johannesburg Campus | SUPERVISOR: ES Principal | START DATE: 1 January 2027 |

POSTING DATE: 06 October 2026| CLOSING DATE: 23 October 2026

Inspire Learning to Build Our Better World. At the American International School of Johannesburg (AISJ), we are committed to providing an exceptional education that empowers global citizens to fulfill their future purpose. Our vision is to inspire learning to build a better world. We seek a dedicated and passionate professional who aligns with our commitment to excellence and believes in the transformative power of education. Every team member is crucial in creating a supportive and nurturing learning environment. At AISJ, we value every employee as a learner and expect them to embody and support the AISJ Portrait of Learner (Resilience, Mindful, Thinker, Globally Connected, Curious, Contributor) through their work. We are dedicated to justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion within our school community.

_______________________________________________________________________________________

Position Overview

The Learner Specific Pathway (LSP) Teaching Partner is an essential educational collaborator who provides specialized support for elementary students with cognitive and developmental disabilities requiring modified and individualized curricula. Working under the direct guidance of the LSP Teacher, Student Support Services Team, and Elementary Principal, the Teaching Partner facilitates learning both within general education classrooms to maximize peer inclusion and through targeted 1:1 and small-group instruction in the specialized LSP setting. Aligned with AISJ’s Vision to inspire learning and build a better world, the LSP Teaching Partner implements scaffolds, positive behavior strategies, and adaptive frameworks that nurture student agency, self-regulation, and holistic development. Through collaborative teamwork, resource preparation, and dedicated care, this role ensures every learner thrives academically, socially, and emotionally.

Qualifications & Experience:

Required Educational Qualifications & Certifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Education, Special Education, Psychology, Child Development, or a related field (Special Education focus preferred).
  • Exceptional command of written and spoken English.

Required Professional Experience

  • Proven experience supporting students in an educational setting, preferably within special education or student support programs.
  • Demonstrated patience, flexibility, and effectiveness in building positive relationships with elementary learners presenting complex cognitive, social, or behavioral profiles.
  • Proven ability to work independently, exercise initiative, and take clear direction from lead educators.
  • Strong digital literacy and computer skills to support instructional technology and student record-keeping.

Preferred Skills & Specialized Expertise

  • Experience or training in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) therapy strategies.
  • Experience using Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) systems and/or Makaton Sign Language.
  • Familiarity with inclusive practices, the IB Primary Years Programme (PYP), and the AISJ Portrait of a Learner.

Key Responsibilities:

Direct Student Support & Individualized Learning

  • Deliver direct 1:1 and small-group instructional support to identified LSP learners within both general education classrooms and specialized LSP learning environments.
  • Implement individualized scaffolds, accommodations, and curriculum modifications under the guidance of the LSP Lead Teacher and Student Support Services team.
  • Assist learners in mastering individualized curriculum goals, reinforcing concepts
  • across disciplinary and transdisciplinary units of inquiry.

Behavioral, Social-Emotional & Regulation Support

  • Support students in developing emotional self-regulation, social interaction, and self-help skills to maintain a safe, inclusive learning environment.
  • Implement individual behavior plans and proactive strategies to assist learners with complex behavioral or emotional needs.
  • Promote student agency and independence, interacting with all learners with dignity, respect, and deep empathy.

Collaboration, Documentation & Data Collection

  • Maintain accurate anecdotal notes, observational records, and logs regarding individual student progress, accomplishments, and behavioral trends.
  • Participate actively in Student Support Services and team planning meetings to review student data, share feedback, and adjust intervention strategies.
  • Communicate consistently and proactively with lead teachers, specialists, and multidisciplinary team members.

Classroom Operations & Resource Management

  • Design, adapt, and prepare specialized instructional materials, sensory tools, and learning aids as directed by the LSP teacher.
  • Manage learning environments and adaptive equipment efficiently to ensure spaces are prepared for active, hands-on learning experiences
  • Perform assigned campus supervision duties during break times, recess, and school gatherings.
  • Assist with after-school activities, Co-Curricular Activities (CCAs), and school-wide events as assigned.
  • Support and chaperone students during off-campus excursions and the Elementary Classroom Without Walls (CWW) program as needed.
  • Participate in ongoing professional development, training cycles, and team workshops to continually build special education skills.

Teacher Competencies:

Planning for Learning

  • Curriculum Design: Creates personalized, challenging learning sequences that build on prior knowledge while ensuring knowledge transfer and regular reflection opportunities.
  • Collaborative Planning: Partners across disciplines and specialties to create cohesive learning experiences

that connect global contexts while anticipating student needs.

  • Inquiry-Based Learning: Designs flexible conceptual units that honor student choice, pace, and multiple pathways to demonstrate understanding.

Maximizing Teacher Efficacy

  • Student Agency & Critical Thinking: Creates self-directed learners who think critically, set goals, and drive their own learning journey.
  • Research-Based Instructional Excellence: Implements proven teaching strategies that adapt to individual student needs through continuous assessment and adjustment.
  • Connected Learning Design: Weaves together global perspectives, real-world applications, and cross-disciplinary connections to create meaningful learning experiences.
  • Collaborative Leadership: Builds a learning community where students develop leadership skills through structured collaboration and personalized engagement.

Reflecting as Practitioners

  • Student Agency: Builds student capacity for self-assessment through modeling, tools, and targeted feedback that drives individual growth.
  • Data-Informed Practice: Analyzes student achievement data to align curriculum, refine teaching strategies, and measure instructional effectiveness.
  • Professional Growth: Engages in collaborative reflection and data analysis with colleagues to continuously improve teaching practices and student outcomes.

Promoting Relationships, Community, & Culture

  • Builds strong community-school partnerships and actively participates in community initiatives to enrich the learning environment.
  • Adapts teaching practices by staying informed of educational and societal changes while understanding each learner's unique cultural background, learning style, and needs.
  • Creates an inclusive learning environment that embraces diversity, challenges stereotypes, and connects learning to students' real-world experiences and cultural contexts.
  • Fosters a growth mindset by encouraging calculated risk-taking and developing students' autonomy, personal responsibility, and ownership of learning.

All community members are expected to be committed to the AISJ Community Principles.

  • We are better when we act together.
  • Our differences make us stronger.
  • Every voice counts. Every voice matters.
  • Every team needs individuals. Every individual needs a team.

Work

Number of Work Days: : Monday through Friday - 188 (one hundred and eighty-eight) days per school year.

Work Day: 7:10 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. daily on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday, and from 7:10 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on Wednesday.

Other Duties As Assigned: The Teacher will be expected to perform any work assigned to them that is within their skills and capabilities and to be flexible about changes to this function that may be required from time to time for operational reasons. This includes other duties as assigned by their supervisor from time to time.

APPLICATION PROCESS

To apply, please complete the electronic form [Click here]. Information captured will be securely stored and used for a reference check on the candidate's compatibility. AISJ reserves the right to appoint the strongest candidate before the closing date if required.

SAFEGUARDING & CHILD PROTECTION

AISJ maintains robust child protection policies to ensure a safe, secure, and caring environment for our students. All employees must undergo criminal background checks, attend annual training, and sign a safeguarding agreement.

PRIVACY

By submitting your CV, you consent to AISJ processing your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy, accessible at AISJ Privacy Policy, and under the Protection of Personal Information Act of 2013.

job.title: Francis Parker School School Bus Driver (Full-Time)
job.description:
Position Description & Application

About Francis Parker School:

Francis Parker School (Parker) is a coeducational independent day school in San Diego, California with 1,330 students in Junior Kindergarten through Grade 12. Founded in 1912, the school’s mission is “to create and inspire a diverse community of independent thinkers whose academic excellence, global perspective and strength of character prepare them to make a meaningful difference in the world.” Parker has two campuses: one in Mission Hills (Lower School, Junior Kindergarten - Grade 5), and a second in Linda Vista (Middle and Upper School, Grades 6 - 12).

Job Description:

The primary goal of the Transportation Department is to promote safety, ensuring all students receive the safest transportation possible. School bus drivers will transport students to and from school and other activities. On school days, drivers pick up students in the morning and return them home or to the designated bus stop in the afternoon. School bus drivers also drive students on field trips and to sporting events and other activities.

Essential Duties/Responsibilities:

  • Follow procedures to ensure the safety of all students, including watching traffic and people carefully to ensure the safety of children getting on and off the bus and assisting students with getting on and off the bus when required
  • Keep order and safety on the school bus
  • Understand and enforce the school system’s rules regarding student conduct and report disciplinary problems to the Director of Transportation
  • Maintain a clean and mechanically-sound bus at all times, including keeping the bus clean and free of debris
  • Perform pre-trip inspections of the bus (as prescribed by law) before leaving the yard, including: checking the braking systems; all belts, hoses & clamps, fluid levels; all lighting systems; suspension, leaf springs & shaft guards; seats tight & secure; tires; heating & cooling systems
  • Obey all traffic laws and state and federal transit regulations
  • Map directions to extra trips

In addition, must be able to:

  • Evacuate students from all exits, including windows, doors, and roof vents
  • Take appropriate action during a vehicle breakdown or collision (securing bus, attending to injured students, preparing accident reports, etc.)
  • Converse with parents in a friendly and professional manner
  • Maintain a given route schedule
  • Maintain a clean bus
  • Maintain proper fuel levels

Requirements

Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or GED strongly preferred
  • California Driver’s License required
  • Commercial (Class B) Driver’s License with School Bus Certification and Passenger Endorsement
  • Minimum one-year experience driving a school bus strongly preferred
  • No at-fault traffic accidents in the last 5 years
  • Clean driving record (no traffic citations in the last 5 years)
  • Ability to carry out the assigned route on time
  • Excellent communication skills
  • Two years of experience working with children preferred
  • Must be at least 21 years of age

In addition:

  • A school bus driver's background is checked by the Department of Justice and/or the FBI prior to receiving a license to drive a school bus.
  • School bus drivers must have a current Department of Transportation Medical Certificate
  • School bus drivers must pass (and maintain throughout the course of their employment) commercial driver’s license medical requirements, including vision and hearing tests
  • School bus drivers must maintain minimum training hours as required by law to retain School Bus Certification
  • School bus drivers must pass the written CHP First Aid Test or have a current First Aid Card
  • School bus drivers must participate in a pre-employment drug and alcohol test and are randomly tested thereafter (school bus drivers may never get behind the wheel of a school vehicle with .01 or greater blood alcohol level)
  • All school bus drivers must attend regularly scheduled safety meetings and attend additional training sessions to maintain the skills needed to safely transport students
  • School bus drivers must have and maintain a clean driving record, both professionally and personally
  • School Bus Drivers are required to maintain their required yearly in-service hours and/or renewal hours

Salary and Benefits

Parker is committed to attracting and retaining the highest quality faculty and staff through a substantial compensation plan, including competitive salary, TIAA retirement benefits, and full medical/dental coverage.

Starting Rate: $32.30/hour

Non-Discrimination:

Parker values diversity and seeks talented students, faculty, and staff from different backgrounds. All employment decisions are made without regard to unlawful considerations of race, color, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and related medical conditions), gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, religion, national origin, ancestry, age, mental or physical disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other basis prohibited by federal, state, or local law.

Application Process:

To be considered, interested candidates must submit the following:

  • Online employment application
  • Cover Letter
  • Resume

Your application will be considered incomplete if you do not include all required information, including completion of the Employment History, Education, and References sections of the online application, required attachments, and responses to all application questions.

Salary Description

Starting Salary $32.30/hour

job.title: Maret School Accounts Receivable Accountant
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Maret School is seeking a versatile, personable, and proactive accounts receivable accountant to serve as a key operational member of the Business Office. This role offers a unique blend of financial stewardship, contract administration, and community-focused service, overseeing all incoming revenue streams — including student tuition, auxiliary programs (after-school, summer camps, books, field trips), and facility rentals.

Throughout the school year, this position serves as the primary financial liaison for Maret families and external partners, ensuring seamless billing processes, accurate payment tracking, diligent follow-up on outstanding balances, and hands-on support during the student enrollment cycle. The position reports directly to the school’s controller. The ideal candidate will have meticulous attention to detail, a commitment to collaboration, and a firm but friendly customer-service approach to collections.

Tuition and Auxiliary Receivables Collections

  • Manage full-cycle accounts receivable for tuition, fees, after-school programs, summer camps, books, field trips, and other student-related expenses
  • Oversee family billing and payment collection schedules through the FACTS platform
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for family billing inquiries, payment plan setups, and payment troubleshooting
  • Monitor aging schedules, conduct polite but persistent outreach on delinquent accounts, and work with families to establish payment arrangements when necessary

Facility Rentals & Auxiliary Vendor Management

  • Draft facilities rental agreements using standard school contract templates for external organizations renting campus spaces
  • Draft agreements using standard templates for third-party after-school vendors
  • Invoice and collect rental fees and vendor fees in a timely manner
  • Track submission of up-to-date certificates of liability insurance for renters and vendors

Enrollment Support

  • Play an active operational role in the annual re-enrollment and new student enrollment process using the enrollment checklist
  • Monitor incoming enrollment agreements for completion, ensuring all financial terms and requirements are met before finalizing enrollment
  • Guide new and returning families through setting up their annual tuition payment plans in FACTS

General Accounting & Office Support

  • Post daily receipts, process bank deposits, and prepare month-end accounts receivable journal entries and reconciliations (FACTS tuition management to the general ledger)
  • Assist with month-end and year-end close processes, as well as annual financial audit preparation
  • Cross-train on accounts payable procedures to serve as a backup for AP during staff vacations and peak cycles
  • Maintain accurate, structured, and organized digital filing systems for all billing, vendor, and rental documentation
  • Prepare reports and presentations to support financial management and reporting to the head of school and board of trustees
  • Assist with other Business Office duties and special projects as assigned

Position Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, or a related field (equivalent practical experience will be considered)
  • 3+ years of general accounting or accounts receivable experience
  • Proficiency with tuition management systems (experience with FACTS is a strong plus)
  • Experience with K-12 school management software (experience with Veracross is a plus)
  • High proficiency in Microsoft Excel and standard accounting software
  • Tactful, empathetic, and professional communication skills and confidentiality when discussing financial matters with parents, faculty, and external partners
  • High degree of accuracy in data entry, reconciliations, journal entries, and record-keeping
  • Strong willingness to learn independent school accounting practices and cross-train in other finance functions (such as accounts payable)

Salary: $75,000–$85,000. The salary offered is determined based on factors including, but not limited to, the selected candidate's experience and education, budget availability, internal salary equity considerations, and available market information.

Maret’s dynamic community and campus in the midst of Washington, DC, create a unique learning environment for students from kindergarten through twelfth grade. Expert teachers inspire students to think both creatively and analytically, seek out multiple perspectives, work hard, and make time for joy as they tackle our challenging curriculum and explore artistic and athletic pursuits. The school’s mission, core values, and educational philosophy ground and guide our work.

Our community strives for equity and inclusion in every aspect of school life. Maret School stands firmly behind the principle that the admission of students, the employment of faculty, the operation of programs, and the governance of the school be open to all who are qualified, regardless of race, ethnicity, color, national origin, gender identity, sexual orientation, or creed. We believe that this principle is both firmly grounded in the spirit of American democracy and in keeping with the civil responsibilities of an independent school.

All adults on campus are role models for our students and are considered part of the faculty. Every Maret employee must abide by our code of conduct.

To apply, please send a cover letter and résumé BY EMAIL ONLY to Dean Shillingford at dshillingford@maret.org. Unfortunately, we will not be able to respond personally to every applicant. You will hear from us only if your experience matches our current needs.

job.title: Ashley Hall Diploma Programme (DP) Coordinator & Grades 9-12 Teacher
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Reports to: Upper School Division Director

Role Duration: 10 months, full time, start August 2027

Position Summary:

The role of the Ashley Hall Diploma Programme (DP) Coordinator is to plan and lead the IB Diploma authorization process, with the ultimate goal of being authorized to offer the IB Diploma by the International Baccalaureate Organization (IBO). The coordinator would oversee the alignment of the school’s curriculum and teaching frameworks to ensure they meet the expectations of the IBO. Through coordination with teachers, administrators, and the IB regional office, the coordinator is responsible for preparing our Upper School for the full delivery of the IB Diploma, including supervising the documentation, reporting, analysis, assessment delivery, and examination delivery and standards as required by the IBO. A key part of this role is ensuring that the school is in compliance with DP requirements. The DP Coordinator has oversight and coordination of all IB related activities, including teacher training and unit development, student evaluation and the student experience. The DP Coordinator is expected to teach an upper school class.

The DP Coordinator has overall responsibility for:

Leadership

- Work with the Assistant Head of School for Teaching and Learning and the Upper School Division Director to develop a step-by-step plan to gain authorization to offer the IB DP

- Offer DP guidance, training, and workshops as needed during regularly scheduled meetings

- Work with the Assistant Head of School for Teaching and Learning, the Upper School Director, and the MYP Coordinator to develop a bridging program in Grades 9 and 10 that will prepare students for the challenge of IB Diploma course work. Refine or develop policies that reflect the IB philosophy and satisfy Diploma Programme requirements

- Support and mentor upper school teachers through all facets of the IB programme

- After implementation/adoption of the programme, support and mentor new upper school teachers in the classroom

- Regularly review and follow all IB rules, regulations and guidelines to support programme implementation and ongoing development to ensure fidelity in the implementation of the DP requirements and specifications necessary for the successful implementation of the programme (as outlined in Programme standard and practices)

- Provide learning engagement input and feedback for upper school teachers

- Support teachers through regular classroom visits and feedback

- Provide opportunities for teachers to observe one another in practice

Communication

- Keep the School’s leadership regularly informed of DP developments

- Maintain communication between Ashley Hall and the IB

- Work with the Division Director to create a communication plan to educate both students and parents about the IB DP program

- Provide curriculum-related parent meetings and workshop opportunities

- Ensure that teachers have access to MyIB and newly published DP documents

- Contribute to the presentation and promotion of the academic program within the Ashley Hall Community

- Collaborate with the PYP and MYP Coordinators on a bi-weekly basis to ensure continuity throughout the program

- Communicate relevant DP professional development opportunities for staff

- Liaise with the coordinator of Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging (DEOB) and Community Partnerships to seek out ways to reinforce the School’s efforts in that area

Professional Development

- In consultation with the administrative team, identify areas for professional development and provide support to upper school teachers prior to the professional development process

- Provide divisional, small group, and individual professional development opportunities as needed

Curriculum

- Coach faculty on the implementation of instructional best practices aligned to the the DP framework

- Participate with school leadership on curriculum and assessment within school and the IBDP

- Provide upper school teachers with relevant and up to date IB and IBDP curriculum documentation and documentation framework support

- Provide guidance and support to upper school teachers in understanding DP Scope and Sequence documents

- Ensure that curriculum documentation is up to date and that DP teachers understand how to use the DP unit planner

Student Experience

- Work with 9th-12th Grade leadership to organize weekly IB-themed assemblies

- Working in collaboration with the school’s College Counselor, provide guidance and support that help students succeed in the IB programme and plan for the next stage of their educational and or career-related experiences.

Parents

- Provide comprehensive information to parents about the DP and the School’s milestones

- Organize parent meetings to:

*Advise parents on the suitability of the IB Program for their child(ren)

*Inform parents about the benefits and requirements of the IBDP

*Notify parents about their child(ren)’s progress

Documentation and Resource Management

- Assist the Upper School Director with scheduling to support implementation of the Programme

- Keep records of all correspondence with the IB, including forms, documents, and reports

- Assist the Assistant Head of School for Teaching and Learning in determining main curriculum resources and other needs for professional development; and in placing resource orders

- Ensure that teachers keep long-range plans for IBDP up to date

- Prepare and submit any documentation required for authorization and evaluation

- Prepare timelines for submission of work to the IB.

- Ensure that all requirements and procedures set by the IB concerning the Programme are adhered to

- Manage the IB Diploma Programme budget

Teaching

- Teach a minimum of one academic course within the successful candidate’s subject-discipline expertise or in a discipline area that compliments curricular programming

- Model effective, research-based instructional strategies

- Help build effective team-oriented relationships that promote effective and purposeful collaborative academic environments where courses are taught with an emphasis on student inquiry, action, and reflection

- Demonstrate proficiency and application experience of relevant technologies to support instruction and student exploration

- Possess the flexibility and willingness to teach and support interdisciplinary courses

Examinations

- With the support of the Upper School Administrative Assistant, ensure that students are registered for examinations

- Ensure conduct of examinations (written and oral) and visiting examiners

- With the support of the Upper School Administrative Assistant, ensure that all internal assessment materials are sent to respective examiners

- Send examination answer scripts to IB examiners on time

- Report examination irregularities

- Organize distribution of results

- Work with school leadership to analyze results and adjust program delivery as necessary

Qualifications:

- Established knowledge of IBDP Programme through teaching in the framework and or coordinating the IB

- A master's degree in teaching, education, education leadership, or a related field pertinent to this specific role

- Proven experience in instructional coaching and applying adult learning principles to support, mentor, and elevate faculty pedagogical practices within an IB framework

- Exceptional self-starter with a high degree of self-management and the ability to take initiative while being in continuous communication and collaboration with multiple stakeholders

- Trained in and/or experience with student-centered and experiential instruction

- Experience coaching teachers

- Excellent written and oral communication skills

- Can demonstrate a record of collaborative teaching

- Possesses an ability to build authentic relationships with colleagues and students

- Is able to create and contribute to a joyful and inclusive community based on open communication, understanding and respect

- Has a committed practice of professional reflection, inquiry, iteration, and innovation

- Actively seeks purposeful growth in themselves and in others

- Reliably meets expectations and deadlines

Faculty at Ashley Hall are expected to cultivate meaningful relationships with the colleagues and students with whom they work. This occurs in various ways during the school day, including meetings and duties.

Since its founding in 1909, Ashley Hall has empowered young women to think critically, act ethically, and embrace their world with confidence. The School serves girls kindergarten through grade 12 (and is co-ed in its Early School, ages 2 to 5 years). Ashley Hall provides a dynamic education grounded in a Reggio approach in its early School and an International Baccalaureate Primary Years Programme in its Lower School. It is currently in the strategic phase of a Middle Years Programme candidacy with the intention of pursuing Diploma Programme candidacy thereafter.

Interested candidates required to submit an official application through Ashley Hall’s website at https://www.ashleyhall.org/careers to be considered for the position.

As part of the online application, candidates will be required to upload a cover letter, resume, and list of references to be considered for the position.

Questions regarding the position can be directed to:

Kimberly Ells-Payne, Human Resources Talent Acquisition & Onboarding Manager

Email: ellsk@ashleyhall.org

Ashley Hall is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability or genetic information.

job.title: Holy Trinity Administrative Assistant
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Reports to: Division Head – The Daisy Lane School

Status: FT, Exempt

Salary Range: $48,000.00 - $53,000.00. Salary commensurate with experience.

About Holy Trinity

Holy Trinity: An Episcopal School is a Pre-School through 8th Grade school grounded in Episcopal values, academic excellence, and a strong sense of purpose. Located on two campuses in Prince George’s County, one in Bowie and one in Glenn Dale, the school offers a comprehensive education within a nurturing, safe, and welcoming community. Students benefit from a challenging academic environment supported by the resources needed to excel academically, artistically, athletically, and spiritually. Holy Trinity encourages students to pursue excellence and embrace responsibility.

Holy Trinity seeks dedicated educators who support our mission and are passionate about being part of a transformative educational experience, one that cultivates each student’s God-given talents and helps shape them into their best selves.

Position Summary:

The Administrative Assistant for The Daisy Lane School must possess a creative can-do spirit, along with the ability to work collaboratively with students, peers, and parents. Being able to work independently and exercising judgment and initiative are also necessary requirements. Lastly, they must possess a positive attitude and demonstrate exceptional organizational skills, technical proficiency, and strong interpersonal abilities to effectively support the educational environment.

Administrative Support:
