job.title: American International School of Johannesburg Activities/Athletics Director
job.description:
Position Description & Application

CAMPUS: Johannesburg Campus | SUPERVISOR: School Director | START DATE: 01 August 2027

POSTING DATE: 29 September 2026 | CLOSING DATE: 16 October 2026

Inspire Learning to Build Our Better World. At the American International School of Johannesburg (AISJ), we are committed to providing an exceptional education that empowers global citizens to fulfill their future purpose. Our vision is to inspire learning to build a better world. We seek a dedicated and passionate professional who aligns with our commitment to excellence and believes in the transformative power of education. Every team member is crucial in creating a supportive and nurturing learning environment. At AISJ, we value every employee as a learner and expect them to embody and support the AISJ Portrait of Learner (Resilience, Mindful, Thinker, Globally Connected, Curious, Contributor) through their work. We are dedicated to justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion within our school community.

POSITION OVERVIEW

The Athletics/Activities Director provides strategic, operational, and educational leadership for the comprehensive K-12 co-curricular, athletics, and activities programs across both the Johannesburg and Pretoria campuses.

Unlike single-campus models, this role directly oversees co-curricular learning school-wide. Supported on-site by the Pretoria Activities Coordinator, the Athletics/Activities Director ensures operational alignment, equity of opportunity, and high program quality across both campus locations. The Director directly supervises five full-time department leaders (K-12 Activities Coordinator, Pretoria Activities Coordinator, Sports Coordinator, Events and Logistics Coordinator, and Aquatics Coordinator) and manages the whole-school K-12 Activities Budget.

The ideal candidate is an experienced, visionary international educational leader with deep expertise in large-scale event staging, complex multi-country travel logistics, student safeguarding, and student-centered program design.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Education, Sports Management, or a closely related field.
  • Administrative Experience: Minimum of seven (7) years of successful leadership as an Athletics/Activities Director or co-curricular director in a leading international school setting.
  • Conference Leadership: Proven experience managing, scheduling, and executing international school conference events and athletic leagues (e.g., ISSEA, SAISA).
  • Personnel Management: Demonstrated track record of recruiting, mentoring, supervising, and evaluating full-time departmental staff, seasonal coaches, and activity sponsors.
  • Risk Management & Safeguarding: Extensive experience establishing risk assessment protocols, duty-of-care frameworks, and international travel safety procedures for global student events.
  • Communication & Tech Agility: Exceptional public speaking, written communication, and cross-cultural negotiation skills; proficient with enterprise management suites (Google Workspace, scheduling/registration software).

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE

  • Advanced Degree: Master’s degree in Education, Educational Leadership, Sports Management, or a related field.
  • Leadership Track Record: Demonstrated, impact-driven leadership in an international school setting.
  • Professional Certification: Certified Athletic Administrator (CAA), Certified International Athletic Administrator (CIAA), or Certified Master Athletic Administrator (CMAA) designation via the NIAAA or international equivalent.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Strategic Leadership & Divisional Collaboration

  • In collaboration with divisional leadership (Elementary, Middle, High School, and Pretoria Campus Leadership), design, align, and evaluate all co-curricular learning experiences to complement academic curricula.
  • Directly supervise, support, and evaluate the departmental leadership team: K-12 Activities Coordinator, Pretoria Activities Coordinator, Sports Coordinator, Events and Logistics Coordinator, and Aquatics Coordinator.
  • Establish clear departmental goals aligned with the AISJ Strategic Plan and Portrait of a Learner.
  • Serve as the primary liaison to international leagues and associations, representing AISJ in ISSEA, SAISA, ISTA, AMIS, and local South African leagues and events.

2. Safeguarding, Risk Management & International Travel Logistics

  • Enforce rigorous child protection, safeguarding, and safety standards across all athletic, aquatic, and co-curricular programs in accordance with AISJ policies.
  • Oversee complex international and domestic travel logistics for large student delegations (flights, visas, housing/billeting, medical clearances, and emergency contingency plans) for events such as ISSEA, SAISA, Model United Nations (MUN), ISTA, and AMIS.
  • Develop comprehensive risk assessments for all off-campus excursions and athletic competitions.
  • Lead mandatory pre-trip safety briefings and orientation sessions for staff, students, and parents prior to all major travel events.

3. K-12 Fiscal & Facility Stewardship

  • Formulate, manage, and audit the comprehensive K-12 Activities Budget to ensure equitable distribution of resources across divisions, gender categories, and activities.
  • Partner with operational and facilities teams across both campuses to optimize the scheduling, maintenance, and safety of athletic fields, aquatics facilities, courts, and performance venues.
  • Oversee the procurement, inventory, repair, and replacement cycle for all athletic uniforms, safety gear, and specialized activity equipment.

4. Program Execution & Student Engagement

  • Coordinate the master K-12 multi-campus activities and athletics calendar to prevent divisional conflicts and optimize venue usage.
  • Ensure full execution of teacher Co-Curricular Activity (CCA) commitments, working alongside division principals to assign and support faculty advisors and coaches.
  • Direct the planning and execution of large-scale tournaments, fine arts festivals, and community athletic events hosted at AISJ.
  • Oversee the Eagle Council, guiding this key student service organization as it provides vital student feedback and leadership on co-curricular and athletic programming.
  • Organize student-athlete and activity recognition events, awards ceremonies, and end-of-season celebrations.

5. Operational Agility & Leadership Adaptability

  • Adapt departmental operations in response to unforeseen disruptions to facilities, the environment, or global travel.
  • Perform essential administrative and leadership duties as assigned by the School Director to support whole-school operations.

APPLICATION & SAFEGUARDING POLICIES

  • Safeguarding Statement: AISJ is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. All candidates undergo rigorous background checks, qualification verification, criminal record screenings, and child protection training prior to appointment.
  • Privacy & Data Protection: Personal data submitted will be processed strictly in accordance with the AISJ Privacy Policy and South Africa’s Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA).
  • Contract Terms: Initial two-year administrative contract, renewable annually based on performance review. Competitive international administrative remuneration and benefits package provided.

APPLICATION PROCESS

To apply, please complete the electronic form [Click here]. Information captured will be securely stored and used for a reference check on the candidate's compatibility. AISJ reserves the right to appoint the strongest candidate before the closing date if required.

SAFEGUARDING & CHILD PROTECTION

AISJ maintains robust child protection policies to ensure a safe, secure, and caring environment for our students. All employees must undergo criminal background checks, attend annual training, and sign a safeguarding agreement.

PRIVACY

By submitting your CV, you consent to AISJ processing your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy, accessible at AISJ Privacy Policy, and under the Protection of Personal Information Act of 2013.

OTHER INFORMATION

  • The first contract is for two years and then extended each year based on an annual review.
  • Interviews will start in November 2026
  • The package for this Administrative position is competitive with others like international schools around the world

job.title: Beaver Country Day School Alumni and Family Engagement Manager
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Description

Reports to: Director of Philanthropy & Engagement

Classification: Full-time, 12-month

About The School

Beaver Country Day School is an independent day school serving 460 students in grades 6-12, located in Chestnut Hill, just outside of Boston. Founded in 1920 and propelled by our progressive roots, our goal is to expand the nature of school. With over 40 local and national partnerships, almost daily field trips, a thriving performing and visual arts program, a robust and varied athletics and fitness program, and a best-in-class research and design center, we combine rigorous academics with real-world application, focusing on teaching content alongside experience applying it to current issues.

The school fosters a joyful environment where students feel confident taking risks and being their authentic selves, where everyone, students and adults alike, feels a sense of belonging, and where teachers have the freedom to innovate and grow alongside their students.

Alumni & Family Engagement Manager

Beaver is looking for an outgoing, relationship-driven professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment. Working across the full lifecycle of the Beaver experience, the Alumni and Family Engagement Manager creates meaningful opportunities for alumni, current families, past parents, grandparents, and other members of the Beaver community to connect with the School and with one another. This individual has an understanding of how to orient, educate, cultivate and leverage very different audiences and has a track record of building and deepening relationships that inspire both volunteerism and philanthropy.

This role will be instrumental in welcoming new members of the community, sustaining relationships beyond graduation, and engaging individuals who are not already actively involved with Beaver. They will take a data-driven approach to the work to make decisions, and track connection, participation, and volunteerism. This individual will be able to show a direct connection from their work to increased philanthropy across the constituencies they engage. The role is highly collaborative and externally facing, partnering across the School to translate institutional priorities into engagement opportunities that strengthen community, broaden participation, and cultivate future volunteer and philanthropic leaders.

Alumni and Family Engagement

  • Develop and execute an annual engagement plan aligned with departmental and institutional priorities.
  • Create meaningful opportunities for alumni, current families, past parents, grandparents, and other members of Beaver's extended community to connect with the School and one another.
  • Lead Reunion planning and other key alumni and family programs, including regional and affinity-based engagement.
  • Conduct outreach and discovery to engage individuals who are not currently connected and identify opportunities for deeper involvement.

Volunteer Engagement

  • Build and steward a broad pipeline of alumni and family volunteers, creating roles as ambassadors, connectors, hosts, mentors, advisors, and philanthropic partners.
  • Serve as the primary P&E liaison to the Parent Association and support its leadership and volunteer structure.
  • Partner with P&E colleagues to identify and cultivate individuals with potential for deeper volunteer and philanthropic leadership.

Programs and Events

  • Lead the planning and execution of designated alumni, family, and institutional programs and events.
  • Partner with colleagues across Beaver to develop engagement opportunities connected to academics, arts, athletics, student life, and institutional priorities.
  • Design programs and events to advance relationship-building and engagement goals, and evaluate their effectiveness over time.

P&E Collaboration and Engagement Strategy

  • Collaborate with P&E colleagues to integrate engagement with cultivation, stewardship, Annual Fund, and campaign priorities.
  • Track engagement and volunteer activity, using participation data and community feedback to inform future planning.
  • Partner with P&E colleagues to ensure that constituent engagement and volunteer information is accurately maintained.
  • Participate fully in the life of Beaver, including occasional evening and weekend programs and
  • events.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree and 3–5 years of relevant experience in alumni or family engagement, advancement, education, nonprofit management, volunteer management, or a related field.Strong relationship-building, communication, program management, and organizational skills
  • Demonstrated ability to recruit, engage, and steward volunteers
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities independently with strong follow-through
  • Collaborative, curious, flexible, and detail oriented
  • Ability to translate broader priorities into concrete programs and plans
  • Enthusiasm for Beaver's mission, commitment to professional growth and to our school commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging
  • Sense of humor and delight in school life

Salary Range:

The salary range for this position is $90,000–$110,000. Please visit our Working at Beaver webpage for information about benefits and more.

Beaver Country Day School is an equal-opportunity employer. It does not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, creed, handicap status, national origin, ethnicity, military veteran status, or other legally protected status in hiring or other employment practices.

job.title: Alcuin School Registrar & Database Manager
job.description:
Position Description & Application

GENERAL POSITION SUMMARY

The Registrar & Database Manager safeguards the accuracy, integrity, and usefulness of Alcuin School's student, family, enrollment, and academic information. The position administers core school data systems and registrar processes so families receive reliable information, faculty and staff can perform their work, and school leaders can make informed decisions. The role serves students from 18 months through grade 12, acts as a custodian of official student records, and handles confidential print and digital records requiring consistent judgment, discretion, and follow-through.

JOB SCOPE

Reporting to the Director of Technology and Innovation, this position serves as the primary administrator for Blackbaud Education Management and coordinates data across Ravenna, ManageBac, CampBrain, and authorized SEVIS workflows. The role owns day-to-day data quality, access administration, seasonal enrollment and academic processing, recurring reporting, and assigned accreditation evidence and data support. It has no formal supervisory responsibility and works closely with Admissions, the Business Office, division leaders, the Health Office, Advancement, Technology, and school leadership. The position exercises judgment within approved policies and escalates financial, policy, privacy, or legal decisions outside its assigned authority.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Student and Family Records

  • Maintain complete and accurate student, parent, guardian, household, and directory records for current and former students in Blackbaud and approved archives, including family relationships, access permissions, and authorized contact information.
  • Process new-student setup, withdrawals, grade or level transitions, and mid-year changes in accordance with approved workflows and deadlines.
  • Administer annual student forms, emergency-release records, pickup authorizations, and related data-validation processes.
  • Reconcile records across systems, investigate discrepancies, and coordinate timely corrections with the appropriate data owners.
  • Apply approved policies and schedules for the retention, archiving, authorized use, secure destruction, backup, and recovery of print and digital student records; coordinate with Technology to protect records against catastrophic loss.
  • Support Admissions in verifying receipt of official student-progress records directly from sending schools before an offer of admission is finalized, and respond promptly to authorized written transcript or student-record requests, escalating any delay or restriction.

Enrollment and Contract Administration

  • Configure and manage annual enrollment and re-enrollment contract cycles using approved templates and language, including tuition and financial-aid fields and dates; verify that configured contracts accurately reflect approved behavioral expectations and financial commitments.
  • Generate, track, and process contracts with Admissions and the Business Office; monitor incomplete contracts, required entries, and checklist completion.
  • Validate and import new-family data from Ravenna into Blackbaud, resolve import errors, and maintain supporting documentation.
  • Produce enrollment-status updates; support clear, timely, and consistent administration of approved admissions and enrollment requirements, deadlines, and financial information; and escalate exceptions that require policy, financial, or leadership decisions.
  • Apply approved admissions and enrollment workflows consistently and in support of the School's nondiscrimination policies; safeguard confidential applicant and financial-assistance information within assigned systems.

Academic Records and Scheduling

  • Maintain course, grade, attendance, report-card, and transcript systems and coordinate official transcript processes to protect the accuracy and integrity of academic records.
  • Support middle and upper school course requests, schedule changes, and the development of master and individual student schedules.
  • Prepare alternative schedules for special events, modified school days, and other approved calendar variations.
  • Maintain the academic-records calendar and perform quality-control reviews for grade entry, report cards, schedules, and transcripts.

Systems Administration and Access

  • Serve as the primary administrator for Blackbaud Education Management and maintain user roles and permissions through approved access and least-privilege practices; conduct documented periodic access reviews and coordinate prompt access changes or removal when roles change.
  • Administer related systems, including ManageBac, CampBrain, Ravenna integrations, and authorized SEVIS workflows, within assigned permissions and applicable requirements.
  • Maintain school forms, calendar items, portal settings, and website content that require system-level access.
  • Coordinate with Technology and system vendors on integrations, testing, upgrades, troubleshooting, and issue resolution.
  • Document material configuration changes, access decisions, periodic reviews, and recurring system controls, including evidence of approval and completion.

Data Reporting, Integrity, and Privacy

  • Produce enrollment, roster, retention, attrition, grade-level, accreditation/self-study, and other approved reports and supporting data for school leadership and operational partners.
  • Establish and apply shared data definitions, validation checks, and reconciliation standards across Blackbaud, Ravenna, ManageBac, CampBrain, and related platforms.
  • Maintain communication lists and distribution groups in coordination with the departments responsible for the underlying data.
  • Protect confidential information and apply the School's approved student-privacy, records-management, retention, destruction, and access-control practices in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local law, including FERPA where applicable.
  • Report suspected data errors, unauthorized access, or privacy concerns promptly through established protocols.

Training, Documentation, and Cross-Department Service

  • Document key workflows, data standards, cycle calendars, quality controls, and backup, recovery, and continuity responsibilities so recurring work can be completed consistently and records remain available after a disruption.
  • Train faculty and staff on relevant systems and workflows and provide responsive, service-oriented support.
  • Partner with Admissions, division leaders, the Business Office, Health Office, Advancement, Technology, and school leadership to coordinate data-dependent work.
  • Support accreditation and institutional-improvement work by maintaining assigned evidence, producing accurate reports, and responding to authorized data requests.
  • Recommend practical process improvements, including responsible automation opportunities, that reduce duplicate entry while preserving review, privacy, and accuracy controls.

MARGINAL FUNCTIONS

  • Participate in cross-functional projects related to school data, technology, enrollment, and operational improvement.
  • Perform other related duties consistent with the purpose and level of the position, as assigned.

Qualifications

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES, AND OTHER REQUIREMENTS

Required:

  • Ability to provide documents verifying authorization to work in the U.S.
  • Must pass Criminal Background Checks and Drug Testing
  • Bachelor's degree in information systems, education administration, business, data management, or a related field.
  • Strong experience with Blackbaud Education Management.
  • Demonstrated directly relevant experience with student information systems, school databases, registrar functions, enrollment operations, or a comparable records environment.
  • Experience administering a system of record, managing user access, reconciling data, and producing accurate operational reports.
  • Ability to manage high-volume, deadline-driven workflows with consistent accuracy, documentation, and follow-through.
  • Working knowledge of confidentiality, data privacy, access controls, and the retention, secure destruction, backup, and recovery of print and digital records, with the ability to learn and apply school-specific requirements.
  • Ability to analyze discrepancies, identify root causes, explain system or data issues in plain language, and coordinate practical solutions.
  • Ability to train and support users with patience, clarity, and an appropriate balance of service and control.
  • Proficiency with spreadsheets, standard office productivity tools, and data reporting functions.
  • Ability to work appropriately in a school serving students from 18 months through grade 12 and to complete required training regarding student safety, harassment prevention, professional boundaries, mandatory reporting, data privacy, and system security.
  • Commitment to ongoing professional growth in registrar practice, data governance, security, and relevant school systems.

Preferred:

  • Experience with Ravenna, ManageBac, CampBrain, SEVIS, or comparable education systems.
  • Experience in an independent school or another multi-program educational environment.
  • Experience documenting workflows, supporting data integrations, or improving cross-system processes.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY

This position has no formal supervisory responsibility. It may coordinate system projects, recurring data cycles, and the work of departmental data owners without direct authority over their employment.

INTERNAL CONTACTS

  • Director of Technology and Innovation, Head of School, Chief Financial Officer / Associate Head of School for Finance & Operations, Associate Head of School for Institutional Advancement, division leaders, and other members of school leadership.
  • Admissions, Business Office, Technology, Health Office, Advancement, faculty, staff, and other employees who create, maintain, or use school data.

EXTERNAL CONTACTS

  • Current and prospective families, authorized educational institutions, and other approved recipients of student records.
  • School-system vendors, implementation partners, and authorized agencies or service providers.

EQUIPMENT AND TECHNOLOGY USED

  • Computer, standard office equipment, secure file-transfer and communication tools, spreadsheets, and school-approved productivity platforms.
  • Blackbaud Education Management, Ravenna, ManageBac, CampBrain, authorized SEVIS access, and related reporting, portal, calendar, and web-administration tools.

JOB CONDITIONS

  • Work is performed primarily in an on-campus office within an active school environment and requires sustained computer use, keyboarding, visual review, and concentration on detailed records.
  • The role regularly handles confidential print and digital records for current and former students and families, including academic and financial information, and must follow approved access, privacy, retention, destruction, backup, and recovery practices.
  • Work volume increases around enrollment and re-enrollment cycles, school-year transitions, scheduling, grading, reporting, and transcript deadlines.

WORKING CONDITIONS

  • Full-time, 12-month, on-campus position with a regular Monday-through-Friday schedule during standard school business hours.
  • Occasional early or late hours may be needed for major system cycles, school deadlines, or issue resolution, with supervisor coordination.
  • No regular travel or on-call assignment is anticipated.

ABOUT ALCUIN SCHOOL

Alcuin School, one of the largest accredited Montessori schools in the U.S., along with the International Baccalaureate Middle Years and Diploma Programs, provides an ideal learning environment that guides and nurtures the full development of the child from 18 months to 18 years of age. Alcuin School is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All persons will receive consideration for employment without regard to gender (including gender identity, gender expression and gender reassignment), race (including color, nationality, ethnic or national origin), religion or belief, marital or civil partnership status, disability, age, sexual orientation, pregnancy or maternity, trade union membership or membership in any other legally protected category. We strive to create an inclusive environment, empower employees, and embrace diversity. We encourage everyone to respond.

job.title: The American School in London Strategic Finance and Planning Specialist
job.description:
Position Description

School Career Site

Reports to: Director of Finance and Operations Hours: Full-time Contract: Permanent Start date: ASAP Overall purpose The Strategic Finance and Planning Specialist provides strategic financial analysis and decision support, supports the School’s long-term financial and capital planning, and contributes to strategic and business planning across the DFO’s portfolio. The role works alongside the DFO and in tandem with the Finance, Facilities and Operations teams, focusing on complex analytical and planning work, including discrete strategic reviews, outside day-to-day departmental operations. The postholder will work independently and collaborate with senior leaders, trustees, department managers and external advisers. Responsibilities Capital Programme and Financial Analysis ● Provide financial analysis to support the feasibility and development of programmes and projects within the facilities master plan. ● Develop and maintain long-term financial models incorporating the capital programme and capital campaign into the School’s overall financial planning. ● Provide ongoing financial analysis, forecasting and scenario modelling to support major capital and financing decisions as plans and assumptions evolve. Strategic Analysis and Financial Planning ● Provide targeted analysis of financial and operational performance, programmes and activities to inform planning and decision-making, working with the Finance Manager as appropriate. ● Develop forecasts and scenario analyses to support long-term financial planning and strategic decision-making. ● Provide financial analysis and decision support for significant initiatives, including compensation, educational and operational programmes, enrolment planning and investment decisions. ● Lead or support strategic reviews and analytical projects on behalf of the DFO, working across the School and with external advisers as required. ● Develop business cases and options appraisals to support significant decisions and initiatives. ● Develop management information and dashboards to support strategic performance monitoring and decision-making. ● Support year-end reporting and governance, including analysis of key matters arising from the statutory accounts and preparation of relevant sections of the Trustees’ Report. Sourcing and Contracting ● Support significant sourcing and vendor-selection processes for professional, outsourced and other major services, including market analysis, tendering and evaluation. ● Draft and review vendor, consultant and other commercial agreements, identifying key commercial, financial and operational considerations. ● Provide commercial analysis to support negotiations, supplier reviews and value-for-money assessments. Research and Governance ● Monitor market, regulatory and sector developments and assess their implications for the School. ● Conduct peer research and benchmarking across financial, staffing, organisational and employment practices to inform planning and decision-making. ● Provide analysis and briefing to support the DFO, Senior Leadership Team and Board committees. ● Develop and review financial, commercial and operational policies and support related governance and compliance work within the DFO’s portfolio. ● Provide analytical support to the School’s Enterprise Risk Management process, including assessment of material risks, their financial implications, and development of risk frameworks and reporting to inform strategic and financial planning. General ● Work collaboratively across the School and with trustees, advisers, external partners, senior leaders and departmental managers. ● Undertake other strategic analysis and project work within the DFO’s portfolio consistent with the purpose and level of the role. ● Any other duties as are within the scope, spirit and purpose of the job, as requested by the Director of Finance and Operations. Essential Criteria The successful candidate will demonstrate: ● Degree-level education or equivalent relevant professional experience. ● Significant relevant experience in financial analysis, financial planning, strategy, consulting, commercial analysis or a related field. ● Strong financial modelling and analytical skills. ● Experience delivering complex analytical or project-based work, including research, benchmarking and preparation of high-quality outputs for senior decision-makers and multiple stakeholders. ● Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex financial and strategic issues clearly. ● Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgement and manage multiple priorities. ● A demonstrated commitment to the safeguarding of children and young people. Desirable criteria ● A recognised professional accountancy or finance qualification, or relevant postgraduate qualification. ● Experience in an independent school, international school, university, charity or other mission-led organisation. ● Experience in one or more relevant areas such as long-term or capital planning, treasury or investment, procurement or contracts, Board and governance support, policy development, or Enterprise Risk Management. ● Experience using business intelligence, dashboarding or data-visualisation tools. This position description is current at the date shown but following consultation may be changed to reflect or anticipate changes in the role that are commensurate with the job title and salary. The American School in London is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all trustees, employees and volunteers to share this commitment. All new appointments will be subject to appropriate checks: Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS enhanced), Disqualification by Association Self-Declaration, Declaration of Criminal Record, checks against the Teaching Regulation Agency (TRA) Prohibition List (Teacher Status Checks) including Identity, Address, Date of Birth, a Full Employment History, Right to Work in the UK, overseas checks where applicable, at least 2 references (one with current or most recent employer, where appropriate) and original documentation of Qualifications (where appropriate). For positions into Senior Management a Prohibition from Management Check (s128 Directive) will also be undertaken. All posts involving direct contact with children are exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974. However, amendments to the Exceptions Order 1975 (2013 & 2020) provide that certain spent convictions and cautions are 'protected'. These are not subject to disclosure to employers and cannot be taken into account. Guidance and criteria on the filtering of these cautions and convictions can be found on the Ministry of Justice website. Shortlisted candidates will be asked to provide details of all unspent convictions and those that would not be filtered, prior to the date of the interview. You may be asked for further information about your criminal history during the recruitment process. If your application is successful, this self-disclosure information will be checked against information from the Disclosure & Barring Service before your appointment is confirmed. job.title: Gilman School Foreman Fellowship
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Salary Range

$45,000.00 - $45,000.00 Salary/year

Level

Experienced

Position Type

Full Time

Education Level

4 Year Degree

Category

Education

Description

FOREMAN FELLOWSHIP

2027-2028

OUR MISSION

Gilman is a diverse community dedicated to educating boys in mind, body, and spirit, with a particular emphasis on academic excellence, athletic participation, and aesthetic appreciation. Gilman seeks to produce men of character and integrity who have the skills and ability to make a positive contribution to the communities in which they live and work.

OUR COMMITMENT

Educating the Whole Boy

For more than a century, Gilman’s mission has remained exceedingly focused: to unlock the greatness within each boy by educating the entire boy—mind, body, and spirit. To accomplish that goal, we provide space and opportunity for crucial learning and self-expression to take place. We believe that boys experience transformative learning when they connect disciplines, people, and ideas in ways that deepen their sense of self and serve the needs of others.

Our rich and comprehensive program, our immeasurably talented and interesting faculty and students, and our belief in the character traits embodied by the Gilman Five—Honor, Integrity, Respect, Humility, and Excellence—combine to form the foundation of an educational environment dedicated to helping boys grow into men of character.

Community, Inclusion, and Equity

Gilman’s commitment to inclusion and equity is founded on the belief that our community is strengthened by the vibrant exchange that occurs when individuals with different backgrounds and heritages share their perspectives with one another. Through the recognition and acceptance of our many differences, we learn to appreciate and respect the complexity of the world in which we live and develop essential skills that help us forge productive relationships with those around us.

We are proud of our history as a school that has, for several generations, taken the lead on matters of diversity, inclusion, and equity. More than 40% of Gilman’s student body and 20% of the School’s faculty identify as people of color. We continue to build on that legacy through our steadfast commitment to inclusivity and equity, as well as initiatives on local, state, and national levels.

OUR SCHOOL

Gilman School is a pre-kindergarten through twelfth-grade private independent day school for boys. Set on a 57-acre campus in the northern part of Baltimore City, Gilman serves roughly 1,000 students in three divisions. The School has a full-time faculty of nearly 140, with an average class size of 16 students.

FOREMAN FELLOWSHIP

Gilman School annually offers the one-year Foreman Fellowship to recent college graduates who have a strong interest in teaching. The Foreman Fellowship honors Johnnie Foreman, Gilman’s longtime Director of Community, Inclusion, and Equity and one of Gilman’s most beloved and outstanding faculty members.

Foreman fellows benefit from the coaching of a mentor teacher and a range of unique professional development experiences.

The Foreman fellow can be assigned to Gilman’s middle or upper school depending on the candidates’ interests and experiences, as well as the school’s annual needs. Specific classroom responsibilities for the Foreman fellow will vary. Most fellows initially observe and shadow their mentor, gradually assuming instructional leadership as the fellowship unfolds.

The Foreman fellow will coach interscholastic and intramural sports, as well as support co-curricular programs, in addition to their work in the classroom. They will also assist with advising and counseling.

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

  • Work closely with a mentor teacher
  • Teach in a subject area that suits your educational background and experience
  • Observe and learn from master teachers in different divisions, pre-k through grade 12.
  • Meet frequently with other fellows and the program director for support and feedback
  • Coach two seasons of athletics, either leading interscholastic teams or working within our intramural program
  • Fulfill other duties appropriate for Gilman faculty members

WHAT YOU WILL NEED TO SUCCEED:

  • The ability to inspire and build relationships with your students
  • The willingness to grow as an educator
  • The desire to connect with students outside of formal interactions
  • An interest in a cohort experience and a collaborative learning community
  • The ambition and drive to earn a master’s degree in education while completing an intensive teaching fellowship
  • A Bachelor's Degree

ADDITIONAL DETAILS

  • POSITION TITLE: Foreman Fellow
  • STATUS/FLSA: Full Time
  • HOURS OF WORK: TBD

EOE

Gilman School is an equal opportunity employer and educator that fully and actively supports equal access for all qualified applicants, regardless of race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability status, Genetic Information or Testing, Family and Medical Leave, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We prohibit retaliation against individuals who bring forth any complaint, orally or in writing, to the employer or the government, or against any individuals who assist or participate in the investigation of any complaint, or otherwise oppose discrimination.

job.title: American International School of Bucharest Secondary School MYP English Language
job.description:
Position Description & Application

  • Division: Secondary School
  • Reports to: Secondary Principal
  • Category: Overseas or Local Hire
  • Start Date: August 2027
  • Contract Length: Initial 2 Year Contract

POSITION OVERVIEW SUMMARY

AISB’s Secondary School seeks a highly qualified and dynamic MYP English Language & Literature teacher. We are looking for an individual who has experience in the Middle Years Programme (MYP) who enjoys working across middle school grade levels. The position will likely include teaching all three grade levels with one co-taught class.

All full-time employees also have an advisory role that includes membership on a grade-level team; this position will include membership on a middle school grade-level team. Advisory teachers support our social-emotional learning program by working with a partner to mentor a homeroom of students, delivering advisory curriculum as part of a focus team, and contributing to community building events.

QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS

Education & Certification

  • Bachelor’s Degree from a University in a relevant discipline
  • Valid and active teaching certification
  • Master’s Degree in subject discipline or the field of education (preferred)

Experience

  • Experience teaching middle school English (required)
  • Experience with both the IB MYP in an international Secondary School environment (preferred)
  • Experience working with, and differentiating for, EAL and LS students
  • Experience delivering a pastoral / advisory program

Core Competencies

  • Excellent interpersonal skills; the ability to work in a highly collaborative environment
  • Excellent communication skills in English (oral and written)
  • Skills and training for effective technology integration

KEY ATTRIBUTES

  • Your philosophy aligns closely with our Learning Principles;
  • You are passionate about providing a safe, inclusive learning environment where children thrive;
  • You actively build relationships and keep student learning at the heart of what you do;
  • You understand how to establish and maintain strong partnerships between school and home ;
  • You have a positive disposition and are solution focused;
  • Your teaching fosters students' capacity to become independent, thoughtful learners in all grade levels;
  • You are flexible, and adapt easily to collaborating with different teams;
  • You are someone who students and colleagues want to be around and you communicate with clarity and kindness;
  • You place a high value on concept-based learning, inquiry and learner agency, and you understand how to develop and implement effective developmentally-appropriate learning plans which reflect these values;
  • You are able to use a range of strategies to assess learning for planning, monitoring and reporting purposes;
  • You are confident and adaptable in using technology to facilitate teaching and learning in powerful ways.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES

Classroom Teaching:

  • Teaching allocation of five classes in an eight block rotating schedule;
  • Documenting curriculum and learning experiences on Toddle, our learning management system;
  • Co-teaching with members of the Learning Support or EAL departments in at least on grade level;
  • Homeroom and advisory lessons with an assigned homeroom partner and on an advisory curriculum focus team.

Department and Grade-Level Team Member:

  • Attend co-planning, department, and grade-level meetings once per eight day cycle;
  • Facilitate student onboarding, team-building, and community events;
  • Participate in an Experiential Week trip with your assigned grade level.

Support of Students and Colleagues:

  • Working with the Learning Support, EAL, and counseling teams to support for students by ensuring that access arrangements are supported in both classroom and exam settings;
  • Working closely with students, parents, the VPs, Grade Leaders & Counselors to address and communicate student success and challenges;
  • Follow the guidelines of the school’s protective behavior policies and protocols and personal data protection policies and procedures, including reporting any situation that might constitute a health and/or safety hazard to students or school employees, and reporting any personal data breach.

Other Responsibilities:

  • Participation in Co-Curricular Activities program: one trimester in the first contract year and two each year after;
  • Supervision of two Personal Projects or Extended Essays per academic year;
  • Active engagement in AISB’s Professional Growth and Evaluation Program;
  • Other appropriate duties as assigned by the Secondary Principal or Core Leadership Team.

Other

AISB is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all students. All faculty and staff members are expected to share this commitment and adhere to the school’s Child Protection Policy. Appointment to this position is contingent upon satisfactory background checks and references.

Please note: AISB follows the guidelines of the school’s protective behavior policies and protocols and personal data protection policies and procedures, including reporting any situation that might constitute a health and/or safety hazard to students or school employees, and reporting any personal data breach.

job.title: American International School of Bucharest Elementary Vice Principal
job.description:
Position Description & Application

  • Division: Elementary School
  • Reports to: Lower School Principal
  • Category: Full-time; Overseas or Local Faculty
  • Start Date: August 2027
  • Contract Length: 2 years initial contract

POSITION OVERVIEW SUMMARY

The American International School of Bucharest (AISB) seeks an inspiring, visionary, collaborative and dynamic educational leader to serve as the Elementary Vice Principal. We are looking for an experienced leader who will work with students, faculty, parents, and leadership teams to actively champion and support students' social and emotional well-being. The Elementary VP is pivotal in supporting the student care process through a multi-tiered approach to promoting students' attendance, punctuality, behavior, academics and well-being working closely with teachers and counselors to support the Social-Emotional Learning program. The Elementary Vice Principal holds operational oversight for key systems which facilitate the smooth running of the Elementary School and the well-being of students.

As a vital member of the Elementary Leadership Team, the Elementary Vice Principal reports directly to the Lower School Principal and works in close partnership with the PYP Coordinator, the Student Support Coordinator and the other Vice Principals working across the School. The Elementary Vice Principal is a key member of the Lower School Leadership Team and the Learning Leadership Team.

QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS

Education & Certification

It is expected that candidates for this position will be highly qualified educators, with:

  • A Degree and Teaching Certification
  • A Master’s degree or equivalent in Educational Leadership, Elementary Education, or a related field (preferred)

Experience

  • A proven track record of successful classroom teaching followed by significant leadership experience that includes implementing social-emotional learning programs and leading pastoral care teams.
  • Significant experience designing, implementing, and optimizing master schedules and operational systems to ensure seamless day-to-day operations across elementary school grade levels

Core Competencies

  • Strong understanding of Multi-Tiered System of Supports (MTSS), Social Emotional Learning (SEL) and Restorative Practices;
  • Skilled at partnering with multiple stakeholders to ensure shared understanding and smooth coordination of Elementary operations;
  • Proven ability to lead teams with empathy, clarity, and high expectations;
  • Strong communication skills, with confidence navigating courageous conversations and feedback;
  • Exceptional organizational skills, systems thinking and the ability to manage multiple priorities;

KEY ATTRIBUTES

  • Demonstrates a growth mindset while being proactive, collaborative, and decisive
  • Dedication to holding students, teachers, and parents to high expectations
  • Ability to foster and maintain positive relationships with all members of the community (students, staff and parents)
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
  • Experience in adult coaching/mentoring
  • Highly organized with systems thinking

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES

Educational Leadership

  • As a core member of the Elementary Leadership Team, support the implementation of the PYP curriculum framework, ensuring alignment with the school's mission.
  • Stay current with educational trends and research and IB program developments through professional learning.
  • Collaborate with teachers and staff to enhance the quality of teaching and learning.
  • Partner with Learning Support and EAL teams to ensure MTSS interventions are coordinated and monitored across tiers.
  • Champion identity-conscious and culturally responsive practice across curriculum, pastoral care, and community life.
  • Provide instructional leadership and ensure social-emotional well-being is embedded across all curricula and pastoral learning.
  • Collaborate with the Elementary Leadership Team and other educational leaders to align pastoral care with the mission of the school.
  • Collaborate with the ELC and Secondary Vice Principals to ensure consistent systems and procedures across the School.

Student Support

  • Take a leading role in creating a safe and positive learning environment for students.
  • Work with the counselors and designated safeguarding lead to support student safety and well-being.
  • Implement strategies to monitor and support students' social and emotional well-being within the PYP framework and in accordance with our Multi-Tiered System of Support.
  • Monitor, assess, and adjust the effectiveness of the elementary social-emotional learning program.
  • Work alongside Elementary Support Services teams to develop and implement programs and initiatives that grow students' social and emotional capacity as part of our Student Care and Response to Intervention programs.
  • Create, maintain and support opportunities for student leadership and agency.
  • Support the Co-Curricular Activities Team to ensure a successful and smooth program for students.

Supporting Positive Behaviors

  • Promote and integrate the school's values and the IB Learner Profile into the daily life of the school.
  • Take a lead in modeling and advancing responsible and respectful behavior.
  • Provide guidance and strategies to teachers for effective classroom management.
  • Maintain shared behavior management systems that emphasize restorative practices and conflict resolution.
  • Collaborate with teachers and counselors to address student behavioral issues and disciplinary matters in a supportive, solutions-focused manner.
  • Investigate and address serious disciplinary incidents, ensuring a fair, consistent process that is respectful of all parties involved.

Operational Leadership

  • In partnership with the Lower School Principal, manage the day-to-day operations, safety protocols, and behavioral and social-emotional needs across the Elementary School, ensuring compliance with school policies and international accreditation standards.
  • Take the lead in scheduling, active supervision, student enrollment, assemblies and facilities management.
  • Maintain and monitor systems to support student attendance and minimise lateness.
  • Analyze attendance, behavior, and well-being data to identify trends and inform intervention planning
  • Participate in budgeting and resource allocation decisions as needed.
  • Lead the transition process from KG to Grade 1 and support the Grade 5 to Grade 6 transition process.
  • Manage assessments and recommendation requests for students transitioning out from AISB.
  • Support Grade Level Leaders and other trip organizers with risk assessments, planning documentation, staffing and other practicalities of overnight residentials

Faculty Development

  • Lead and support professional development opportunities for faculty.
  • Mentor and grow the capacity of faculty and Learning Leaders across the Elementary School
  • Assist in the recruitment, evaluation and mentoring of faculty and staff
  • Contribute to Learning Walks to support effective teaching practices across the Elementary School.
  • Provide professional development opportunities for teachers to enhance their understanding and implementation of social-emotional learning practices.

Parent and Community Engagement

  • Foster strong relationships with parents and the broader school community.
  • Organize and participate in parent-teacher conferences and educational events.
  • Facilitate Student Study Team meetings, Student Care meetings and parent meetings.
  • Support the onboarding and transition of new-to-school families throughout the year
  • Organize and participate in parent education programs related to social emotional learning and upholding community agreements.

School Policies and Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with school policies, local educational regulations, and IB Standards & Practices.
  • Support the Principal in developing and updating school policies and procedures.
  • Lead the updating of policies and procedures related to student well-being.
  • Support the Elementary Leadership Team in the preparation for the accreditation visits (IB and NEASC)

Crisis Management

  • Assist in managing crises and emergencies within the school, working with the Principal to ensure the safety and well-being of students and faculty.
  • Play a key role in the Elementary School’s response team, ensuring that students and staff receive the necessary support during challenging situations.

Other duties

● Perform other duties as assigned by the Principal to support the overall functioning of the school.

CAMPUS AND LIFE IN BUCHAREST:

AISB's home is a beautiful, purpose-built ten-hectare campus located in the green suburb of Voluntari, offering the perfect balance of space and proximity to central Bucharest. As a safe, vibrant, and cosmopolitan capital, Bucharest captivates expatriates with its historic charm, tree-lined avenues, and a booming, modern cultural scene. Expatriate educators at AISB enjoy a high quality of life. Bucharest remains one of the most affordable European capitals, allowing for good savings potential paired with a generous school benefits package, including comprehensive health care, flights, and an extensive housing subsidy.

AISB At A Glance:

  • Enrollment: Close to 900 students from 60+ nationalities (Ages 2 to 18). Faculty & Staff: 280+ dedicated professionals, with over 63% of faculty holding advanced degrees.
  • Student-Teacher Ratio: An average student-to-teacher ratio of 6:1, allowing for genuinely personalized learning.

GDPR & DATA PROTECTION DISCLAIMER

By submitting an application for this position, you acknowledge and agree that the American International School of Bucharest (AISB) will process your personal data in compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the school’s personal data protection policies. Your data will be collected and processed solely for recruitment and selection purposes. Unsuccessful candidate documentation will be securely deleted or archived in accordance with legal retention periods unless explicit consent is provided for future opportunities.

Other

AISB is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all students. All faculty and staff members are expected to share this commitment and adhere to the school’s Child Protection Policy. Appointment to this position is contingent upon satisfactory background checks and references.

Please note: AISB follows the guidelines of the school’s protective behavior policies and protocols and personal data protection policies and procedures, including reporting any situation that might constitute a health and/or safety hazard to students or school employees, and reporting any personal data breach.

job.title: American International School of Bucharest Secondary School Counselor
job.description:
Position Description & Application

  • Division: Secondary School
  • Reports to: Secondary Principal
  • Category: Overseas or Local Hire
  • Start Date: August 2027
  • Contract Length: Initial 2 Year Contract

POSITION OVERVIEW SUMMARY

AISB Counselors aspire to cultivate a compassionate, safe and inclusive environment where all students feel affirmed, heard and empowered to be themselves and take courageous action in life. They deliver a comprehensive developmental counseling program; work in partnership with students, parents, faculty and staff; advocate for and value the diversity of all students within a global context; and foster wellbeing and the holistic development of each student.

AISB Counselors believe that all students:

  • Have the ability and the right to learn, grow and develop;
  • Have the right to a caring adult professional advocate at school;
  • Have the right to feel safe, supported, and accepted in school;
  • Have unique skills, strengths and potential.

QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS

Education & Certification

  • A university degree in a related field;
  • A school counseling certification or relevant accreditation;

Experience

  • At least 5 years previous experience in a school setting;
  • International school experience (preferred);
  • Working with and/or understanding of MYP & DP (preferred);
  • Understand and/or have experience implementing a Social-Emotional Learning curriculum;
  • Working with and understanding young learners and their development;

Core Competencies

  • Excellent interpersonal skills; the ability to work in a highly collaborative environment;
  • Excellent communication skills in English (oral and written);
  • Skills and training for effective technology integration.

KEY ATTRIBUTES

  • Ability to connect and relate warmly to children and adults;
  • A holistic and strength based approach to working with children and families;
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality;
  • Excellent listening, observational, verbal and written communication skills;
  • The ability to collaborate with others and consider alternative perspectives;
  • A commitment to professional growth;
  • A proactive approach and ability to take initiative when needed;
  • Ability to navigate emotionally intense situations;
  • Patient, enthusiastic, sensitive and flexible.

job.description:
Position Description & Application

  • Division: Secondary School
  • Reports to: Secondary Principal
  • Category: Overseas or Local Hire
  • Start Date: July 2027
  • Contract Length: Initial 2 Year Contract

POSITION OVERVIEW SUMMARY

The Secondary School seeks a highly qualified and dynamic MYP Pedagogical Coordinator. We are looking for an experienced MYP Coordinator to oversee the guidance of students through middle and into high school as they progress through the requirements of the Middle Years Programme. Candidates should be knowledgeable about and interested in supporting the development of both the MYP and alternative graduation pathways. The MYP Pedagogical Coordinator is expected to maintain a thorough understanding of all aspects of the Middle Years Programme as well as to work with students, faculty, parents and leadership in order to actively endorse and promote the principles which underpin this programme and AISB’s Future Designs. The MYP Pedagogical Coordinator reports to the Secondary School Principal and is an active member of the Curriculum, Instruction, and Assessment, Learning Leadership, and Secondary School Leadership teams.

At AISB, we are passionate about the well-being of students and helping to mentor them through their journey as adolescents. Therefore, all teachers are committed to working with Grade Level teams in developing and delivering a responsive advisory and mentoring program to meet the needs of our students. The MYP Pedagogical Coordinator works closely with the grade level leaders in 6-10 to support this program.

QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS

Education & Certification

  • Bachelor’s Degree from a University (required)
  • Active Teaching Certification (required)

Experience

  • Substantial experience of successful teaching within the IB Middle Years Programme
  • Experience in a position of added responsibility such as Learning Leader, Grade Leader, Coordinator
  • Experience collaborating with teams to design engaging and effective learning experiences for Secondary students
  • Experience working with and supporting English as an Additional Language (EAL) and Learning Support students, and of working collaboratively with teachers and counselors in the support of all students.

Core Competencies

  • Utilizing a strengths-based and solution-focused approach;
  • Flexible, adaptable, and collaborative;
  • Effective communicator who is clear, concise, and kind: in communication and disposition.

KEY ATTRIBUTES

  • Your philosophy aligns closely with our Learning Principles;
  • You are passionate about providing a safe, inclusive learning environment where children thrive;
  • Building relationships is important to you and student learning is at the heart of what you do;
  • You understand how to establish and maintain strong partnerships between school and home ;
  • Your teaching fosters students' capacity to become independent, thoughtful learners in all grade levels;
  • You place a high value on concept-based learning, inquiry and learner agency, and you understand how to develop and implement effective developmentally-appropriate learning plans which reflect these values;
  • You are able to use a range of strategies to assess learning for planning, monitoring and reporting purposes;
  • You are confident and adaptable in using technology to enrich teaching and learning in powerful ways.
  • You bring value to AISB by generously sharing skills and knowledge and openly encouraging the exchange of ideas at all levels.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES

MYP Administration:

  • Maintaining regular contact with the IB and assuming overall responsibility for administering, distributing, completing and returning all relevant documentation;
  • Supporting and advising teaching staff regarding the administration of the MYP and access to and use of IBIS;
  • Ensuring faculty have the necessary IB training and completing registration for IB workshops;
  • Drafting, issuing and administering the exam and invigilation timetables for MAP testing of all MYP students as well as Grade 10 end of year exams;
  • Overseeing the registration process for all MYP students and providing oversight of the Personal Project (PP) process, in collaboration with the PP Coordinator;
  • Maintaining the MYP at AISB and MYP Admin Google Drives, which house all essential MYP administrative and curricular materials;
  • Working with the registrar and counselors to ensure reports and transcripts are accurate.

Support of Faculty and Students:

  • Supporting and guiding the middle years Service Learning program to ensure the effective implementation, development and completion of the IB and AISB components;
  • Guiding MYP faculty in the documentation of curriculum material and the migration of this material to Toddle;
  • Working closely with students, parents, the VPs, Grade Leaders & Counselors to address and communicate student challenges;
  • Informing and updating parents, students, and the outside community about the goals and structure of the MYP program, as well as ensuring they are aware of alternative elective and pathway options in high school
  • Working with the GLL for Grades 9 & 10, as well as the DP Coordinator and high school counselors, to oversee the course selection process for electives and pathways;
  • Working with the Learning Support, EAL, and counseling teams to support for students who need additional support by ensuring that access arrangements are supported in both classroom and exam settings;
  • Supporting the development and documentation of curriculum pathways for non-DP students and guiding Learning Leaders and teachers in adjusting and documenting curriculum to satisfy High School curriculum requirements;
  • Supporting the learning of both taught and self-taught students within the Home Language program;

Other Responsibilities:

  • Teaching allocation of a maximum of two classes (up to 40%);
  • Follow the guidelines of the school’s protective behavior policies and protocols and personal data protection policies and procedures, including reporting any situation that might constitute a health and/or safety hazard to students or school employees, and reporting any personal data breach.
  • Other appropriate duties as assigned by the Secondary Principal or Core Leadership Team.

TEAM RESPONSIBILITIES

In addition to core responsibilities, the MYP Pedagogical coordinator is a member of and carries the following responsibilities on each of these teams:

Secondary Leadership Team

  • To plan and facilitate both the New Faculty Orientation and Secondary Orientations;
  • To facilitate professional learning by regularly visiting classrooms and engaging in Learning Walks;
  • With the DP Coordinator, leading the team of Secondary Learning Leaders through coaching and mentoring, supporting curriculum development, and facilitating meetings and retreats;
  • With the DP Coordinator, organizing, communicating and overseeing reporting processes.
  • To plan and assist in leading parent coffees and other informational sessions;
  • To support the Admissions team by communicating with prospective families and providing input on applications;
  • To support recurring and hiring;

Learning Leadership Team

  • To develop the continuity and effectiveness of curriculum and pedagogy across the whole school, including the accreditation process;
  • To manage the whole-school Professional Learning Budget;
  • To lead and design whole school and sectional professional learning opportunities;
  • To disseminate information and ensure understanding of MYP programmes to the wider community;
  • To serve on committees for our Future Design commitments.

Curriculum, Instruction, and Assessment Team

  • Coordinate and lead the curriculum review process;
  • Create and review procedures and policies to align teaching and learning across the school;
  • Conduct Learning Walks to build understanding of teaching and learning across the school;
  • Review professional learning requests;
  • Collect and analyze data about teaching and learning and make recommendations about next steps.

OTHER
