job.title: Mid-Peninsula High School Full-Time High School Physical Education & Substitute
job.description:
Position Description

Dedicated to the belief that all students belong with expert and compassionate teachers, Mid-Peninsula High School empowers students with the knowledge and purpose to impact a complex world. Mid-Pen is committed to caring for and supporting our 116 students from around the Bay Area by developing authentic, personal relationships with them and their families. We seek candidates who are highly skilled, deeply committed, and who derive both professional and personal joy from working with fascinating students, supportive parents and guardians, and wonderful colleagues.

Mid-Peninsula High School in Menlo Park, CA, seeks a part-time Physical Education (PE) and substitute teacher. This position would begin as soon as possible. We seek a candidate who wants to be a member of a thriving and compassionate community and who can embrace the roles of teacher, advisor, and colleague with passion and excellence. A candidate can expect to be paid between $83,160 and $126,104.

What should a PE & substitute teacher expect?

As members of Mid-Pen’s staffulty, we all contribute to the life of the school by upholding our core values: respect, kindness, responsibility, and belonging. These values inform the relationships we form with students, families, and colleagues. We believe that students learn best when they are seen, cared for, and held in a safe place with appropriate boundaries. Our highly relational staffulty do their best to meet students where they are, partnering with the Learning Support Team to support students who learn differently, with the School Counselor for support with Core (our advisory system), and with the administration as necessary.

Mid-Pen has a diverse student population with varying degrees of physical ability. Our PE classes generally include a warm-up, learning the basics of a sport, practicing the skills, and then cooling down by the end of class. Units include many team sports (volleyball, basketball, soccer, etc.) and individual sports (archery, running, calisthenics, etc.).

Our PE classes run during periods 1, 2, and 4, and each class period meets four times a week. During the remaining periods (3, 5, and 6), our new teacher would be available to sub classes as needed, set up lunch daily, and provide other support for our colleagues and students. Ideally, our new teacher would have some expertise in soccer and/or volleyball and could coach a sport in the afternoon for an added stipend. Our new teacher will also serve as our shuttle van driver in the mornings for pickup at the Caltrain station in Menlo Park, and will also drive students to and from games and practices. Therefore, our new teacher will need to have a valid driver's license.

What kinds of skills and mindsets are needed for a PE teacher at Mid-Pen?

An ideal candidate will be an active person with an infectious, upbeat energy, a compassionate and patient demeanor, and a willingness to meet students where they are while also encouraging and supporting them in doing their best. They will find joy in working with high school students on a personal level, and they should be able to effectively lead a PE class by developing clear objectives, strong relationships, and a keen eye for productive fun. Applicants should send a cover letter and resume to employment@mid-pen.org The school will accept applications until the position is filled. Find more information about our school at www.mid-pen.org

Mid-Peninsula High School is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Mid-Pen adheres to an employment policy that prohibits discriminatory practices or harassment against applicants or employees based on race, color, creed, age, gender, gender identity, gender expression, religion, ethnicity or national origin, sexual orientation, genetic information, pregnancy or pregnancy-related medical conditions, any protected military or veteran status, physical disability, or any other category protected by applicable Federal, State, or Local law.

Primary responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

● Teaching three sections of Physical Education classes, and substituting classes as needed

● Running our morning shuttle between Caltrain and campus

● Collaborating with the Athletics Director to continually develop curriculum and pedagogy that best serve our students

● Potentially coaching in the afternoons for an additional stipend

● Being a collegial and spirited member of the school community, attending meetings and check-ins as necessary, and being a presence at extracurricular events occasionally

● Conveying a passion for teamwork and enthusiasm for content

Skills, Mindset, and Background:

● A willingness to embrace the Mid-Pen Mission Statement and core values, and a strong desire to be a positive, active, and joyful presence in the school's daily life, are required.

● A bachelor’s degree in a related field is required. A master's degree or other relevant graduate-level work is a plus.

● Three years of relevant experience, ideally in a secondary school setting

● Strong interpersonal skills, close attention to detail, and willingness to work collaboratively are essential.

● A desire to partner with colleagues and families, flexibility, a commitment to issues of justice/equity/diversity/inclusion, and a sense of humor are required.

job.title: The Lawrenceville School Assistant Director of Stewardship
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Job Type

Full-time

Description

Summary:

The Assistant Director of Stewardship is responsible for overseeing the gift acknowledgement process, assisting in major stewardship reporting, updating database stewardship records and requesting needed reporting, and managing visible donor recognition and related activities. The Assistant Director is responsible for creating and managing grant proposals and foundation updates. Additionally, they actively contribute to the management and planning of leadership donor events, activities for giving societies, and major stewardship publications (e.g. Report of Giving).

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

Gift Acknowledgements Process

  • Manage all aspects of the acknowledgement process end-to-end, collaborating with colleagues as needed, crafting messages, sending materials, documenting correspondence, overseeing others staff involved
  • Maintain documentation of the ack process to be shared as needed (SOP)
  • Ensure acknowledgements are being sent to donors in a timely manner
  • Meet regularly with CAO and/or others to review needed special outreach
  • Evaluate systems regularly for improvement, streamlining processes and use creativity and technology as able.
  • Manage special situation acknowledgement projects as needed (e.g. select tributes)

Donor Reports

  • In partnership with team members, help prepare, produce, and deliver on signature stewardship reporting for endowment funds, faculty named chairs, and named scholarships:
  1. Review and prep data for donor and fund information as needed based on the report
  2. Pulling/requesting lists and data for mailing, content, etc.
  3. Replicating templates and executing needed mail merges and individualization for report content
  4. Outreach to campus partners for needed content and planning purposes
  5. Helping coordinator organize mailing and creation of materials
  6. Reviewing final reports for accuracy and checking on “matching data”
  7. Ensuring RE records are properly updated with report sends
  • Assist in writing, submitting, and management of grant relationships in addition to stewardship of grant funders.

Visible Donor Recognition and Events

  • Manage and oversee the production, installation, placement, and all related activities for plaques (and related visible recognition); including working with frontline team for donor approvals on plaque language and location
  • Serve as team liaison for B&G on plaque-related installations on campus; and serve as team liaison for planning BOT-related ceremonies
  • Create and maintain records for the School on plaque placement, history, and mapping, to serve as a main reference guide for all plaques on campus
  • Assist in the planning and strategic development of various donor recognition activities for giving societies and other special occasions, including Weeden Lecture Dinner, groundbreakings, dedications, society gatherings, memorials, ribbon-cuttings, etc.

Stewardship Record Management and Data/List

  • Keep RE (database) records and shred filing system organized updated with fund-donor relationships, donor recognition and fund names, and other needed stewardship information
  • Develop processes with Adv Services and other team members for getting needed update information on stewardship from update systems (e.g. new named fund agreements, obituaries)
  • Oversee and produce lists for annual/quarterly, and ad-hoc, donor and gift/fund reviews for with frontline team for donor approvals on plaque language and location
  • Manage giving society lists and top donor dashboards/lists and develop and manage distribution of needed lists to relevant team members

Participate in professional development activities; Keep apprised of industry best practices, and recommend how the School might improve or modify its stewardship program in accordance with those practices.

Participate in School and Team activities (e.g. smeetings, retreats, etc.)

Fulfill administrative functions for role and team

Perform other duties as requested

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree required.
  • Minimum of 3-5 years’ related experience in stewardship, communications, alumni relations, fundraising, or a related field is highly preferred.
  • Excellent writing and organizational skills, along with clear and concise verbal communication skills, required. A successful candidate will be comfortable communicating in a variety of mediums -- writing letters, compiling longer narratives, as well as writing for email, video, and social media.
  • A creative, entrepreneurial approach to assigned work is required. Prior experience in stewardship, special events, or in managing donor/client relationships, is highly preferred.
  • Prior experience in fundraising preferred. Prior experience with fundraising in an independent school setting is highly preferred.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and Google Software is required. Experience working with one or more donor databases preferred.
  • Must be highly motivated, self-directed and achievement-oriented, and show a fine attention to detail. Must be able to successfully manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Must work well with donors, colleagues (including senior administrators), and other constituents; comfortable working alone and with others.
  • Must have availability to work some nights and weekends. Occasional travel will be required.

Work Characteristics and Physical Demands:

The work environment characteristics and physical demands described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  1. Physical demands are in excess of those for sedentary work. Must be able to remain on their feet for extended periods of time, go up and down flights of steps, as well as stoop, kneel, crouch, and lift.
  2. Routinely use standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, fax machines, etc.
  3. Must be capable of using visual display terminal with continuous wrist movement on a keyboard
  4. Required to stand for long periods of time
  5. Required to, talk, hear, walk, use hands to finger, handle or feel and reach with hands and arms
  6. Required to work evenings, weekends and holidays in conjunction with School calendar and events
  7. Must be able to lift up to 25lbs. without assistance
  8. Ability to see with normal parameters.
  9. Operate in a professional work environment
  10. This is an on-campus position.

The Lawrenceville School is a diverse and inclusive community and makes all employment decisions without regard for an individual’s race, creed, color, religion, national origin, nationality, sex, pregnancy, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, veteran status, physical or mental disability (including AIDS and HIV related illness), genetic information, refusal to provide genetic information, refusal to submit to genetic testing, ancestry, familial status, marital status, domestic partnership status, civil union status, atypical cellular or blood trait, military service, application for military service, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. The Lawrenceville School will also provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals in accordance with applicable law.

The Lawrenceville School conducts pre-employment screening for all positions which includes a criminal background check, verification of work history, academic credentials, licenses, and certifications. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of the background check.

Eligible employees receive a competitive benefit package that includes health insurance coverage, paid leave and retirement plan options and many other valuable programs.

Salary Description

$62,000.00 - $72,000.00 annually

job.title: The Hotchkiss School Athletics Facilities Maintenance & Ice Rink Manager
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Schedule: As a professional management role, this position requires flexibility to maintain facility coverage, operational responsiveness, and resolution of emergent facility needs. Non-ice season hours are generally Monday through Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. During the ice rink season (November 1 through early March), the schedule is generally four weekday shifts and one full weekend day, with additional evening or event coverage as dictated by athletics schedules, facility demands, and operational necessity. The position is considered essential to operations during inclement weather or other emergencies.

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Athletics Facilities Maintenance & Ice Rink Manager for the Mars Athletic Center (MAC) provides hands-on operational leadership, facility oversight, and maintenance staff management for the athletic facilities. As a working manager, they ensure operational excellence, staff cross-training, and seamless operational continuity.

The Athletics Facilities Maintenance & Ice Rink Manager coordinates closely with the Director of Athletics to oversee MAC facility maintenance. They direct all ice rink operations, serving as the lead for ice maintenance, ammonia refrigeration safety, and event coverage. They oversee equipment, facility readiness, compliance and safety, and support for practices, games, tournaments, rentals, and other programs.

During non-ice periods, the position oversees and supports athletic maintenance operations within the Mars Athletic Center and other assigned athletics facilities. These responsibilities include seasonal facility conversions, event setup and breakdown, equipment and storage organization, facility inspections and custodial services, and general operational support. This is a working-manager role, setting the example for operational excellence.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

Athletics Facilities Management Support

  • Lead, mentor, and supervise MAC maintenance staff and rink staff while the ice is down.
  • Ensure staff are cross-trained in all MAC maintenance and custodial duties to ensure operational flexibility and continuity.
  • Coordinate staff scheduling for optimal coverage, minimizing overtime wherever possible.
  • Proactively build and refine facility operational procedures.
  • Lead conversion of Dwyer Rink between ice, indoor turf, summer programming, and event configurations.
  • Support operational readiness throughout the Mars Athletic Center and other assigned athletics spaces.
  • Lead setup, breakdown, and reset for games, tournaments, camps, community use, and School events.
  • Lead athletics equipment movement, receiving, storage, inventory, and distribution.
  • Lead custodial operations for the entire athletic facility.
  • Conduct routine facility inspections and report safety, maintenance, access, or cleanliness concerns.
  • Lead the equipment-room, laundry, building-access, and related Athletics functions.
  • Support other Athletics facility projects and seasonal operating needs as directed.

Rink Management

  • Manage overall ice rink operations, staff and vendor scheduling, daily workflow, and facility coverage.
  • Supervise, train, and mentor rink technicians in all aspects of rink maintenance.
  • Demonstrated knowledge and experience necessary to serve as the operational lead for maintaining the ammonia refrigeration system in compliance with OSHA requirements and other applicable regulations, in partnership with qualified outside service professionals, Facilities Services, and Safety and Security.
  • Ensure compliance with all school safety policies, environmental standards, and hazardous material protocols.
  • Lead the installation, maintenance, repair, and breakdown of ice surfaces.
  • Safely operate and perform routine maintenance on ice resurfacing and skate sharpening equipment.
  • Oversee climate control, ice quality monitoring, and refrigeration system checks.
  • Maintain facility cleanliness, building accessibility, and spectator safety standards.
  • Operate ice resurfacing equipment.
  • Operate skate sharpening equipment.
  • Lead and perform custodial duties.
  • Perform additional duties as needed and assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience required.
  • Current Certified Ice Technician (CIT) and Certified Pool Operator (CPO), or ability to obtain within the first year of employment.
  • Proven track record in a leadership role with a demonstrated ability to lead by example and cross-train staff.
  • Strong technical capabilities and ability to learn new software.
  • Excellent communication, organizational and customer service skills.
  • Strong attention to detail.
  • Must possess a valid driver’s license.

PHYSICAL CONDITIONS:

  • Required to lift approximately 50+ pounds.
  • Bend, stoop, reach and kneel.
  • Climb up to 4 flights of stairs.
  • Work with or be in areas where hazardous materials may be present.
  • Work in the ice rinks with cold temperatures.
  • Stand for long periods of time.
  • Sit for long periods of time on a tractor, etc.
  • Walk for long periods of time on different types of terrain.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

The essential functions and basic skills have been included. It is not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all functions, responsibilities, skills and abilities. Additional functions and requirements may be assigned by supervisors as deemed appropriate.

The Hotchkiss School is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to basing judgments concerning the employment of individuals upon their qualifications and abilities. The School is firmly committed to equal employment and advancement opportunities for all employees and applicants in all phases of the employment process (including recruitment, hiring, assignment, terms, and conditions of employment, compensation, benefits, training, promotion, transfer, discipline, and termination).

job.title: The Hotchkiss School Childcare Director
job.description:
Position Description & Application

The Childcare Director for the Cynthia White Children’s Center (CWCC) leads a team of early childhood educators to create and implement high-quality programming while managing the center’s daily operations. The Childcare Director builds strong partnerships with families to nurture each child’s healthy development. They are committed to creating an inclusive environment where each child can have a sense of belonging and the opportunity to thrive in meaningful ways.

The Children’s Center operates on the campus of The Hotchkiss School and was originally established to primarily serve the faculty and staff of the School, with a portion of the enrollment offered to the public. The Director is responsible for the development and management of the center’s annual operating budget in consultation with the Chief Financial and Operations Officer (CFOO), ensuring that expenditures and resourcing are fiscally appropriate and support the best interests of The Hotchkiss School and the Center’s enrolled children.

The Childcare Director successfully balances a variety of responsibilities, from daily operations and staff supervision, to program planning and development, while cultivating positive relationships with children and their families.

The School is eager to accept applications from individuals who are excited to support an inclusive and warm working and learning environment.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

Team Leadership and Program Development

  • Attract, develop and retain a team of “best in class” educators to be passionate and committed professionals.
  • Work cooperatively with staff to establish effective and healthy team dynamics.
  • Ensure all staff participate in ongoing professional development to implement early childhood programming that inspires the healthy development of the children.

Curriculum and Child Development

  • Ensure that the curriculum and activities align with the Hotchkiss mission, promoting values of diversity and inclusion.
  • Oversee Lead Teachers’ planning and implementation of curriculum and themes displayed.
  • Oversee Assistant Teachers’ coordination of enrichment activities, ensuring that themes and skills taught align with the curriculum.
  • Supervise and participate in outdoor and indoor play and activities.
  • Coordinate child assessments and parent conferences at least twice per year.
  • Oversee student observation guidelines and processes to ensure staff appropriately report ongoing development. communicating about the general well-being and progress of each child to their parent/guardian.
  • Be aware of and appropriately communicate about possible illness, maintaining staff, child, & parent/guardian confidentiality.

Operations and Compliance

  • Effectively communicate with both the CFOO and Associate Head of School when deliberating enrollment strategies and supporting internal Hotchkiss community needs.
  • Work closely with the CFOO on the development and management of the center’s annual operating budget, ensuring that expenditures and resourcing are fiscally appropriate.
  • Partner with Human Resources to develop and implement a staffing strategy that supports the approved budget and enrollment.
  • Conduct OEC-specific background checks on new hires.
  • Manage enrollment, processing of applications and accounting related to tuition payments.
  • Ensure classrooms are equipped with the materials that children need to learn, to explore their interests, and to express their creativity.
  • Oversee the Center’s purchasing needs of all supplies and equipment while maintaining an inventory of the same.
  • Evaluate and develop CWCC procedures and policies, guided by both Hotchkiss policies and procedures as well as those mandated under State of CT licensure, including local and state health and safety codes.
  • Maintain all applicable documentation required for State of CT licensure and inspection.
  • Accurately and confidentially manage required record keeping of medical, informational, emergency contact, and consent-for-treatment forms on each attending child while complying with state guidelines.
  • Be cognizant of insurance policies and liabilities as they relate to the Center.
  • Ensure proper supervision and delegation of responsibilities, ensuring the care and safety of children at all times during any approved absence.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned or needed to maintain a safe learning environment.

EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE REQUIRED:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Early Childhood Development required, Master’s Degree preferred.
  • Minimum of 3-5 years as a director or leadership role (such as assistant director) in a licensed daycare or preschool setting. Experience at the director level is preferred.
  • State of CT certified Day Care Director or willingness to complete course certification prior to employment.
  • Certification in First Aid and CPR required, renewed annually.
  • Working knowledge of early childhood development programs, methods, materials, and practices used in early child care educational settings, required.
  • Experience with implementing safety practices and procedures in a daycare setting is preferred.
  • Experience with CT state licensure requirements preferred.
  • Computer skills with the ability to use Excel and Word and Google Suite applications.

SKILLS:

  • Possess the emergency response acumen to decisively handle emergency situations.
  • Ability to maintain an environment of cheerfulness and security for children entrusted to the Center.
  • Understand judicious use of authority within the program.
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills: diplomacy and tact and the ability to work effectively with parents/guardians and staff within a diverse school community.
  • Demonstrated strong organizational skills for prioritizing, multi-tasking and functioning under a variety of deadlines, with an attention to detail.
  • Able to maintain a professional demeanor: adept at external and internal customer service.
  • Desire and ability to demonstrate flexibility and patience.
  • Ability to prepare accurate reports from various statistical or other detailed information.
  • Possess the ability to effectively direct, instruct, schedule, supervise, and evaluate the work of CWCC staff.
  • Be a Team player: ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships.

PHYSICAL CONDITIONS:

  • While performing the duties of this job, the Director and CWCC staff are frequently required to walk, run (when needed to supervise children), stand, sit, squat, reach, talk and hear.
  • Must be able to occasionally climb or balance, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl.
  • Must be able to frequently lift and/or move 20-25 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move 35-50 pounds carrying children.
  • Must be able to push a stroller and take long walks.
  • Must be able to remain patient and effective with frequent interruptions.
  • Must be able to change diapers, feed, and/or clean children and assist children in using the restroom. Children are newborn up through preschool age.
  • The Hotchkiss School is a tobacco-free environment.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

The essential functions and basic skills have been included. It is not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all functions, responsibilities, skills and abilities. Additional functions and requirements may be assigned by supervisors as deemed appropriate. This position description is subject to change at any time.

The Hotchkiss School is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to basing judgments concerning the employment of individuals upon their qualifications and abilities. The School is firmly committed to equal employment and advancement opportunities for all employees and applicants in all phases of the employment process (including recruitment, hiring, assignment, terms and conditions of employment, compensation, benefits, training, promotion, transfer, discipline and termination).

In accordance with applicable law, the School does not discriminate against any individual based on age, ancestry, color, genetic information, learning disability, marital status, past or present history of mental disability, national origin, physical disability, race, religious creed, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

job.title: Lowell School After Care and Summer Program Coordinator
job.description:
Position Description & Application

After Care and Summer Program Coordinator

Lowell School, a progressive school serving approximately 300 students in NW Washington, DC, is seeking a dedicated and dynamic After Care and Summer Program Coordinator. This is a 12-month, full-time, exempt leadership position responsible for the daily management, staffing, logistics, and quality assurance of our extended-day programs year-round. Reporting directly to the Director of Auxiliary Programs, you will serve as a key operational bridge among regular school hours, after-school enrichment, and summer programming. The position's primary goal will be to ensure that all before-care, after-care, break camp, and summer program activities deliver a safe, nurturing, highly organized, and progressively minded experience for children from preschool through 8th grade—extending Lowell's commitment to student agency, inquiry-based learning, and child-centered care into all out-of-school time.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Program Operations: Manage end-to-end daily operations for before care, after care, and summer after care, overseeing student check-in/check-out, snack distribution, homework support, and activity rotations.
  • Summer and Break Camps: Serve as the full-time on-site coordinator for summer programming (December planning through July/August execution) and execute coverage programs during school breaks and professional development days.
  • Staff Leadership: Coordinate daily staff assignments to maintain required adult-to-child supervision ratios, while training and mentoring after-care assistants, enrichment instructors, and seasonal summer staff.
  • Student Care and Safety: Foster an inclusive, engaging community grounded in progressive educational practices, utilizing the Responsive Classroom approach, social-emotional learning principles, and student-driven activity design.
  • Family Communication: Serve as the primary day-to-day operational contact for parents during program hours, upholding exceptional customer service standards and drafting routine program announcements.

What You Bring to Lowell

  • Minimum three to five years of experience leading youth programs, after-school care, or summer camps, preferably within an independent school environment.
  • Ideally, a Bachelor's degree in education, youth development, recreation management, or a related field is preferred (a master's degree is a plus).
  • Exceptional interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.
  • Proficiency with database/registration software (e.g., CampBrain, Veracross, Blackbaud) and Microsoft Office/Google Workspace.
  • Current certification in First Aid, CPR, and AED, or willingness to complete within 30 days of hire.
  • Working knowledge of or demonstrated commitment to progressive education practices (i.e., experiential learning, student agency, child-centered behavior guidance).
  • Familiarity with Responsive Classroom principles, positive behavior interventions, and DC childcare licensing requirements.

Schedule and Physical Demands:

  • Academic Year: Regular working hours typically span 10 am–6 pm, Monday through Friday.
  • Summer & Break Camps: Hours typically span 8 am–6 pm, with flexibility required for early-release days and occasional evening school events.
  • Physical Requirements: Ability to walk extensively across campus, stand for extended periods in various weather conditions, lift up to 25 lbs. of program supplies, and respond rapidly during emergencies.

Expected Salary Range and Benefits:

  • $55,000–60,000
  • Lowell School offers a comprehensive compensation and benefits package that includes health, dental, and vision insurance, retirement plan contributions, paid time off, and professional development support.

Click HERE to apply.

job.title: Prep for Prep Professional Advancement Program Manager
job.description:
Position Description

Organization Summary: Prep for Prep is a premier educational and leadership development program that develops ethical and effective leaders who reflect our society. Prep is approaching its 50th anniversary and setting a bold vision for its future. Prep identifies New York City’s most promising students, prepares them to excel at the nation’s top independent schools, and supports their academic, professional, and personal growth through middle school, high school, college graduation, and beyond.

Learn more at prepforprep.org.

Position Summary: The Professional Advancement Program Manager is primarily responsible for executing and continuously improving Prep for Prep's Student Internship Program and career development programming, with a primary focus on high school students. The Program Manager reports to the Director of Professional Advancement and works collaboratively with the Assistant Director, who primarily supports college students.

Responsibilities for this role include, but are not limited to, these primary areas:

Support the execution of the Student Internship Program

  • Manage the internship recruitment and selection process for high school students, including interviewing, tracking placement activities, employer outreach, and matching students with opportunities based on skills and interests.
  • Provide career advising throughout the internship cycle, including internship search support, interview preparation, and placement.
  • Review and provide feedback on student resumes and cover letters to ensure they are professional and competitive.
  • Track student participation in workforce readiness activities in Salesforce and support efforts to ensure students complete required career preparation milestones.
  • Research and evaluate external programs aligned with students' academic and career interests and manage associated outreach, application support, and organizational relationships.
  • Collaborate with Post-Placement Counseling and Undergraduate Affairs to identify and nominate students for professional and leadership development opportunities and ensure relevant academic and program considerations are incorporated into placement and advising decisions.
  • Act as a liaison between students, employers, and Prep for Prep staff to address concerns and maximize student success.

Event Management and Employer Engagement

  • In collaboration with the Assistant Director, manage logistics for academic-year and summer career seminars, including promotion, registration, attendance, and day-of coordination.
  • Manage logistics and implementation of corporate workforce readiness initiatives, including mock interviews, 1-on-1 resume reviews, and other career preparation activities.
  • Maintain relationships with assigned employer contacts and support the Director and Assistant Director in developing employer partnerships and internship opportunities.

Program Management and Evaluation

  • Maintain accurate student and program records within Salesforce and generate reports on student participation, placements, employer engagement, and program outcomes.
  • Collect, analyze, and synthesize student and employer evaluation data to assess program effectiveness.
  • Partner with the Director and Assistant Director to identify and implement program improvements based on data, feedback, and emerging workforce trends.

General Department Communications

  • Communicate career, internship, and professional development opportunities to current students and early-career alumni.
  • Respond to student, employer, and partner inquiries and follow up promptly.

Qualifications, Skills, Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree required.
  • 3–5 years of experience in career advising, workforce development, internship programming, talent development, employer relations, or a related field, preferably supporting high school and/or college students.
  • Detail-oriented, highly organized, and an excellent problem-solver with strong project management skills and the ability to manage multiple and competing priorities effectively.
  • Ability to work effectively with high school students, undergraduates, colleagues, community stakeholders, employers, and supporters from a range of backgrounds and experiences.
  • Strong interpersonal, communication, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to exercise sound judgment and work effectively with a variety of constituent groups.
  • Commitment to Prep for Prep’s mission and demonstrated interest in supporting students' academic, professional, and career development.
  • Proficiency with Salesforce or similar CRM/database systems and Google Workspace.

Salary Range: $70,000 - $72,000

How to Apply: Please email a cover letter and resume with the subject line “Professional Advancement Program Manager” to personnel@prepforprep.org and gingles@prepforprep.org.

job.title: St. Mark's School Marketing Coordinator
job.description:
Position Description

The Marketing Coordinator is a creative, organized, and collaborative communications professional responsible for supporting the school's marketing and communications efforts across digital and print platforms. Reporting to the Associate Director of Marketing & Communications, this position plays a key role in telling the school's story through social media, website content, email communications, photography, and event coverage.

The ideal candidate is a strong writer and visual storyteller who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys engaging with a vibrant school community, and is comfortable managing multiple projects simultaneously. This position requires occasional evening and weekend work to support campus events and community engagement activities.

Essential Responsibilities:

Social Media Management

  • Manage and maintain the school's social media channels, including content planning, creation, scheduling, publishing, and community engagement.
  • Develop compelling content that highlights student life, academics, athletics, arts, and community events.
  • Monitor social media trends and recommend strategies to increase audience engagement and brand awareness.

Website Management

  • Maintain and update website content to ensure accuracy, relevance, and consistency with institutional branding.
  • Collaborate with faculty and staff to gather and publish news, announcements, and event information.
  • Support ongoing website improvements and user experience initiatives.

Email Communications

  • Create, format, and distribute external email communications to prospective families, current families, alumni, and other key constituents.
  • Ensure communications align with the school's brand standards and messaging strategy.
  • Assist with audience segmentation and communication scheduling.

Photography and Content Creation

  • Capture high-quality photography across campus for use in marketing materials, social media, website content, publications, and advertising.
  • Organize and maintain digital photo assets.
  • Assist with basic photo editing and content production.

Event Coverage

  • Attend and document school events, programs, performances, athletic contests, and community activities.
  • Produce timely content for digital channels following events.
  • Coordinate with event organizers to identify storytelling opportunities and key moments.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Digital Media, or a related field.
  • 1–3 years of professional experience in marketing, communications, social media management, or related work.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Proficiency with social media platforms and content management systems.
  • Experience with photography and visual storytelling.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously.

Preferred

  • Experience working in an educational or nonprofit environment.
  • Familiarity with email marketing platforms.
  • Experience with Adobe Creative Cloud, Canva, or similar design software.
  • Basic knowledge of website content management systems.
  • Video capture and editing experience.
  • Ability to create visually compelling marketing materials and digital content.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to move throughout campus and attend events in various locations.
  • Ability to carry photography equipment and other marketing materials as needed.
  • Ability to work on a computer for extended periods.

Schedule

This is a full-time, 12-month position. Occasional evening and weekend hours are required to support school events, performances, athletic contests, and other community activities.

Compensation & Benefits

  • $40,000–$60,000, commensurate with experience.
  • Comprehensive benefits package, including health, retirement, paid time off, and professional development opportunities, consistent with school policies.

To Apply

job.title: Prep for Prep Director of Development
job.description:
Position Description

Organization Summary: Prep for Prep is a premier educational and leadership development program that develops ethical and effective leaders who reflect our society. Prep is approaching its 50th anniversary and setting a bold vision for its future. Prep identifies New York City’s most promising students, prepares them to excel at the nation’s top independent schools, and supports their academic, professional, and personal growth through middle school, high school, college graduation, and beyond.

Learn more at prepforprep.org.

Position Summary: The Director of Development is a member of the organization's Leadership Team and a senior member of the Advancement team. The Advancement team provides services across the entire Prep for Prep organization — supporting staff, amplifying the organization’s brand, and stewarding and strengthening its external relationships. Along with the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Advancement Officer, the Director of Development will craft the strategy and lead efforts to secure philanthropic resources to fuel Prep for Prep’s mission. The role will also prioritize supporting the CEO in engaging a dynamic board to support the organization’s sustainability.

Reporting to the Chief Advancement Officer, the Director oversees a team of five responsible for prospecting, stewarding, and securing financial donors. The Director also collaborates with the Advancement team to engage and leverage the organization’s alumni and partnerships to meet various organizational needs. The Development team also handles development operations, events, administration, and revenue data management across the organization.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Planning & Leadership

  • Partner with the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Advancement Officer to develop a comprehensive annual fundraising plan aligned with the organization’s priorities.
  • Collaborate with the Chief Executive Officer to establish annual fundraising goals, budgets, and performance metrics.
  • Lead, mentor, and develop a development team to perform at a high level.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and results.
  • Oversee and strengthen institutional, individual, and event-based fundraising streams to support annual and long-term revenue goals.
  • Monitor fundraising performance and pipeline activity, using data and reporting to inform strategy and decision-making.
  • Oversee annual giving campaigns.
  • Oversee fundraising events, including but not limited to our annual gala, which accounts for a significant portion of annual revenue.
  • Directly manage vendor relationships
  • Develop and oversee additional fundraising events

Donor Cultivation & Stewardship

  • Cultivate, solicit, and steward donors capable of making major and leadership-level gifts.
  • Develop individualized donor engagement strategies and solicitation plans
  • Lead the full donor lifecycle, including identification, cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and renewal strategies.
  • Assure current grant compliance.
  • Prepare and oversee a team that prepares proposals, grant agreements, impact reports, and donor communications.
  • Ensure exceptional stewardship practices that foster long-term donor relationships and increased giving.
  • Support the Prep for Prep Board of Trustees in fundraising and relationship-building efforts.
  • Oversee the management of the Prep for Prep Associates Council in fundraising and relationship-building efforts.
  • Develop relationships with corporate sponsors and foundation representatives.

Development Operations

  • Ensure accurate donor records and prospect management within the CRM database.
  • Streamline and strengthen internal systems for gift processing, acknowledgments, reporting, and donor stewardship to ensure an exceptional donor experience.
  • Collaborate with Finance and Advancement Operations to support revenue tracking, projections, and reconciliation processes.
  • Foster collaboration across advancement teams: development, alumni affairs, professional advancement, and communications.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred.
  • 7+ years of fundraising experience, with a demonstrable track record of closing major gifts, and at least 3 years of experience managing a team.
  • Proven ability to develop and execute a comprehensive fundraising strategy that achieves ambitious revenue goals.
  • Exceptional interpersonal and written communication skills, with the ability to inspire and engage diverse audiences.
  • Relentless follow-through: a reputation for making outreach, following up persistently, and never letting a promising lead go cold.
  • Experience with Salesforce or comparable CRM for donor tracking, pipeline management, and reporting.

Preferred

  • Experience fundraising for educational equity, youth development, or leadership development organizations.
  • Familiarity with the New York City philanthropic community, including independent school and alumni networks.
  • Established relationships with foundations and individual philanthropists in New York City and/or nationally.
  • Experience working with volunteer leadership and engaging board members in fundraising.
  • Knowledge of planned giving and endowment fundraising.

Core Competencies

  • Tenacity and resilience: does not give up when doors are slow to open
  • Relationship-building: warm, authentic, and skilled at cultivating trust over time
  • Strategic thinking paired with hands-on execution
  • Strong organizational skills and meticulous attention to deadlines and follow-through
  • Mission-aligned, equity-centered leadership
  • Comfort with data and metrics-driven fundraising

Working Conditions

This is a hybrid position, with three days in the office and two days remote. However, depending on the department’s needs, this role may be required to work in-person more than three days per week. Evening or weekend work may be required around donor events, cultivation activities, and major organizational events.

All employees of the organization should see their roles as: one, contributing to achieving this goal in the highest possible quality, and two, working in conjunction with all other members of the staff. In light of this, the tasks listed above serve as a general framework for this position's responsibilities. Flexibility and continued quality improvement are necessary for this institution and require individuals not to perceive any job description as fixed.

Compensation: $200K

To apply, interested candidates should send their resume and cover letter, with the subject line “Director of Development,” to personnel@prepforprep.org and lgivner@prepforprep.org.

job.title: The Lawrenceville School Math Specialist
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Job Type

Part-time

Description

The Math Specialist is responsible for providing individualized academic support to Lawrenceville students facing academic challenges in foundational math coursework. This is a fully in-person position, as the essential functions of the role require direct, on-campus engagement with students, faculty, and staff.

The Math Specialist will work collaboratively with the Educational Support team, teaching faculty, and academic advisors to provide students with individualized, evidence-based instructional strategies that support their math coursework and align with the School’s curriculum. The role requires building strong, in-person relationships with students and providing targeted learning opportunities to support their academic success; neither students nor faculty may attend these sessions virtually, in light of the potential distractions and reduced effectiveness inherent in virtual interactions.

This position follows the academic calendar, and the employee is expected to work around 10 hours per week. A flexible schedule including afternoons and evenings is required.

To ensure full consideration, please submit a cover letter and three professional references, in addition to your resume.

Responsibilities:

  • Provide in-person individual and/or group instruction to identified students in Geometry, Algebra 1, Algebra 2, Trigonometry, and Pre-Calculus.
  • Conduct in-person meetings to assess students’ needs which requires real-time, on-campus interaction to ensure effective communication and student engagement as well as accurate assessment.
  • Generate appropriate remedial assistance:

Develop self-awareness, self-advocacy, and personalized strategies to maximize learning.

Implement research-based interventions to assess and assist students with their math challenges.

Monitor and document student progress, sending weekly reports to the student, their academic advisor, and the Director of

Educational Support.

Foster a positive and engaging learning environment through direct, in-person instruction, which is essential for student

success.

  • These responsibilities necessitate on-campus presence for effective support and accurate and timely assessment.
  • Teach and monitor math skills that integrate into Lawrenceville’s curriculum.
  • Attend on-campus professional meetings and training sessions to stay updated on best practices in math instruction and student support. Participation in these in-person meetings is critical to effective collaboration and alignment with institutional goals.
  • Perform other duties as requested.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree (preferably a Master’s) in Mathematics, Special Education, or a related field.
  • Expertise in a variety of math-specific instructional methodologies and techniques, with a proven ability to apply these approaches to foster students' confidence and academic growth in math coursework.
  • Demonstrated success in working with students with learning differences and/or academic challenges.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Highly proficient with Microsoft Office Suite and Google GSuite tools, as well as comfort using technology and systems to document work with students. Demonstrated ability to learn and use effectively departmental and school-wide tools and databases.
  • Strong organizational and problem-solving skills. Operate efficiently, learn, and adapt quickly. Ability to manage ambiguity and proactively find solutions.

Work Environment and Physical Demands

  • This is a fully in-person role that requires on-campus presence for all student interactions.
  • Physical demands are in excess of those for sedentary work. Must be able to remain on their feet for extended periods of time, go up and down flights of steps, as well as stoop, kneel, crouch, and lift.
  • Routinely use standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, fax machines, etc.
  • Must be capable of using visual display terminal with continuous wrist movement on a keyboard.
  • Required to talk, hear, walk, use hands to finger, handle or feel, and reach with hands and arms.
  • Must be able to work flexible hours to accommodate students’ schedules. This includes both day and evening responsibilities.
  • Must be able to lift up to 20lbs. without assistance.
  • Ability to see with normal parameters.
  • Operate in a professional work environment.

The Lawrenceville School is a diverse and inclusive community and makes all employment decisions without regard for an individual’s race, creed, color, religion, national origin, nationality, sex, pregnancy, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, veteran status, physical or mental disability (including AIDS and HIV related illness), genetic information, refusal to provide genetic information, refusal to submit to genetic testing, ancestry, familial status, marital status, domestic partnership status, civil union status, atypical cellular or blood trait, military service, application for military service, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. The Lawrenceville School will also provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals in accordance with applicable law.

The Lawrenceville School conducts pre-employment screening for all positions which includes a criminal background check, verification of work history, academic credentials, licenses, and certifications. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of the background check.

Eligible employees receive a competitive benefit package that includes health insurance coverage, paid leave and retirement plan options and many other valuable programs.

Salary Description

$56.00 per hour

job.title: The Pingry School Basking Ridge Operations Officer
job.description:
Position Description & Application

The Pingry School, a prestigious K-12 coeducational, independent day school with a rich history dating back to its founding by Dr. John F. Pingry in 1861, stands at the forefront of academic excellence in the United States. With campuses located in Basking Ridge, Pottersville, and Short Hills, New Jersey, Pingry is celebrated for its academic programs, a student-written Honor Code that underpins our community values, and a comprehensive commitment to arts, athletics, community, and civic engagement. Our mission is to inspire in our students a lifelong passion for learning, personal development, and social responsibility, preparing them to be global citizens and luminaries of the 21st century. Rooted in relationships and guided by our foundational philosophy, Pingry is a vibrant community of more than 1,100 students hailing from over 90 towns across New Jersey and New York. At Pingry, we are united by a love of learning and a commitment to preparing students to navigate the complexities of the 21st century with confidence and integrity. For more information, we invite you to visit our website at pingry.org or connect with The Pingry School on Facebook, X, and Instagram to discover why we love school.

Position Summary

Operations Officers are a vital part of our campus life, supporting a safe, secure, and highly efficient learning environment. In this full-time role, you serve as a highly visible, personable professional ambassador and a logistical "utility player". You balance front-of-house hospitality, greeting visitors with warmth and managing building access, with behind-the-scenes operational and safety coordination. Reporting directly to the Reception and Operations Supervisor - Basking Ridge, you ensure consistent coverage, a professional desk presence, and strict alignment with campus protocols. You will work collaboratively with Facilities, Athletics, and Auxiliary programs to seamlessly execute daily campus activities, school events, and afternoon/evening transitions.

This is a 12-month, full-time position, primarily based at Pingry’s Basking Ridge campus. This role is scheduled to work Tuesday through Saturday, 7:30am - 4:00pm. Depending on the school calendar and operational requirements, duties and schedules may occasionally change, however candidates with availability Tuesdays through Saturdays are strongly preferred. We are seeking a proactive, composed, and customer-service-oriented professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment where no two days are the same. This role is perfect for someone who balances a "security-first" mindset with a "service-first" approach.

You will excel in this role if:

  • You have a naturally warm, professional, and welcoming demeanor. As a primary campus representative, you pride yourself on ensuring all students, employees, and families feel welcome while maintaining firm access control and screening protocols.
  • You balance working autonomously with being an integrated team player. You smoothly shift gears from monitoring the reception area to helping set up an event, handling package deliveries, or coordinating logistics with external vendors.
  • You handle high-visibility multitasking, busy lobbies, and operational challenges with a composed mindset and sound judgment. You possess the strong interpersonal skills necessary to facilitate difficult conversations professionally when issues arise.
  • You notice the small details, from risk assessment during routine security rounds to tracking event calendars. You bring a high level of discretion and strong attention to detail when managing campus safety or assisting with operational documentation.
  • You are comfortable working with digital visitor management systems and security platforms. You easily leverage Google Workspace tools (Gmail, Calendar, Docs, Sheets) to handle phone, email, and tracking inquiries, ensuring timely and accurate information-sharing across departments.

Key Responsibilities

Campus Ambassadorship & Reception:

Serve as a front-facing representative; greet visitors, manage phone and email inquiries, and execute visitor screening and check-ins via school systems (SchoolPass, Ruvna) to maintain strict access control.

Safety & Surveillance:

Conduct routine security rounds to assess risks, monitor campus surveillance systems (Milestone XProtect), look for irregular activity, and maintain a vigilant, approachable security presence. Operational &

Logistics Support:

Partner with the Supervisor to manage incoming mail, sort package deliveries, update campus athletic/event calendars, and assist with general logistics or vendor coordination.

Event Coordination & Traffic Flow:

Collaborate cross-departmentally with Athletics, Facilities, and Auxiliary Programs to support seamless event setups, breakdowns, and safe vehicle parking/traffic flow during peak periods.

Emergency Readiness:

Maintain an expert working knowledge of Pingry’s emergency response protocols and communication platforms, confidently supporting monthly safety drills and critical incidents.

Honor Code Stewardship:

Model the school’s core values of integrity and respect in every daily interaction with students, faculty, and the public.

Qualifications & Requirements

  • High school diploma or equivalent is required.
  • Prior experience in a school, hospitality, operations, or a highly visible front-facing environment is strongly preferred.
  • Excellent organizational, oral, and written interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to foster collaborative relationships with diverse internal and external stakeholders.
  • Valid First Aid/CPR/AED certification (or the willingness to obtain accreditation upon hire via school-provided training).
  • Ability to prioritize and manage multiple time-sensitive tasks independently in a fast-paced environment.
  • Physical ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods, regularly traverse or move across a multi-building campus to conduct safety checks, and safely transport or position event equipment or package deliveries weighing up to 50 lbs.
  • A deep commitment to fostering a diverse, equitable, and inclusive community aligned with the mission, pillars, and DEIB values of The Pingry School.

Qualified candidates are invited to apply online at https://www.pingry.org/careers.

The salary range for this position is $22-$28/hour. Final compensation will be determined based on experience and education.

Pingry offers a comprehensive benefits package to full-time employees, including, but not limited to, medical, dental, and vision coverage; retirement plans with employer matching; life and disability insurance; tuition remission for employees' children; and access to wellness and professional development resources.

A full list of benefits is available at www.pingry.org/careers.

The Pingry School aspires to be an anti-racist community and is committed to the principles of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion. Pingry is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. The Pingry School's employment policy is that individuals will receive equal opportunity in all matters pertaining to recruitment, employment, salary, promotion, and assignment, regardless of race, religion, color, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy status, genetic information, marital status, amnesty or status as a covered veteran, or other basis proscribed by federal, state, and local law. All employment is decided based on qualifications, merit, and business need.

job.title: Jubilee Lead Faculty
job.description:
AN INVITATION TO APPLY

Jubilee College is committed to building a founding team that reflects the full diversity of the world its students will help create. If the mission of this college speaks to you, if the questions it takes seriously are questions you have been carrying, if the place calls to you, we encourage you to apply. Jubilee is not looking for a perfect resume. It is looking for the right person. If you meet many but not all of the qualifications listed here, please do not let that stop you. The most important thing is not what your path has looked like, but where it has brought you, and where you believe it is going.

PROCEDURE TO APPLY

Interested candidates are invited to CLICK HERE to submit the following materials confidentially as a single PDF file:

  • A cover letter that includes:
  • Why you are interested in this opportunity and the vision of Jubilee College
  • A description of your prior experience and how your skills and passions align with this work
  • A current curriculum vitae
  • A statement of educational philosophy
  • The names, email addresses, and telephone numbers of five references, including at least two recent supervisors. References should speak to your ability to be an effective administrator and to work successfully with colleagues (references will be contacted only with the candidate’s permission). Please indicate your relationship with each reference (i.e. supervisor, colleague, or direct report).

Please address any questions by email to maryrose@strategenius.org.

SEARCH CALENDAR

Applications due: November 15, 2026

Semifinalists interviews: Weeks of November 30th and December 7th, 2026

Finalists interviews: Week of January 4th and 11, 2026

Announcement: Week of January 18th, 2027

Start date: Early 2027

This position is being offered in a spirit of gift — Jubilee deeply believes that communities are built on generosity, reciprocity, and care for the whole person. So they hope to have an active dialogue with seriously interested candidates.

A base salary of $120,000–$135,000 is where the compensation conversation begins. A health insurance stipend, paid time off, and funds for professional development are baseline benefits. Beyond that, the total compensation package includes meaningful non-cash benefits that bring the real value of this offer well above the base salary. The successful candidate will receive a free, well-appointed one-bedroom townhouse on the ground floor of Jubilee's fully renovated classroom building — a former elementary school located in the heart of downtown Dunsmuir and a 15-minute bike ride from the Upper Campus — with all utilities included, valued at $18,000 annually. When the first cohort begins in August 2028, a full meal program values at $7,000 per year is also provided. Relocation assistance will be offered as well.

More broadly, the founding Lead Faculty will have the opportunity to travel domestically and internationally alongside students, and will enjoy daily exposure to one of the most remarkable networks of founders, advisors, visiting faculty, and spiritual leaders assembled around any educational institution in the country.

Jubilee is committed to understanding what the right candidate actually needs to thrive, not just financially but in every dimension of their life, and to doing its best to meet those needs.

job.title: The Pingry School Pingry Coaching Fellow
job.description:
Position Application & Description

The Pingry School, a prestigious K-12 coeducational, independent day school with a rich history dating back to its founding by Dr. John F. Pingry in 1861, stands at the forefront of academic excellence in the United States. With campuses located in Basking Ridge, Pottersville, and Short Hills, New Jersey, Pingry is celebrated for its academic programs, a student-written Honor Code that underpins our community values, and a comprehensive commitment to arts, athletics, community, and civic engagement. Our mission is to inspire in our students a lifelong passion for learning, personal development, and social responsibility, preparing them to be global citizens and luminaries of the 21st century. Rooted in relationships and guided by our foundational philosophy, Pingry is a vibrant community of more than 1,100 students hailing from over 90 towns across New Jersey and New York. At Pingry, we are united by a love of learning and a commitment to preparing students to navigate the complexities of the 21st century with confidence and integrity. For more information, we invite you to visit our website at pingry.org or connect with The Pingry School on Facebook, X, and Instagram to discover why we love school.

Position Summary: Launch Your Coaching Career

The Pingry School invites passionate, coach-minded individuals to apply for the Coaching Fellow – Pathway of Excellence. This dynamic, year-long residency is designed to develop the next generation of high-impact leaders in the coaching profession. Located in the heart of New Jersey’s elite sports landscape, this program offers direct access to a premier K-12 athletics culture and serves as a true launchpad for careers in athletic administration, sports psychology, and elite coaching.

The Experience

As a Pingry Coaching Fellow, you will lead or assist across six athletic seasons (three at the Middle School level and three at the Upper School level). You will work alongside experienced mentors to develop student-athletes across a broad developmental spectrum, from rising learners to future NCAA Division I recruits and Olympians, all within a high-expectation, high-integrity environment.

2026-27 Priority Placements

We are seeking versatile candidates with expertise in one or more of the following areas. Ideal applicants will possess the flexibility to support specific program needs across Fall, Winter, and Spring seasons at both the MS and HS levels:

  • Field Sports & Turf: Support our programs in Football (Varsity/MS), Soccer (Freshman/MS), Field Hockey (Varsity/JV/MS), and Softball/Baseball.
  • Court Sports: Key roles available in Volleyball (Varsity/Freshman/MS), Basketball (JV/Freshman/MS), and Tennis (JV).
  • Aquatics & Ice: Specialized openings in Water Polo (Varsity/MS) and Ice Hockey (Varsity/MS).
  • Specialized Athletics: Opportunities in Wrestling, Fencing, Dance, Cross Country, and Track & Field.

The Ideal Candidate

Whether you are a former collegiate athlete, a recent graduate in sports management, or an experienced club coach transitioning to school-based athletics, you bring a growth mindset and a deep commitment to student development. As a Fellow, you will model sportsmanship and Pingry’s core values, honor, character, and intellectual engagement, while participating in the broader life of the school through advising and club leadership.

We encourage you to apply if you are eager to grow, ready to contribute, and motivated to make a meaningful impact on the next generation of student-athletes.

Responsibilities

  • Coach across six athletic seasons (three Middle School and three Upper School), demonstrating flexibility, age-appropriate instruction, and alignment with evolving program needs.
  • Collaborate across departments, working with coaches, athletic trainers, strength and conditioning staff, and administrators to advance wellness, performance, and inclusive team culture.
  • Model mentorship and leadership by fostering a structured, student-centered environment that supports physical, emotional, and social growth aligned with Pingry's values.
  • Lead and contribute to all aspects of athletic preparation, including practice planning, film review, game-day execution, and player development with an emphasis on skill-building, teamwork, and sportsmanship.
  • Engage in professional development, coach training, and Pingry-led learning opportunities to expand your toolbox and sharpen your coaching identity.
  • Support co-curricular life through potential advising, club leadership, or administrative contributions that further community and student engagement.
  • Communicate proactively with student-athletes and families regarding schedules, expectations, and developmental progress.
  • Uphold compliance with all school policies, safety procedures, and athletic regulations.

What Makes This Opportunity Different

  • Career-Ready Experience: This is not a volunteer role or casual assistantship. Coaching Fellows gain real responsibility, real visibility, and real development in preparation for long-term careers in sports and education.
  • Intentional Mentorship: Fellows receive ongoing feedback, shadow head coaches, and build connections across Pingry and the broader athletic ecosystem.
  • Broad Impact: You’ll engage with student-athletes in grades 6–12, shaping not just their athletic performance but their leadership and mindset.
  • Future Opportunity: Coaching Fellows play a role in shaping the future of Pingry Athletics and may be considered for future coaching, administrative, or leadership roles at Pingry or beyond.
  • Building Community through Competition: Our teams include student-athletes who go on to compete in the Ivy League, ACC, NESCAC, and Olympic programs, providing real preparation for coaches aspiring to lead at the next level.

Qualifications

  • Demonstrated understanding of coaching in at least one sport at the middle school, upper school, club, collegiate, or professional level; multi-sport coaching experience is strongly preferred.
  • Genuine passion for working with student-athletes and a proven ability to foster individual growth, team development, and a positive, inclusive culture.

  • Personal trainers or educators with strong athletic leadership experience
  • Individuals with long-term aspirations in coaching, athletic administration, or student-athlete development

Qualified candidates are encouraged to apply online at https://www.pingry.org/careers.

The salary range for this position is $21,000-$31,000. Final compensation will be determined based on experience, education, and internal organization and peer data at Pingry are also considered.

Latin School of Chicago provides its students with a rigorous and innovative educational program in a community that embraces the diversity of people, cultures and ideas. Latin School of Chicago is seeking an Instrumental Music Assistant Teacher primarily for fifth through twelfth grade band. The Assistant Teacher will also assist with chorus classes. The Assistant Teacher program's goal is to provide each Assistant Teacher with an authentic teaching and learning experience under the supervision of a lead music teacher. The starting salary for this full-time position is $31,799. A high-quality employee-only benefits package is included.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Assist the lead teacher in the day-to-day operation of the classroom, including prepping materials and activities, clean up, and organization of materials

  • Proficiency with Google Workspace and ability to manage digital content effectively
