job.title: Landon School Senior Accountant
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Job Type

Full-time

Description

If you are eager to make a meaningful impact, find fulfillment in your work, and join a community of dedicated individuals passionate about young people and education, consider working at Landon School, where we foster the intellect, health, and happiness of boys.

Situated on a picturesque 75-acre campus in Bethesda, Maryland, Landon is an all-boys school serving grades 3–12. At Landon, we believe all employees play a vital role in educating, supporting, and encouraging our boys.

Landon School is seeking a Senior Accountant to join its Business Office. Reporting to the Controller, the Accountant will play a key role in the School’s accounting operations, financial reporting, month-end and year-end close, reconciliations, audit preparation, and internal controls.

This is not an entry-level accounting position. The successful candidate will bring meaningful accounting experience, a strong understanding of GAAP, and the ability to independently manage accounting responsibilities, identify and resolve issues, and improve processes. Experience in nonprofit, independent school, higher education, or another fund-accounting environment is strongly preferred.

Responsibilities

General Accounting & Financial Reporting

  • Support the Controller in maintaining the accuracy and integrity of the general ledger, including preparing journal entries, accruals, prepaid expenses, deferred revenue, allocations, and other accounting entries.
  • Perform monthly balance sheet and general ledger reconciliations, research and resolve discrepancies, and assist with monthly and annual close processes.
  • Prepare financial reports and supporting schedules and analyze account activity and budget-to-actual results to identify unusual transactions, trends, errors, and necessary adjustments.

Nonprofit & Fund Accounting

  • Support accounting and reconciliation for restricted and unrestricted funds, contributions and pledges, endowment and investment activity, and releases of donor restrictions.
  • Maintain supporting schedules for restricted funds, endowments, capital projects, fixed assets, and other designated funds.
  • Work closely with Development and other departments to ensure financial activity is accurately reconciled and recorded in the general ledger.

Cash, Investments & Balance Sheet Management

  • Prepare and review bank, investment, and other significant balance sheet reconciliations and research and resolve outstanding items.
  • Maintain schedules for cash, investments, prepaid expenses, accrued liabilities, deferred revenue, fixed assets, and other balance sheet accounts.
  • Assist with recording investment activity, income, realized and unrealized gains and losses, fees, and other cash and investment activity.

Audit, Tax & Compliance

  • Play a significant role in the annual financial statement audit, including preparing audit schedules, reconciliations, supporting documentation, and responses to auditor requests.
  • Assist the Controller with information required for Form 990 and other regulatory filings and help ensure compliance with GAAP and School accounting policies.
  • Support the implementation of recommendations resulting from audits and internal control reviews.

Internal Controls & Process Improvement

  • Work with the Controller and CFO to evaluate accounting procedures, strengthen internal controls, and identify opportunities to improve accuracy, efficiency, and accountability.
  • Help document accounting procedures, maintain appropriate segregation of duties, and support accounting system improvements and integrations.
  • Proactively identify accounting issues and work with the Controller to develop and implement solutions.

Business Office Support

  • Collaborate with the Controller, CFO, Accounts Payable, Student Accounts, Development, Auxiliary Programs, and other departments to ensure transactions are recorded accurately and timely.
  • Provide accounting guidance to colleagues and serve as a resource on account coding, documentation, and appropriate accounting treatment.
  • Serve as a backup for critical accounting functions and participate in Business Office projects and initiatives as needed.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field with significant accounting coursework and a minimum of two years of progressively responsible accounting experience.
  • Strong knowledge of U.S. GAAP with demonstrated experience in general ledger accounting, reconciliations, journal entries, month-end close, financial reporting, and annual audits.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, experience with accounting systems, and strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Excellent attention to detail with the ability to independently manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
  • Strong communication skills and a high degree of integrity, discretion, professionalism, and sound judgment.

Preferred

  • Accounting experience within a nonprofit organization, independent school, college/university, or other fund-accounting environment.
  • Experience with nonprofit accounting, including donor restrictions, contributions, endowments, investments, fixed assets, capital projects, and Form 990 preparation.
  • Experience with Veracross or a similar accounting/ERP system and working directly with external auditors.
  • CPA, CPA candidate, CMA, or another relevant professional accounting credential is preferred but not required.

Compensation and Benefits

In addition to joining a supportive and collaborative community, Landon School offers a competitive salary and an outstanding benefits package. The expected salary range for this position is $85,000 - $100,000 annually. Landon is committed to supporting our employees both professionally and personally. Employees enjoy:

  • Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage
  • A retirement plan with generous employer contributions
  • Generous amount of paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays
  • Employer paid life insurance and short- and long-term disability protection
  • Opportunities for professional growth and development
  • Complimentary daily lunch on campus
  • And more!

Salary Description

$85,000 - $100,000

job.title: Deerfield Academy Associate Director of the Deerfield Fund
job.description:
Position Description & Application

**SIGN-ON BONUS**

The successful candidate will receive a $1,000 sign-on bonus ($500 paid at time of hire and $500 paid at the end of 90 days of employment.

Reporting to the Director of the Deerfield Fund, the Associate Director is a senior member of the Deerfield Fund team and manages the work of the Assistant Director of the Deerfield Fund for Young Alumni. The Associate Director assists the Director with the development of the overall fundraising strategy as well as the planning, implementation and assessment of yearly campaigns and appeals. The Associate Director leads donor stewardship and manages the 20th and 25th class reunion fundraising and efforts.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities

Fundraising and Reunions Management

  • Assist the Director of the Deerfield Fund in developing overall strategy as well as specific annual fundraising campaigns including mail & digital appeals, Day of Giving, phonathons etc.
  • Assist the Director in analyzing Deerfield Fund program metrics to determine ROI and guide future planning and allocation of resources
  • Take the lead on the development and implementation of a comprehensive donor stewardship program
  • Manage overall Deerfield Fund appeals timeline and production schedule; work with Communications Office and outside vendors to ensure Deerfield Fund communications are designed and delivered as required
  • Co-manage overall class volunteer program with Director; ensure consistent practices in volunteer recruitment, training and management across classes
  • Direct all aspects of Reunion fundraising for the 20th and 25th reunion classes, including: goal setting; recruitment, training and management of alumni volunteers; solicitation of annual, capital and planned gifts; and close collaboration with colleagues in Leadership Gifts
  • Collaborate closely with Alumni Relations on 20th and 25th reunion programing
  • Manage a portfolio of leadership gift prospects with focus on identifying, cultivating and soliciting individuals for leadership-level donations
  • Track and report on leadership-level prospect activity; update contact reports on a timely basis
  • Participate in weekend and evening activities on and off campus as needed to advance the goals stated above

Management of Staff

  • Manage the overall work performance, objectives, and career development of the Assistant Director of the Deerfield Fund for Young Alumni
  • Oversee class fundraising and program goal setting for Assistant Director of the Deerfield Fund for Young Alumni
  • Provide leadership within the department and assume responsibility for the management of the department in the absence of the Director of the Deerfield Fund
  • In collaboration with the Human Resources Department and Director of the Deerfield Fund, support the recruitment, orientation, and training of new Deerfield Fund employees to ensure optimal staffing, according to Academy Best Practices in Hiring

Performs other duties as assigned

Job Specifications

  • Bachelor’s degree required
  • 5-7 years of experience in Advancement or similar related work experience
  • Excellent verbal and written communication and organizational skills
  • Experience providing leadership, management and mentorship to staff
  • Experience in managing volunteers
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team
  • A high level of integrity and a strong work ethic
  • Skilled with MS Word and Office and familiarity with integrated databases
  • Ability and willingness to travel
  • Demonstrated commitment to diversity and inclusion and to serving the needs of a diverse community
  • Ability to manage, and sensitivity to, highly confidential information

Physical Job Demands

  • Close visual acuity to analyze data and figures and to view a computer terminal
  • Ability to sustain substantial movements of the wrist, hands and/or fingers
  • Ability to occasionally lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects up to 10 lbs.
  • Ability to occasionally stoop, kneel or reach

Working Conditions

The worker is in an office environment, and while in the office is not substantially exposed to adverse environmental conditions. While traveling (10% overnight travel on average each month), the worker is subject to outside environmental conditions.

Special Instructions for Applicants

Application materials must include:

  • A cover letter summarizing interests and qualifications
  • A complete resume or curriculum vitae

Compensation & Benefits

Deerfield Academy offers a competitive total compensation package, where base compensation or salary is just one component. Pay within the published range is determined by factors such as qualifications, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience, allowing for growth and progression within the role.

We also offer a comprehensive suite of benefits to eligible employees, including:

  • Health & Financial: Medical, dental, and vision insurance; a 403(b)-retirement plan; and employer-paid life and disability plans.
  • Time Off: Generous paid time off and paid holidays.
  • Campus Perks: Tuition remission, fitness center access and complimentary dining hall meals

job.title: The Hotchkiss School Program Director, Varsity Rowing
job.description:
Position Description & Application

The Hotchkiss School seeks an accomplished, energetic, and student-centered Program Director to lead and develop the School's Varsity Rowing program. Rowing at Hotchkiss is established and competing, and the program is now ready for a director to strengthen its competitive standing and deepen its place within the life of the School.

The Program Director is responsible for the overall leadership, administration, and success of the Varsity Rowing program while fostering an environment that promotes competitive excellence, sportsmanship, character development, and personal growth.

Hotchkiss is committed to building this program around the right person. Accordingly, the position may be structured as a faculty appointment or as a coaching-focused role, depending on the successful candidate’s background and interests. We welcome applications from candidates from various coaching backgrounds, and we are glad to discuss how the role might be shaped.

The Program Director will mentor student-athletes both on and off the water, develop a positive and inclusive team culture, and support the School's mission by helping students pursue their academic, athletic, and personal goals. The Program Director will oversee all aspects of the program, including practice planning, athlete development, regatta management, recruiting, and collaboration with college admissions and placement efforts.

The Program

The program is entering its seventh season and currently fields both boys’ and girls’ squads, each racing coxed fours. The team carries a healthy roster with strong student interest. The Program Director leads both squads, supported by a staff of assistant coaches. The Program Director also leads the winter rowing concentration, a conditioning season for athletes preparing for the competitive spring season. The central priority for the incoming director is competitive development and the conversion of established participation and enthusiasm into sustained results.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Lead all aspects of the Varsity Rowing program, including planning, organization, and day-to-day operations.
  • Design and implement comprehensive practice plans focused on individual skill development, boat cohesion, physical preparation, and competitive performance.
  • Teach and develop rowing fundamentals and rowing technique, leadership, sportsmanship, and mental performance.
  • Foster a positive, inclusive, and accountable team culture that reflects the values and mission of The Hotchkiss School.
  • Serve as a mentor and role model for student-athletes, supporting their academic, personal, and athletic development.
  • Evaluate athlete performance and provide meaningful feedback to support continuous improvement.
  • Supervise assistant coaching staff, coordinating their work across both squads.
  • Oversee boathouse operations, including the care, maintenance, and inventory of shells, oars, launches, and related equipment in collaboration with the Athletics Department.
  • Collaborate with admissions and athletics staff to support enrollment and retention efforts involving prospective student-athletes.
  • Guide student-athletes and families through the college recruiting process, including communication with college coaches, evaluation of opportunities, and preparation of recruiting materials.
  • Maintain regular communication with student-athletes, families, faculty, and athletics administrators.
  • Coordinate team travel, scheduling, equipment management, and operational needs in collaboration with the Athletics Department.
  • Support multi-sport participation and collaborate with colleagues across the athletic department to promote a positive student-athlete experience.
  • Contribute to the overall success of the Athletics Department by performing all other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Required Qualifications

  • Demonstrated success coaching rowing at the high school, collegiate, youth/club, or comparable competitive level.
  • Strong knowledge of athlete development, skill instruction, practice planning, race strategy, and program management.
  • Experience supervising, mentoring, and developing assistant coaches.
  • Proven ability to build and sustain a positive team culture that prioritizes accountability, inclusion, and personal growth.
  • Excellent communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with students, families, faculty, administrators, and alumni.
  • Demonstrates a commitment to diversity, inclusion, and cultural awareness through actions, interactions, and communications with others.
  • Eligible for a Connecticut Public Service License or comparable out-of-state license to transport students.
  • CPR, First Aid, and AED certification or ability to obtain certification upon employment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree
  • Collegiate rowing experience
  • Experience coaching in an independent school or boarding school environment
  • Experience organizing clinics, camps, showcases, and recruiting events.
  • Familiarity with video analysis platforms and modern athlete development tools.
  • Demonstrated record of helping student-athletes gain admission to and compete at highly selective collegiate institutions.
  • Experience with fundraising, communications, or athletics administration is desirable.

Application Information

Through the online application process, interested candidates should submit a cover letter that addresses their interest in coaching at Hotchkiss with a focus on their ability and interest in working in an intentionally diverse and inclusive residential community. Applicants should submit their cover letter, résumé, a statement of coaching philosophy, and contact information for three references.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply by October 1 for the fullest consideration.

Additional Information

The essential functions and basic skills have been included. It is not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all functions, responsibilities, skills, and abilities. Additional functions and requirements may be assigned by supervisors as deemed appropriate. This position description is subject to change at any time.

The Hotchkiss School is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to basing judgments concerning the employment of individuals upon their qualifications and abilities. The School is firmly committed to equal employment and advancement opportunities for all employees and applicants in all phases of the employment process (including recruitment, hiring, assignment, terms and conditions of employment, compensation, benefits, training, promotion, transfer, discipline, and termination).

In accordance with applicable law, the School does not discriminate against any individual based on age, ancestry, color, genetic information, learning disability, marital status, past or present history of mental disability, national origin, physical disability, race, religious creed, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

Department: Athletics

Reports to: Director of Athletics

Schedule: Flexible and negotiable, variable afternoon practice hours, evenings, weekends, and school vacation periods as required

Travel: Frequent for Athletic Contests and Recruiting Events

job.title: Making Waves Academy Special Education Teacher
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Our Faculty salary scale ensures equitable pay progression commensurate with experience, education, and professional certifications. Scheduled Weekly Hours 40 (academic year).

Faculty Salary Scale

Our Mission: Commitment to Intergenerational Change

When you join Making Waves Academy (MWA), you are committing to interrupt inequity by supporting every Wave-Maker’s journey to a rewarding life dream. This role is instrumental in ensuring rigorous, holistic support for students from the 5th grade to career success. We seek a data-driven leader and advocate ready to make a lasting impact on our students and the community.

What you’ll be doing…

At Making Waves Academy, we value the expertise of our Special Education Teachers as leaders of inclusion and instructional adaptation.

We offer a professional environment where you will focus on delivering high-impact Specialized Academic Instruction (SAI) and driving measurable academic growth for students with IEPs. Our model emphasizes full collaboration with general education colleagues to seamlessly integrate students, ensuring they have meaningful access to rigorous grade-level curriculum throughout the school day.

Your Core Deliverables:

  • Provide Specialized Academic Instruction (SAI), primarily through push-in support combined with pull-out support focusing on targeted interventions in reading, writing, math, and general academic support to ensure student progress toward IEP goals.
  • Establish and maintain a well-organized, structured, and inclusive classroom environment. Implement and maintain a positive behavior support program using appropriate techniques that complement student treatment.
  • Administer, analyze, and reflect upon quantitative and qualitative student data (including IEP progress data, school-wide benchmarks, and classroom data) to inform instructional practice.
  • Write high-quality, effective IEPs, IEP goals, and IEP progress reports.

You’ll need to have:

  • Bachelor's degree and strong content area knowledge, and valid state teaching credential or eligibility to obtain one (support is provided for eligible applicants). CA Education Specialist Instruction Credential in [Mild/Moderate Support Needs), CLAD/BCLAD, and 3+ years’ experience in a special education setting is preferred.
  • Highly organized, goal-oriented, resilient, and possess a strong desire to work collaboratively in a team-first setting. Unwavering commitment to closing achievement gaps and raising student expectations.
  • While not required, fluency in Spanish will be a significant advantage in this role, allowing for broader engagement with our diverse campus community.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Making Waves Academy is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to veteran status, disability or other legally protected characteristics.

Compensation and Benefits

Joining Making Waves Academy means securing a robust, comprehensive total rewards package designed to support your long-term financial, physical, and professional well-being right here in the Bay Area. We ensure your stability and growth so you can focus on maximizing every Wave-Maker's potential.

Financial Well-being

We offer competitive, above-market salaries that reflect your vital expertise in educational support, recognizing your commitment to our students. Beyond your base pay, you will have immediate access to a dedicated retirement savings plan, helping you build financial confidence for the future.

Health and Wellness

Your health is our priority. We proudly cover 100% of most premiums for medical, dental, vision, chiropractic, and acupuncture options for you and your family. We also offer benefits such as employee assistance programs to support your mental and emotional wellness.

Time to Recharge

We believe educators need time to recharge. You will receive generous paid time off, plus all school holidays and breaks. This schedule is designed to ensure meaningful time away from campus, facilitating a sustainable and healthy work-life balance that is critical to preventing burnout.

Professional Growth

We commit to your continuous improvement! You will benefit from ongoing training, dedicated collaboration time, and resources specifically designed to enhance your instructional and behavioral support expertise. You’ll be part of a culture that sees professional growth as essential to our mission.

job.title: International School Bangkok Middle School P.E. / Wellness Teacher
job.description:
Position Description

The ISB educator Profile

ISB educators embody key attributes integrated with our core values to create a vibrant, inclusive learning community. They are adaptable professionals who thrive in dynamic environments, remaining flexible and ready to pivot to meet the evolving needs of our students. ISB’s ideal team player combines deep subject expertise and strong pedagogy with humility, drive, and a positive disposition for supporting young learners.

We believe

At ISB, we believe that education is a dynamic, creative, and collaborative human endeavor. We are seeking a passionate Middle School P.E./Wellness teacher to join our faculty and help students explore, investigate, and make sense of the world.

We seek educators who navigate diverse teaching responsibilities with ease and work closely with students, families, counselors, and administrators to foster a rich community of inquiry. Our teachers bring curiosity, creativity, and a commitment to collaboration to their work, designing meaningful learning experiences that support students' academic, social, and emotional growth.

Beyond the classroom, our educators support students in co-curricular programming, trips, activities, performances and are available to support and celebrate their growth and development as they strive to reach their full-potential.

Our Middle School Program

The Middle School at International School Bangkok (ISB) offers a well-rounded US curriculum experience in Thailand that balances care, challenge, choice, and opportunity to foster personal and academic growth. Our international middle school serves grades 6-8 (ages 11-14) providing a balance of care, challenge, choice, and opportunity to help students grow.

Our globally-minded curriculum aligns with international standards while meeting students at their level. Alongside core subjects of English, Social Studies, Math, Science, World Languages, and PE, students explore music, arts, design, and more.

Students develop interpersonal skills, responsibility, and a sense of community. The Wild Panthers Outdoor Education Program offers annual adventure experiences at ISB’s Environmental Wilderness Campus.

Position Overview

ISB seeks a P.E. / Wellness Teacher who will deliver grade level physical education and health instruction in Middle School, guided by the SHAPE and Ontario standards. This teacher will be an active member of the collaborative teaching teams and contribute to the success of the program. Wellness topics are delivered through the PE program in grades 6 & 7 and in a stand-alone semester-long class in grade 8. All teachers contribute to ISB’s mission and Core Values to develop socially and globally competent, academically-prepared learners.

Required Qualifications

● Teaching license or certification for middle school years

● Subject expertise in the primary area of employment

● Teaching experience in a similar type of international school and this age group (11-14 years old) is an advantage

● Commitment to the Social and Emotional Learning (SEL) of adolescent students

● Commitment to plan and accommodate for diverse learners and their needs

● Have experience with, and a belief in, an active approach to teaching and learning

job.title: The Harker School Afternoon Enrichment Specialist, Middle School
job.description:
Position Description & Application

The Harker School is seeking a dedicated and enthusiastic Afternoon Enrichment Specialist to join our Middle School Enrichment and Supervision Team for the 2026–2027 academic school year.

This is a part-time position for the 2026–2027 academic school year. The anticipated work schedule is Monday through Friday, approximately 1:00 p.m. to 6:30 p.m., with a minimum of 25 hours per week. Hours may vary based on departmental needs.

The successful candidate is expected to work all scheduled school days through the end of the academic year on June 3, 2027.

Please note: This position is not eligible for benefits.

Qualifications

  • Must be 18 years of age.
  • Have current certification in both first aid and CPR, if not, will attend class(s) provided by Harker
  • Prior experience working with children is preferred.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Create experiences. Build community. Make a difference.

  • Model positive behavior and bring school values to life through daily interactions.
  • Lead and support after-school staff in planning engaging activities, events, and student experiences.
  • Create a safe, inclusive, and welcoming environment for students during lunch and after-school programs.
  • Supporting staff with design and creative activities that encourage growth, connection, and fun.
  • Build positive relationships with students, families, and colleagues through strong communication.
  • Serve as a dependable adult role model who leads with energy, professionalism, and school spirit.
  • Support student supervision, dismissal procedures, shuttle coordination, and campus safety.
  • Participate in training and professional development focused on adolescent growth and engagement.
  • Follow safety procedures and maintain accurate documentation and reporting.

Ideal Qualities

Creative • Flexible • Student-Centered • Team Player • Organized • Positive • Reliable

Required Knowledge and Skills:

  • Ability to communicate and work with groups of all age and skill levels and provide necessary direction and instruction to students
  • Must have ability to work independently, work with others, and work with guidance of supervisor
  • Must be self-motivated
  • Excellent time management and prioritization skills
  • Ability to adapt to change and handle multiple situations and tasks
  • Must maintain a positive attitude and professional outlook
  • Ability to communicate in effective English with staff, parents and children
  • Ability to observe student behavior, assess its appropriateness, enforce appropriate safety regulations and emergency procedures, and apply appropriate behavior-management techniques
  • Physical and emotional ability to respond to situations requiring first aid and emergency situations
  • Ability to remain standing for extended periods (up to 3 hours at a time)
  • Capable of working in a variety of weather and climate conditions
  • Physically able to lift, carry, or hold items weighing 10 pounds or more

Working Conditions

No hazardous or unpleasant working conditions. Climate elements must be withstood (IE wearing sunscreen on warm days), as well as prolonged standing.

Our Mission

Our mission is to educate students for success at college and beyond and to foster kindness, respect and integrity within a safe and nurturing environment. We achieve academic excellence through the development of intellectual curiosity, personal accountability and a love of learning. Our comprehensive program and exceptional faculty and staff help students discover, develop and enjoy their unique talents. We honor individuality, embrace diversity, and promote leadership and service, preparing students to take their place as global citizens.

Compensation:

Pay for this position is determined according to The Harker School's established pay scale and is based on relevant education and experience, as evaluated by the Human Resources Department. The posted pay range reflects the full pay scale for this position. While the maximum rate is included for transparency, most new hires can expect to fall within the lower to middle portion of the pay scale based on their qualifications and experience.

job.title: The Bryn Mawr School Part-Time Online AP Microeconomics Teacher
job.description:
Position Description

Pay Range: $9,000

Start Date: January 1, 2027

The Bryn Mawr Online School is seeking a remote faculty member to teach one section of AP Microeconomics in our high school. The ideal candidate will have a strong educational background with a degree in a related discipline, secondary school teaching experience, and a genuine desire to teach and learn from young people. The functions and responsibilities for this role include, but are not limited to:

  • 3–5 years of teaching experience; a minimum of one year of online teaching experience preferred
  • Relevant credentials in the subject area(s) to be taught preferred
  • High School teaching experience preferred
  • Experience developing lesson plans for high school students
  • Knowledge of proven strategies for student success in the subject area
  • Comfort using a variety of pedagogical strategies
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Effective organizational skills
  • Demonstrated proficiency with the technology necessary to succeed in an online learning environment
  • Desire and ability to work with Upper School students of diverse backgrounds and ability levels in pursuit of their educational goals
  • Ability to organize tasks and manage time to meet many and varied deadlines; manage groups of students in a classroom environment; and communicate effectively with students, parents, school administrators, and other staff, including on topics that may be sensitive

How to Apply

Qualified candidates should send a letter of interest, resume, and a list of at least three current professional references to Elaine Swyryn, Associate Head of School, at resumes@brynmawrschool.org. Please enter “AP Microeconomics - BMOS” as the subject line.

The Bryn Mawr School is an equal opportunity employer, adhering to all federal, state, and local laws that prohibit employment discrimination based on race, color, national origin, age, sex, gender identity, religion, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, and veteran status.

job.title: The Calhoun School Facilities Coordinator
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Job Title: Facilities Coordinator Department: Facilities

Direct Report: Director of Facilities FLSA status: Exempt

Position status: Full-time Classification: Staff

Salary Range: 60K–80K

POSITION SUMMARY

The Facilities Coordinator reports to the Director of Facilities and is responsible for supporting the day-to-day maintenance and operation of the facilities (building and grounds) at all locations. This role will provide strong project management, administrative, and coordination support to the Facilities team. The facilities coordinator will also oversee some staff. Some weekend, early morning, or after hours work will be required to support various events and happenings at the school.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES:

Project Management & Tracking

  • Assist the Director in planning and executing facility upgrades, repairs, renovations, and special projects.
  • Maintain comprehensive project files, including blueprints, warranties, permits, and close-out documents.
  • Coordinate facility needs for school events (e.g., graduation, board meetings, athletic events), including furniture set-up and HVAC scheduling. Work with mechanics, porters, and other staff to ensure events operate smoothly.
  • Assist the Director in managing evacuation drills, lockdown drills, and other school-wide drills.
  • Provide project management support for summer break maintenance work, winter break maintenance work, and other maintenance projects that happen during breaks.
  • Other responsibilities as assigned

Administrative Operations

  • Manage the school’s maintenance request system, assigning tasks to the team and following up to ensure completion.
  • Create punch lists for maintenance, cleaning, and security staff to complete on regular schedules
  • Maintain up-to-date records for fire safety, elevators, health department inspections, and OSHA compliance.
  • Support the Director with staff-facing documents including the evacuation manual
  • Manage the space rental process and collaborate with other departments to ensure rentals are successful and do not disrupt other programming.
  • Manage the application for facilities related grants including DCAS and NPSE.
  • Support the Director with the procurement and inventory of facility supplies, from cleaning materials to office furniture.
  • Willingness to get various certifications such as S12, F07, and S95.
  • Other responsibilities as assigned

Vendor & Contractor Coordination

  • Serve as a point of contact for external vendors as needed.
  • Assist in soliciting quotes for services, comparing bids, and drafting contracts for the Director’s review.
  • Coordinate building access for contractors and ensure they adhere to school safety protocols while on campus.

job.title: International School Bangkok High School English Teacher
job.description:
Position Description

The ISB Educator Profile

ISB educators embody key attributes integrated with our core values to create a vibrant, inclusive learning community. They are adaptable professionals who thrive in dynamic environments, remaining flexible and ready to pivot to meet the evolving needs of our students. As true collaborators, they view education as a shared endeavor—actively co-planning, co-teaching, and building strong relationships with colleagues and families. They serve as optimistic problem solvers who approach every challenge with a positive outlook, turning obstacles into opportunities for innovation and growth. Above all, their practice is student-centered, ensuring that all pedagogical and design choices are rooted in student learning and well-being. Ultimately, ISB educators embody our mission by demonstrating curiosity, courage, and empowerment in their lives, work, and professional growth. ISB’s ideal team player combines deep subject expertise and strong pedagogy with humility, drive, and a positive disposition for supporting young learners.

We believe

At ISB, we believe that education is a dynamic, creative, and collaborative human endeavor. We are seeking a passionate High School English teacher to join our faculty and help students explore, investigate, and make sense of the world. Our vibrant school environment thrives on the energy and dedication of our faculty. We seek educators who navigate diverse teaching responsibilities with ease and work closely with students, families, counselors, and administrators to foster a rich community of inquiry. Our teachers bring curiosity, creativity, and a commitment to collaboration to their work, designing meaningful learning experiences that support students' academic, social, and emotional growth. Beyond the classroom, our educators support students in co-curricular programming, trips, activities, performances and are available to support and celebrate their growth and development as they strive to reach their full-potential.

Position Overview

ISB seeks a High School English teacher with skill and experience teaching High School English. The ideal candidate will have experience across a range of courses in the English subject area, with an interest in developing innovative and engaging courses. The successful candidate is an excellent teacher, a team player, a positive collaborator, uses technology appropriately, is student-centered, and ignites students’ interest in English through their passion and engaging and up-to-date pedagogy.

Required Qualifications and Experience

● A valid teaching license or certification

● At least three years of relevant and recent teaching experience

● Experience with, and a belief in, an inquiry approach to teaching and learning

● Experience teaching English Language Learners

● Experience using data to inform instruction through a Professional Learning Community (PLC)

Preferred Qualifications

● Experience teaching IB and/or AP (preferred)

● Experience teaching a standards-based curriculum using the Common Core Standards (preferred)

Pedagogical Practice requirements

● Has an Inquiry-based approach to teaching and learning

● Ability to adapt teaching to the context

● Highly Skilled in using a varied pedagogical and assessment toolkit

● Can challenge and extend all learners

● Can integrate the teaching of skills to prepare students for life beyond the classroom

● Identifies, selects, and utilizes instructional resources to meet the needs of students with varying backgrounds, learning styles, and special needs.

● Uses data to improve learning

Mindsets and Dispositions

● Cares for students

● Commitment to the Social and Emotional Learning (SEL) of students.

● Strong work ethic

● Contributes positively to the culture of the school

● Strong and effective communication skills

● Open-minded and adaptable

● Demonstrates growth-mindset and passion for lifelong learning

● Culturally competent

● Reflective on their practice

Core Responsibilities

● Teach five high school courses.

● Serves as an Advisor in the High School Advisory Program.

● Collaborate as an effective member of high school teams (PLC, Department, Grade Level, etc.)

● Positively contribute to school culture through the support and sponsorship of a student club or non-stipended extracurricular activity.

● Participates in professional development training and attends required presentations.

● Meets professional obligations through efficient work habits such as meeting deadlines, honoring schedules, and working with colleagues. ● Ensures student growth and achievement is continuous and appropriate for age group, subject area, and /or program classification. ● Provides a positive and safe environment in which students are encouraged to actively engage in the learning process.

● Performs other duties and responsibilities as assigned by their supervisor.

Application Details

Interested candidates should complete the online application (www.isb.ac.th/job-opportunities) at the earliest opportunity and before the deadline of February 1, 2027. Search Associates candidates need only apply through APLI on the Search Associates platform, and finalists will be invited to complete the secondary screening via TruFit Talent. All other applicants can apply directly through TruFit Talent using the link provided in the vacancy announcement on the school website. Please note that if an outstanding applicant is identified early in the search process, ISB reserves the right to make an appointment prior to the deadline.

Compensation and Benefits

ISB provides a competitive compensation and benefits package that is commensurate with the candidate’s experience and aligned with global international school standards. Benefits provided to the employee and up to two dependent children.

The Middle School at International School Bangkok (ISB) offers a well-rounded US curriculum experience in Thailand that balances care, challenge, choice, and opportunity to foster personal and academic growth. Position Overview

The Middle School Dean of Academics is a key instructional leader who partners with the Principal to oversee academic programming for approximately 470 students and over 60 faculty. This role focuses on refining curriculum, instruction, and assessment to enhance teaching and learning for understanding.

The Dean of Academics leads MS faculty in curricular coherence, works closely with learning specialists and departmental leaders, evaluates faculty performance, champions professional growth through coaching, and partners with the Learning Design Center team to develop and implement our guaranteed curriculum. By leveraging data to drive instructional decisions, the Dean fosters a collaborative, student-centered environment and maintains clear communication across the school community.

Core Responsibilities

● Leads teams in applying the principles and practices of highly effective collaborative teams

● Guides teacher collaborative teams in using data to inform instruction based on student needs to intentionally plan for differentiation, intervention, and extension.

● Oversees the development of a viable master schedule that supports the academic and social emotional growth of MS students.

● Engages in ongoing professional development to implement research-supported practices.

● Communicates collaboratively with families to enhance student well-being and learning.

● Contributes to a positive school culture through shared purpose and community care.

● Balances high expectations with comprehensive support systems.

● Other duties as requested by the Principal.

Required Qualifications

● A bachelor's degree from an accredited university

● Minimum of three years of experience as a learning-focused leader

● Valid teacher and/or administrative certification

● Previous administrative experience

● Previous international school experience

● Demonstrated success in a multicultural school environment

● Experience in staff supervision and performance evaluation

● Proven success in instructional improvement and faculty development

Competencies and Skills

● Expertise in assessment and teaching for understanding

● Ability to inspire excellence and a commitment to continuous professional learning

● Capacity to build trust and leadership credibility

● Superior interpersonal and communication skills

● Supportive, student-centered, and approachable

● Strong analytical, strategic planning, and decision-making skills

● Collaborative approach with diverse school stakeholders

● Trustworthy, open-minded, optimistic, and energetic leader

● Creative problem solver

Personal Attributes

● Inclusive, fair, and empathetic leader

● Highly effective communicator with a proven capacity to build trust and community

● Composed and consistent under pressure

● Globally minded and culturally proficient

● Ethical and transparent in decision-making

● Highly collaborative and reflective practitioner

● Resilient and solution-oriented

job.title: The St. Paul's School for Boys Assistant Director of College Counseling
job.description:
Position Description

Voted one of Baltimore’s top workplaces, the St. Paul’s Schools is a family of independent schools located in Brooklandville, Maryland. With more than 1,400 students from ages 6 weeks to grade 12, St. Paul’s Pre and Lower School (coed), St. Paul’s School for Boys, and St. Paul’s School for Girls share a 120-acre campus, an Episcopal affiliation, and a focus on developing confident, well-balanced students who will use their education and ethics to improve the world.

A coordinated structure allows The St. Paul’s Schools to preserve the small school feel within each school while sharing resources and certain programs to maximize opportunities for students. With St. Paul’s unique model, boys and girls are taught together and separately at just the right times in their development. The St. Paul’s School is a community that leads with love and creates and a community of authentic belonging.

St. Paul’s School for Boys, founded in 1849, is a college-preparatory day school serving boys in grades 5 through 12. The school’s mission, “Seek truth, knowledge, and excellence; live by faith, compassion, and integrity,” is the daily standard for all members of our community. St. Paul’s School for Boys’ students are thoughtful young men who thrive in an educational community that emphasizes strong relationships, personal growth, and the collective pursuit of integrity.

Opportunity Statement

The Assistant Director of College Counseling supports boys and their families through every stage of the college search, application, and admission process. This role partners closely with faculty, advisors, and staff across the school community to promote each student’s academic, personal, and social growth. Additionally, the Assistant Director is expected to build strong relationships with college admissions officers and develop a deep understanding of higher education institutions through ongoing collaboration and outreach. In addition to their college counseling responsibilities, this professional is expected to be actively engaged in the broader school community through supporting the mission of the school, building positive relationships with students, families and colleagues and contributing to the school life through committees, events, and activities. This is a 10 month position.

What You’ll Do

  • Meet regularly with students and families to provide personalized guidance on course selection, standardized testing, extracurricular involvement, summer opportunities, and developing a well-balanced college list.
  • Participate in divisional and school-wide meetings; represent the office in lieu of director when needed.
  • Support students through the application process, including essay review, interview preparation, and completion of school forms and recommendations.
  • Write and submit school reports and recommendation letters that highlight each student’s accomplishments, strengths, and character.
  • Collaborate with faculty, coaches, administration, and staff to deliberate a holistic understanding of each student to support them through their admissions process.
  • Implement appropriate programming for students and parents (e.g., athletic liasion, college nights, workshops, mock interviews).
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with college admission representatives through campus visits, professional networks, and hosting events that expand opportunities for students.
  • Communicate proactively, clearly, and in a timely manner with students, families, and faculty regarding deadlines, requirements, and trends in college admission.
  • Collaborate with faculty, advisors, and administrators to support adolescent males and foster a deeper understanding of their experiences throughout the college admissions process.
  • Continue to establish and maintain mutually beneficial relationships with counterparts at St. Paul’s School for Girls.
  • Stay current with changes in higher education and admission practices by attending conferences, visiting campuses, and engaging in professional networks.
  • Confidence in using appropriate technology and resources, such as SCOIR, College Money Method, Teams.
  • Contribute to other school programs and activities as appropriate and serve as a positive representative of the school’s mission and values.

Who You Are

  • Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree in education, counseling, or a related field preferred.
  • Minimum of three years of experience in college counseling, college admissions, or a related field.
  • Strong ability to build relationships with students, families, colleagues, and higher-education professionals.
  • Excellent interpersonal, communication, and organizational skills and ability to work independently.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information with discretion.

At St. Paul’s Schools, we are dedicated to fostering a nurturing and inclusive learning environment where every individual is celebrated for their unique strengths and contributions. We believe that diversity enriches education, empowering students to reach their fullest potential. By embracing a culture of inclusion, we prepare our students to succeed in an increasingly interconnected and multicultural world. We stand firmly against all forms of prejudice, including those related to race, ethnicity, religion, socioeconomic background, gender identity, sexual orientation, and physical appearance.

The St. Paul’s Schools has a compensation scale based on direct years of experience and degree held. Compensation for the role will depend on a number of factors, including a candidate’s years of experience, education and skills. For this opportunity, our salary range is $55,000 to $65,000 annually. Candidates with additional experience or qualifications may be offered a salary outside of the range shown. In addition, full-time team members gain access to our robust benefits package designed to support your well-being, inside and outside of work. This includes a competitive healthcare package (medical, dental, and vision), disability protection, participation in our 403(b) retirement plan which has an immediate employer contribution and a generous time off package, including wellness days because we believe you may need a day off ‘just because!’.

Beyond the basics, we offer extras like a lunch stipend, access to multiple fitness centers on campus and professional development experiences to continue your learning. In addition, full-time employees who choose The St. Paul’s Schools for their children’s educational journey, are eligible to receive a tuition remission benefit. Your salary will be commensurate with your experience and reflect the value you bring to our team.

Interested candidates can send their cover letter, resume and list of references to Shannon Duckett, Executive Director of Human Resources, at sduckett@stpaulsmd.org. The St. Paul’s Schools is an equal opportunity employer.

job.title: The Calhoun School Associate Director of Advancement
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Salary Range: 100K–130KSalary/year

Position Type: Full-time, exempt

Job Shift: Day

Education Level: 4 Year Degree

Travel Percentage: Occasional for events

Category: Education

The Calhoun School is seeking an Associate Director of Advancement for the 2026 - 2027 school year. Reporting to the Director of Advancement, the Associate Director of Advancement is a new position designed to accelerate growth in annual giving and alumni engagement, and support an ambitious major gifts strategy. The successful candidate will be a highly relational, creative and goal-oriented professional capable of serving as a warm and articulate ambassador of Calhoun’s progressive mission. This role will supervise a small team of advancement staff, providing day-to-day direction, guidance, and support to ensure the effective execution of the advancement office's mission and goals.

At Calhoun, we value Curiosity, Kindness, and Excellence. This position is essential in ensuring that every constituent—from families newly joining our community to longtime donors attending a signature event—feels seen, heard, and valued within our joyful community.

Key Responsibilities

  • Annual Fund
  • Partner with the Director of Advancement to design and execute the school’s Annual Fund strategy, including an annual Giving Day
  • Manage day-to-day operations of The Calhoun Annual Fund (CAF) including timelines, appeals, and stewardship
  • Coordinate and implement multi-channel solicitations (email, direct mail, digital)
  • Recruit, train, and support parent, alumni, grandparent and other volunteers, tracking volunteer lists and updates
  • Lead CAF volunteer meetings
  • Solicit a portfolio of leadership ($2,500+) donors
  • Recommend major gift prospects to the Director of Advancement
  • Create and run regular reports tracking fundraising progress, lapsed donors, etc.
  • Calhoun Advancement Events
  • Partner with the Admissions and Advancement Coordinate to prepare prospect briefings for the Head of School, Director of Advancement and Trustees prior to all Advancement Events
  • Recommend engagement strategies for event guests
  • Attend and actively engage with guests at all Advancement Events
  • Serve as the lead on the Calhoun Benefit, recruiting and coordinating volunteers, identifying and soliciting auction and raffle donations, designing a marketing and communications strategy
  • Major Gifts and Special Projects
  • Oversee the major gifts pipeline document, ensuring that prospects are tracked, volunteer assignments are kept up to date and fundraising totals are accurate
  • Prepare reports for Head of School, Director of Advancement, Board of Trustees
  • Partner with the Advancement Communications and Operations Manager to ensure timely pledge agreements are processed and entered into Raiser’s Edge
  • Maintain the pledge payment calendar and send pledge payment reminders
  • Support the Admissions and Advancement Coordinator in prospect research and preparing briefings for solicitors
  • Partner with the Director of Advancement on major gift communications and marketing efforts
  • Alumni Relations
  • Partner with Advancement colleagues to design and execute a comprehensive alumni relations program, including a calendar of events and volunteer engagement
  • Identify, cultivate and solicit alumni leadership donors for The Calhoun Annual Fund, and recommend alumni major gift prospects to the Director of Advancement
  • Partner with the Dean of Diversity, Equity and Belonging to support the Alumni of Color Network (ACN), attending ACN meetings as requested and supporting the ACN calendar of events

This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications associated with the position. Calhoun reserves the right to modify, add, or remove duties and to assign other duties as necessary.

Commitment to Diversity Work

Calhoun is committed to addressing issues of social justice, diversity, equity, and anti-bias education in our curriculum and in our community. Teachers must be willing learners and participants in supporting this work.

Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

Calhoun is committed to recruiting, hiring and supporting a diverse staff and welcomes applicants of all gender, sexuality, religious, ethnic, racial and cultural identities. Calhoun does not unlawfully discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of one’s actual or perceived race; color; religion; sex/gender (including gender identity); creed; sexual orientation; marital status; pregnancy; ethnicity; national origin, ancestry, age, and disability.

Qualifications

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in fundraising, not limited to independent schools
  • Bachelor’s degree required, advanced degree in related field preferred
  • Strong project management and organizational skills
  • Ability to work across multiple teams
  • Familiar with RENXT or other advancement databases

job.title: St. Andrew's School Leadership Gifts Officer
job.description:
Position Description

St. Andrew’s School develops the independence, character, mind, and spirit of its students to prepare them for lives of citizenship, service, and purpose. Join the school as our leadership gifts officer and help advance this mission as a key member of the advancement department.

All students live, learn, and play in the natural beauty of our 2,200-acre campus. At the center of our community are curious, motivated, and diverse students who are accepted without regard to their families’ means. Each young person is challenged and valued, and students are truly known by the lifelong mentors who teach, coach, and advise them. Human connection, face to face, is the foundation of our program. Friendship and joy define our spirit; “faith and learning” is our motto.

Position Summary:

The leadership gifts officer reports to the director of advancement and serves as the primary advancement lead for reunion giving and leadership-level gifts. This role is responsible for designing and executing comprehensive reunion giving strategies, cultivating and soliciting leadership-level donors, and building long-term philanthropic partnerships that advance St. Andrew’s mission.

The leadership gifts officer manages a portfolio of leadership-level donors and reunion prospects to secure significant unrestricted Saints Fund gifts. The ideal candidate is a strategic relationship builder with the confidence and skill to inspire meaningful philanthropic investment through personalized, in-person engagement. Flexibility is essential, including the ability to travel overnight approximately 30–40% of the time and attend evening and weekend events as needed.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Leadership-Level Donor Engagement & Solicitation

  • Manage a portfolio of approximately 80–100 reunion and leadership-level donors and prospective donors.
  • Qualify a minimum of 25 prospective major-gift donors.
  • Conduct at least 10 donor visits monthly, focused on delivery, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  • Develop individualized, donor-centered strategies that align philanthropic interests with St. Andrew’s strategic priorities.
  • Solicit leadership gifts and guide peer-to-peer solicitations when appropriate.

Reunion Giving Leadership

Lead reunion giving as a primary strategy for advancing alumni through the philanthropic lifecycle, growing leadership-level Saints Fund participation, and building a sustainable pipeline for future major-gift donors.

  • Serve as the strategic lead for reunion giving, overseeing volunteer recruitment and peer-to-peer solicitation workflows while maintaining a personal focus on leadership-level ($2,500+) commitments.
  • Develop and execute multi-year reunion giving strategies that increase leadership Saints Fund donors and dollars while deepening long-term alumni engagement.
  • Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward reunion and leadership Saints Fund donors with capacity for increased annual giving and consideration for future major gifts.
  • Partner with alumni relations, advancement leadership, and volunteer class leaders to expand the leadership Saints Fund donor base by reunion cohort.
  • Recruit, train, and support reunion gift volunteers to drive peer-to-peer engagement and increased giving.
  • Set annual leadership Saints Fund goals, benchmarks, and timelines in collaboration with the director of development.
  • Collaborate with donor relations and communications teams on targeted messaging, recognition, and stewardship.

Fundraising Strategy & Institutional Impact

  • Secure leadership-level gifts in support of annual giving.
  • Prepare and present compelling proposals and gift opportunities in collaboration with advancement colleagues.
  • Meet or exceed individual fundraising goals while contributing to broader advancement and reunion fundraising objectives.

Collaboration & Volunteer Engagement

  • Partner closely with alumni relations to ensure a coordinated, relationship-driven reunion experience.
  • Plan and participate in joint donor visits with the head of school, director of advancement, trustees, senior administrators, faculty, and key volunteers.
  • Collaborate with advancement colleagues, including Saints Fund, donor relations, and communications, to ensure consistent strategy, messaging, and donor experience.

Operations, Reporting & Stewardship

  • Utilize a moves management approach in coordination with advancement operations to guide donors through the giving cycle.
  • Maintain accurate and timely donor records in the school’s database.

job.title: St. Stephen's and St. Agnes School Sports Fields and Facilities Technician
job.description:
Position Description

St. Stephen's and St. Agnes School is seeking a dedicated and proactive Sports Fields and Facilities Technician to join the Buildings and Grounds (B&G) team at the Upper School campus in Alexandria, Virginia. Reporting to the B&G Campus Supervisor, the Sports Fields and Facilities Technician will play a vital role in ensuring the optimal condition and performance of the athletic fields by maintaining safe, high-quality playing surfaces and facilities for various sports.

Duties/Responsibilities:

  • Oversee the day-to-day maintenance of athletic fields on the assigned campus.
  • Prepare athletic fields for practices and events, ensuring a safe playing surface.
  • Mark and stripe fields according to sport-specific dimensions and regulations.
  • Mow and maintain turf grass to the specified height for athletic activities.
  • Implement aeration, moisture control, and top dressing to maintain collegiate-level sports field surfaces.
  • Apply fertilizers and nutrients to promote resilience and recovery to ensure turf health.
  • Monitor and adjust irrigation systems to maintain optimal soil moisture and ensure proper drainage to prevent waterlogging and ensure consistent playing conditions.
  • Manage turf areas to recover quickly from heavy use and adverse weather.
  • Implement pest management strategies to protect turf from insects and diseases.
  • Identify and control weeds using safe and effective methods.
  • Coordinates with outside contractors when necessary to address turf-related issues promptly.
  • Manages online work order management system requests related to athletic fields.
  • Schedules routine and annual safety and maintenance inspections.
  • Serve as the primary liaison between B&G and the Athletic Department, meeting regularly and communicating proactively to coordinate field and facility maintenance, seasonal transitions, event preparation, weather-related impacts, closures, repairs, improvements, and capital priorities.
  • Orders and maintains inventory of necessary maintenance supplies and equipment.
  • Assists with event set up and breakdown.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned.

Note: The position may have opportunities to participate more directly in the school's athletics program. Willingness and ability to also coach an athletic team in the afternoons is valued. Coaching responsibilities would be compensated separately through the school's established coaching stipend structure.

Required Skills/Abilities:

  • Knowledge of sports field construction, turf varieties, and athletic field specifications.
  • Proven experience in athletic field or turf grass maintenance.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to meet sport-specific field requirements.
  • Ability to operate and maintain specialized turf equipment.
  • Adhere to safety protocols and guidelines for athletic field maintenance, including the safe use of equipment and chemicals.
  • Strong communication skills (oral and written) and ability to communicate effectively with individuals at varying levels.
  • Proficient with computers or related software as needed to complete reports, logs, and inventory.
  • Must be able to work occasional nights and weekends.

Education and Experience:

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • At least 3 years of turfgrass maintenance experience is required.
  • Have mower mechanics skills to maintain equipment.
  • Driver's license.

Physical Requirements:

  • Must be able to stand and walk extensive campus properties for prolonged periods of time and work outdoors in various weather conditions.
  • Must be physically able to operate required equipment.
  • Must be able to lift 50 pounds at a time.

Overview:

St. Stephen's and St. Agnes School is an affirming and collegial community committed to our mission to "pursue goodness as well as knowledge and to honor the unique value of each of our members as a child of God in a caring community." SSSAS is an age 3 to Grade 12 Episcopal day school located on three campuses six miles from Washington, D.C., in beautiful and historic Alexandria, Va. We believe that educating the whole child by tending to their individual academic, social/emotional, cultural, and physical needs, prepares them to be knowledgeable, kind, and empathetic citizens in a complex world. Combining a rigorous academic program with outstanding opportunities in the arts, athletics, and service learning for our students, SSSAS is a community that values diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging, and we seek candidates who share these same values.

Our culture promotes lifelong learning, and employees have a wealth of opportunities available to them to continue expanding their knowledge of both their disciplines and in their field of education. Cultural competency workshops for all faculty and staff, regular, small-group DEIB exploration/workshops, support for graduate studies, summer study grants, and conferences (e.g., People of Color Conference, the National Association of Independent School Annual Conference, and CASE-NAIS) are just a few of the ways in which we support and encourage our Saints faculty and staff to continue to develop and learn in their field and as part of our community.

READY TO JOIN OUR COMMUNITY?

We understand your time is valuable, and that is why we have a very quick and easy application process. If you feel that you would be right for this job, please fill out our initial 3-minute, mobile-friendly application. We look forward to meeting you!

Interested applicants should apply through the SSSAS website at

https://www.sssas.org/about-us/employment

For more information about St. Stephen's and St. Agnes School, we invite you to visit our website at www.sssas.org

job.title: St. Andrew's School Facilities Care Technician
job.description:
Position Description

St. Andrew’s School develops the independence, character, mind, and spirit of its students to prepare them for lives of citizenship, service, and purpose. Be at the center of this mission by joining the school as our facilities care technician, a key member of the facilities department.

All students live, learn, and play in the natural beauty of our 2,200–acre campus. At the center of our community are curious, motivated, and diverse students who are accepted without regard to their families’ means. Each young person is challenged and valued, and students are truly known by the lifelong mentors who teach, coach, and advise them. Human connection, face to face, is the foundation of our program. Position Summary:

St. Andrew’s School is seeking a full-time facilities care technician based on a 40-hour work week, year-round with extra hours on a periodic basis. Actual hours will be assigned based on the needs of the department. Some weekend and special event coverage may be required. Employees in this position are eligible for overtime payment. This is a critical member of our community who works to ensure the cleanliness, health, safety, and aesthetics of the campus.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Perform institutional and residential duties that include a variety of cleaning tasks such as, cleaning/sanitizing bathrooms, vacuuming, dusting, cleaning screens and windows, gathering and removing trash, sweeping, mopping floors, and changing bed linens.
  • Working independently or assist other facilities care technicians as assigned.
  • Assist with setting up for special events, which includes moving tables, chairs, and furniture.

Job Requirements:

  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Possession of a current, valid driver’s license.
  • Self-motivated, ability to follow directions and work with little to no supervision.
  • Ability to work well with others as a team player; a pleasant personality is essential.
  • Ability to operate cleaning machines.
  • Prior housekeeping experience is preferred but not required.

Physical Demands:

  • Work involves exposure to unusual elements, such as extreme temperatures, dirt, dust, fumes, smoke, unpleasant odors, and loud noises.

job.title: St. Andrew's School Mental Health Counselor
job.description:
Position Description

Job Title: Mental Health Counselor

Reports to: Director of Counseling

Department: Student Life

Employment Type: Full-Time Faculty

FLSA: Exempt

Posted: September 8, 2026

St. Andrew’s School develops the independence, character, mind, and spirit of its students to prepare them for lives of citizenship, service, and purpose. Be at the center of this mission by joining the school as our mental health counselor, a key member of the student life department.

All our students live, learn, and play in the natural beauty of our 2,200-acre campus. At the center of our community are curious, motivated, and diverse students who are accepted without regard to their families’ means. Each young person is challenged and valued, and students are truly known by the life-long mentors who teach, coach, and advise them. Human connection, face to face, is the foundation of our program. Friendship and joy define our spirit; “Faith and Learning” is our motto.

Position Summary:

St. Andrew’s seeks a mental health counselor. The counselor will report to the director of counseling to develop and implement wellness initiatives that foster student well-being and support social and emotional growth. The counselor will provide individual short-term supportive counseling and provide interventions to address a variety of mental health and learning challenges that affect adolescents, including crisis assessment. The counselor must be well versed in all areas of clinical counseling with regard to adolescent student needs, parent and professional communication, and collaboration with administration and faculty.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Assessing, diagnosing, and managing a large and diverse caseload of adolescents.
  • Providing ongoing psychotherapy and/or adjustment counseling, teaching a semester-long wellness course for IV formers (tenth graders).
  • Maintaining a positive professional relationship with members of the school community.
  • Additional duties include sharing on-call coverage during the weeknights and weekends.
  • Reviewing psychological testing of applicants and students, training school counseling personnel.
  • Maintaining required health records for all students seen in a timely fashion.
  • Collaborating with the school’s consulting psychiatrist, associate head of school, athletic director, dean of student affairs, and the director of health services, and participating in regular administrative meetings.
  • When needed, the counselor may coordinate referrals to mental health professionals and implement treatment recommendations.
  • The counselor will also be asked to participate in the community life of St. Andrew’s through attendance at occasional weekend and evening events.

Job Requirements:

  1. Five years of relevant experience providing counseling/therapy services to adolescents.
  2. Familiarity with the boarding school setting is highly desirable.
  3. Knowledge of the ethical and legal considerations related to counseling practices.
  4. Passion for working with and living in a community with adolescents.
  5. Generalist in terms of counseling, prepared to deal with a variety of mental health issues such as adjustment issues, anxiety, depression, and eating disorders, among others.
  6. Knowledge of different therapeutic approaches, including cognitive behavioral therapy.
  7. Excellent relationship building and communication skills, both verbally and in writing.
  8. Effective communication with students, parents, faculty, and staff regarding mental health and social wellness; consult with parents of children with identified concerns and make recommendations for follow-up evaluation and/or treatment.
  9. Ensure that all required health records are maintained in a timely fashion and in a manner which retains medical confidentiality and complies with HIPAA.
  10. Design and deploy faculty and staff psychoeducation workshops to support and elevate student wellbeing.
  11. Coordinate and facilitate communication and exchange of pertinent information with outside counselors/providers.
  12. Provide weeknight and weekend on-call coverage for after-hours crisis management and risk assessments on a rotating basis with other counselors.
  13. A Master’s or Doctoral degree in school counseling, social work, marriage and family counseling, mental health counseling, or professional counseling is required.
  14. Must be licensed or eligible for clinical licensure and working towards full clinical licensure in the state of Delaware (ex: LCSW, LPC, LMFT) upon hire.
