job.title: St. Andrew's School Assistant Athletic Trainer
job.description:
Position Description

St. Andrew’s School develops the independence, character, mind, and spirit of its students to prepare them for lives of citizenship, service, and purpose. Be at the center of this mission by joining the school as our assistant athletic trainer, a key member of the athletics department.

All students live, learn, and play in the natural beauty of our 2,200-acre campus. At the center of our community are curious, motivated, and diverse students who are accepted without regard to their families’ means. Each young person is challenged and valued, and students are truly known by the lifelong mentors who teach, coach, and advise them. Human connection, face-to-face, is the foundation of our program. Friendship and joy define our spirit; “faith and learning” is our motto.

Position Summary:

Sports Medicine at St. Andrew’s is not only about the treatment of athletic injuries, but also the holistic care, development, and growth of each student on campus. The athletic training facility at St. Andrew’s is a hub of energy and excitement every day before sports. The positivity and enthusiasm of the athletic trainers set the tone for many of the athletes for the afternoon and work in concert with the coach/mentor model of the school. Our work with the St. Andrew’s athletes goes beyond the opportunity to heal, to also connect and mirror the transformative process of the classrooms, sports fields, and dorms. The assistant athletic trainer should fully

embrace the role of caregiver and mentor.

St. Andrew’s is an associate member school in the Delaware Interscholastic Athletic Association and a member of the Delaware Independent School Conference.

This position will report to the director of athletics and work collaboratively with a sports medicine doctor. The incumbent must be prompt, dependable, and flexible, providing sideline medical coverage for practice and games.

This position will work approximately 20 hours per week beginning August 18, 2026, until May 31, 2027. Typical hours are 3:15 PM to 6:30 PM, Monday through Friday. Other shifts outside of the typical hours may occasionally be necessary based on game schedules and as needed on Saturdays.

Breaks include a fall long weekend (4 days), Thanksgiving break (9 days), winter break (18 days), a winter long weekend (4 days), spring break (15 days), and a spring long weekend (4 days).

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Injury Prevention

  • Identifying and mitigating risks to prevent injuries, including implementing safety protocols approved by the director of athletics.
  • Providing education on proper rehabilitation, exercises, and training techniques, and promoting healthy lifestyles.
  • Demonstrate of become familiar with various DIAA Sports Medicine guidelines, such as the Heat Restriction Policy and Concussion Management Guidelines.

Clinical Evaluation and Diagnosis

  • Assessing and diagnosing injuries and illnesses, utilizing various methods and tools within the scope of your education and DE state license and recommending referral to medical professionals when necessary.
  • Discuss all clinical assessments with the director of athletics before progressing with treatment.

Immediate and Emergency Care

  • Providing immediate on-field or on-site care for injuries and illnesses, including first aid, stabilization, and the potential activation of EMS.
  • Demonstrate knowledge and comfort with St. Andrew’s approved Emergency Action Plans and communication with all roles and personnel involved with our system of care.

Treatment and Rehabilitation

  • Implement treatment plans and rehabilitation programs to restore injured athletes’ abilities to participate, utilizing modalities, exercises, manual therapy, and other therapeutic techniques.
  • Communicate, coordinate, and progress all treatment and rehabilitation plans with the approval of the director of athletics.

Organization and Administration

  • Maintain documentation of all assessments and treatments.
  • Maintain the assessment and care of injured visiting athletes are communicated to the athlete’s coaching staff, the athlete’s parent(s), and the visiting team’s athletic trainer.

Professional Responsibility

  • Maintain ethical standards, adhere to professional guidelines, and engage in continuing education to stay current in the field.
  • Maintain professional boundaries with all student athletes to establish the essential foundation for building trusting and respectful relationships.

Job Requirements:

  1. A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in training, sports medicine, exercise science, kinesiology, or related field.
  2. Must be BOC certified, possess Delaware state athletic training licensure, and be CPR certified.
  3. Must be able to lift 100 pounds maximum with frequent lifting and/or carrying of objects like coolers or weight room equipment.
  4. Medium strength is required to position athletes for examination. May assist athletes as needed in ways such as, but not limited to, helping them on and off field, the exam table.
  5. Must be comfortable driving a golf cart to the sports field to take medical supplies and/or water coolers.

Conditions of Hire:

A thorough background check—inclusive of fingerprinting, a Child Protection Registry Check, a motor vehicle record check, and other relevant screenings—is required as a condition of employment.

Applicants must complete satisfactory reference checks, confirmation of compliance with federal and state employment laws, and any other required condition of employment.

job.title: Hackley School Admissions Coordinator
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Salary Range

$50,000.00 - $60,000.00 Salary/year

Position Type

Full Time

Description

Position Overview

Hackley School seeks an Admissions Coordinator for a 12-month staff position responsible for supporting all aspects of the admissions process. The Admissions Coordinator will work with the Associate Director of Enrollment Management, the Director of Enrollment Management, the Associate Director of Admissions and Outreach, and other members of the Admissions Team, as well as the Communications Team, to help the School meet short- and long-term enrollment goals identified by School Leadership and the Board of Trustees.

The Admissions Coordinator reports to the Associate Director of Enrollment Management and is a member of the Admissions Team.

Specific Responsibilities

  • Primary point of contact for all inquiries and visitors
  • Greet and welcome visitors upon arrival, arriving by 7:30 AM on days when early visitors are expected
  • Answer the main admissions phone line and, when needed, other office lines
  • Manage the Admissions email account; create content/templates for text and email communications in Veracross and individual responses
  • Manage incoming and outgoing mail for the Admissions Office
  • Schedule visitors and maintain the Admissions Office calendar for campus tours, information sessions, and interviews for the Admissions Team, and several faculty interviewers.
  • Create interview, tour and admissions events in Veracross
  • Coordinate family schedules with Lower, Middle and Upper School schedules
  • Review and schedule online tour and interview registrations
  • Send daily notifications to faculty and staff of interview schedules and applicant visits
  • Send confirmation emails for visiting families
  • Provide administrative support and coordination of Admissions events, including but not limited, to two fall Saturday Open Houses
  • Prepare and send invitations to prospective families for events and update online registration forms as needed
  • Prepare photocopies and information packets, arrange facilities bookings and catering, and ensure that all events are listed on the all-school calendar
  • Communicate with offices across campus
  • Attend and help administer event registration and check-in
  • Manage application files (more than 700 a year) and maintain application status correspondence with applicant families to support timely submission of required materials.
  • Partner with the Associate Director of Admissions and Outreach to oversee and manage the Student Ambassador Program
  • Partner with the Admissions Team for office support and backup
  • Provide data entry and document management to produce reports for divisional offices, Advancement Office and Hackley Parent Association, as well as ad hoc reports for marketing purposes and historical data collection, etc.
  • Work with the Finance Office regarding per diem payments to interviewers and evaluators
  • Transcribe notes from Board of Trustees committee meetings as needed
  • Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree required and a minimum of two years’ relevant is preferred. Admissions, Independent School and/or teaching experience will be helpful, as would paid or volunteer experience as a student ambassador or tour guide.
  • Genuine interest in families and education, a sense of humor and warmth, and a positive outlook.
  • Enjoy meeting new people and assisting them on the phone, over email and in person
  • Able to work as part of a goal-oriented team in an environment that can be fast-paced; must also have a growth mindset and desire to learn new skills
  • Strong organizational, multi-tasking and prioritizing skills, as well as a professional demeanor and manner
  • Strong knowledge of the Microsoft and Google suites, including facility with mail merge, labels, name tags and letter formatting, preferred
  • Experience with admission databases such as Veracross, preferred
  • Written and spoken fluency in Spanish or Mandarin is a plus

Salary and Benefits

The salary range for this position is $50,000 - $60,000, depending on experience.

Hackley School offers a comprehensive benefits package, which includes a medical, dental and vision package; sick and vacation time; life insurance, AD&D and long-term disability insurance; flexible spending or health savings account; tuition remission; and the possibility of eventual on-campus housing. This is an on-campus position, and Hackley does not offer a remote/hybrid work environment.

Mission and History

Hackley School is a nonsectarian coeducational K-12 independent school located in Tarrytown, NY. Founded as a boarding school in 1899, Hackley enrolls approximately 855 students, including about 25 five-day boarding students in grades 9-12.

Students experience joy in the classroom and make life-long connections with each other and with our dedicated faculty, 40% of whom reside on campus. Robust extracurricular programming on our 285-acre campus creates unique opportunities for each student to learn and grow beyond the boundaries of the school day. Hackley graduates have the knowledge and confidence to pursue their passions and the drive to make a difference.

Hackley challenges students to grow in character, scholarship, and accomplishment, to offer unreserved effort, and to learn from the varying perspectives and backgrounds in our community and the world.

job.title: Marlborough School Advancement Database Coordinator
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Advancement Database Coordinator

Office of Advancement

Full-time, Non-exempt Staff

Founded in 1889, Marlborough School is an independent girls college-preparatory school for grades 7 through 12 located in Los Angeles, California. Marlborough is the oldest independent girls’ school in the Southern California region. Central to Marlborough’s vision that Equity Leads Education is the belief in and passion for empowering young women to use their immense talents to better the world and become trailblazers in their own right. Bolstered by world-class faculty and staff, Marlborough students are challenged and inspired to work towards their own personal best and, in doing so, have an almost endless array of courses, extracurriculars, electives, and programs to spark their curiosity, deepen their compassion for one another, and lead lives of purpose.

Position Overview

Under the direction of the Advancement Services Manager, the Advancement Database Coordinator plays a key role in powering Marlborough School’s fundraising and alumnae engagement efforts. Using Raiser’s Edge NXT and other Advancement technology platforms, the Coordinator manages essential gift and constituent data with accuracy and independence while providing the information and insights that enable the Advancement team to build meaningful relationships and achieve its fundraising goals. This is an exciting opportunity for a detail-oriented, curious professional who enjoys working with data, solving problems, and finding better ways to support a high-performing Advancement team. As an active member of the Marlborough community, the Coordinator participates in School and Advancement events, provides excellent customer service, and serves as an enthusiastic ambassador for girls’ education and philanthropy.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

  • Oversee the accurate and timely processing and importing of daily gifts and pledges, including online gifts, credit cards, checks, stock, gifts-in-kind, matching gifts, and memorial and honorary gifts into Raiser’s Edge NXT. Maintain cash receipt journals, gift backup, pledge records, corporate matching gift confirmations, and support monthly reconciliation with the Business Office.
  • Coordinate timely acknowledgment and receipt of all gifts. Create acknowledgments for memorial and honorary gifts and generate and distribute pledge reminders.
  • Partner with the Business Office on monthly gift reconciliation, ensuring accurate alignment between Raiser’s Edge, cash receipt journals, and General Ledger entries.
  • Maintain constituent records and data hygiene, including individual and bulk updates, and partner with the Registrar and other School administrators to coordinate data updates.
  • Create complex queries, exports, mailing and email lists, reports, and other data files to support Advancement and School initiatives.
  • Configure and maintain custom online giving forms to ensure accurate gift and data capture, as well as seamless integration with Raiser's Edge NXT.
  • In collaboration with the Advancement Services Manager, evaluate and improve database workflows, identifying and implementing opportunities to increase accuracy, efficiency, and consistency.
  • Support Advancement events through pulling invitation and registration lists, tracking RSVPs, preparing nametags, and on-site event registration support.
  • As a welcoming and knowledgeable representative of Marlborough, provide responsive, professional customer service to students, families, alumnae, donors, faculty, staff, trustees, and other members of the School community through email, phone, and in-person interactions, including occasional reception desk coverage and School events.
  • Participate in Advancement and School-wide meetings, professional development opportunities, and relevant conferences and workshops.
  • Perform other related duties and special projects as assigned.

Skills and Abilities

  • Embodies, upholds, and articulates Marlborough School’s mission, vision, and values.
  • Exercises discretion and maintains the confidentiality of sensitive constituent and financial information.
  • Highly organized, analytical, and detail-oriented, with strong problem-solving skills and a commitment to data integrity.
  • Works independently and across teams, manages competing priorities, exercises sound judgment, and takes ownership of projects in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated commitment to providing exceptional customer service to a broad range of School constituencies and vendors.

Qualifications

  • Three or more years of progressively responsible experience in advancement services, fundraising operations, or constituent database management at a nonprofit, preferably in independent schools, higher education, or similar environment.
  • Demonstrated experience with gift processing, constituent record management, donor acknowledgments, data exports, mailing/email lists, reporting, and process improvement.
  • Proficiency with Raiser’s Edge NXT or a similar CRM; experience with Omatic and online fundraising platforms such as GiveCampus preferred.
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Word, including complex data files and mail merges; familiarity with Google Workspace.

Work and Schedule Requirements

  • Location & Hours: On-site position in Los Angeles, CA. Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Occasional early morning meetings, evening events, and weekend support as assigned.
  • Year-End Peak: Due to high-volume year-end giving processing, on-site coverage during the final two weeks of December is a requirement of this role.
  • Physical Demands (Office): Ability to perform stationary desk work for extended periods, including operating a computer and standard office equipment, with or without reasonable accommodation.
  • Physical Demands (Event Support): Ability to stand, walk, and assist with event activities, including guest check-in, nametags, and light equipment setup, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and eligible dependents, with additional voluntary coverage options
  • Generous paid time off including school closures, summer hours, vacation, sick, birthday, and holiday pay
  • 403(b) retirement plan with employer matching contributions
  • Meal allowance for on-campus cafeteria
  • Wellness incentives, discounts, and access to professional development funds
  • Competitive salary at: $33.65–$40.85 per hour ($70,000–$85,000 annually)

job.title: Ashley Hall Lead School Nurse
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Reports to: Assistant Head of School for Student Affairs

FLSA Status: Exempt

Role Schedule: 10-Month, Full-Time (plus 1 week before school resumes and after school closes)

Salary: Commensurate with experience

Job Description

Ashley Hall is seeking a highly qualified Lead School Nurse to provide oversight and day-to-day operations of the School’s Health Center. This position ensures the delivery of whole-person healthcare while aligning with the highest clinical, ethical, and regulatory standards.

Key Responsibilities

- Health Services Coordination and Administration

- Serve as an active member of the school nursing team.

- Supervise school nurses and coordinate schedules.

- Establish and implement departmental policies and procedures in accordance with - South Carolina law and best clinical practices.

- Develop annual objectives, structure operations, and manage the department budget and expenditures.

- Prepare reports and attend Administrative Team meetings as requested.

- Recommend staffing and facility needs to the Assistant Head of School for Student Affairs.

- Ensure compliance with all regulatory and accreditation standards.

- Clinical Practice and Oversight

- Assess student and employee health concerns, provide nursing care within the scope of South Carolina RN practice, implement evidence-based nursing interventions, and coordinate referrals to community healthcare providers as appropriate.

- Maintain current BLS certification.

- Provide or coordinate CPR, AED, and First Aid training for employees and students.

- Maintain clinical protocols and standing orders in collaboration with the school's consulting physician and in accordance with South Carolina law.

- Oversee campus emergency preparedness, including inspections of AEDs, bleeding control kits, and emergency medications.

- Manage memorandums of agreement with health partners such as MedPro, Electronic Health Records

- Maintain CLIA Waiver license

Collaboration and Training

- Partner with Counseling, Admissions, and Human Resources to address student and staff wellness needs.

- Collaborate with the Assistant Head of School for Student Affairs to deliver training related to health, safety, and emergency response.

- Coordinate on-site vaccination clinics and annual immunization tracking in compliance with SC DPH requirements

- Health Records and Technology Management

- Oversee student and employee medical records in August Schools and Practice Fusion platforms.

- Assign and monitor staff access to professional platforms related to nursing services

- Ensure data compliance and oversee accurate recordkeeping for all trainings and inspections.

- Quality Improvement & Regulatory Compliance

- Monitor departmental quality indicators and identify opportunities for process improvement.

- Ensure compliance with DPH, OSHA, HIPAA/FERPA, CLIA, , and school policies.

- Maintain required documentation for inspections and audits.

Qualifications

- Bachelor of Science in Nursing, required

- Master’s Degree, preferred

- Current unrestricted South Carolina RN license

- National School Nurse Certification (NCSN), preferred

- Three-five years school nursing experience

- Prior supervisory or leadership experience preferred

- Experience with regulatory compliance and electronic health records

- Current BLS Certification

- BLS Instructor Certification, preferred

- Strong clinical background in acute care

- Proven decision-making and organizational skills

Physical Requirements

- Prolonged periods of working on a computer or moving around campus

- Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds occasionally (e.g., emergency supplies, training equipment)

- Ability to respond promptly to emergencies and walk long distances on campus

- Manual dexterity to operate medical and office equipment

- Visual acuity to monitor health conditions and manage digital records

Employment Eligibility & Screening Requirements

Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of all required screenings - and clearances, including:

- Criminal background check (state and federal)

- Reference Checks

- Sex offender registry check

- Tuberculosis (TB) screening

-Verification of eligibility to work in the United States

- Any additional screenings required by South Carolina state law or Ashley Hall policy

- Time Commitment

- Typical Hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m.; schedule may vary depending on school needs

- Evenings/Weekends: Occasional attendance or coverage for school events and emergency response

- Schedule: Full-time, 10-Month, Full-Time (plus 1 week before faculty return and after faculty depart)

Questions regarding the position can be directed to:

Kimberly Ells-Payne, Talent Acquisition and Onboarding Manager

Email: ellsk@ashleyhall.org

Since its founding in 1909, Ashley Hall has empowered young women to think critically, act ethically, and embrace their world with confidence. The School serves girls from kindergarten through grade 12 (and is co-ed in its Early School, ages 2 to 5 years). Ashley Hall provides a dynamic education grounded in a Reggio approach in its Early School and an International Baccalaureate Primary Years Programme in its Lower School.

Ashley Hall is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, protected veteran status, disability or genetic information or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

job.title: Beaver Country Day School Operations and Stewardship Manager
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Reports to: Director of Philanthropy & Engagement

Classification: Full-time (12-month)

About The School

Beaver Country Day School is an independent day school serving 460 students in grades 6-12, located in Chestnut Hill, just outside of Boston. Founded in 1920 and propelled by our progressive roots, our goal is to expand the nature of school. With over 40 local and national partnerships, almost daily field trips, a thriving performing and visual arts program, and a best-in-class research and design center, we are able to combine rigorous academics with real-world application, focusing on teaching content combined with experience applying it to current issues.

The school fosters a joyful environment where students feel confident taking risks and being their authentic selves, where everyone, students and adults alike, feels a sense of belonging, and where teachers have the freedom to innovate and grow alongside their students.

Operations and Stewardship Manager

Reporting to the Director of Philanthropy & Engagement, the Operations and Stewardship Manager plays a central role in ensuring that Beaver’s fundraising and engagement work is supported by accurate data, strong systems, thoughtful stewardship, and efficient processes.

The Manager oversees the day-to-day operations of the P+E team’s database and fundraising systems, including gift processing, reporting, data integrity, Annual Fund and campaign tracking, prospect management, and the flow of constituent information across the school. Working closely with colleagues throughout Beaver, the Manager will help ensure that student, parent, alumni, and donor information is captured regularly and maintained in ways that strengthen both current fundraising efforts and long-term engagement.

The Manager also coordinates Beaver’s donor stewardship and acknowledgment program, developing systems and an annual stewardship calendar to ensure that donors, particularly those supporting named funds, endowed funds, and special giving initiatives, receive timely, accurate, and meaningful recognition and reporting.

Data & Operations Responsibilities

  • Oversee the administration, accuracy, and ongoing maintenance of Raiser’s Edge and other Philanthropy & Engagement information systems.
  • Maintain constituent, gift, prospect, and engagement data with a high degree of accuracy.
  • Manage gift processing and ensure the timely and accurate preparation of gift receipts, acknowledgment letters, and related documentation.
  • Produce regular and custom reporting to support the Annual Fund, major gifts, campaign initiatives, endowment, planned giving, and other fundraising priorities.
  • Manage recurring operational processes including annual database rollover, pledge reminders, appeal and solicitor assignments, Board and volunteer lists, and other annual projects.
  • Conduct regular data audits and proactively identify and resolve errors, inconsistencies, and gaps in constituent information.
  • Partner with the Business Office to support monthly and annual gift reconciliation and financial auditing processes.
  • Maintain clear documentation of data standards, procedures, and key operational processes.
  • Provide training and support to P&E colleagues in the effective use of Raiser’s Edge and other fundraising and reporting systems.
  • Support the smooth day-to-day operations of the P&E office, including shared administrative and organizational needs as they arise.
  • Participate fully in the life of the Beaver community, including selected evening and weekend activities.
  • Support additional Philanthropy & Engagement initiatives and special projects as needed.

Stewardship & Donor Relations Responsibilities

  • Coordinate and manage Beaver's stewardship program, including the annual stewardship calendar and timely reporting to donors.
  • Maintain accurate records of stewardship requirements, donor recognition preferences, fund purposes, and other commitments associated with gifts.
  • Work with P&E colleagues and campus partners to gather information, stories, financial updates, and other materials needed for donor reports and stewardship communications.
  • Help identify opportunities to strengthen and personalize the donor experience through thoughtful use of data, reporting, and engagement information.

Annual Fund, Campaign and Fundraising Support Responsibilities

  • Maintain all database systems and accurate information to support annual fund operations and ensure success.
  • Support the creation and maintenance of prospect and volunteer assignments, ask amounts, campaign attributes, and other information needed to execute fundraising strategies.
  • Partner with fundraising colleagues to ensure that relevant information from donor and prospect interactions is captured consistently and can be used effectively in future outreach and decision making.
  • Assist with prospect research and information gathering as needed to support Annual Fund, major gift, and campaign activity.

Desired Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • Three to five years of experience in advancement operations, development services, fundraising operations, database management, or a related field
  • Experience working with Raiser’s Edge (preferred) or a comparable fundraising database
  • Strong facility with data, reporting, and information systems, with the ability to translate information into useful reports and tools for colleagues
  • Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy and integrity
  • Strong organizational and project management skills, including the ability to manage multiple priorities, anticipate deadlines, and follow projects through to completion
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and improve systems, processes, and workflows
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Sound judgment and discretion in handling confidential donor, financial, and constituent information
  • A collaborative working style and a record of building productive relationships with colleagues across departments and areas of expertise
  • Intellectual curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to learn
  • Experience with diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging practices and commitment to ongoing growth in this area

Salary Range:

The salary range for this position is $80,000 - $95,000. Please visit our Working at Beaver webpage for information about benefits and more.

Beaver Country Day School is an independent day school serving 460 students in grades 6-12, and located in Chestnut Hill, just outside of Boston. Founded in 1920 and propelled by our progressive roots, our goal is to expand the nature of school. With over 40 local and national partnerships, almost daily field trips, a thriving performing and visual arts program, and a best-in-class research and design center, we are able to combine rigorous academics with real-world application, focusing on teaching content combined with experience applying it to current issues. Our athletic program offers first-rate athletic and fitness opportunities that prioritize the whole athlete. The school fosters a joyful environment where students feel confident taking risks and being their authentic selves, where everyone—students and adults alike—feels a sense of belonging, and where teachers have the freedom to innovate and grow alongside their students.

The Middle School Math Support Team Member will work closely with our Middle School Math teachers, who teach integrated math courses combining topics in Geometry, Algebra and Statistics for grades 6-8. job.title: The ISSF Girls Basketball Coach - Grades 4-8
job.description:
Position Description & Application

The International School of San Francisco

Middle School Coach

(2-3 weekday afternoon practices; plus games on weekday afternoons, evenings and/or weekends)

Season starts Nov 16, 2026 (pre season hours available starting Oct 5) through mid February 2027

The International School of San Francisco is seeking positive, passionate and knowledgeable coaches. The International School of San Francisco Athletic Department operates within a K-12 independent school setting, working with over 600 students enrolled in grades 5-8th. In keeping with the Mission of the School, the Jaguar Athletic experience is a journey, which will be a source of growth, pride and enthusiasm for all members of our community. From the novice to the college-bound athlete, student-athletes have the opportunity to participate in competitive team and individual sports, developing healthy practices of mind, body and character for themselves, their teams and their school. Our international community brings together people from many backgrounds. Together we strive to create a shared culture that develops compassionate, confident and principled people who will make the world better. We base our community on these values: Respect, Integrity, Inclusion, Collaboration, and Curiosity.

Job Duties and Expectations

All head coaches and assistant coaches report directly to the Athletic Director and have the primary responsibility for administering all levels of their sport. The successful candidate will be required to follow the procedures of the high school’s athletic program, as well as those of the International and California Interscholastic Federation.

Communication

Coaches will provide clear communication for student-athletes and families regarding expectations and philosophy. In the case where a conflict arises coaches will be available to help seek resolution at the appropriate time which will not take place immediately before or after a contest.

Player Development

Coaches will assist in the total development of all student-athletes by using positive methods to create an ideal learning environment therefore helping them through their life journey, not just their athletic journey. Coaches will create and implement a meaningful practice structure to enhance instruction, development, and effective use of time for all members of the team within the program.

Player Evaluation

Coaches will use a holistic approach when evaluating a student-athlete using qualities such as skill, character, integrity, leadership, coach ability, and a love for the sport. Skill alone will not supersede the Core Principles of the Jaguar family. Coaches will select student-athletes that best represent our School’s Mission without regard to ability or status. Coaches will incorporate a student-driven, mid and post-season review that will be shared with the student-athletes.

Team Leadership

Coaches will foster an environment that will develop positive leadership qualities both on and off the field of play. Coaches will select Team Captains and Student-Athlete Advisory Committee.

(SAAC) members based on character and leadership ability rather than athletic performance or status. Adhere to Chain of Command. Coaches understand that coaching at our School is a privilege and not a right. They will uphold the Mission of the school and conduct themselves accordingly.

Qualifications

  • Experience coaching at the middle school, high school, college or club level.
  • Should have experience working, playing or coaching in a value-based athletic program.
  • Must be reliable, prompt and dependable.
  • Must be able to have transportation.
  • Ability to pass a full background check.
  • Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Applicants should include a letter of interest, current resume, and three references

job.title: The ISSF Maternelle & Lower School Instructional Support Teacher
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Our School

The International School of San Francisco is a bilingual, multicultural learning community where students learn to navigate the complexities of the world with confidence, empathy, and joy. Our vibrant urban campus is situated in the heart of the city and serves nearly 1,100 students beginning at age 2 and continuing through grade 12.

Mission

Guided by the principles of academic rigor and diversity, The International School of San Francisco offers programs of study in French and English to prepare its graduates for a world in which the ability to think critically and to communicate across cultures is of paramount importance.

Opportunity

Working at The International School of San Francisco opens up a myriad of opportunities both personal and professional. When minds and cultures from around the world come together, boundless curiosity takes hold; faculty and staff benefit from that deep intellectual engagement and joyful discovery as we live out our values of respect, integrity, inclusion, collaboration, and curiosity. Each employee is both teacher and learner in our vibrant, multicultural, multilingual school community.

Position Overview

The Maternelle & Lower School Instructional Support Teacher is a full-time faculty member who plays a vital role in ensuring instructional continuity and excellence across the Lower School. Working collaboratively with French and English teaching teams, this educator provides high-quality classroom instruction, supports student learning across grade levels, and contributes to the daily life of our bilingual, multicultural school community.

This position combines classroom teaching, instructional support, and faculty collaboration.

This is a full-time, exempt faculty position reporting to the Lower School Principal.

The teacher is assigned to the Lower School for the full academic year and participates fully in the professional life of the school.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Provide high-quality instruction in French and English classrooms during planned and unplanned teacher absences.
  • Deliver lessons that align with the school's curriculum and maintain continuity of learning.
  • Foster a safe, inclusive, and engaging classroom environment that promotes student growth and well-being.
  • Build positive relationships with students across grade levels and become a trusted member of the Lower School community.
  • Collaborate closely with classroom teachers, specialists, learning support staff, and administrators to ensure a seamless educational experience for students.
  • Provide small-group or individualized instructional support when classroom coverage is not required.
  • Support classroom management and reinforce school-wide expectations for student behavior.
  • Participate actively in faculty meetings, professional learning, school events, and other community activities.
  • Maintain effective communication with colleagues and administrators regarding student progress and classroom needs.
  • Demonstrate flexibility by supporting the evolving instructional needs of the Lower School throughout the school year.

Education/Qualifications

  • A laser focus on each student's academic, social-emotional, and personal growth.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent required; advanced degree preferred.
  • Ability to teach effectively in both French and English is required.
  • Demonstrated success in elementary classroom teaching.
  • Strong classroom management skills and the ability to build positive learning environments.
  • Excellent interpersonal, organizational, and communication skills.
  • Collaborative, flexible, and proactive approach to teaching and problem-solving.
  • Commitment to working in a multilingual, multicultural, and inclusive school community.
  • Authorization to work in the United States or eligibility to obtain appropriate work authorization or visa sponsorship.

This is a Full Time, Exempt position. The salary range is $65,153-$110,975 based on experience and qualification.

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY POLICY

job.title: Holy Trinity Facilities Support
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Salary Range:

$20.00 To $23.00 Hourly

Reports to: Director of Facilities

Status: Full time, Exempt

Salary Range: $20.00 - $23.00 per hour

About Holy Trinity

Holy Trinity: An Episcopal School is a Pre-School through 8th Grade school grounded in Episcopal values, academic excellence, and a strong sense of purpose. Located on two campuses in Prince George’s County, one in Bowie and one in Glenn Dale, the school offers a comprehensive education within a nurturing, safe, and welcoming community. Students benefit from a challenging academic environment supported by the resources needed to excel academically, artistically, athletically, and spiritually. Holy Trinity encourages students to pursue excellence and embrace responsibility.

Holy Trinity seeks dedicated educators who support our mission and are passionate about being part of a transformative educational experience, one that cultivates each student’s God-given talents and helps shape them into their best selves.

Position Summary:

Holy Trinity School is seeking a dependable and service-oriented Facilities Support team member to assist in maintaining a safe, clean, and welcoming campus environment for students, faculty, staff, and visitors. This position supports the Facilities Director in the day-to-day upkeep, repair, and operation of school buildings, grounds, and equipment. Responsibilities:

  • Assist with routine maintenance and repair of school buildings, classrooms, offices, and common areas.

job.title: Maret School Facilities Operations Technician
job.description:

Maret School is seeking a dependable, hands-on facilities operations technician to join our facilities team. We are looking for someone who takes pride in their work, pays attention to detail, and enjoys supporting a busy school community. The ideal candidate is proactive, reliable, team-oriented, and willing to assist with a wide variety of campus operations needs while helping maintain a safe, clean, and welcoming environment for students, faculty, and visitors.

Responsibilities

job.title: Mary McDowell Friends School School Nurse
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Description

McDowell Friends School (MMFS) invites applications for a full-time School Nurse beginning immediately.

Job Title: School Nurse

Reports to: Senior School Nurse

Position Overview

The School Nurse will support the mission of the school by ensuring the health and wellness of the school community. Provide daily and ongoing health care to the school community and communicate necessary information in a timely manner. Oversee and maintain accurate and up-to-date health records for the school community. Work collaboratively with the health staff.

Essential Responsibilities and Duties

  • Promotes and protects the optimal health status of school-age children.
  • Provides health assessments.
  • Obtains an annual health history and updates as necessary.
  • Observes the child for development and health patterns in making a nursing assessment.
  • Identifies abnormal health findings.
  • Develops and implements student health plans.
  • Interprets the health status of students to parents and school personnel.
  • Initiates referral to parents, school personnel, or community health resources for intervention, remediation, and follow-through.
  • Provides ongoing health counseling for students, parents, and school personnel.
  • Utilizes existing health resources to provide appropriate care of students.
  • Maintains, evaluates, and interprets cumulative health data to accommodate the individual needs of students.
  • Plans and implements school health management protocols.
  • Develops procedures and provides for emergency nursing management for injuries/illnesses.
  • Promotes and assists in the control of communicable diseases.
  • Provides health education and anticipatory guidance.
  • Provides direct health education as needed, and health counseling to assist students and families in making decisions on health and lifestyles that affect health.
  • Participates in health education directly and indirectly for the improvement of health by teaching persons to become more assertive health consumers and to assume greater responsibility for their own health.
  • Serves as a resource person to the school staff members in health instruction.
  • Coordinates school and community health activities and serves as a liaison health professional between the home, school, and community.
  • Acts as a resource person in promoting health careers.
  • Engages in research and evaluation of school health services to act as a change agent for school health programs and school nursing practices.
  • Manages and administers medication (including controlled substances) as prescribed by physician or designee.
  • Monitors parameters and reports to parents, physicians, and teachers as necessary.
  • Accompanies students and faculty on day trips.
  • Ensures first aid bags are prepared with appropriate supplies, emergency medications and medications needed for trips.
  • Completes accident reports for employees injured onsite timely.
  • Order supplies for the nursing office as needed.

Communications

  • Meets and communicates regularly with Senior School RN.
  • Updates administration regarding emerging health issues for emergencies.

Competencies

  • Communication Proficiency.
  • Ethical decision-making to manage and evaluate patient care.
  • Confidentiality (HIPAA/FERPA).

Diversity and Equity Commitments

  • Understand and participate in all school-wide diversity and equity initiatives.
  • Examine administrative practice through the lens of race, identity, equity, and privilege.
  • Provide an equitable framework for leadership decisions.
  • Support a school culture that allows for social identities to feel welcome.

Supervisory Responsibility

This position has no supervisory responsibilities.

Position Type/Expected Hours of Work

This is a full-time 40-hour, exempt 10-month position that follows the academic calendar. Evening and weekend work may be required as job duties demand and will be scheduled in advance. Attendance is required on professional development and parent-teacher conference days.

Travel

On occasion, travel between campuses is necessary for meetings, which are scheduled with advance notice and are within walking distance from each other.

As a part of your job requirement, all nursing staff are required to go on at least one overnight trip every school year. Your supervisor will provide you with the schedule of trips for the year and determine which trip(s) you will participate in. While we will try to facilitate the trip that best fits your schedule, there are no guarantees that your preference will be honored.

Work Environment & Physical Demands

This job requires the ability to maintain the physical capacity required to navigate the school environment and to ensure the safety of the students. Moderate physical activity. Requires handling of average-weight objects up to 25 pounds or standing and/or walking for more than four (4) hours per day. Classroom locations vary based on student schedules and work location; this position occasionally ascends/descends stairs to reach rooms in the building (one to five flights). This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, and filing cabinets. Work environment involves exposure to potentially dangerous materials and situations that require following extensive safety precautions and may include the use of protective equipment.

Regularly exposed to the risk of bloodborne diseases; Contact with patients under a wide variety of circumstances. Exposed to unpleasant elements (accidents, injuries, illnesses), subject to varying and unpredictable situations. Handles emergency or crisis situations, may perform emergency care. Possess the ability to work accurately and in an organized fashion in a high-paced and often stressful environment.

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Other Duties

Please note that this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of the activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time, with or without notice.

Requirements

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Registered Nurse in New York State.
  • 2+ years of direct experience in a pediatric or urgent care setting.
  • Familiarity with professional and technical emerging knowledge.
  • Problem-solving skills and ability to multitask.
  • Compassionate with good communication skills.
  • Ability to work cooperatively and collaboratively with school-age children (K-12) and external agencies.
  • Willingness to learn and adapt to a new environment.

Preferred Education & Experience

  • Experience in the private education sector.
  • Independent school system a plus.

Application

To apply, please upload a letter of interest, resume, and contact information for three professional references as a .pdf (preferable) or Word document. If your background and experience are appropriate for the position, you will be contacted directly by a member of our search committee.

We offer a rewarding work experience in downtown Brooklyn, NY, where we encourage employees to bring their whole selves to work. We recognize, appreciate, celebrate, and honor our diverse community as we build an awareness of who each individual is and who we are collectively.

Applicants who enhance the diversity of the school's faculty and administration are strongly encouraged to apply. Please visit our website for more information on our school and a full list of vacancies.

In compliance with NYC’s Pay Transparency Act, this position's annual base salary range is $75,000 - $90,000. Mary McDowell Friends School considers factors such as (but not limited to) the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate’s work experience, education/training, essential skills, internal peer equity, and market and organizational considerations when extending an offer.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Employment at Mary McDowell Friends School is based solely on qualifications and competence for a particular position, without regard to race, color, ethnic origin, nationality, age, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, disability, familial status, or any other category protected by the law. Mary McDowell Friends School’s policy of non-discrimination extends to all employment practices, including but not limited to hiring, transfer, promotion, training, compensation, benefits, layoffs, and termination.

Position Summary:

Holy Trinity Episcopal School is seeking a highly organized, service-oriented, and technically capable SIS & Database Manager / Technology Support Specialist to manage the day-to-day operations of the school's Blackbaud Student Information System (SIS) while also providing hands-on technology support to faculty, staff, students, and families.

This position combines two critical areas of school technology: student information system and database administration and front-line technology support. The position serves as a primary point of contact for Blackbaud SIS questions and support while assisting with classroom technology, student and faculty devices, user accounts, software, printers, connectivity, and the school's 1:1 device program.

  • Experience administering a Student Information System; Blackbaud experience strongly preferred.
  • Experience in school, nonprofit, or similar tech support settings preferred.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills across Windows, laptops/tablets, printers, and Microsoft 365.
  • Strong Excel/data-management skills and comfort with databases and reporting.
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to explain technical issues to non-technical users.
  • Strong organization, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Ability to travel between campuses and lift/set up classroom technology equipment.

Disclosure(s):

job.title: Episcopal High School Long-Term Substitute English Teacher
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Position Description

Episcopal High School seeks an energetic, student-centered educator to join our English Department for two consecutive parental leaves. We welcome candidates interested in fulfilling the combined duration as well as those available for single-term assignments. The ideal candidate brings a passion for literature and composition, inclusive pedagogical practices, and an eagerness to engage with a dynamic boarding school community.

  • First Leave Period (November 2 – December 18, 2026): 4 sections total — 2 sections of 9th-Grade Fundamentals in Literature and Composition and 2 sections of 11th/12th-Grade Electives.

Compensation

  • $660 - $880 per week.

job.title: Maret School After School Counselor 2026-2027
job.description:
Position Description

Maret School is seeking passionate and positive role models with a strong work ethic who actively embrace lifelong learning to serve as After School Counselors.

About After School

Maret’s After School program offers a welcoming environment where children from kindergarten through eighth grade can relax and unwind. The program is a safe, comfortable, low-key option for families who are unable to pick up their children at the regular dismissal time. After School offers supervised free time along with structured activities such as playground games, arts and crafts, storytime, and board games.

Students in grades 3–8 also participate in an hour-long study hall. During this time, After School counselors provide homework assistance, helping students complete assignments, daily reading, and projects. After School also offers childcare for evening events and day-long programming that runs during non-federal holiday school closures as a service to families.

Duties include:

  • Help maintain a safe, healthy, and nurturing environment for all children.
  • Oversee students during outdoor playtime, enrichment activities, and study hall sessions in indoor and outdoor spaces for the duration of After School hours.
  • Collaborate professionally with Maret faculty and other After School Counselors to promote the general well-being of Maret students.
  • Engage with students through art activities, games, and other enrichment exercises.
  • Model self-confidence and a positive self-image to provide an environment of acceptance and support for each student.
  • Attend daily meetings before the start of After School.
  • Assist the After School Director in the accurate and timely reporting of student attendance, inventory, and incidents.
  • Provide childcare for evening events and Gap Camp on school holidays.

The ideal candidate will possess the following qualities:

  • Experience working with children or a genuine interest in learning how to work in an after-school setting.
  • Ability to work with children in a physically active environment
  • Flexibility to work with children from kindergarten through 8th grade.
  • Ability to interact with parents, children, and co-workers in a warm, empathetic, and confident manner.
  • Ability to work consistently Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday from 2:15 p.m. – 6:00 p.m., and Wednesdays from 1:00 p.m. – 6:00 p.m. Counselors are expected to work for the entire week, but there is flexibility for those who can only commit to certain days. Candidates must be available to work on Wednesdays from 1:00 p.m. – 6:00 p.m.
  • Certifications (or the ability to obtain certifications) in CPR and First Aid, pass a pre-employment background check, and attend required training on youth development.

Maret’s dynamic community and campus in the midst of Washington, DC, create a unique learning environment for students from kindergarten through twelfth grade. job.title: Fay School Early Learning Center Full-Time Support Teacher
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Description:

The Early Learning Center at Fay School (ELC) seeks a dynamic and flexible early childhood educator to function as a substitute and support for classroom instructional staff daily across our five classrooms. The ELC is a high-quality program that educates children ages 2 years nine months through 5 years with developmentally appropriate lessons and activities. The support teacher will work closely with Lead Teachers, Assistant Teachers, Teachers Aides, and the Associate Director of the Early Learning Center to provide and maintain a nurturing, consistent environment that meets the children’s cognitive, emotional, social, and physical needs. The ELC Support Teacher position is Monday - Friday, 8:30 am - 4:30 PM with some flexibility required, depending on the coverage needs. This is a 10 month, school-year position and is eligible for benefits.

Qualifications:

Candidates should have completed coursework from an accredited higher education program in child development, psychology and/or early childhood education. A minimum of one year of classroom experience in an early childhood setting is required. Candidates should have strong verbal and written communication skills and enjoy working in a shared and cooperative environment.

Responsibilities include:

  • Support the mission, philosophy, and core values of the ELC
  • Assist in the implementation of educational activities and experiences under the guidance of the Lead or Assistant Teacher and Teachers Aide
  • Maintain strong partnerships with families
  • Prepare and maintain a classroom environment that supports inquiry and discovery
  • Ensure a safe and secure classroom environment
  • Actively support and promote a school culture of equity, inclusion, and belonging.

Fay seeks candidates who will reflect and enhance the racial, cultural, and gender diversity of our school community. This is an hourly position with an hourly rate of $21.30. Interested candidates should send a cover letter, resume, and list of three references via our secure employment application portal.

job.title: Episcopal High School Head Varsity Baseball Coach
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Salary Range

$7,500.00 Salary

Position Type

Seasonal

Education Level

Not Specified

Description

Episcopal High School is seeking a head varsity baseball coach starting in the 2026-27 school year. This is a part-time, stipend opportunity. The successful candidate is an educator who is deeply committed to the role that baseball can play in helping a large group of boys who hail from a wide variety of backgrounds learn and grow, not just as exceptional student-athletes but as young men of character and leaders.

As a member of the competitive Interstate Athletics Conference (IAC) in the Greater Washington, DC area, Episcopal has a rich academic and athletic tradition and is deeply committed to fostering a successful athletic program as a crucial, co-curricular classroom in which students pursue excellence and develop as healthy, determined, collaborative, and ethical leaders for the future. For more information about EHS, please visit the school’s website.

Specific responsibilities and characteristics will be to:

  • Demonstrate and share expert knowledge of baseball from a tactical, learning, organizational, and best practices perspective, resulting in sustained competitive excellence.
  • Attract and manage a talented group of assistant coaches and foster a collaborative and developmentally appropriate approach for the JV program with the JV coaches.
  • Value strength & conditioning, nutrition, and participation in multiple sports in helping student-athletes to realize their full potential as athletes.
  • Offer year-round, positive leadership for the baseball program (9th-12th). The coach will help baseball grow physically, socially, emotionally, and spiritually.
  • Work in partnership with the admissions office, both to communicate to prospective students and families the values and ideals of the entire Episcopal community and to attract students who aspire to excel in both the classroom and on the baseball field at Episcopal High School.
  • Support players’ transitions to college, inclusive of establishing relationships with college and university programs in support of the recruiting process.
  • Value a meritocracy and build a belief among boys that achievement comes through hard work and teamwork.
  • Encourage a sense of belonging for all boys who are a part of the program through relationship-building with and among the boys that is based on the development of their character as well as their athletic ability.
  • Understand the academic responsibilities of the boys, follow their progress as students, and support their full participation as positive members and leaders in a demanding, boarding high school community.
  • Build relationships with member schools in our league and work collaboratively to make the league stronger.
  • Understand the VISAA and IAC policies and rules and support the implementation of those policies and rules.
  • Pursue ongoing professional development and supervise assistant coaches in support of their professional development.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • Cultural competency for working within a diverse school community
  • Strong organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills

job.title: Harvard-Westlake School Assistant FRC Robotics Coach
job.description:
Position Description & Application

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

We’re looking for assistant coaches/mentors to support our FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC) program. Candidates would work alongside the Head Coach and other mentors to guide high school students through engineering, design, fabrication, programming, testing, and competition activities.

Harvard-Westlake is one of the nation's leading independent schools — and what makes it exceptional isn't just the students or the resources; it's the people. You'll join a community of smart, mission-driven colleagues who are genuinely invested in each other's growth and in building something meaningful together.

WHAT YOU BRING

We know that strong candidates come from a variety of backgrounds and pathways. If you meet most of the qualifications below and are excited about this role, we encourage you to apply.

Preferred Experience

  • Mechanical design/CAD and fabrication
  • Electrical systems
  • Programming/software/controls
  • FRC or other competitive robotics experience
  • Engineering or other relevant technical experience
  • Mentoring, coaching, or working with high school students

SCHEDULE

Availability for some weekday afternoon/evening practices and Saturdays is preferred, with additional availability during the January-April build and competition season. Exact schedules and responsibilities can be coordinated based on experience and availability. This is a part-time position scheduled to work less than 20 hours per week.

COMPENSATION

This is a non-exempt position with a base compensation of $18.50 - $24.00 per hour, based on experience and qualifications.

ABOUT HARVARD-WESTLAKE

Harvard-Westlake is an independent school with two campuses in Los Angeles and approximately 1,600 students enrolled in grades 7–12. Classes for grades 7–9 take place on the Middle School campus in the Holmby Hills neighborhood, while grades 10–12 are housed on the Upper School campus in Studio City. A third campus, River Park, focused on athletics and recreation, is scheduled to open in Fall 2026.

We are dedicated to fostering a community of belonging and to advancing diversity and inclusion across all aspects of school life. We seek educators and staff who demonstrate a commitment to inclusive practice and to fostering a community of belonging; who can work flexibly, independently, and collaboratively in a dynamic environment with individuals from a wide range of backgrounds; and who exemplify professionalism, openness, and generosity in their interactions with students and colleagues.

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY & ACCOMMODATIONS

Harvard-Westlake School is an equal opportunity employer. We seek to recruit, develop, and retain a diverse workforce and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, or any other legally protected status. Harvard-Westlake is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the application and hiring process. If you require an accommodation to participate, please contact hr@hw.com, and we will work with you to meet your needs.

job.title: St. Mark's School Administrative Assistant & Office Manager Support
job.description:
Position Description

St. Mark’s School seeks a dynamic, highly organized, and collaborative Administrative Assistant & Office Manager to support the Assistant Head of School for Enrollment and oversee the daily operational, administrative, and hospitality functions of the Admission & Enrollment Office.

The ideal candidate will combine high-level administrative foresight with exceptional hospitality, ensuring smooth daily calendar and workflow execution for executive leadership while creating a welcoming, professional, and seamless environment for visiting prospective families, student tour guides, and campus partners. Additionally, this position will oversee and manage details of events, travel, presentations, etc.

Key Responsibilities

Support to the Assistant Head of School for Enrollment

  • Calendar & Priority Management: Proactively manage and optimize the Assistant Head’s calendar and meeting preparation.
  • Communication & Briefing: Draft, proofread, and prepare reports, presentations, and meeting agendas for internal and external audiences.
  • Travel & Expense Coordination: Handle domestic and international travel arrangements, itinerary details, and expense report processing for enrollment leadership and travel team members.

Office Management & Enrollment Operations

  • Hospitality: Assist/oversee the day-to-day presentation and climate of the Admissions office, ensuring a warm, inclusive, and professional atmosphere for prospective students, families, consultants, and campus visitors.
  • Daily Office Operations: Manage office inventory, supply ordering, budget tracking/invoicing processing, etc. (printing/collateral stock, coffee/refreshments).
  • Admissions Workflow Support: Serve as a key operational contact within the admissions database, assisting with visitor check-ins, record maintenance, and processing prospective family inquiries and emails.
  • Event Coordination: In collaboration with the Admissions team, coordinate logistics for key enrollment events, including Open Houses, Revisit Days, campus tours, off-campus receptions, etc.
  • Student Ambassador & Tour Guide Assistance: Assist in scheduling, tracking, and coordinating student tour guides and parent volunteers for campus visits and special events.

Qualifications & Competencies

  • Experience: Administrative support or office management experience, preferably in an independent school, higher education, or customer-centric non-profit environment.
  • Technical Skills: High proficiency with Google Workspace and Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint). Experience with enrollment/admissions CRM databases and travel/expense software is strongly preferred.
  • Interpersonal & Communication Skills: Outstanding written, verbal, and listening skills. Ability to interact with diverse populations—including prospective families, alumni, trustees, faculty, and students—with warmth, discretion, and diplomatic tact.
  • Organizational Mastery: Exceptional attention to detail, time management, and the ability to multitask in a fast-paced, high-volume seasonal environment.
  • Discretion: Absolute integrity and commitment to maintaining strict confidentiality regarding sensitive student, financial aid, and personnel records.

About St. Mark’s School

St. Mark's School is a coed boarding high school with approximately 375 students located 22 miles west of Boston and 12 miles east of Worcester. Founded in 1865 as an intentionally small residential community, St. Mark’s prepares students for lives of purpose, courage, and integrity. We cultivate sound judgment through intellectual and spiritual curiosity within a global community that knows and values each student.

St. Mark's School provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, age, sex, sexual orientation, disability or genetics, and any other characteristic or status protected by law.

job.title: Santa Catalina School Upper School Counselor
job.description:
School Description

Santa Catalina School is a vibrant, independent, Catholic school offering student-centered co-education to PreK through grade 8 and an all-girls’ boarding and day college preparatory upper school serving grades 9 through 12. Santa Catalina exists to develop in each student a striving for excellence, a maturing awareness of moral and spiritual values, a sense of responsible purpose, and a determination to serve the world with courage, grace, and compassion. With the cornerstones of excellence, spirituality, service, and responsibility, the school is committed to providing a supportive learning community for each student to grow in their intellectual, personal, and spiritual life, making Santa Catalina a transformational educational experience for its students.

Position Summary

Santa Catalina School, a nationally recognized, independent, Catholic school in Monterey, California, seeks a team of colleagues who are able and ready to respond to school needs as they arise. The Upper School Counselor is responsible for the effective organization and coordination of the school’s counseling services. Reporting directly to the Head of Upper School, and working closely with the Dean of Students and the Director of Resident Life, the Upper School Counselor provides individual and group counseling, assists and communicates appropriately with advisors and parents, serves on appropriate school committees, and is an active presence on campus.

Description

The school counselor is responsible for supporting the social, emotional, and personal well-being of Upper School students. The Counselor will serve as an integral member of the Student Support Team, collaborating with teachers, advisors, administrators, and families to promote student health, wellness, and success.

Santa Catalina School believes that each employee makes a significant contribution to its success. That contribution should not be limited by the assigned responsibilities. Therefore, this position description is designed to outline primary duties, qualifications, and job scope, but not limit the incumbent nor the organization to just the work identified. It is our expectation that each employee will offer his/her services wherever and whenever necessary to ensure the success of our endeavors.

Essential Responsibilities

● Assist students with issues of educational, emotional, personal, and social development and adjustment

● Work as a member of a cohesive team in support of positive student growth

● Counsel students on a drop-in and/or scheduled basis

● Assess the counseling needs of individual students

● Coordinate, in collaboration with Upper School Administration, any necessary counseling with off-campus health providers

● Support and communicate with advisors as appropriate

● Work in concert with the Director of Health and Wellness in preparing residential, class-based, and/or faculty presentations

Other Responsibilities

● Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

● Two years experience as a school counselor with background in adolescent development

● Master’s degree in school counseling

● California State School Counseling Certification or the equivalent

● A commitment to the mission and identity of Santa Catalina School

● A desire to participate fully in the Santa Catalina community

● Successful completion of a LiveScan criminal background check as required by law

● Demonstrated commitment to the American School Counselor Association Ethical Standards for School Counselors

Competencies

● Demonstrated evaluative and facilitative skills

● Excellent verbal and written skills

● Approachable and welcoming demeanor

● Cultural competence and enthusiasm for working with a diverse and dynamic community

● Strong interpersonal skills, including good listening, humor, tact, intuition, and confidentiality

● Excellent writing, communication, and public speaking skills

● Ability to create responsive, caring, and appropriate relationships with students, families, and colleagues

● Strong organizational and record-keeping skills and digital literacy

● Understanding of the dynamics of a school community

● Ability to assess and respond to the needs of the school and act as a representative of the school

● Commitment to professional growth and education

● Ability to function well under stress

Supervisory Responsibilities

● This position does not supervise other employees

Working Conditions and Compensation

● Be able to sit and meet with students for extended periods of time each day

● Work at a desk and computer screen for extended periods of time each day

● Ability to access buildings and facilities throughout a 36-acre campus, with reasonable accommodations, in order to meet with students and faculty

● Additional time is required beyond a normal day or week for evening and weekend meetings to attend school events and represent the school in the community

● Work in a school environment with a wide variety of challenges, deadlines, and people

● Salary Range: $75,000–$100,000 depending on experience

Equal Employment Opportunity Santa Catalina School is an equal-opportunity employer. Employment at Santa Catalina School is based solely on qualifications and competence for a particular position, without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions and reproductive health decision-making), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, national origin, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic characteristics, citizenship, military or veteran status, off-duty and off-premises use of cannabis, age, victims of a qualifying act of violence or other categories defined by state law, federal law or local ordinance.

To Apply

Interested candidates should visit our website to complete and submit an application, resume, and cover letter: santacatalina.org/employment. Electronic submission of candidate papers in .pdf format is preferred.

Santa Catalina provides reasonable accommodations to employees and applicants with disabilities. Applicants who need accommodations to participate in the application process should contact employment@santacatalina.org.
