job.title: The Lawrenceville School English Teaching Fellow/University of Pennsylvania
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Job Type

Full-time

Description

The Lawrenceville School, an independent boarding and day school located in central New Jersey, seeks dynamic individuals to join our community as a member of the Independent School Teaching Residency (ISTR) program, a two-year teaching fellowship offered in conjunction with the University of Pennsylvania Graduate School of Education (PennGSE), beginning in June 2027.

We are now accepting applications for our two-year teaching fellowship program for 2027-2028 in English.

ISTR Fellows join their departments at Lawrenceville as fully engaged members of the faculty, teaching their own classes from the start. Fellows will fulfill co-curricular responsibilities (in athletics, performing arts, or publications) and residential duties, including being a member of a House team, chaperoning student events, and advising a group of students in year two.

Fellows are paired with a mentor teacher in their discipline who offers support and coaching through regular classroom observations and ongoing conversations about life at Lawrenceville. Regular meetings with the cohort of eight fellows provide collegiality and a strong peer group of early career educators.

Teaching fellows are an integral part of a vibrant campus life. Our community lives, works, and eats together, all in enticing proximity to the variety of attractions in Philadelphia and New York.

Teaching fellows are required to live in school housing (basic utilities included). They are provided three meals per day in the school dining center and have access to athletic facilities.

If hired by Lawrenceville, fellows join their cohort at PennGSE, where they complete a rigorous two year course of study led by PennGSE professors and academic leaders from other boarding schools in pursuit of a Masters of Education from PennGSE. Throughout the year, fellows participate in regular distance learning sessions and gather in person four times–in June, October, January and April–on the UPenn campus in Philadelphia and at various host school locations around New England.

Upon completion of the two year fellowship, recent graduates have found desirable teaching and coaching opportunities at both boarding and day schools across the country (including Lawrenceville), as well as have gone on to pursue additional advanced degrees or consultant work.

The ideal candidate values hard work, learning and growth as an early career educator, and wants to collaborate to build community, connection and belonging for the students and faculty at Lawrenceville.

Essential Responsibilities

Teaching (two different preparations/courses)

  • In year one, two sections in Fall term and three sections in the Winter and Spring
  • In year two, four sections in Fall term and in either Winter or Spring, three in the other

Residential

  • Supervise a student dormitory as a member of a duty team one night a week from 6:00 - 11:30 pm.
  • Participate in Saturday programming as scheduled by the School.
  • Provide weekend chaperone coverage up to twice per term.
  • In addition, in year two, serve as an academic advisor to a group of six to eight students.
  • Live on campus with a cohort of other fellows and participate in the residential life of the School

Co-Curricular

  • Coach at least one season of interscholastic athletics
  • Lead/Co-lead one additional term of co-curricular activity (athletic, performing arts, community service, student publications, experiential learning)

Other duties as assigned

Requirements

  • A Bachelor's degree in a relevant field
  • Relevant experience working with young people
  • Relevant experience in an area of co-curricular school life
  • Comfort working in a fast-paced, demanding academic environment
  • The desire to engage in the life of a boarding school community
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Strong time management and organizational skills
  • A growth mindset

When completing the application, please submit the following to Lawrenceville’s employment portal. We will not review incomplete applications.

  • Resume
  • Cover letter
  • College transcript (can be unofficial)

Three letters of recommendation (two must be academic references, and one should be a work-related reference). Letters of recommendation can be submitted via email to professionalreferences@lawrenceville.org

References should be received by November 5th and be sent to professionalreferences@lawrenceville.org. Please instruct the person providing the reference to put the applicant's name and position they are applying for (eg: History Teaching Fellow) in the subject line of the email.

Applications are due October 31st, 2026

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. without sponsorship. We do not provide visa sponsorship for this role.

For finalists, on campus interviews will be held between November 10th and November 17th. The Lawrenceville School will arrange transportation to and from campus as well as lodging during the interview. Interviews take place over the course of an afternoon/evening and the following day.

Work Characteristics and Physical Demands: The work environment characteristics and physical demands described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Physical demands are in excess of those for sedentary work. Must be able to remain on their feet for extended periods of time, go up and down flights of steps, as well as stoop, kneel, crouch, and lift.
  • Routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, fax machines, etc.
  • Must be capable of using visual display terminal with continuous wrist movement on a keyboard
  • Required to stand for long periods of time
  • Required to talk, hear, walk, use hands to finger, handle or feel and reach with hands and arms
  • Must be able to lift up to 25lbs. without assistance
  • Ability to see with normal parameters.
  • Operates in a professional work environment
  • Will work outside of normal working hours

Additional information

  • Working at Lawrenceville
  • Overview of ISTR at Lawrenceville
  • Class Schedule

The Lawrenceville School is a diverse and inclusive community and makes all employment decisions without regard for an individual’s race, creed, color, religion, national origin, nationality, sex, pregnancy, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, veteran status, physical or mental disability (including AIDS and HIV related illness), genetic information, refusal to provide genetic information, refusal to submit to genetic testing, ancestry, familial status, marital status, domestic partnership status, civil union status, atypical cellular or blood trait, military service, application for military service, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. The Lawrenceville School will also provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals in accordance with applicable law.

The Lawrenceville School conducts pre-employment screening for all positions which includes a criminal background check, verification of work history, academic credentials, licenses, and certifications. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of the background check.

Eligible employees receive a competitive benefits package that includes health insurance coverage, paid leave and retirement plan options, and many other valuable programs.

Salary

The annual salary range for this residential position is $25,000.00 - $27,000.00, plus a $5,000.00 stipend. Additionally, The Lawrenceville School pays approximately 80% of fellows' graduate school tuition.

job.title: Lowell School Aquatics Instructor
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Aquatics Instructor

Are you passionate about working with kids and helping them reach their goals? Do you thrive in a fun and engaging environment where you can continue to grow and build community? Are you passionate about education, cultivating a positive team culture, and encouraging a healthy lifestyle? You might be looking for us if you answered yes to these questions!

We Offer:

  • Water Safety Instructor training (WSI)
  • Lifeguarding, CPR, AED, and First Aid training/certification
  • Certified Pool Operator training/certification

Shifts Require Day, Evening, and/or Weekend Availability:

  • Monday–Friday from 9 am–3 pm
  • Monday–Friday from 3:30 pm–7 pm
  • Saturday from 8:30 am–4 pm

Qualifications:

job.title: The Lawrenceville School History Teaching Fellow/University of Pennsylvania
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Job Type

Full-time

Description

The Lawrenceville School, an independent boarding and day school located in central New Jersey, seeks dynamic individuals to join our community as a member of the Independent School Teaching Residency (ISTR) program, a two-year teaching fellowship offered in conjunction with the University of Pennsylvania Graduate School of Education (PennGSE), beginning in June 2027.

We are now accepting applications for our two-year teaching fellowship program for 2027-2028 in History (a background in World or US history is required).

ISTR Fellows join their departments at Lawrenceville as fully engaged members of the faculty, teaching their own classes from the start. Fellows will fulfill co-curricular responsibilities (in athletics, performing arts, or publications) and residential duties, including being a member of a House team, chaperoning student events, and advising a group of students in year two.

Fellows are paired with a mentor teacher in their discipline who offers support and coaching through regular classroom observations and ongoing conversations about life at Lawrenceville. Regular meetings with the cohort of eight fellows provide collegiality and a strong peer group of early career educators.

Teaching fellows are an integral part of a vibrant campus life. Our community lives, works, and eats together, all in enticing proximity to the variety of attractions in Philadelphia and New York.

Teaching fellows are required to live in school housing (basic utilities included). They are provided three meals per day in the school dining center and have access to athletic facilities.

If hired by Lawrenceville, fellows join their cohort at PennGSE, where they complete a rigorous two year course of study led by PennGSE professors and academic leaders from other boarding schools in pursuit of a Masters of Education from PennGSE. Throughout the year, fellows participate in regular distance learning sessions and gather in person four times–in June, October, January and April–on the UPenn campus in Philadelphia and at various host school locations around New England.

Upon completion of the two year fellowship, recent graduates have found desirable teaching and coaching opportunities at both boarding and day schools across the country (including Lawrenceville), as well as have gone on to pursue additional advanced degrees or consultant work.

The ideal candidate values hard work, learning and growth as an early career educator, and wants to collaborate to build community, connection and belonging for the students and faculty at Lawrenceville.

Essential Responsibilities

Teaching (two different preparations/courses)

  • In year one, two sections in Fall term and three sections in the Winter and Spring
  • In year two, four sections in Fall term and in either Winter or Spring, three in the other

Residential

  • Supervise a student dormitory as a member of a duty team one night a week from 6:00 - 11:30 pm.
  • Participate in Saturday programming as scheduled by the School.
  • Provide weekend chaperone coverage up to twice per term.
  • In addition, in year two, serve as an academic advisor to a group of six to eight students.
  • Live on campus with a cohort of other fellows and participate in the residential life of the School

Co-Curricular

  • Coach at least one season of interscholastic athletics
  • Lead/Co-lead one additional term of co-curricular activity (athletic, performing arts, community service, student publications, experiential learning)

Other duties as assigned

Requirements

  • A Bachelor's degree in a relevant field
  • Relevant experience working with young people
  • Relevant experience in an area of co-curricular school life
  • Comfort working in a fast-paced, demanding academic environment
  • The desire to engage in the life of a boarding school community
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Strong time management and organizational skills
  • A growth mindset

When completing the application, please submit the following to Lawrenceville’s employment portal. We will not review incomplete applications.

  • Resume
  • Cover letter
  • College transcript (can be unofficial)
  • Three letters of recommendation (two must be academic references, and one should be a work-related reference). Letters of recommendation can be submitted via email to professionalreferences@lawrenceville.org

References should be received by November 5th and be sent to professionalreferences@lawrenceville.org. Please instruct the person providing the reference to put the applicant's name and position they are applying for (eg: History Teaching Fellow) in the subject line of the email.

Applications are due October 31st, 2026

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. without sponsorship. We do not provide visa sponsorship for this role.

For finalists, on campus interviews will be held between November 10th and November 17th. The Lawrenceville School will arrange transportation to and from campus as well as lodging during the interview. Interviews take place over the course of an afternoon/evening and the following day.

job.title: The Lawrenceville School Digital Literacy Librarian
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Summary:

Recognizing the increasingly critical role that AI, technology, e-resources, and digital collections play in the future of academic scholarship, the Digital Literacy Librarian will design, implement, and lead a comprehensive information, digital, and media literacy curriculum. Working collaboratively with faculty and campus partners, the position will integrate digital citizenship values and information literacy skills across the academic disciplines. This role will lead the design of instruction and outreach to students and faculty, which will inspire and lead the community in exploring the potential of AI in education, while actively guiding faculty and students in navigating its ethical, safe, and responsible use (See our AI Vision Statement: https://www.lawrenceville.org/about-us/ai-at-lawrenceville. Key responsibilities include co-designing lesson plans and assignments with faculty, teaching general and discipline-specific classes, conducting faculty outreach, developing program assessments, and providing campus-wide leadership for the Digital Literacy program.

This position will have service desk and student supervision duties, including one evening per week until 9:50 p.m. and some weekend shifts. As part of the librarian team, this position will also contribute to the strategic planning for library programs, collections, and space. The ideal candidate will have some experience with digital projects and/or experience with digital content management systems.

This is a 10-month position, and it follows the academic calendar.

To ensure full consideration, please submit a cover letter in addition to your resume.

Essential Responsibilities:

  • Develop, coordinate, and implement the library’s information and media literacy instruction program, which includes group, individual, and online components, such as LibGuides. Design and conduct the library instruction and orientation sessions for classes. Instruct individual library users on the use of print and electronic resources.
  • Partner with administrators, departmental faculty, and course team leaders to ensure that digital literacy skills (media literacy, AI, digital citizenship) are embedded systematically throughout the school. More broadly, establish collaborative and supportive partnerships with faculty, students, and staff in support of faculty and student engagement with the academic services and resources of the library.
  • In accordance with our AI Vision Statement, lead and collaborate with campus technology leaders, Dean of Academics, Dean of Faculty, Director of Student AI Projects, ITS, faculty, and others, on promoting the ethical use of AI, digital citizenship and the application of library resources and technology in the classroom. Stay current with emerging technologies and act as the library liaison to various student and faculty initiatives in the areas of AI and technology.
  • Support the ethical and effective use of media, technology, and AI tools across the research lifecycle, including discovery, analysis, writing, data visualization, and digital creation. Provide guidance on responsible use, including transparency, attribution, bias, copyright, and academic integrity.
  • Work with the Stephan Archives staff to leverage and highlight the growing archival digital collections.
  • Work closely with the Community Engagement Librarian and team to market and brand library resources, services, and programs, specifically to increase awareness of electronic resources and digital collections.
  • Assist faculty in developing information resources for coursework using LibGuides, Google Education, and Canvas, the school’s learning management system. Create research guides, instruction resources, digital materials, videos/tutorials, and make those resources available to students, faculty, and staff.
  • Assist in other general duties, including special projects and programs, collection development, and strategic planning as requested by the Library Director
  • Work professionally and cooperatively within the Bunn Library, the School, and the broader Lawrenceville community.
  • Other duties as assigned

Requirements

  • Masters in Library/Information Sciences from an ALA-accredited institution.
  • Customer service and outreach experience.
  • At least 2 years of demonstrated experience teaching information, media, and digital literacy in an academic or school library setting.
  • Experience with digital humanities, archival collections, or other digital projects preferred.
  • Experience in Educational Technology, Instructional Design, or Digital Innovation preferred.
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, both oral and written.
  • Able to show initiative and flexibility. Must be able to adapt to users who have a wide variety of technology proficiency levels.
  • Strong time management skills and the ability to prioritize.
  • Must be detailed-oriented, congenial, patient, and reliable.
  • Ability to work in a collaborative team.
  • Ability and experience to plan, manage, and oversee projects, meet deadlines, and to prioritize work in alignment with the service goals of the library and school.
  • Formal training and/or experience with the design and delivery of instruction;
  • Strong knowledge about the use of AI in libraries and research, digital content, electronic resources, ebooks, publishing trends, and library technology.
  • Demonstrated interest in critical thinking about the use of AI tools and its impacts on the research and learning process;
  • Demonstrated ability to continuously learn new skills, technologies, and methods and to apply those to your work.
  • Ability to work effectively with a diverse population including young people (teenagers) and adults from diverse cultures.

Work Characteristics and Physical Demands: The work environment characteristics and physical demands described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • This is a fully in-person role that requires on-campus presence for all student interactions.
  • Physical demands are in excess of those for sedentary work. Must be able to remain on their feet for extended periods of time, go up and down flights of steps, as well as stoop, kneel, crouch, and lift.
  • Routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, fax machines, etc.
  • Must be capable of using visual display terminal with continuous wrist movement on a keyboard
  • Required to, talk, hear, walk, use hands to finger, handle or feel and reach with hands and arms
  • Must be able to work flexible hours to accommodate students’ schedules. This includes both day and evening responsibilities.
  • Must be able to lift up to 20lbs. without assistance
  • Ability to see with normal parameters.
  • Operates in a professional work environment

The Lawrenceville School is a diverse and inclusive community and makes all employment decisions without regard for an individual’s race, creed, color, religion, national origin, nationality, sex, pregnancy, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, veteran status, physical or mental disability (including AIDS and HIV related illness), genetic information, refusal to provide genetic information, refusal to submit to genetic testing, ancestry, familial status, marital status, domestic partnership status, civil union status, atypical cellular or blood trait, military service, application for military service, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. The Lawrenceville School will also provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals in accordance with applicable law.

The Lawrenceville School conducts pre-employment screening for all positions which includes a criminal background check, verification of work history, academic credentials, licenses, and certifications. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of the background check.

job.title: Charles River School Custodian
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Reports to: Director of Buildings and Grounds

Classification: Full-Time, Non-Exempt

Schedule: Tuesday–Friday, 3:00 p.m.–11:00 p.m.; Saturday, 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.

Compensation: $20.00 per hour

About Charles River School

Charles River School (CRS) honors the pursuit of academic excellence and the joy of childhood. We nurture each child by igniting curiosity, encouraging creativity, and cultivating intellectual engagement. Our graduates know themselves, understand others, and shape the future of our diverse world with confidence and compassion.

Founded more than 100 years ago, CRS is a progressive, independent PreKindergarten–8 school located in Dover, Massachusetts. The school’s beautiful campus serves as a hub for learning, community engagement, athletics, and enrichment activities throughout the year.

Position Overview

Charles River School seeks a dependable, service-oriented Custodian to join our Buildings and Grounds team. Reporting to the Director of Buildings and Grounds, the Custodian plays a vital role in maintaining a clean, safe, welcoming, and well-functioning campus for students, faculty, staff, families, and visitors.

Working primarily during evening hours, this position is responsible for cleaning and maintaining school facilities, supporting campus events, and serving as the primary on-site representative for after-hours building use. The Custodian will assist outside organizations and renters using school facilities and help ensure that campus spaces are secure and properly maintained.

Primary Responsibilities

Facilities Cleaning and Maintenance

  • Clean and maintain classrooms, offices, hallways, restrooms, gymnasium spaces, and common areas.
  • Vacuum, sweep, mop, dust, and sanitize facilities according to established standards.
  • Empty trash and recycling receptacles throughout campus.
  • Replenish restroom and custodial supplies as needed.
  • Perform routine inspections of campus facilities and report maintenance concerns to the Director of Buildings and Grounds.
  • Assist with seasonal cleaning projects and special facilities needs.

Building Operations and Security

  • Open, secure, and monitor designated campus spaces during evening and weekend hours.
  • Ensure that buildings are properly locked, alarmed, and secured at the end of each shift.
  • Respond appropriately to facility-related issues that arise during scheduled hours.
  • Assist with room setups and breakdowns for school and community events.

Community and Rental Support

  • Welcome and assist outside groups, athletic organizations, and other approved renters using CRS facilities.
  • Provide access to reserved spaces and answer basic facility-related questions.
  • Monitor facility use to ensure compliance with school guidelines and expectations.
  • Communicate any concerns or incidents to the Director of Buildings and Grounds.

Team Collaboration

  • Work collaboratively with members of the Buildings and Grounds team to maintain high standards of campus appearance and functionality.
  • Support special projects and other duties as assigned.
  • Contribute to a positive, professional, and service-oriented environment.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred.
  • Prior custodial, facilities, maintenance, or building operations experience preferred.
  • Ability to work independently and manage responsibilities with minimal supervision.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to cleanliness and safety.
  • Excellent reliability, punctuality, and customer service skills.
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and perform physical tasks including walking, bending, climbing stairs, and moving equipment.
  • Ability to interact professionally and courteously with students, families, staff, renters, and visitors.

Desired Qualities

  • Dependable and trustworthy.
  • Strong work ethic and sense of ownership.
  • Positive attitude and willingness to help others.
  • Flexibility and ability to adapt to changing priorities.
  • Commitment to supporting the mission and values of Charles River School.

Compensation and Benefits

This is a full-time, non-exempt position reporting to the Director of Buildings and Grounds. Compensation is $20.00 per hour. Eligible employees receive access to Charles River School’s benefits package, including health and retirement benefits in accordance with school policy.

Charles River School is an Equal Opportunity Employer and seeks candidates who will contribute to and support the diversity and excellence of our school community.

job.title: Head-Royce School After-School Program Counselor
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Part-time, Beginning August 10th, 2026 (0.4 FTE, 10 month)

Head-Royce School is a diverse K–12 community nestled in the Oakland hills that serves families seeking a transformative educational experience. Our mission is to develop students of character, intellect, and creativity.

The After-School Program (ASP) provides a high quality experience for students through a balance of student-led and adult-led activities, games, and play spaces. The After-School team consists of enthusiastic individuals who share a passion for creating a healthy, welcoming and playful environment after school.

Responsbilities

  • Provide energetic, positive support to students in order to foster a safe, enriching and fun atmosphere for all involved in after-school programming
  • Manage student safety; ensure all students are accounted for and all fellow staff members are aware of student whereabouts throughout the day
  • Proactively supervise, initiate and participate in various student-led activities during unscripted and scripted time
  • Actively engage in initiating activities and games with students of all grade levels (K-6)
  • Lead one enrichment class for two of the three trimesters in a topic approved by the Director of Extended Learning
  • Report any unsafe conditions in a timely manner and provide accident/incident reports when necessary
  • Be proficient, aware, prompt, and responsive when communicating with co-counselors and Director of Extended Learning via walkie talkie
  • Collaborate with co-counselors and Director of Extended Learning to ensure smooth flow of daily activities
  • Provide conflict-management mentoring and facilitation to students
  • Respond to parent and children concerns in an effective, professional manner
  • Be active, flexible, resourceful and creative in responding to the needs of students and parents
  • Make intentional and strategic use of prep time and slow times to plan activities, games, and ensure we are ready for the next day (snack, clean up, materials ready, etc.)

Qualifications

  • Candidates should possess strong interpersonal communication skills and ability to relate with people and children from a variety of educational, cultural and socio-economic backgrounds.
  • Other essential qualities important to the position are:
  • The ability to be professional, positive, flexible, fun and energetic.
  • A “go-getter” attitude, positive energy and “can do” mentality.
  • Counselors must enjoy a collaborative team setting and be willing to engage in frequent communication with fellow staff members.
  • Requires a minimum of one-year experience working with children/youth. This position is ideal for staff looking to enter a career in teaching, child development, recreation management and/or education administration.
  • Water safety & CPR/First Aid certified (Training will be provided)
  • Ability to provide proof of Fingerprint, SB848 and TB clearance.

Dress code- The After-School Program is both informal and professional.

  • Please dress comfortably for the everyday activities that are a part of your job responsibilities while maintaining a professional appearance.
  • All clothing must be neat, clean, and in good repair. Employees should avoid wearing tight, torn, or worn clothing, and sweatpants. In addition, others should not be able to see any undergarments, midriff, or other skin that could prove distracting to students, inappropriate or unprofessional for school.
  • Shoes must be appropriate and must not inhibit staff members from performing daily activities with students and co-staff.

$17.34 - $24 an hour

Compensation: Head-Royce is committed to attracting and retaining outstanding employees through competitive compensation. Rate is assigned based on relevant experience and education.

Start Date: August 10th, 2026;

End Date: June 8, 2027

Website: www.headroyce.org/asp

This position will have a 2-4 year appointment. It doesn't change the at-will nature of the job, but allows new individuals the opportunity to participate in the role. The Director of Extended Learning will work with ASP staff members on a transition plan between year 2 and year 4 of this appointment. There may be exceptions to this general policy, where administration seeks either an earlier change of employment or a continuation of the current role for reasons of stability with the program.

Located on a 22-acre campus in Oakland, California, Head-Royce School (HRS) is a pre-eminent, co-educational, independent, K-12 day school with a 139-year history. Our mission is to develop students of character, intellect, and creativity. We deliver on our mission by living our values:

  • Students First: We prioritize student learning, development, and well-being.
  • Academic Excellence: We pursue knowledge and assess our learning to better ourselves and our community.
  • Diversity: We embrace our different perspectives, backgrounds, experiences and identities to expand and enrich what we can learn and do together.
  • Belonging: We create the conditions in which everyone thrives and brings their authentic selves.
  • Civic Engagement: We connect students to the local community and beyond to enhance their academic experiences and foster genuine engagement.

Head-Royce enrolls approximately 930 students in K-8 division (Lower and Middle Schools) and 9-12 grades in the Upper School — and provides a dynamic, whole-child education to every student. We envision a future where education unlocks the promise and purpose of every student to better the world.

HRS is unable to provide immigration sponsorships such as H1B Visas. Open to all applicants authorized to work in the U.S and willing to undergo both Livescan background check and TB screening as part of the hiring process. Employment is also contingent upon successful completion of background checks and compliance with California SB 848, which requires prior educational institution employers to disclose credible complaints, substantiated investigations, or discipline involving egregious misconduct.

Required Disclosure: AB 2534 & SB 848- In accordance with Education Code section 44939.5 (as amended by California AB 2534 & SB 848) and Education Code 44051 (as amended by SB 848) applicants for all positions are required by law to provide a complete list of every school district, county office of education, charter school, state special school, diagnostic centers operated by the CA Department of Education, and/or private schools with which they have previously been employed, regardless of the length of service. Please include any full-time, part-time and/or substitute employment positions on your application. Failure to disclose all previous educational employment, regardless of length or location, may result in the disqualification of your application and/or may be deemed dishonestly in the hiring process and subject to discharge should you become employed.

Head-Royce provides equal employment opportunities on the basis of merit, fitness, qualifications, and experience. The school’s commitment to equal employment opportunity extends to all job applicants and employees and to all aspects of employment. Head-Royce makes employment decisions without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions and breastfeeding), reproductive health decision-making, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, citizenship, military or veteran status, age, or other categories defined by state law, federal law or local ordinance. Head-Royce prohibits discrimination or harassment based on these classifications. Discrimination and harassment based on a perception that anyone is in any of these protected classifications or is associated with a person who has or is perceived as being in any of these protected classifications, are also prohibited. Head-Royce School seeks to be a community in which every individual is treated with sensitivity, courtesy and respect.

job.title: The Hotchkiss School Post Office Associate
job.description:
Position Description & Application

POSITION SUMMARY:

If you have a background in retail or related fields and are looking for a role where you can make a tangible difference, we encourage you to apply to join us as a Post Office Associate. Your expertise in customer service and attention to detail will be highly valued in our mission to serve the Hotchkiss community. Even if you don’t have experience in a mail room or post office, but have related experience, we are ready to support you with training.

The Post Office Associate, under the guidelines of the US Postal regulations, sorts, meters, delivers, and transports mail for the community of 1,200 students and employees. This position is accountable for high-quality work performance in support of the best interests of the Hotchkiss community, to which this department serves.

The Post Office and Central Receiving accept incoming packages and mail for the School, which the team processes for organized, efficient, and accurate distribution. They provide the School community with internal postal and shipping services for outgoing mail and packages. In addition, they provide interoffice mail distribution services for the community.

The staff operate as a team and assist one another to ensure the continuity of these essential operations. They provide excellent customer service for the community with a high level of quality in receiving, mailing, and shipping services.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Maintain confidentiality with information received or distributed, maintaining the trust of the School community.
  • Sort UPS packages received in Central Receiving on a daily basis.
  • Cross-train in Central Receiving to provide satisfactory coverage of Central Receiving when needed.
  • Work in the Procuredesk program to fill stock orders.
  • Meter, sort, and distribute mail and packages.
  • Complete Postal, Customs, UPS, and FedEx forms and prepare mail and parcels for dispatch.
  • Distribute UPS, Federal Express, U.S.P.S., and other carrier packages.
  • Sell stamps, handle cash drawers, and charge on debit/credit cards.
  • Assist in the delivery and picking up of interoffice and outgoing mail between building locations.
  • Run postage and prepare outgoing mail for pick-up.
  • Create and print daily postal reports from the mailing machine.
  • Comfortable with various software applications.
  • Serve as a courteous and professional representative of the organization at all times.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High School diploma or General Education Degree (GED).
  • Ability to lift and carry heavy items as needed, while adhering to safe lifting practices.
  • Prior experience in a Post Office or mail room is preferred but not required.
  • Prior experience in a retail or related environment is preferred but not required.
  • Demonstrated ability to maintain effective and professional working relationships and superior communication skills.
  • Excellent time management skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Willingness to work flexible hours if required by the School's needs.
  • Excellent telephone and customer service skills.
  • Good organizational skills and ability to multitask.

PHYSICAL CONDITIONS:

While performing the essential duties of this job,

  • Possess a valid, OSHA-compliant Forklift Operation certification or be able to obtain employer-certified licensing within six months of employment (training and certification provided by the School).
  • The employee is regularly required to use their hands to type on a computer keyboard or controls.
  • Prolonged heavy lifting and the ability to lift packages approximately 5 ½ feet off the floor.
  • Ability to lift 70 pounds (postal weight limit). Heavier packages require 2 employees.
  • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods throughout the entire work day.
  • Ability to continuously reach and bend.
  • The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate, occasionally loud.
  • The Hotchkiss School is a tobacco-free environment.

job.title: The Hotchkiss School Business Office Associate
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Description

Department: Business Office

FLSA: Non-Exempt

Designation: Full Time, Calendar Year, Staff

Schedule: 35 hours per week, in-office

Report to: Controller

Travel: N/A

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Business Office team is committed to advancing the mission of the School by providing accurate and timely financial services, exceptional customer support for the School community, and responsible stewardship of the School's resources.

The Business Office Associate supports the daily financial, administrative, and operational activities of the Business Office. This position performs a broad range of accounting, purchasing, payment processing, systems administration, and program support responsibilities and serves as a key liaison between the Business Office and departments across campus.

The ability to create a warm and welcoming environment for all members of the community who work with the Business Office is required. The ideal candidate is organized, detail-oriented, adaptable, comfortable learning new systems, and able to manage multiple priorities in a collaborative, service-oriented environment. The Associate’s responsibilities will naturally shift to meet emerging priorities and administrative needs. Inhabiting a proactive mindset and strong adaptability are essential for success in this role.

Experience working in a private school or nonprofit organization is preferred but not required.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Assists with the preparation of monthly departmental journal entries.
  • Assists with monthly account reconciliations and investigates variances.
  • Enters, prepares, and processes routine journal entries in the accounting system.
  • Completes weekly gift uploads to the accounting system and verifies the accuracy and completeness of uploaded data.
  • Verifies, records, and reconciles applicable bank transactions and bank fees.
  • Assists the Controller with investment-related reconciliations, including obtaining and maintaining investment manager statements.
  • Reviews and processes transactions for the Business Office purchasing card (credit card) program and maintains complete supporting documentation.
  • Administers the School's prepaid card program, including funding cards for Athletics, Student Activities, and other school programs; reviews receipts and supporting documentation for accuracy and ensures expenses are properly coded.
  • Manages individual cardholder budgets within the prepaid card platform.
  • Processes approved payments for athletic officials through Arbiter and prepares the related general ledger entries.
  • Reconciles credit card and prepaid card activity and prepares and records related payment transactions in the general ledger.
  • Serves as the primary Business Office liaison for the School's golf program by providing administrative and financial support; creates and maintains related forms and systems, including FACTS and Square point-of-sale and web configurations.
  • Administers golf membership activities and communications, including season opening and ongoing member correspondence, management of the golf program email account, membership tracking, and preparation of recurring membership reports.
  • Assists with financial administration of the Student International Travel Program, including travel budget review, expense reconciliation, and related financial reporting.
  • Provides accounts payable support and backup coverage for other Business Office personnel as needed.
  • Cross-trains in Business Office functions to provide operational backup and ensure continuity of service.
  • Maintains accurate, complete, and organized accounting and administrative records in accordance with the School's record retention policies.
  • Provides documentation and support for month-end and year-end closing activities, annual audits, and other financial reporting requirements.
  • Provides administrative support for the School's auxiliary services, including vendor-related support, as needed.
  • Recommends process improvements to increase efficiency and strengthen internal controls.
  • Maintains confidentiality of financial, employee, student, and donor information.
  • Participates in special projects and performs other accounting, administrative, and related duties as assigned.

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE REQUIRED:

  • Associate degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, or a closely related field preferred; equivalent relevant experience will be considered.
  • Experience supporting business office, accounting, accounts payable, purchasing, administrative, or customer service functions preferred. Experience working in a private school or nonprofit organization is preferred.
  • Working knowledge of business office practices, procedures, recordkeeping, and office technology.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to provide responsive, welcoming service and build effective working relationships with a wide range of constituents.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment with flexibility and adaptability as priorities and projects change.
  • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple tasks, timelines, and changing deadlines.
  • Experience handling confidential and sensitive information with professionalism and discretion.
  • Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Excel, and the ability to learn and effectively use accounting, payment, purchasing, and administrative software systems.
  • Ability to maintain accuracy in data entry, transaction processing, account reconciliation, and proofreading.

PHYSICAL CONDITIONS:

  • Office environment
  • Sedentary position, repetitive motion on keyboard.
  • Frequent interruptions.
  • Ability to lift up to 20 lbs., bend, stoop and reach.

job.title: Head-Royce School 2nd-6th Grade Math Specialist
job.description:
Position Description & Application

OPENING: 2ND-6TH GRADE MATH SPECIALIST (Full time beginning Aug 2026)

Lower/Middle School has an immediate opening for a 2-6th math specialist. This position will support our recent efforts to differentiate and enrich our math program. Our educational philosophy focuses on helping students develop the skills necessary to succeed as responsible global citizens in the 21st century. We’d love you to join our faculty and create classrooms that seek to inspire in our students a lifelong love of learning by encouraging them to participate in experiential opportunities, take risks, view the world through multiple lenses, utilize innovative tools, build empathy and demonstrate proficiencies through a range of assessments that include real world problems and performances. In addition to classroom expectations, faculty also take on community duties and participate in the life of the community.

Classroom-centered responsibilities

  • Scheduled one to two times a week into each 2nd-6th math classroom to do student pull-out for enrichment or remediation- would work in conjunction with the student needs identified by the classroom teacher and log weekly classrooms activities
  • Meet with 2nd-6th grade classroom teachers to discuss support needs and to suggest enrichment and remediation materials
  • Observe teacher and provide feedback as well as coaching on approach and instruction in math

Other Lower and Middle School Job Responsibilities

  • Work with teachers and administrators in interpreting CTP/Milestones data and designing approaches to improve student achievement and instruction; provide summary reports to Head of Lower and Middle School
  • Attend Lower/Middle division or grade level meetings, when needed, and math department meetings
  • Work with math department to assess the efficacy of the math curriculum
  • Attend and provide professional development workshops in the area of math differentiation including Youcube, etc.
  • Research best practices in math and co-create math curriculum from the Upper Elementary and into Middle School
  • Create opportunities for K-8 math experiences, including estimation challenges, the Julia Robinson Math Festival, and others.

Skills

  • Collaborative, collegial, and flexible teacher with other student-centered educators
  • Clear communicator with students, colleagues, and parents, both orally and in writing
  • Demonstrated success partnering with parents to support the educational needs of their students.
  • Possess a growth mindset, a love of learning, and patience
  • Strong organizational, planning, and communication skills
  • Flexible in pedagogical approach, using multiple modalities to deliver a concept
  • Clear desire to use a variety of teaching approaches in order to reach different student populations and adapt to better serve their learning styles and needsIntegrates technology to enhance the student experience
  • Practiced in differentiated instruction
  • Demonstrated understanding of curriculum design, pedagogical approaches and developmental appropriateness in order to deliver engaging, active, student-centered lessons, practice, and assessment
  • Familiar with and uses different kinds of assessment (formative and summative)

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree required in Mathematics or Math Education
  • Minimum 5 years experience teaching at the primary elementary level
  • Strong academic background, experience in multicultural education and an awareness of ecological literacy
  • Genuine fondness for working with students of this age

Additional Qualifications we hope to find, but not required:

  • Advanced degrees in the field of education

Other Requirements

  • Must provide clearance background screening, TB and SB848

$76,600 - $130,998 a year

*Dependent on Years of Experience Teaching and Education Level

Location: Oakland, California

Education: Bachelor’s degree required

Start Date: August 2026

Website: headroyce.org

Other Considerations

Travel: Light travel potentially throughout the year

Education: Bachelor's Degree Required

To Apply

Interested candidates are asked to submit a letter of interest and a current resume to our website.

Applications will be reviewed as they are received.

Located on a 22-acre campus in Oakland, California, Head-Royce (HRS) is a pre-eminent, co-educational, independent, K-12 day school with a 137-year history. Our mission is to inspire in our students a lifelong love of learning and pursuit of academic excellence, to promote understanding of and respect for diversity that makes our society strong and to encourage active and responsible global citizenship.

Head-Royce enrolls 900 students in the three separate divisions—Lower, Middle and Upper—and provides a dynamic, whole-child education to every student.

Please note - HRS is unable to provide immigration sponsorships such as H1B Visas. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States and be willing to undergo both Livescan background check and TB screening as part of the hiring process.

Head Royce is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions including but not limited to employment, training, promotion, demotion, transfer, leaves of absence and termination based on qualifications and without regard to protected status. We will not discriminate based on age, color, creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding or related medical conditions), gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, national origin or ancestry, race (including traits historically associated with race, such as hair texture and protective hairstyles), religion, registered domestic partner status, physical or mental disability, a medical condition including genetic characteristics, military or veteran status, reproductive health decision making or any other consideration made unlawful by federal, state or local laws Head-Royce School seeks to be a community in which every individual is treated with sensitivity, courtesy and respect.

job.title: St. Mark's School Spanish Teacher (Temporary Leave replacement)
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Contract type: temporary leave replacement

School Type: Boarding

Schedule: This is a temporary, part-time position starting around mid-November (before Thanksgiving Break) and ending in early April.

Inspire a love of language and guide students to discover the power of stories, ideas, and their own voices.

Why Join Us

At St. Mark’s, we believe that language opens doors to cultures, perspectives, and meaningful human connection. We’re seeking a Spanish teacher who is passionate about language acquisition and cultural exploration, and who delights in guiding students as they build confidence in communication, engage in lively conversation, and deepen their understanding of the Spanish-speaking world. We seek an educator who brings experience, enthusiasm, and skill in teaching Spanish with a commitment to thoughtful curriculum design.

This position does not come with school provided housing.

What You’ll Do

You’ll be a teacher, mentor, and co-creator of learning. Your role will include:

  • Teaching one section of Spanish III, which meets (during regular 5-day weeks) on Mondays 8:00-9:05 a.m., Tuesdays 12:55-2:00 p.m., and Thursdays 11:15 a.m.-12:20 p.m. (Note: the schedule will shift during 4-day and 3-day weeks.)
  • The opportunity to also cover a section of Spanish I may be possible, depending on the candidate’s interest and availability and the School’s needs.
  • Giving meaningful, timely feedback that challenges and inspires
  • Collaborating with department colleagues

What We’re Looking For

  • A degree in Spanish or a related, interdisciplinary field is essential
  • Native or near-native language skills in Spanish and English
  • Some experience teaching at the secondary level (2+ years preferred)
  • Ability to connect with diverse learners and teach inclusively
  • Strong communication, organization, and collaboration skills
  • Comfort with educational tech tools (Google Suite, etc.)

Why You’ll Love It Here

  • A warm, close-knit community of students and colleagues
  • Access to campus facilities, from the fitness center to nature trails
  • A chance to grow professionally

Salary Range: $5,000-$7000. Pay is commensurate with experience.

About St. Mark’s

St. Mark’s School is a coeducational boarding high school of ~375 students, located in Southborough, MA (22 miles west of Boston). Since 1865, we’ve prioritized deep curiosity, character formation, and community.

We are committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds and experiences

job.title: Children's Day School Middle School Athletic Coach
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Middle School Athletic Coach

At Children’s Day School, what you learn and who you become are equally important.

Children’s Day School (CDS) is a welcoming community in the big city, a farm and garden among urban streets, an advocate for change and uplifting progressive values, an independent school with down-to-earth values, and an institution that is always asking how we can do this better.

We strive for balance, so students become both academically successful and grounded. They leave CDS confident, with the humility to listen and the resolve to speak up for what they see as right.

CDS is a co-educational preschool through eighth-grade school serving over 450 students in the Mission Dolores neighborhood of San Francisco with two campuses, two sheep, and lovely people.

To learn more about CDS, visit our website at www.cds-sf.org.

CDS is seeking enthusiastic and positive coaches to join our Middle School Athletics Program throughout the 2026 – 2027 school year. We are looking for individuals who are passionate about working with middle school students and helping young athletes grow both on and off the field or court.

Our athletics program includes the following sports:

  • Cross Country (Fall)
  • Volleyball (Fall)
  • Basketball (Winter)
  • Futsal (Spring)

A CDS coach is committed to the personal growth and development of student-athletes. In addition to teaching sport-specific skills and strategies, our coaches foster teamwork, confidence, resilience, leadership, sportsmanship, and a lifelong love of physical activity. Coaches play an important role in creating an inclusive, positive, and supportive environment where every student feels valued and challenged.

Time Commitment

Most coaching positions require two after-school commitments per week, typically consisting of one practice and one game, or two practices depending on the league schedule.

Practice & Game Schedule

  • Morning Practice: 7:30 a.m. – 8:15 a.m. (varies by season)
  • Afternoon Practice: Approximately 3:30 p.m. – 5:00 p.m.
  • Home Games: Generally between 3:45 p.m. – 5:15 p.m.
  • Away Games: Typically a two-hour commitment between 3:30 p. m. – 6:30 p.m.
  • Practice days are determined by the league schedule and coach availability.

Practices and home contests are held near Children's Day School, while away competitions take place at neighboring independent and public schools throughout San Francisco.

Each sport consists of a regular season schedule with opportunities for league playoffs and championship competition.

Responsibilities

  • Plan and lead safe, engaging, and developmentally appropriate practices.
  • Teach sport-specific fundamentals while emphasizing teamwork, effort, and sportsmanship.
  • Foster a positive, inclusive, and supportive team culture.
  • Collaborate with the Middle School Athletics Director to establish team goals and expectations.
  • Support the social and emotional development of student-athletes.
  • Communicate effectively with families using the school's online communication platforms.
  • Attend all scheduled practices, games, playoffs, and championship events, if applicable.
  • Assist with equipment setup and breakdown.
  • Manage attendance, uniforms, and student safety in accordance with school policies.
  • Represent Children's Day School with professionalism and integrity at all times.

Minimum Qualifications

  • At least 18 years of age.
  • Experience coaching or working with middle school-aged students (head coaching experience preferred).
  • Strong knowledge of the sport(s) being coached.
  • Effective communication, leadership, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to build positive relationships with students, families, school staff, league officials, and opposing teams.
  • CPR and First Aid certification (or willingness to obtain certification before the season begins).

Physical Requirements

This position requires standing, walking, demonstrating athletic skills, and actively participating in practices and competitions for extended periods.

Children's Day School is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all students, families, faculty, staff, and coaches.

Compensation

This is an hourly, non-exempt position that pays $100.00 per hour ($2,500 for each team coached for the season).

Clearance Requirements

  • Live Scan background check
  • SB 848 verifications
  • TB Assessment
  • Eligible to work in the U.S.

To Apply

Apply on our website at careers.cds-sf.org. Include resume, and cover letter.

job.title: Carlthorp School After-School Theater Co-Teacher
job.description:
Position Description

Carlthorp School is seeking an enthusiastic, creative, and collaborative educator to lead our K-6 after-school theater program. This part-time stipend position is an exciting opportunity for someone passionate about performing arts and working with elementary-aged students to help cultivate confidence, creativity, collaboration, and joyful performance experiences. The After-School Theater Co-Teacher will oversee our annual theatre productions, including a fall play and spring musical, while helping students develop performance skills and showcase their talents as part of our growing performing arts program.

Position Overview

  • Position Type: Part-Time Stipend Position
  • Program Duration: September – April
  • Compensation: $300 per session, including tech weeks and performances
  • Student Audience: Kindergarten through 6th grade

Weekly Rehearsal Schedule

  • Rehearsals held 1x per week
  • Time: 3:15 - 4:45 p.m.

Production Responsibilities

The Theater Teacher will:

  • Direct and oversee a fall play and spring musical
  • Lead weekly rehearsals and prepare students for performances
  • Help coordinate auditions, casting, blocking, and choreography/staging, as appropriate
  • Support students in developing confidence, collaboration, and performance skills
  • Coordinate and organize props, costumes, and set pieces
  • Assist with set building and overall production preparation
  • Communicate rehearsal schedules, expectations, and performance details with families
  • Collaborate with school leadership and staff to ensure successful productions
  • Foster a positive, inclusive, and engaging environment for all participants

Tech Week & Performance Dates

Fall Play

  • Tech Week Rehearsals: Dec. 1-3 (3:15 - 5:15 p.m.)
  • Performances: Dec. 4 (School Preview & Evening Performance), Additional Evening Performance TBD

Spring Musical

  • Tech Week Rehearsals: April 5-8 (3:15 - 5:15 p.m.)
  • Performances: April 9 (School Preview & Evening Performance), Additional Evening Performance TBD

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will:

  • Have experience working with elementary-aged students
  • Have experience in theatre, musical theatre, directing, or performing arts education
  • Be organized, collaborative, and creative
  • Demonstrate strong communication skills with students, families, and colleagues
  • Enjoy building a vibrant and engaging arts program that celebrates student voice and talent
  • Be comfortable supporting all aspects of a production, including staging, props, sets, and logistics

We are looking for someone who believes in the power of the arts to build confidence, community, and creativity in children and who is excited to help students shine both on and off the stage.

Interested candidates should email a cover letter and resume to resume@carlthorp.org.

job.title: La Jolla Country Day School Extended Day Group Leader
job.description:
Position Description & Application

La Jolla Country Day School is seeking enthusiastic, caring, and dependable Group Leaders to join our Lower School and Middle School After-School and Extended Day Program. The program provides a safe, healthy, and engaging balance of creative, educational, and recreational activities for students after the school day. The program operates on School days Monday through Friday, and Faculty work days. Typical hours are 2:30 - 5:30 pm.

The ideal candidate enjoys working with children, builds positive relationships with students, and brings energy, patience, good humor, and a strong sense of responsibility to an after-school environment. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who is interested in gaining experience working with children in a supportive school community.

What You’ll Do

  • Supervision & Safety
  • Actively supervise students and maintain continuous visual awareness, including walking playground perimeters
  • Manage the playground and student behavior in accordance with school policies while promoting safety and healthy choices
  • Follow all school safety, security, and emergency procedures
  • Remain mobile while on duty
  • Program Operations
  • Take accurate attendance using the childcare app and physical attendance sheet
  • Coordinate with outside vendors providing enrichment programs
  • Student Relationships & Communication
  • Build positive relationships with students and learn and use their names
  • Provide guidance and encouragement while supporting positive behavior
  • Maintain open communication with parents/guardians, School staff, and educators

Who You Are

  • Student-Centered: You enjoy working with children and are attentive to their individual needs and developmental stages.
  • Positive Role Model: You bring enthusiasm, patience, good humor, and clear expectations to your work with students.
  • Engaging Leader: You create fun, supportive experiences and keep students actively engaged.
  • Collaborative Professional: You communicate effectively and work well with students, families, and colleagues.
  • Responsible & Adaptable: You are dependable, self-motivated, and able to respond calmly to changing circumstances.
  • Inclusive & Growth-Oriented: You are open to learning and feedback and contribute to a welcoming, inclusive environment grounded in respect and culturally responsive practices.

Qualifications

  • Must be at least 18 years of age at the time of hire
  • Experience working with children preferred
  • Genuine enthusiasm for working with children and an understanding of child development
  • Strong interpersonal, communication, and relationship-building skills
  • Ability to positively manage student behavior and maintain a safe, respectful environment
  • Ability to respond calmly and appropriately in emergency situations
  • Basic computer skills and comfort using technology for attendance and communication
  • Reliable transportation

Work Environment & Physical Requirements

  • Part-time, hourly, in-person role on the La Jolla Country Day School campus
  • Work takes place in classrooms, outdoor areas, and other campus spaces
  • Requires active supervision, including standing, walking, and moving throughout campus
  • Ability to participate in and supervise recreational and physical activities
  • Ability to respond promptly to student needs and emergency situations

Pay Range

$18.75–$25 per hour

An offer to a successful candidate will depend on several factors, including, but not limited to, experience, training, practical knowledge, and education.

To be considered, please submit

  • A current resume/CV
  • A cover letter describing your experience working with children and your interest in joining the La Jolla Country Day School community

We value authenticity in the application process and ask candidates to refrain from using AI tools to generate their application materials.

job.title: Drew School Baseball Coach
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Job Type

Temporary

Description

The Drew School, a member of the Bay Area Conference, invites applications for the Boys Assistant Baseball Coach position. Drew School seeks a candidate whose experience will contribute to the School's commitment to diversity and inclusiveness.

Please note, this position is temporary/seasonal. This position will be starting in February 8, 2027 and ending May 7, 2027.

Job Description

Boys Assistant Baseball Coaches are responsible for carrying out coaching and administrative duties for the boys soccer program including:

  • Prepare and organize practice sessions
  • Attend and support interscholastic competitions
  • Instruct soccer players on proper rules, regulations, and etiquette
  • Communicating with players, parents, and administration
  • Drive school vehicles
  • Serving as a mentor to student-athletes helping them develop academically, physically, and socially
  • Performing related duties as assigned

Pay: Stipend of $6,000 for the season

About Drew Athletics

Drew athletes find their voice by building a commitment to competition, athleticism, fitness, and teamwork that helps bolster confidence, leadership, and school spirit. The athletic program provides student-athletes with opportunities to achieve athletic excellence and learn vital team-building skills. All students are encouraged to join a team and get involved in athletics at Drew, regardless of their background or skill level.

Drew is a coeducational independent high school enrolling 300 students, competing in the Bay Area Conference and a member of the CIF and NCS. Drew is an equal opportunity employer.

job.title: Crossroads School Associate Dean of College Counseling
job.description:
School Position Description

Application Site

Description

The candidate must have excellent listening, organizational and communication skills. Public speaking experience, multi-tasking ability and comfort with a fast-paced environment are expectations. The best candidates will possess an easy-going personality, a great sense of humor, a fully charged work ethic and a love of working with teenagers. More specifically, the ideal Associate Dean of College Counseling will be skilled at, and excited to provide individualized and specific college counseling services for students with a range of interests and talents across a full socioeconomic and human spectrum; preference will be given to those candidates who combine expertise in all of the aforementioned with one or more of the following strengths:

  • Spanish language fluency
  • Standardized testing administration and/or experience with learning differences
  • University of California and NCAA course approval and management
  • Financial Aid
  • Intersectional work experience as a classroom teacher and/or Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion practitioner.
  • Recent experience as an undergraduate college admissions officer
  • Athletic Recruiting
  • Visual and Performing Arts portfolio-based applicants
  • Experience working with Test Prep companies, college touring companies, and other 3rd party relationships
  • Experience working with the web-based platform SCOIR

Primary Responsibilities (these may vary depending on the hiring timeline):

  • Meet with seniors as needed to create and finalize college lists, review essays, proofread/edit applications, etc.
  • Author highly personalized letters of recommendation for high school seniors.
  • Participate in all office-sponsored programming (including the occasional nights and weekends) and show enthusiasm for enhancing or reimagining programming.
  • Participate in the larger Crossroads School community via a wide-range of campus-wide programs and events.
  • Commit to engage in community-wide Equity and Social Justice programming, dialogue and activism.
  • Utilize college counseling technology (i.e.: Scoir, Blackbaud, Google Docs) to both guide students through the college selection process and manage enrollment data.
  • Show willingness to learn technological skills and/or systems in order to manage and assess current practices.
  • Handle highly sensitive material with discretion.
  • Engage in professional development opportunities, such as visiting colleges and universities throughout the academic year and representing Crossroads at national and regional college admission counseling conferences.
  • Meet with college representatives (both on campus and through professional development opportunities) in order to establish and/or develop collegial relationships.
  • Collaborate with the College Counseling team to author communications for internal and external use.

Qualifications

  • Commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion.
  • Bachelor’s degree required/Master’s degree preferred.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience in college counseling and/or college admissions, higher education, classroom teaching and/or other school-based advising/counseling practice.
  • Outstanding written, oral, interpersonal, and presentation skills.
  • Strong critical thinking abilities surrounding trends and best-practices in the college to career landscape.
  • Technological proficiency and an openness to learn, including an openness to learn from students.
  • Strong organizational and problem-solving skills

job.title: The School at Columbia University Leave Replacement, Math Teacher, Grades 6-8
job.description:
Position Description & Application

Description

The School at Columbia University is an independent K-8 school founded in 2003 with the goal of providing an excellent education to a diverse student body. Our intentional school culture embraces shared beliefs across disciplines and grades, which underlie important values expressed through everyday behaviors and visible symbols throughout our community.

We dedicate ourselves to fostering in our students, personal resourcefulness and integrity, a sense of social responsibility, and a lifelong appreciation of learning through an innovative, socially and emotionally supportive, and academically challenging program. We adhere to a common code of civility among all constituents. We tailor our instruction so that the needs of the individual students are met. A committed faculty and administration strive to create a school that will stand as a model for what K-8 education can be, and serve as a genuine and enduring partnership between Columbia University and its neighbors.

Responsibilities:

  • Teach an integrated mathematics curriculum to middle-school students in a K-8 setting, possibly with a teaching partner to about 20 students
  • Collaborate in the design and implementation of an integrated curriculum
  • Work to ensure academic excellence, by fully knowing students and adapting curricula to meet their needs
  • Keep careful anecdotal and assessment records to write accurate, comprehensive student reports that reflect student growth and support their future education
  • Write detailed math teacher recommendations for all Grade 8 students (if selected to teach 8th grade) as part of the high school placement process, including collaboration with the placement team and participation in meetings with families as needed
  • Act as an advisor to a group of middle-school students
  • Chaperone day and overnight trips and supervise curricular and community events in support of the teaching team, student experience, and the academic, advisory, and student life programs
  • Fulfill all duties, responsibilities, and commitments as outlined in the school’s Guidebook and the organization’s code of conduct
  • Engage in ongoing communication with parents/guardians
  • Perform other responsibilities as assigned

Qualifications

  • B.A./B.S. degree in Education, Mathematics, or an equivalent degree or educational qualification from an accredited college or university
  • At least two years of full-time teaching experience in K-8 public or independent schools beyond student teaching
  • At least two years of teaching mathematics, preferably pre-Algebra and Algebra
  • Strong skills in mathematics learning with problem-solving, number sense, and understanding of the core web-based technologies and applications
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Wide-ranging intellectual and educational interests

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree in a related field
  • Knowledge of Spanish
  • Knowledge of latest research and thinking about mathematics education
  • Familiarity with new technologies

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

Columbia University is an Equal Opportunity Employer / Disability / Veteran

Pay Transparency Disclosure

The salary of the finalist selected for this role will be set based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to departmental budgets, qualifications, experience, education, licenses, specialty, and training. The above hiring range represents the University’s good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation at the time of posting.

Columbia University in the City of New York

Department

The School at Columbia

Location

Morningside
