job.title: The Agnes Irwin School Campaign Assistant
job.description:
Job Application & Description

The Campaign Assistant will serve as an integral member of the Campaign team and the primary support staff for the Director of Development and larger campaign team. They support the creation of campaign materials & reports; support individual and group cultivation, solicitation and stewardship; help manage campaign-related meetings and committees; and assist with general campaign projects. The Campaign Assistant helps ensure that the Campaign Team provides the necessary support to the Head of School, other key administrators, the Campaign Chairs, and other campaign volunteers. Serving as the primary liaison between the campaign team, committees, and advancement services, the Campaign Assistant is a highly focused project manager who thrives on managing timelines, ensuring accuracy, and producing materials that reflect a high set of standards, ultimately helping drive the campaign forward.

This position is funded through the campaign budget.

Campaign Coordination:

  • Serve as an active member of the Development Office by participating in planning the strategic direction of the campaign and assisting in the recommendation and implementation of new ideas and opportunities.
  • Maintain and help develop pipelines by identifying donors, recording actions/tasks, tracking opportunities in the office’s CRM, and developing reports for the campaign team.
  • Oversee production and maintain campaign reports in partnership with the members of the advancement services team.
  • Ensure timely acknowledgment of all campaign gifts and pledges.
  • Coordinate the production, distribution, and rigorous follow-up of all Letters of Intent, Gift Agreements, and pledge reminders in partnership with the advancement services team.
  • Manage and audit the master campaign calendar, tracking critical milestones and ensuring all team members and volunteers meet strict deadlines.
  • Participate in donor research for individuals and foundations. Serve as the liaison between the campaign team and any external researchers hired to support the campaign work.
  • Prepare donor packets for individual and group solicitation meetings in partnership with gift officers and the Director of Development.
  • Perform special projects as assigned by the Campaign Leadership and Committee.
  • Support the Director of Development with the creation of slide decks for board meetings, committee meetings, all school meetings, and other events as they arise.
  • Support planned and deferred giving initiatives such as the creation of large or small mailings, list generation, reporting, etc.

Campaign Committees Support

  • Coordinate and support staff and volunteer Campaign meetings, including catering, printed and digital materials, calendar management, and meeting notes.
  • Lead operational support for Campaign Committees. Create agendas and slide decks, track volunteer action items, and proactively follow up to ensure accountability.
  • Support volunteers by providing requested information and keeping the committee informed of timelines and important deadlines.
  • Work with the Director of Donor Engagement to create and distribute invitations, announcements, and other campaign communications to the public

Campaign Database Coordination and Website Content:

  • Enter and maintain donor opportunities in the donor database.
  • Design, implement, and maintain real-time tracking programs and visual dashboards to report campaign progress to the Board of Trustees and Campaign Chairs.
  • Generate financial and action reports as necessary in conjunction with existing staff.
  • Enter notes to track conversations and meetings and/or support team members with their actions.
  • Audit campaign gift coding and database entry to ensure flawless financial recording and reporting.
  • Ensure website content is up to date throughout the campaign, including donor recognition, goal setting, and timelines.

Other duties as assigned

Education/Skills required:

  • 2+ years of experience in development, data analytics, or project management (Capital Campaign experience highly preferred).
  • Strong writing, communication, and interpersonal skills required.
  • CRM Experience required. Raiser’s Edge/NXT experience preferred.
  • Strong skills in Google Slides and Canva are required. Basic understanding of InDesign is desirable.
  • Advanced proficiency in Google Sheets/Excel is required. Must love numbers and possess a proven ability to interpret data sets into clean, visual reports.
  • Exceptional organizational skills with a demonstrated ability to manage multiple moving parts, prioritize effectively, and stay laser-focused on tasks without losing sight of deadlines.
  • Broad understanding of fundraising and capital campaigns.
  • Bachelor of Arts or comparable degree.
  • Ability to function independently and in collaboration with staff, Trustees, volunteers, and donors.
  • Strong skills as a self-starter.
  • Detail oriented.
  • This position requires some evening and weekend work, depending upon the campaign events calendar.

job.title: Edmund Burke School Assistant Director of Development/Annual Fund
job.description:
Job description

ABOUT EDMUND BURKE SCHOOL

Founded in 1968, Edmund Burke School is an independent, co-ed day school for 6th-12th grade on a city campus in Washington, DC – interweaving academic challenge, experiential learning, and civic engagement in a welcoming, inquisitive community. Long committed to progressive pedagogy, Burke centers the intellectual and creative lives of students and emphasizes active learning, responsive teaching, and engagement with the world around us. Administrators, faculty and staff bring a diversity of experiences and expertise to Burke, enjoy learning from and collaborating with one another, and commit to continual growth and professional development. Moveover, Burke adults thrive in a community where the growth and learning of young people is the collective focus and priority for all.

JOB SUMMARY

The Assistant Director of Development/Annual Fund supports all areas of the Development Office, as directed by the Director of Development & Alumni Relations, with a specific emphasis on the cultivation, solicitation and stewardship of individual donors through the Burke Annual Fund. This is a full-time, year-round position, which is annually contracted from July 1–June 30.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

● Responsible for meeting the Annual Fund goal set by the Board of Trustees.

● Conceptualizes and executes an Annual Fund plan to maximize income and participation from a variety of constituents – parents, alumni, past parents, grandparents, faculty, staff, trustees and other friends of the school – utilizing a variety of techniques, including a major annual Day of Giving, direct mail, outreach through email, phone and texts, proposal writing, face-to-face solicitations, matching gifts, and third-party giving.

● Coordinates with colleagues to thoughtfully build and steward donor relationships, and nurture a culture of giving through various communications, materials, events and gift acknowledgements.

● Leads various events to include a major donor stewardship event.

● Coordinates with the Assistant Director of Development, Advancement Services to segment donor lists and to ensure the data integrity of gift information, biographical and relational data in Burke’s development database, Raiser’s Edge. Executes reports and analyzes data to inform Annual Fund and major donor approaches and strategies.

● Develops a robust volunteer program including parents, trustees, alums, faculty/staff and others in support of the Annual Fund, and recruits, trains and supports Annual Fund volunteers on an ongoing basis throughout the year.

● Works with the Director of Development to coordinate the cultivation and stewardship of major donor prospects.

● Synthesizes information from a variety of sources to develop comprehensive prospect research reports, as needed for staff and volunteers throughout the cultivation, solicitation and stewardship cycle. ● Works with colleagues to support engagement with Burke alumni, and is specifically responsible for executing giving programs with alumni.

● Works within a small cohesive team, supporting all Development Office initiatives and events as needed, most importantly the annual auction each spring, but also including stewardship events, alumni relations activities and events, and major donor, planned giving and campaign activities

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

Education/Experience:

● BA preferred

● 3-5 years of direct fundraising experience, preferably focused on Annual Fund efforts and in an independent school setting.

● previous experience with direct mail, email and phonathon solicitations.

● substantial experience with a development Constituent Relationship Management (CRM) database

● experience with the Blackbaud’s Raiser’s Edge is strongly desired

● Experience with a data mining software desirable; experience with Blackbaud’s ResearchPoint preferred

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

● goal-oriented, able to meet deadlines

● possess strategic thinking and detail-oriented skills,

● ability to work well independently and as part of a collaborative team.

● excellent computer skills, with strong proficiency in Google Drive, Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel and other Office products and Google applications.

● Must be able to attend weekend and evening activities, as necessary.

● Possesses strong verbal and written communication skills.

● Excellent interpersonal and organizational skills.

COMMITMENT TO EQUITY AND INCLUSION

At Edmund Burke School, we have a longstanding commitment to equity and inclusion. We are dedicated to hiring people of diverse backgrounds and perspectives, and we honor the dignity and worth of all people. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, physical abilities, sexual orientation, age, religion, national origin, or veteran status. We expect the values and work of prospective candidates to align with our mission on equity and inclusion. The culture of the Edmund Burke School aims to embrace differences, develop sensitivity to the perspectives of others, and prevent isolation of any one group of individuals.

Salary Range: $70,000-$85,000 based on relevant experience and other job-related factors

TO APPLY

Interested candidates should email a cover letter and resume to Jennifer Kozak Rawlings, Director of Development & Alumni Relations at jennifer.rawlings@burkeschool.org

job.title: Charles River School Development Associate
job.description:
Job description

Charles River School seeks a warm, motivated, and relationship-driven advancement professional to serve as Development Associate. Reporting to the Director of Development, this position plays a meaningful role in building and sustaining a vibrant culture of philanthropy across the CRS community.

The Development Associate will lead alumni engagement and prospect management efforts — developing and implementing an alumni engagement model, managing a portfolio of prospects, and supporting Annual Fund solicitations in partnership with senior staff. This role oversees CRS’s alumni network, coordinates regional events and Alumni Association activities, and serves as a primary point of contact for Alumni Class Agents and Ambassadors.

Beyond alumni relations, the Development Associate will manage an events portfolio spanning all Development Office constituencies, from donor receptions and volunteer appreciation events to campaign initiatives.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone who combines genuine relationship-building instincts with fundraising confidence, organizational rigor, and a deep enthusiasm for the mission of Charles River School. This is an in-person position based on campus five days per week; a four-day on-campus schedule may be considered for the right candidate.

Primary Responsibilities

Prospect Management 45%

  • Manage a portfolio of alumni prospects; directly solicit Annual Fund gifts and partner with senior staff and volunteers on solicitations as needed.
  • Build the alumni donor pipeline by identifying and researching prospective donors, recommending leadership gift targets, and developing solicitation strategies.
  • Liaise with Alumni Class Agents and Alumni Ambassadors to maintain a steady pipeline of outreach, donor visits, and stewardship activities.
  • Deliver a high-quality alumni donor experience through regular correspondence, timely acknowledgements, and meaningful stewardship that deepens long-term relationships.
  • Maintain accurate constituent records and engagement tracking within the school’s database.
  • Partner with school leadership to communicate the impact of philanthropic support through storytelling, data, and donor recognition.

Alumni Engagement: 30%

  • Develop and implement an alumni engagement model that deepens connections and inspires philanthropic participation across all off-campus constituencies, including alumni, past parents, grandparents, and friends of CRS.
  • Oversee CRS’s alumni network, coordinate regional events with volunteers, and support the Alumni Association including membership, meetings, communications, and online content.
  • Draft and manage Development communications including donor acknowledgements, stewardship reports, event materials, and alumni outreach.

Events Management 25%

  • Manage a comprehensive events portfolio spanning all Development Office constituencies, including alumni gatherings, donor receptions, volunteer appreciation events, and fundraising events. This role requires local and occasional regional travel to support events, donor visits, and alumni gatherings.
  • Oversee all event logistics from start to finish — timelines, invitations, registration, volunteer coordination, vendor communication, setup, follow-up stewardship, and metrics tracking.
  • Collaborate with faculty, staff, and school leadership to ensure events reflect CRS’s mission, culture, and values.
  • Proactively identify new event opportunities aligned with the strategic objectives of the Development Office, including campaign events.

Desired Skills and Qualities

  • Enthusiastic commitment to CRS’s progressive educational mission and community values.
  • Exceptional interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
  • Strong organizational abilities and attention to detail with the capacity to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • A natural collaborator who works effectively across constituencies including staff, volunteers, trustees, and families.
  • Demonstrated cultural competency and commitment to equity and inclusion.
  • Creativity, flexibility, professionalism, and a strong sense of initiative.
  • Fundraising intuition — a natural ability to build trust, read relationships, and move donors along a giving journey with patience and purpose.
  • Confidence, warmth, and a sense of humor that complement the culture of CRS.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree.
  • 2–3 years of experience planning and executing events at scale, ideally with a fundraising focus.
  • Demonstrated experience with volunteer management.
  • Experience managing donor relationships and making direct solicitations preferred.
  • Comfort and confidence making direct asks for financial support, volunteer commitments, and philanthropic engagement.
  • Ability to communicate effectively and respectfully in-person, on the phone, and via
  • email/text with donors, board members, volunteers, and colleagues.
  • Demonstrated ability to work in a fast-paced environment, meet concurrent deadlines, organize time and priorities, and to do so in collaboration with diverse stakeholders
  • High degree of integrity, initiative, and resourcefulness.
  • Proficiency with donor management and event systems; experience with Veracross or similar CRM a plus.
  • Experience in alumni relations, annual giving, or advancement in an independent school or nonprofit setting preferred.

Compensation and Benefits

This is a full-time, exempt position reporting to the Director of Development. The salary range is $45,000 – $55,000, commensurate with experience.

CRS offers a competitive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision insurance, retirement plan contributions, flexible spending accounts, life and disability insurance, and professional development support. As a school community, employees also benefit from a collegial, mission-driven environment and the rhythms and culture of independent school life.

Applicants of diverse, underrepresented backgrounds are encouraged to apply. Interested candidates should submit a cover letter and resume to crsjobs@charlesriverschool.org with Development Associate in the subject line.

job.title: Vermont Academy Leadership Gifts Officer
job.description:
Leadership Gifts Officer

  • Start Date: September 1, 2026
  • Location: Saxtons River, Vermont
  • Reports To: Chief Advancement Officer
  • Collaborates Closely With: Head of School, Advancement Team, Trustees, Alumni, Parents, and Volunteers
  • The Opportunity: What Will You Do & How Will We Partner?
  • Vermont Academy seeks a strategic, relational, and highly motivated Leadership Gifts Officer to help advance one of the most important moments in the school’s history. As Vermont Academy approaches its 150th anniversary and launches the Where Vision Meets Purpose Campaign in support of Vision 2030, this role will help shape the philanthropic future of the institution.
  • At Vermont Academy, advancement work is deeply relational. It is rooted in listening carefully, building authentic trust, and connecting donors to a compelling vision for young people and the future of the school. The Chief Advancement Officer will work closely with the Leadership Gifts Officer who will cultivate and steward meaningful partnerships with alumni, families, grandparents, and friends of Vermont Academy—helping supporters align their philanthropy with the mission, priorities, and long-term sustainability of the school.
  • This role combines frontline fundraising, strategic planning, donor stewardship, and an understanding of campaign management. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable building relationships over time, executing sophisticated fundraising strategies, and helping coordinate the systems and momentum necessary for a successful comprehensive campaign.
  • Working closely with the Chief Advancement Officer and Head of School, this individual will help drive leadership annual giving, work on bridging mid level donors into major donors, campaign planning, and endowment growth during a transformative chapter in Vermont Academy’s history.
  • Your Core Responsibilities
  • This is a full-time, 12-month administrative position with significant travel (75%) and active engagement in school life.
  • Major Gifts & Relationship Management
  • Manage and strategically advance a dynamic portfolio of approximately 100–125 major gift prospects and donors, including alumni, current parents, parents of alumni, grandparents, and friends of the school.
  • Develop and implement individualized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies designed to deepen engagement and secure philanthropic support, primarily in the $10,000–$50,000 range, while also supporting select six-figure opportunities.
  • Identify, qualify, and build the major gift pipeline through prospect research, referrals, relationship mapping, and ongoing engagement strategies.
  • Conduct meaningful donor conversations that connect Vermont Academy’s mission, strategic priorities, and student experience to philanthropic investment opportunities.
  • Arrange, prepare for, staff, and follow up on donor meetings involving the Head of School, Chief Advancement Officer, trustees, and other key school leaders.
  • Develop a deep understanding of Vermont Academy’s academic programs, student life, strategic plan, and institutional priorities in order to articulate a compelling case for support.
  • Campaign Leadership & Strategic Advancement
  • Partner closely with the Chief Advancement Officer on the planning and execution of the Where Vision Meets Purpose Campaign and other strategic fundraising initiatives.
  • Support campaign planning efforts including prospect strategy, timelines, donor communications, cultivation events, volunteer coordination, and proposal development.
  • Help coordinate leadership giving strategies tied to annual, capital, endowment, deferred, and non-cash gifts.
  • Conduct and oversee prospect research for campaign and leadership-giving priorities, including research on newly enrolled families and emerging donor opportunities.
  • Collaborate with the Director of Annual Giving and the Alumni Engagement Officer to ensure thoughtful donor movement and coordinated engagement across giving levels.
  • Analyze giving trends and prepare reports, updates, and prospect strategy materials for senior leadership and Board committees.
  • Maintain accurate and strategic documentation of donor engagement and solicitation activity within Advancement’s database, utilizing Blackbaud Raisers Edge and related systems.
  • Stewardship & Donor Experience
  • Lead thoughtful stewardship efforts for leadership and major donors, including those supporting endowed or named funds.
  • Partner with the Advancement team to create annual impact reports, campaign updates, stewardship materials, and personalized donor communications.
  • Ensure donors experience consistent, meaningful recognition and engagement through events, reporting, outreach, and ongoing relationship management.
  • Help foster a culture of gratitude, professionalism, and responsiveness throughout the Advancement Office.
  • Community Engagement & School Partnership
  • Participate actively in school life, including attendance at major events, performances, athletic competitions, assemblies, and community programming.
  • Recognize that advancement work is most effective when grounded in authentic connection to the daily life of the school.
  • Serve as a collaborative and mission-aligned partner across departments and constituent groups.
  • Support additional Advancement initiatives and special projects as needed.
  • The Vermont Academy Team Member: Who Are You?
  • You are:
  • A compelling relationship-builder who leads with warmth, authenticity, and professionalism.
  • A strategic thinker who can balance long-term vision with disciplined execution.
  • A highly organized self-starter who thrives in a fast-moving, entrepreneurial environment.
  • A collaborative colleague who values teamwork, trust, and shared purpose.
  • A strong communicator who can tell the Vermont Academy story with clarity, confidence, and heart.
  • Someone energized by building meaningful partnerships in support of transformational student experiences.
  • You bring:
  • Bachelor’s degree required.
  • Minimum of 5 years of advancement or fundraising experience, preferably in independent schools, higher education, or mission-driven nonprofits.
  • Demonstrated success in major gifts, leadership giving, campaign strategy, and donor stewardship.
  • Strong understanding of fundraising operations, prospect management, and moves management strategy.
  • Exceptional written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Experience with Advancement CRM systems such as Raiser’s Edge, Advancement NXT, Boost, or similar platforms.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and relationships simultaneously.
  • Sound judgment, discretion, and professionalism when handling confidential information.
  • Willingness to travel extensively and work evenings and weekends as needed.
  • About Vermont Academy: Who Are We?
  • Founded in 1876, Vermont Academy is a small New England boarding and day school nestled in the foothills of the Green Mountains. Rooted in four pillars—Land, Community, Ingenuity, and Independence—VA blends rigorous academics with outdoor education, innovation, and a profound sense of belonging.
  • Our students are encouraged to be true to their best selves; our educators create space for students to lead, explore, create, and thrive. We teach by doing. We believe knowledge cannot change the world if it is left inside a book. Personalized education is not a luxury—it is what prepares students to shape a better future.
  • Building toward Vision 2030 and our 150th Anniversary Campaign, Vermont Academy is investing boldly in:
  • Experiential and applied learning
  • Student wellness and healthy excellence
  • Entrepreneurial and environmental programming
  • Revenue-driving campus improvements
  • Community, belonging, and transformational student experiences
  • Our Commitment to Belonging
  • Vermont Academy actively seeks to build and sustain an inclusive and equitable working and learning environment. We believe every team member enriches our community by bringing a broad range of identities, perspectives, and experiences to the work of teaching and learning. We value the whole person and strive to reflect that in how we work, live, and grow together.
  • Compensation
  • Full-time hybrid, 12-month administrative position
  • Salary Range: $85,00 - $95,000
  • Benefits include health insurance, retirement plan, and meals when school is in session
  • This is a non-housed, hybrid campaign position. Remote work for applicants living in the Greater Boston or the Tri-state (CT/NY/NJ) Metropolitan region, will be strongly considered.
  • To Apply
  • Please submit one PDF including:
  • Letter of interest, addressed to Chief Advancement Officer, Kevin J Driscoll
  • Current résumé
  • A list of three or more professional references with contact information (phone and email)
  • Send materials to kdriscoll@vermontacademy.org

job.title: The Chapin School IT Support Specialist
job.description:
Job Application & Description

The Chapin School, an independent K-12 day school for girls located in New York City, seeks an IT Support Specialist.

All candidates are encouraged to be familiar with Chapin’s website and mission.

About this role

Our technology team keeps a predominantly Mac environment running for students, faculty, and staff, and effective support requires understanding the impact that technological friction can have on student outcomes. Reporting to the Director of Technology and working alongside the wider technology team and our Managed Services Providers (MSPs), the IT Support Specialist is the first person our community turns to when they need help or support. This role is responsible for responding directly to the day-to-day issues that arise for our staff and students, resolving them promptly and with empathy so that teachers can focus on teaching and students on learning, while building trust in the technology and in the people behind it.

The IT Support Specialist role is a full-time, year-round, on-site position with occasional adjustments to working hours to support school events.

Core Duties & Responsibilities

  • Serve as the first point of contact for technical support via our ticketing system, telephone, email, and in person. Triage, resolve, and escalate issues within established procedures
  • Provide student and staff support for macOS, iPadOS, and the applications our community relies on, including diagnosis, software installation, and configuration
  • Set up, deploy, maintain, and repair Apple hardware and peripherals, and manage devices through Jamf Pro and our endpoint management tools
  • Support the device lifecycle for students, faculty, and staff: provisioning, enrolment, and end-of-life, in line with procedures set by senior technology staff
  • Provide account and access support within Google Workspace and related cloud services, including password, MFA, and access tasks under established controls
  • Provide A/V, livestreaming, and classroom technology support for lessons, meetings, assemblies, and events, including setup, troubleshooting, and maintenance of equipment
  • Provide front-line support for our learning management system (Canvas), including helping teachers set up class pages and answering day-to-day questions
  • Support technical onboarding and offboarding of faculty and staff including device and account provisioning
  • Maintain accurate ticket, asset, and inventory records
  • Contribute to documentation, knowledge-base articles, and standard operating procedures
  • Apply security controls and procedures in daily work, help maintain endpoint and update compliance, and flag anomalies to senior technology staff
  • Contribute to a security-conscious culture by supporting awareness initiatives and helping the community use technology safely
  • Collaborate with the wider technology team and our managed service providers, and serve as an on-site point of contact for routine support and coordination
  • Additional responsibilities as needed to meet the needs of the school

Required Skills and Knowledge

  • Two or more years in end-user or service desk support with a focus on Apple devices
  • Hands-on troubleshooting and repair of macOS and Apple hardware
  • Experience with Jamf Pro or another mobile device management (MDM) platform
  • Experience supporting users through a ticketing system
  • Working knowledge of Google Workspace administration and common cloud applications
  • Basic networking literacy, including wireless and connectivity troubleshooting
  • Basic familiarity with Windows in a secondary or legacy capacity
  • Strong communication and customer-service skills and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team.

Highly Valued Experience

  • Experience in K-12 education or a similar educational environment
  • Apple certifications (e.g. Apple Certified Support Professional, Apple Device Support) or Jamf certification (Jamf 200 or higher)
  • A/V and livestreaming experience, YoloLiv a plus
  • Familiarity with classroom technologies such as Apple TV, video conferencing, and Veracross
  • Basic scripting or automation (Bash, AppleScript, or similar)
  • Foundational understanding of data structures, validation, and import/export workflows
  • CompTIA A+ or an equivalent foundational certification
  • Understanding of service management frameworks (ITIL or similar)

Physical Requirements

This is an on-site role, and regular in-person presence during the school day is an essential function of the position. A substantial and recurring portion of support, such as troubleshooting and handling devices in classrooms and offices, replacing cabling or peripherals, deploying and collecting equipment, and supplementing classroom A/V support, requires hands-on work that cannot be performed remotely.

With or without reasonable accommodation, this role requires the ability to lift and move equipment of up to approximately 40 lbs unassisted (such as boxes of devices and monitors), to assist with moving heavier equipment such as servers as part of a team, and to position and install hardware including displays. The role involves periods of standing and frequent, time-sensitive movement between floors and across the school's campus throughout the day, often while relocating equipment.

How to apply: Please submit your résumé and cover letter for consideration. Applications will be considered on a rolling basis.

Compensation: Commensurate with experience, the range is $75,000-85,000 annually

job.title: Jabali Academy Rising Rhythms Jazz Ensemble Instructor (Elementary/Middle)
job.description:
https://jabaliacademy.org/jobs/

Job Title: Rising Rhythms Jazz Ensemble Instructor (Elementary/Middle School)

Reports To: Director of Arts & Culture / Head of School

Employment Type: Part-Time / Seasonal / Contract (as applicable)

Position Overview:

Jabali Academy seeks a passionate and culturally grounded music educator to serve as the Rising Rhythms Jazz Ensemble Instructor. Rising Rhythms introduces students to the fundamentals of making music together through the powerful tradition of jazz—an art form born from the creativity, resilience, and collective spirit of African American communities. The instructor will guide students with little or no prior jazz experience in developing essential musical skills while fostering an appreciation for jazz as both artistic expression and cultural storytelling. This role supports the Academy’s mission to cultivate confident, culturally rooted scholars through arts education grounded in heritage, identity, and community.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Lead weekly ensemble rehearsals for beginner-level jazz students in grades 4–6 (or as assigned).
  • Teach foundational jazz concepts including rhythm, listening, call-and-response, improvisation, and ensemble coordination.
  • Foster a positive, affirming, and culturally responsive learning environment that reflects the historical and cultural significance of jazz.
  • Support students in developing musical confidence, discipline, and collaborative skills.
  • Prepare students for school performances, showcases, and community events.
  • Select and arrange age-appropriate and skill-appropriate repertoire.
  • Integrate brief cultural and historical context into instruction to deepen students’ understanding of jazz’s roots and legacy.
  • Communicate regularly with school leadership regarding student progress and program needs.
  • Maintain a safe, organized, and respectful rehearsal environment.

Qualifications:

  • Experience teaching instrumental music to elementary and/or middle school students, preferably in a group or ensemble setting.
  • Strong knowledge of jazz fundamentals and ensemble performance.
  • Ability to work effectively with beginner musicians.
  • Demonstrated commitment to culturally responsive teaching and an appreciation for the African American musical tradition.
  • Proficiency in one or more jazz instruments (piano, drums, brass, woodwinds, bass, etc.).
  • Strong classroom management and relationship-building skills.
  • Alignment with Jabali Academy’s mission and values.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Degree in Music, Music Education, Jazz Studies, or related field (or equivalent professional experience).
  • Experience working in independent schools, community arts programs, or culturally grounded educational settings.
  • Performance experience in jazz or related musical genres.

Core Competencies:

  • Cultural competence and historical awareness
  • Ability to inspire and motivate young learners
  • Collaborative and community-centered approach
  • Strong organizational and communication skills
  • Commitment to student growth and artistic excellence

job.title: Jabali Academy Legacy Notes R&B A Cappella Director (4th–6th Grade)
job.description:
https://jabaliacademy.org/jobs/

Job Title: Legacy Notes R&B A Cappella Director (4th–6th Grade)

Reports To: Director of Arts & Culture / Head of School

Employment Type: Part-Time / Seasonal (Spring Semester) / Contract

Position Overview:

Jabali Academy seeks a dynamic and culturally responsive vocal music educator to lead Legacy Notes, an R&B a cappella ensemble for 4th–6th grade students. Legacy Notes develops students’ vocal technique and musicianship while teaching the power of collective music-making rooted in the rich tradition of R&B and African American vocal harmony. Meeting twice weekly during the spring semester, the ensemble emphasizes sight reading, vocal blending, harmonizing, and introductory vocal arranging within a supportive and collaborative environment.

The Director will prepare students for performances at the Empowering Minds Gala and other community events, cultivating confidence, discipline, and artistic excellence.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Lead twice-weekly rehearsals for 4th–6th grade a cappella ensemble
  • Teach foundational vocal techniques including breath support, tone production, diction, and healthy vocal habits
  • Instruct students in sight reading, harmony building, vocal blending, and basic arranging
  • Select and arrange age-appropriate R&B repertoire
  • Foster a positive, affirming, and culturally grounded rehearsal space
  • Prepare students for public performances, including the Empowering Minds Gala and other community showcases
  • Integrate cultural context about the roots and evolution of R&B and vocal harmony traditions
  • Track student growth and provide constructive feedback
  • Communicate regularly with school leadership regarding program progress and needs
  • Maintain a safe, organized, and engaging rehearsal environment

Qualifications

  • Experience teaching vocal music to elementary or middle school students
  • Strong knowledge of R&B vocal traditions, harmony, and ensemble singing
  • Ability to teach beginner to intermediate sight reading and harmony skills
  • Demonstrated skill in arranging or adapting music for youth vocal ensembles
  • Commitment to culturally responsive teaching practices
  • Strong classroom management and relationship-building skills
  • Alignment with Jabali Academy’s mission and values

Preferred Qualifications

  • Degree in Music, Vocal Performance, Music Education, or related field (or equivalent professional experience)
  • Experience directing youth choirs or a cappella groups
  • Background in African American musical traditions
  • Performance experience in R&B, gospel, soul, or related genres

Core Competencies

  • Ability to build student confidence and stage presence
  • Collaborative leadership style
  • Cultural awareness and historical grounding
  • Strong communication and organizational skills
  • Passion for developing young voices in community

job.title: Jubilee College Director of Operations and Programs
job.description:
PROCEDURE TO APPLY

Interested candidates are invited to submit the following materials confidentially as a single PDF file:

  • A cover letter that includes:
  • Why are you interested in this opportunity and the vision of Jubilee College
  • A description of your prior experience and how your skills and passions align with this work
  • A current curriculum vitae
  • A statement of educational philosophy
  • The names, email addresses, and telephone numbers of five references, including at least two recent supervisors. References should speak to your ability to be an effective administrator and to work successfully with colleagues (references will be contacted only with the candidate’s permission). Please indicate your relationship with each reference (i.e. supervisor, colleague, or direct report).

Please address any questions by email to maryrose@strategenius.org.

SEARCH CALENDAR

Applications due: September 15, 2026

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, with priority given to those submitted by Tuesday, September 15, 2026

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

This position is being offered in a spirit of gift — Jubilee deeply believes that communities are built on generosity, reciprocity, and care for the whole person. So they hope to have an active dialogue with seriously interested candidates.

A base salary of $80,000–$90,000 is where the compensation conversation begins, not where it ends. A health insurance stipend, paid time off, and funds for professional development are baseline benefits. Also, housing is among the additional benefits Jubilee is open to discussing as part of the compensation package, for example, and on-campus options may be available based on the needs and preferences of the successful candidate.

More broadly, the founding Director of Operations & Programs will have the opportunity to travel domestically and internationally alongside students, and will enjoy daily exposure to one of the most remarkable networks of founders, advisors, visiting faculty, and spiritual leaders assembled around any educational institution in the country.

Jubilee is committed to understanding what the right candidate actually needs to thrive, not just financially but in every dimension of their life, and to doing its best to meet those needs.

job.title: University & Careers Counselor (The Bahamas)
job.description:
For Immediate consideration to start January 2027

Application Instructions

Please attach the following materials in one single PDF file:

  • A cover letter indicating your particular interest in and qualifications for this position
  • A current resume
  • A list of 5 references

Complete these 2 additional Forms:

Interest Form

A short Biography

University & Careers Counselor - The Bahamas

As a University & Careers Counselor, you’ll be responsible for supporting students in making informed decisions about their academic, university/college, and career pathways.

The role provides personalised up-to-date guidance and support to students on higher education options, career planning and university/college applications, helping students to maximise their potential and achieve successful post-study outcomes.

The post holder will work closely with students and their families to understand their individual strengths, interests, and goals, and help them identify suitable university/college options to support their chosen pathways.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Conducting one-on-one counselling sessions with students to assess their academic, extracurricular, and personal backgrounds, and develop personalized college / university admission plans.
  • Assisting students in researching colleges and universities (primarily US, UK and Europe as locations), including evaluating academic programs, campus culture, and financial aid opportunities.
  • Providing guidance on standardized testing requirements, preparation strategies, and registration procedures for exams such as the SAT and ACT.
  • Guide students through application processes (e.g. UCAS or equivalent), including personal statements, course selection, admissions tests, and interviews.
  • Organizing and facilitating college / university visits, information sessions, and workshops to educate students and families about the college admissions process.
  • Collaborating with school administrators, teachers, and other stakeholders to ensure a supportive and cohesive approach to college counselling.
  • Keeping abreast of trends and developments in college / university admissions, including changes to application requirements, admission policies, and financial aid programs.
  • Attending relevant conferences, such as ACAC, to remain professionally well networked.
  • Maintaining accurate records of student interactions and application deadlines using our counselling software system.
  • Providing support and guidance to students who may require additional assistance, such as those from underrepresented backgrounds or with special needs.
  • Develop resources and materials to proactively support outstanding careers learning and university preparation.

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE WILL HAVE:

  • Bachelor's degree in counselling, education, psychology, or a related field (Master's degree preferred).
  • Previous experience working in university / college admissions, counselling, or a related field is highly desirable.
  • Strong knowledge of admissions processes, including standardised testing, application requirements, and financial aid options.
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build rapport and establish trust with students and families from diverse backgrounds.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment, with strong organisational and time management skills.
  • Commitment to upholding ethical standards and promoting equity and access in the college admissions process.
  • Familiarity with counselling software systems and other technology tools used in university/college counselling.
  • Certification or licensure in counselling or related field is a plus.

Trinity Episcopal School is seeking a dedicated and enthusiastic Extended Day (TED) Teacher for the 2025-26 academic year. TED Teachers play a vital role in creating a safe, nurturing, and engaging environment for students during after-school hours. Responsibilities include supporting the daily operations of the Extended Day program, implementing age-appropriate activities, and working collaboratively with team members to enrich the overall school experience for our students.

Position Details:

job.title: Santa Catalina School Head Junior Varsity Soccer Coach
job.description:
Job description

Position Description

Under the direction of the Athletic Director, Santa Catalina is seeking a Head Junior Varsity Soccer Coach to lead the soccer program and team. The coach assists with game management, supervision, and organization for their team and all players, abiding by school, league, and CIF rules and regulations. This position is responsible for coaching student-athletes in strategies and techniques to prepare them for athletic competition. The ideal candidate will motivate student-athletes to develop an appreciation for competition and their sport.

Santa Catalina School believes that each employee makes a significant contribution to its success. That contribution should not be limited by the assigned responsibilities. Therefore, this position description is designed to outline primary duties, qualifications, and job scope, but not limit the incumbent nor the organization to just the work identified. It is our expectation that each employee will offer his/her services wherever and whenever necessary to ensure the success of our endeavors.

Essential Responsibilities

● Assist in coordinating and supervising the soccer team

● In coordination with the Athletic Director, schedule all non-league games and tournaments

● Promote an appreciation of physical fitness, teamwork, and sportsmanship

● Attend athletic meetings as required, including coach meetings and season parent meetings

● Report all game results to the score report Google Doc.

● Maintain appropriate behavior on the part of athletes at practices, games, and in transit to and from events

● Prioritize an environment of safety for our student-athletes and provide first aid when required

● Communicate effectively and appropriately with students and parents, in partnership with the Athletic Director

● Manage and maintain program equipment

● Communicate effectively with the Athletic Director

● Complete all required trainings in timely fashion

● In-Season Expectations:

○ Must be present Monday–Friday from 3:45–6:00 p.m. for team practice

○ Attend Open House

○ Attend coaches’ parents meeting

○ Attend Cougar Fan Day

● Off-Season Expectations:

○ Attend pre-season mandatory league meetings at Palma School

○ Attend post-season meetings at Palma School

○ Consistently check Catalina email once a week

Other Responsibilities

● Other duties as assigned for the success of the athletics program

Supervisory Responsibilities

● This position shares supervisory responsibilities for assistant coaches with the Athletic

Director

Qualifications

● High school diploma or equivalent

● Experience teaching soccer skills and strategies that apply to the skill level of the players

● Ability to establish and maintain a positive working relationship with faculty, staff, administrators, students, parents, and community members

● Valid driver’s license

● CPR/first aid certification

● CIF Fundamentals of Coaching Certification required

● A commitment to the mission and identity of Santa Catalina School

● A desire to participate fully in the Santa Catalina community

● Successful completion of a LiveScan criminal background check as required by law

Competencies

● Approachable and welcoming demeanor

● Cultural competence and enthusiasm for working with a diverse and dynamic community

● Strong interpersonal skills, including good listening, humor, tact, intuition, and confidentiality

job.title: Burgundy Farm Country Day School Rita Adrosko Visiting Artist
job.description:
https://burgundyfarm.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/BURGUNDY-VISITING-ARTIST-Overview-and-Application-Link.pdf

OVERVIEW

With its inception in 2024, the Rita Adrosko Visiting Artist Fund was established to realize a long-held dream of bringing visiting artists to campus each school year, expanding and enriching Burgundy’s arts program. From the youngest ages, students at Burgundy are immersed in the visual and performing arts, graduating with proficiency and a deep appreciation for music, visual arts, and theater.

In our youngest grades, students begin to explore artistic composition and color theory, learn to read music, collaborate on theatrical performances, and start learning an instrument by the second grade. As students move into the upper elementary and middle school years, they begin to specialize in an area of artistic choice, while still exploring the full range of artistic expressions through elective classes.

The Rita Adrosko Visiting Artist enhances our core program by bringing in outside artists and art educators to inspire and elevate a particular field of artistic expression. Visiting artists will work with a variety of student age groups, from Junior Kindergarten to 8th grade, with our faculty and staff, and will engage with our parent community.

Because each artist's situation is unique, we will work with individuals to determine the best time of the year, the number of days/hours on campus, and the specific aspects of the visit. 2024-25 Visiting Artist, Jason Curry

PROGRAM

With Burgundy students ranging from ages 4-14, there is a wide range of program possibilities that are fun, engaging, and developmentally appropriate. We expect that artists may be more comfortable with a specific age range (i.e., early childhood, elementary, or middle), and will work with the artist to prioritize teaching in the range that best fits the artist's skill set. With that said, we also want the visiting artist to impact the full community. The visiting artist will work closely with the arts faculty and administration to determine age-appropriate programming; however, the responsibility for developing and executing programmatic elements lies with the visiting artist.

Visiting artists should expect and plan for one evening event that engages parents and teaches them about the work that the artist does and is doing with our community of learners.

COMPENSATION

The stipend amount depends on teaching and artistic experience, length of the visit (both in terms of hours per day and number of days), and travel/lodging needs. We will work with the successful applicant to determine fair compensation.

HOW TO APPLY?

Application Form

job.title: Jabali Academy Lead Teacher of Diaspora Studies
job.description:
https://jabaliacademy.org/jobs/

Job Title: Lead Teacher of Diaspora Studies

Program: Roots of Knowledge Empowerment Institute

Reports To: Academic Director / Head of School

Employment Type: Short-Term Contract (Week-Long Institute)

Position Overview

The Roots of Knowledge Empowerment Institute seeks a knowledgeable, dynamic, and culturally grounded educator to serve as Lead Teacher of Diaspora Studies for its week-long cultural enrichment program. This role centers the exploration of key historical moments, cultural movements, and global connections within the African Diaspora in an age-appropriate and empowering way for elementary and middle-grade students.

The Lead Teacher will design and facilitate engaging lessons that connect history, literature, identity, and character development. The program also introduces students to influential African American writers and explores themes of resilience, creativity, and cultural pride through selected texts and guided discussion.

This position requires a strong commitment to culturally responsive pedagogy and the ability to cultivate curiosity, confidence, and critical thinking in young scholars.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Design and lead daily interactive lessons focused on significant movements, figures, and themes within the African Diaspora
  • Introduce students to selected works by African American writers and facilitate thoughtful, age-appropriate literary discussions
  • Connect historical content to themes of identity, resilience, and global citizenship
  • Develop hands-on learning activities that reinforce understanding through creative expression, group work, and reflection
  • Collaborate with sports instructors (tennis and golf) to reinforce connections between discipline, character, and cultural empowerment
  • Prepare students for a culminating presentation, showcase, or reflection activity
  • Maintain a structured, affirming, and intellectually stimulating learning environment
  • Communicate regularly with program leadership regarding student engagement and progress

Qualifications

  • Experience teaching African Diaspora studies, African American history, social studies, humanities, or related subjects
  • Demonstrated knowledge of key historical movements, global African connections, and African American literary traditions
  • Ability to translate complex historical themes into age-appropriate instruction
  • Strong facilitation skills that encourage student voice and critical thinking
  • Commitment to culturally responsive and identity-affirming education
  • Excellent organizational and communication skills

Preferred Qualifications

  • Degree in African American Studies, History, Diaspora Studies, Humanities, or Education (or equivalent experience)
  • Experience working in independent schools, cultural institutions, or enrichment programs
  • Background in integrating literature with historical instruction
  • Experience leading project-based or discussion-centered learning

Core Competencies

  • Cultural fluency and historical grounding
  • Ability to inspire confidence and intellectual curiosity
  • Skilled discussion facilitator
  • Strong curriculum planning and instructional design
  • Commitment to empowering students through knowledge and character development

job.title: Santa Catalina School Auxiliary Programs Coordinator
job.description:
https://www.santacatalina.org/userfiles/santacatalinaschoolv2mvc/01-who-we-are/Job%20Descriptions/Santa%20Catalina%20School%20Auxiliary%20Program%20Coordinator.pdf

School Description

Santa Catalina School is a vibrant, independent, Catholic school offering student-centered co-education to PreK through grade 8 and an all-girls’ boarding and day college preparatory upper school serving grades 9 through 12. Santa Catalina exists to develop in each student a striving for excellence, a maturing awareness of moral and spiritual values, a sense of responsible purpose, and a determination to serve the world with courage, grace, and compassion. With the cornerstones of excellence, spirituality, service, and responsibility, the school is committed to providing a supportive learning community for each student to grow in their intellectual, personal, and spiritual life, making Santa Catalina a transformational educational experience for its students.

Position Summary

Santa Catalina School, a nationally recognized PreK–12 independent, Catholic school in Monterey, California, seeks a Programs Coordinator for the Auxiliary Programs Department. The Auxiliary Programs Department houses three robust summer camp programs, middle school leadership programs, the After-School Enrichment Program for Santa Catalina Lower and Middle School, facilities rentals, and other emerging auxiliary programs.

Santa Catalina’s summer camps serve over 400 students with excellent programming from June through August. The After-School Enrichment Program serves Santa Catalina Lower and Middle School students daily from August to June. Facility rentals and other emerging auxiliary programs all support increasing awareness of Santa Catalina School. We are looking for a person with competence, self-direction, collaboration skills, and excellent communication skills to manage and support all aspects of these auxiliary programs.

The Auxiliary Programs Coordinator reports to the Director of Auxiliary Programs and performs administrative and operational tasks to maintain the smooth operation of the department. This position supports program organization and facilitation and directly works with students in various programs. This position requires interaction with the internal and external Santa Catalina community.

Position Description

The Auxiliary Programs Coordinator supports all aspects of the Auxiliary Programs Department, including multiple out-of-school-time programs and campus facilities rentals. Under the direction of the Director of Auxiliary Programs, this position assists with all logistics and scheduling of campus facility rentals, and performs enrollment and registration tasks for summer programs, the after-school program, Middle School Scholars programs, and other emerging auxiliary programs. The Coordinator collects, organizes, and processes participants’ forms; manages communication with parents and other constituents; and organizes rosters and other pertinent participant information for all auxiliary programs. This position supports program organization and facilitation for all auxiliary programs as needed, including assisting the after-school program, facilitating various elements of summer programs, and more. This is a year-round hourly position.

Santa Catalina School believes that each employee makes a significant contribution to its success. That contribution should not be limited by the assigned responsibilities. Therefore, this position description is designed to outline primary duties, qualifications, and job scope, but not limit the incumbent nor the organization to just the work identified. It is our expectation that each employee will offer his/her services wherever and whenever necessary to ensure the success of our endeavors.

Essential Responsibilities

● Assist the Director of Auxiliary Programs in smooth departmental operations and support emerging auxiliary programs

● Collaborate with the Director of Summer at Santa Catalina and Director of After-School Enrichment to support program operations, including daily after-school program support

● Communicate with vendors and other constituents to support campus facility rentals, including scheduling, invoicing, and other logistical support

● Communicate to parents actively and serve as a liaison for all parent communications for auxiliary programs

● Manage registration and enrollment for After-School Enrichment and Summer at Santa Catalina in two databases and collaborate with student billing

● Manage daily attendance and record keeping for all auxiliary programs

● Manage forms, calendars, emails, and telephone calls

● Compile and organize forms, rosters, schedules, and more for all auxiliary programs

● Maintain office calendar to ensure multiple department tasks are organized and completed

● Organize credit card statements and help support supply purchasing for both programs

● Support recruitment for auxiliary programs by preparing for open houses, recruitment events, and more

● Support social media posting for Summer at Santa Catalina in collaboration with the Director of Summer at Santa Catalina

● Provide daily program support for After-School Enrichment, including set-up and student supervision

● Provide program planning and facilitation support for all summer programs, including camper supervision and staff coordination, support, and feedback

● Provide onsite support for facility rental groups

● Partner with auxiliary team members and other departments for the hiring and onboarding of seasonal staff and vendors

● Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

● Bachelor’s degree required or equivalent work experience

● At least two years of experience in educational program management and operations

● At least two years of experience with event management and customer service

● Working proficiency in Spanish is preferred

● A commitment to the mission and identity of Santa Catalina School

● A desire to participate fully in the Santa Catalina community

● Successful completion of a LiveScan criminal background check as required by law

● Successful completion of a CPR/First Aid certification upon being hired

Competencies

● Cultural competence and enthusiasm for working with a diverse and dynamic community

● Youth development competence and an enthusiasm for educating young minds

● Excellent communication skills in an office environment: verbal, written, in-person, and video

● Excellent customer service skills: problem solving, patience and understanding, and ability to listen and respond to parent questions and needs

● Ability to create responsive, caring, and appropriate relationships with students, families, and colleagues

● Manage confidential files

● Proficiency in Google Suite is preferred

● Database proficiency desired, but not required

● Previous experience is preferred, but a willingness to learn is required

● Excellent organizational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple projects and meet deadlines

● Strong ability to relate to others ,including staff, faculty, students, and campers

Supervisory Responsibilities

● This position does not supervise other employees

Working Conditions and Compensation

● Work at a desk and computer screen for extended periods of time each day

● Ability to access buildings and facilities throughout a 36-acre campus, with reasonable accommodations

● Work in a school environment with a wide variety of challenges, deadlines, and people

● Additional time is required beyond a normal day or week for for evening weekend meetings to attend school events and represent the school in the community

● Santa Catalina School offers competitive insurance and retirement benefits

● Salary Range: $23-$26 per hour, depending on experience

Equal Employment Opportunity

Santa Catalina School is an equal-opportunity employer. Employment at Santa Catalina School is based solely on qualifications and competence for a particular position, without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions and reproductive health decision-making), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, national origin, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic characteristics, citizenship, military or veteran status, off-duty and off-premises use of cannabis, age, victims of a qualifying act of violence or other categories defined by state law, federal law or local ordinance.

To Apply Interested candidates should visit our website to complete and submit an application, resume, and cover letter: www.santacatalina.org/employment. Electronic submission of candidate papers in .pdf format is preferred.

Santa Catalina provides reasonable accommodations to employees and applicants with disabilities. Applicants who need accommodations to participate in the application process should contact employment@santacatalina.org.

For more information about Summer at Santa Catalina, please visit our camp website: www.santacatalina.org/summer-at-santa-catalina.

The Athletic Department operates within a K-12 independent school setting, working with over 600 students enrolled in grades 5-8th. In keeping with the Mission of the School, the Jaguar Athletic experience is a journey, which will be a source of growth, pride and enthusiasm for all members of our community. From the novice to the college-bound athlete, student-athletes have the opportunity to participate in competitive team and individual sports, developing healthy practices of mind, body and character for themselves, their teams and their school. Our international community brings together people from many backgrounds. Together we strive to create a shared culture that develops compassionate, confident and principled people who will make the world better. We base our community on these values: Respect, Integrity, Inclusion, Collaboration, and Curiosity.

Job Duties and Expectations

All head coaches and assistant coaches report directly to the Athletic Director and have the primary responsibility for administering all levels of their sport. The successful candidate will be required to follow the procedures of the high school’s athletic program, as well as those of the International and California Interscholastic Federation.

Communication

Coaches will provide clear communication for student-athletes and families regarding expectations and philosophy. In the case where a conflict arises coaches will be available to help seek resolution at the appropriate time which will not take place immediately before or after a contest.

Player Development

Coaches will assist in the total development of all student-athletes by using positive methods to create an ideal learning environment therefore helping them through their life journey, not just their athletic journey. Coaches will create and implement a meaningful practice structure to enhance instruction, development, and effective use of time for all members of the team within the program.

Player Evaluation

Coaches will use a holistic approach when evaluating a student-athlete using qualities such as skill, character, integrity, leadership, coach ability, and a love for the sport. Skill alone will not supersede the Core Principles of the Jaguar family. Coaches will select student-athletes that best represent our School’s Mission without regard to ability or status. Coaches will incorporate a student-driven, mid and post-season review that will be shared with the student-athletes.

Team Leadership

Coaches will foster an environment that will develop positive leadership qualities both on and off the field of play. Coaches will select Team Captains and Student-Athlete Advisory Committee

(SAAC) members based on character and leadership ability rather than athletic performance or status. Adhere to Chain of Command. Coaches understand that coaching at our School is a privilege and not a right. They will uphold the Mission of the school and conduct themselves accordingly.

Qualifications

  • Experience coaching at the middle school, high school, college or club level.
  • Should have experience working, playing or coaching in a value-based athletic program.
  • Must be reliable, prompt and dependable .
  • Must be able to have transportation.
  • Ability to pass a full background check.
  • Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Applicants should include a letter of interest, current resume, and three references.

Salary Range for this position is $2,000 - $4,500 depending on experience and team level.

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY POLICY

The International School of San Francisco is committed to providing an open, fair, inclusive, non-discriminatory environment for all individuals across differences of race, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, socio-economic status, ethnicity, age, physical ability, or medical condition. We seek to increase the presence, representation and inclusion of U.S. historically under-represented people of color, international, bilingual and bicultural students, faculty and staff; and, to provide an environment that will attract and retain individuals identified as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, questioning and intersex (LGBTQQI).

job.title: The School at Columbia University Security Coordinator
job.description:
https://opportunities.columbia.edu/jobs/security-coordinator-new-york-united-states

  • Job Type: Officer of Administration
  • Bargaining Unit:
  • Regular/Temporary: Regular
  • End Date if Temporary:
  • Hours Per Week: 35
  • Standard Work Schedule:
  • Building:
  • Salary Range: $66,300 - $68,000

The salary of the finalist selected for this role will be set based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to departmental budgets, qualifications, experience, education, licenses, specialty, and training. The above hiring range represents the University's good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation at the time of posting.

Position Summary

Reporting to the Manager, Operations, the Security Coordinator, Systems and Preparedness is responsible for administering and continuously improving The School at Columbia University’s security operations infrastructure and preparedness practices for students, employees, and visitors. The role involves access control, security documentation, incident reporting, event security risk review support, and readiness training and drill coordination. The position assesses evolving security and safety situations and exercises some independent judgment in determining appropriate preventive or responsive actions to protect students, teachers, staff, families and visitors, including escalation to University partners and external emergency services when warranted. The Security Coordinator demonstrates professionalism at all times and also exhibits The School’s core organizational values of caring, respect, integrity, and diversity in carrying out daily responsibilities.

This role requires post coverage, patrol and fixed position monitoring. In addition there are system responsibilities, documentation, and preparedness deliverables.

Work schedule

Standard schedule: Monday through Friday, 11:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., with flexibility to support events, drills, tabletop exercises, and incident response outside standard hours as needed, which includes weekends.

Responsibilities

Security Systems Administration

  • Administers the School’s access control system and related security technology workflows, including access provisioning and credential lifecycle management. When requested, access audits and documentation of access standards.
  • Maintains a high visibility when conducting security checks throughout The School.
  • When requested, maintains system data integrity, access groups, permissions, and reporting outputs; troubleshoots access issues and coordinates resolution with the Manager of Operations and vendors as needed.
  • Maintains standard operating procedures for visitor access, credentials, and access exceptions; implements approved updates with the Operations Manager and communicates process changes to stakeholders.
  • Safeguards The School property.

Security Planning Documentation and Event Risk Reviews

  • Maintains and updates site specific security documentation for daily operations and events to ensure alignment with established School procedures and applicable University standards.
  • Reviews security plans for on site and off site events and conducts risk reviews with the Operations Manager that identify vulnerabilities, required mitigations, and technology or process needs; supports implementation of approved measures, including access configurations and communications plans.

Incident Documentation Standards, Analysis, and Improvement Tracking

  • Prepares incident reports, routes information correctly, and maintains logs in a timely manner
  • Coordinates post incident reviews focused on lessons learned and corrective action; tracks completion of improvements and documents outcomes.

Preparedness training and Drill Coordination

  • Coordinates the schedule, logistics, materials, and evaluation tools for drills and tabletop exercises; documents results and improvement actions.
  • Provides age appropriate security and safety education to Kindergarten through Grade 8 children in partnership with school leadership.
  • Provides CPR Training to Administration, Teachers and Staff.

Situation Assessment and Independent Judgment for Safety

  • Assesses security and safety situations in real time, evaluates severity and potential impact, and makes independent judgment calls on immediate protective actions consistent with established protocols and legal requirements.
  • Independently determines appropriate escalation and coordination steps, including notification of leadership, University Public Safety partners, and external responders when warranted.
  • Applies independent judgment to implement interim safeguards during elevated risk situations, including access control adjustments, movement controls, and documentation requirements, while ensuring timely communication to appropriate stakeholders.

Compliance Monitoring Support

  • Stays current on laws and requirements impacting NYC schools and child safety and translates requirements into operational checklists, documentation updates, and staff guidance for leadership review and incorporation into practice.

Operational support during exceptions

  • Provides on site security presence during major events, drills, incidents, or temporary coverage gaps as needed.
  • Supports dismissal operations by ensuring authorization and access control processes are functioning as designed and escalates exceptions per established procedures.

Package Handling and Deliveries

  • Ensures all deliveries are logged into SPLAM, safely stored and delivered to final recipient.
  • Receives all mail, including Columbia internal mail, and coordinates its distribution to the appropriate recipients.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree required and or equivalent of five to seven years of prior security experience.
  • 2 years of progressively responsible experience in security operations administration, access control systems support, emergency preparedness coordination, risk analysis, campus safety operations, or a closely related area.
  • Demonstrated ability to exercise independent judgment in assessing risk, determining escalation, and implementing approved operational safeguards that materially impact the safety of students, teachers and staff.
  • Strong written communication and analytical skills, including incident documentation standards, trend analysis, and reporting.
  • Ability to work effectively with students, teachers, faculty, staff, families, vendors, visitors and public safety partners, with calm professionalism in high pressure situations.
  • Ability to develop training materials and coordinate drills and tabletop exercises with clear documentation of outcomes.
  • Ability to move throughout School facilities and surrounding areas, including stairs, and to remain on feet for extended periods when required for drills, events, or incident response.
  • Flexibility to support events and emergency response outside standard hours as needed.
  • Must be flexible and available to change shifts, work on weekends and attend overnight trips with notice
  • Ability to lift and deliver packages.

Licenses and certifications

  • NYS Security Guard license required.
  • Current CPR certification required; CPR Instructor Certification preferred or obtained within a defined timeframe.
  • Fire Guard license required or obtained within a defined timeframe.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Public Safety, Emergency Management, Risk Management, or related degree.
  • Experience with access control and video or security technology platforms (for example Genetec, Lenel, or comparable systems).
  • Ability to engage in conversational Spanish.
  • Equal Opportunity Employer / Disability / Veteran
  • Columbia University is committed to the hiring of qualified local residents.
